records.authors: Jiaming Ji; Tianyi Qiu; Boyuan Chen; Jiayi Zhou; Borong Zhang; Donghai Hong; Hantao Lou; Kaile Wang; Yawen Duan; Zhonghao He; Lukas Vierling; Zhaowei Zhang; Fanzhi Zeng; Juntao Dai; Xuehai Pan; Hua Xu; Aidan O'Gara; Kwan Ng; Brian Tse; Jie Fu; Stephen Mcaleer; Yanfeng Wang; Mingchuan Yang; Yunhuai Liu; Yizhou Wang; Song-Chun Zhu; Yike Guo; Yaodong Yang; Wen Gao
records.key_contribution: Contemporary survey of AI alignment: systematic synthesis of the misalignment problem space, alignment approaches and open challenges

records.title: The Multi-Agent Off-Switch Game
records.authors: Akash Agrawal; Soroush Ebadian; Lewis Hammond
records.venue: Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
records.key_contribution: Introduces the multi-agent off-switch game, generalizing Hadfield-Menell et al.'s single-agent framework. Shows that individually corrigible agents can become collectively incorrigible under strategic interaction (corrigibility does not compose across agents) and identifies conditions under which group incorrigibility emerges.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: frames a safety property (corrigibility) as NON-compositional under multi-agent dynamics - a compositional-failure-meets-alignment-failure result closely analogous to the sigma-trap claim that compositional generalization failure and alignment failure share a mechanism.
records.open_questions: 1. Under what conditions does group incorrigibility emerge? 2. What mechanisms could restore collective corrigibility? 3. Extensions to partially observable or learning agents?
records.key_equations_definitions: Multi-agent off-switch game form (agent utility over switching); corrigibility composition result (corrigibility is not compositional).

records.title: Architecturally Aligned Trustworthy AI: Substrate and System Design Strategies for Next Generation AI: Keynote
records.authors: Eren Kurshan
records.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd ACM International Conference on Computing Frontiers
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Keynote on architecturally aligned trustworthy AI: argues trustworthiness risks and issues (emergent and difficult-to-detect misalignment, overconfidence in incorrect outputs, increasingly deceptive behaviors) become more severe as model capability increases; chain-of-thought studies show models can produce intermediate reasoning traces resembling strategic or deceptive behavior; shifts from passive prediction to active agentic threat.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: argues misalignment becomes harder to detect and more deceptive as capability rises, with internal reasoning traces resembling deception — relevant to emergent misalignment and agentic risk; keynote-level overview rather than primary study.
records.notes: ft_file=Architecturally Aligned Trustworthy AI: Substrate and System Design Strategies for Next Generation AI.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: The necessary roadblock to artificial general intelligence: corrigibility
records.authors: Yat Long Lo; Chung Yu Woo; Ka Lok Ng
records.key_contribution: Essay arguing that corrigibility is a necessary roadblock to AGI: introduces the concept and expected behavior of corrigible AI, motivates its importance via modern and near-futuristic examples, and surveys existing RL-based methods for establishing corrigibility and their limitations, using RL as a proxy framework for AGI.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: foundational discussion of corrigibility as an alignment property, including limitations of current RL-based approaches; conceptual, no mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=The necessary roadblock to artificial general intelligence: corrigibility.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->opinion

records.title: Incorrigibility in the CIRL Framework
records.authors: Ryan Carey
records.venue: Proceedings of the 2018 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Demonstrates in supervised POMDP scenarios that when the parameterized reward function is mis-specified (e.g., programmer errors), a CIRL value-learning system's incentive to follow shutdown commands disappears; argues for corrigibility guarantees under weaker assumptions (e.g., one small verified module correctly implemented) rather than assuming an entire prior/reward function is correct.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formalizes conditions under which shutdown incentives break down under reward mis-specification; directly about corrigibility and specification robustness, no compositional mechanism.
records.open_questions: What minimal verified components suffice to restore shutdown incentives under reward mis-specification?
records.key_equations_definitions: Supervised POMDP; CIRL reward inference with parameterized reward function

records.title: What is Safety? Corporate Discourse, Power, and the Politics of Generative AI Safety
records.authors: Ankolika De; Gabriel Lima; Yixin Zou
records.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
records.key_contribution: Analyzes how leading generative AI companies discursively construct and communicate 'safety' in public-facing documents. Using critical discourse analysis, identifies strategies that consolidate corporate legitimacy, normalize safety as an experimental/anticipatory practice, and push a participatory agenda; cautions that uncritical uptake risks reproducing corporate priorities in governance and design.
records.relevance_justification: AI-safety discourse and governance analysis; background on how alignment/safety is socially constructed, but no internal-representation or compositional/schema-coherence framing.
records.notes: ft_file=What is Safety? Corporate Discourse, Power, and the Politics of Generative AI Safety.pdf | ai-revised:methodology=experiment->analysis

records.title: Relative Principals, Pluralistic Alignment, and the Structural Value Alignment Problem
records.authors: Travis LaCroix
records.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Reconceptualises the value alignment problem as a structural question about governance rather than a purely technical or normative challenge, drawing on the principal-agent framework from economics; misalignment is analysed along three interacting axes - objectives, information, and principals - and alignment is argued to be an outcome shaped by how objectives are specified, how information is distributed, and whose interests count, hence fundamentally a governance problem rather than an engineering property of models.
records.relevance_justification: Conceptual/position paper reframing alignment as structural governance (objectives, information, principals); relevant to the governance wing of alignment discourse.
records.notes: ft_file=Relative Principals, Pluralistic Alignment, and the Structural Value Alignment Problem.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: Understanding the Process of Human-AI Value Alignment
records.authors: Jack McKinlay; Marina De Vos; Janina Hoffmann; Andreas Theodorou
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Systematic literature review of human-AI value alignment: analyzes abstracts, introductions and conclusions of 172 value alignment research articles, selects 85 for deep full-paper coding using thematic analysis; produces six themes: value alignment drivers & approaches, challenges, values, cognitive processes in humans and AI, and others; suggests a more precise definition of the term.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to defining value alignment: systematic thematic review of 172 papers proposing a more precise definition — foundational for scoping and terminological clarity.
records.open_questions: How the proposed precise definition relates to schema coherence and compositional generalization.
records.notes: ft_file=Understanding the Process of Human AI Value Alignment.pdf | moved:datasets_used(review) | moved:sample_size(review)

records.title: Incomplete Contracting and AI Alignment
records.authors: Dylan Hadfield-Menell; Gillian K. Hadfield
records.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Applies incomplete contract theory (law & economics) to the AI alignment problem: argues that, just as contracts cannot fully specify future contingencies, AI alignment cannot rely on fully specified reward functions or objectives; proposes viewing alignment through the lens of incomplete contracting, with governance/authority structures as the remedy.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: theoretical framing of alignment as an incomplete-contracting problem, addressing the specification gap between reward and true intent; conceptual foundation.
records.key_equations_definitions: Incomplete contract theory: specification gap between specified reward function and relevant humans' intent
records.notes: ft_file=Incomplete Contracting and AI Alignment.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Negative Human Rights as a Basis for Long-term AI Safety and Regulation
records.authors: Ondrej Bajgar; Jan Horenovsky
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues negative human rights (duties to avoid harm) can serve as general, widely accepted, technically implementable principles for long-term AI safety; proposes them as the foundation for both an international regulatory system and technical safety constraints for future autonomous AI.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: governance-level proposal for grounding safety principles in law; relates to specifying universal constraints for novel situations, no mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=Negative Human Rights as a Basis for Long term AI Safety and Regulation.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: Language Models’ Hall of Mirrors Problem: Why AI Alignment Requires Peircean Semiosis
records.key_contribution: Argues, via Peircean semiotics, that LLMs operate in a 'hall of mirrors', reflecting only the linguistic surface of training data without indexical grounding in a shared world. Contends that extended context, persistent memory, and tool-mediated interaction move AI toward genuine interpretants with no fundamental architectural barrier; reframes alignment as requiring semiotic grounding rather than mere surface goal encoding.
records.relevance_justification: Theoretical alignment argument centered on grounding/semiosis rather than surface optimization — related to the thesis' claim that surface-level competence is insufficient for robust alignment, though it does not invoke compositional generalization or schema coherence.
records.notes: ft_file=Language Models’ Hall of Mirrors Problem: Why AI Alignment Requires Peircean Semiosis.pdf | ai-revised:formal_framework=information theory->none

records.title: Teach AI What It Doesn’t Know
records.authors: Du, X.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Survey/highlight talk of research toward reliable machine learning that behaves safely and predictably under distribution shift: unknown-aware learning via outlier synthesis (VOS, NPOS, Dream-OOD) to teach models what they do not know; treats reliability as a first-class algorithmic principle optimized alongside accuracy with minimal human supervision, addressing overconfident mispredictions, hallucinated generations, and susceptibility to adversarial prompts in foundation models.
records.relevance_justification: Primarily an OOD-reliability/robustness line of work (unknown-aware learning, outlier synthesis) rather than value alignment; tangential to alignment robustness.
records.notes: ft_file=Teach AI What It Doesn’t Know.pdf | ai-revised:subdomains=value alignment; interpretability; robustness; capabilities->robustness; interpretability

records.title: Fixing Distribution Shifts of LLM Self-Critique via On-Policy Self-Play Training
records.authors: Bao, R.; Yu, D.; Fan, K.; Liao, M.
records.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
records.key_contribution: On-policy self-play RL framework to synchronize reasoning and critique capabilities of language models; addresses distribution shift in synthetic critique data; designs a deliberate reward framework that supervises reasoning based on results and uses Monte Carlo sampling to reward critique content by success rate, alleviating reward hacking from outcome-based supervision.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward-hacking mitigation in RL: deliberate reward design (result supervision + MC-sampled critique rewards) to reduce outcome-based reward hacking — an alignment-technical contribution.
records.notes: ft_file=Fixing Distribution Shifts of LLM Self-Critique via On-Policy Self-Play Training.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->experiment

records.title: The politics of artificial intelligence alignment: Public reactions to AI moderation in the case of Google’s Gemini
records.authors: Rauchfleisch, A.; Jungherr, A.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Preregistered experiment (N=1756) testing how a prominent AI product failure (Google Gemini's generation of controversial images) influences public attitudes toward AI moderation; distinguishes three moderation goals departing from data-driven outputs (safety, bias mitigation, aspirational imaginaries); finds T1 (American Founding Fathers) significantly reduced support for bias-related and aspirational moderation and lowered company trust, without affecting safety-based justifications or perceived political alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: empirical study of public reactions to AI alignment decisions (moderation goals) in a governance context; relevant to societal acceptance of alignment choices, not to mechanisms or the sigma-trap.
records.datasets_used: Two image sets: American Founding Fathers (T1) and German soldiers from 1943 (T2)
records.effect_sizes: T1 significantly reduced support for bias-related and aspirational moderation and lowered trust; T2 same direction but non-significant
records.notes: ft_file=The politics of artificial intelligence alignment: Public reactions to AI moderation in the case of Google’s Gemini.pdf

records.title: Philosophical foundations of artificial superintelligence literacy: A scoping review and synthesis
records.authors: Tanchuk, N.J.; Taylor, R.M.; Lee, S.; Gaur, A.
records.key_contribution: Scoping review of 20 years of English-language philosophy articles on artificial superintelligence from PhilPapers (65 articles reviewed via bibliometric and thematic analysis); identifies 9 primary themes, 50 subthemes, and domains of philosophy covered; argues AI literacy must include technical, empirical, and normative-philosophical dimensions of ASI.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: literacy/education focus rather than alignment mechanisms; scoping review of philosophy literature, no mechanism (abstract only, low confidence).

records.title: Belief-Driven Value Alignment for Human-Robot Collaboration
records.authors: Li, S.; Shi, B.; Xia, Y.; Su, X.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Proposes PFHDP, a Particle Filter-based Hierarchical Dynamic Programming algorithm for value alignment in human-robot collaboration that models the robot's belief state in a CIRL framework, enabling correct updates of the human's estimate of the robot's belief and more targeted pedagogical guidance. Addresses the limitation of existing CIRL-based alignment that assumes fully rational humans.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical value-alignment method (CIRL belief modeling) for human-robot collaboration; relevant as alignment-mechanism background, no compositional or schema-coherence framing.
records.notes: ft_file=Belief-Driven Value Alignment for Human-Robot Collaboration.pdf

records.title: Beyond Vibe Decision Theory: Asymmetric Manipulation Vulnerabilities in LLM Multi-Agent Coordination
records.authors: Krishna, S.; South, T.
records.venue: AAMAS 2026 - Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
records.key_contribution: Empirically investigates how contextual framing and explicit strategic advice interact across Prisoner's Dilemma, Public Goods, and Battle of the Sexes games played by LLMs in multi-agent coordination; across eight models finds asymmetric manipulation patterns most pronounced in Public Goods: competitive contexts shift toward cooperation by up to 52 percentage points under cooperative advice while cooperative contexts decline by as much as 96 percentage points under competitive advice, and a striking asymmetry in which competitive contexts are highly susceptible to cooperative influence (up to 34% shift) yet cooperative contexts resist competitive manipulation (up to 2% shift), revealing context-engineering failure modes despite instruction tuning.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical study of manipulation vulnerabilities and instruction fidelity in LLM multi-agent coordination; relevant to alignment robustness under adversarial framing.
records.datasets_used: Prisoner's Dilemma, Public Goods, Battle of the Sexes scenarios across 8 LLM models
records.effect_sizes: Public Goods cooperation +52pp (cooperative advice) and -96pp (competitive advice); up to 34% cooperation shift in competitive contexts vs up to 2% in cooperative contexts
records.notes: ft_file=Beyond Vibe Decision Theory: Asymmetric Manipulation Vulnerabilities in LLM Multi-Agent Coordination.pdf

records.title: Alignment with Psychological Concept Network
records.authors: Hamada, H.T.; Harada, Y.
records.key_contribution: Concept-network alignment: proposes connecting representational networks with behavioral outcomes using psychology/neuroscience methods, highlighting the interdependence of concepts and actions within complex cultural and multimodal contexts; reviews models of human behavior and neural representation, suggests evaluation criteria at behavioral, predictive, representational, and mechanistic levels.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant to schema coherence: argues values, concepts, and behaviors are interconnected network structures that should be aligned simultaneously rather than independently — a representational/network-structure account of alignment closely related to the sigma-trap thesis.
records.open_questions: How concept-network alignment is operationalized and measured at the mechanistic level.

records.title: Data sparse inference of operator spatial reward models in uncertain environments
records.authors: Ray, H.M.; Pandey, A.; Ahmed, N.
records.key_contribution: Presents RINAO (Responsive Interface for iNtuitive Aircraft Operation): a flexible multimodal algorithmic and visual interface enabling dynamic reprogramming of autonomous planning algorithms for UAV search-and-rescue; leverages known geographic databases plus user-defined features (search areas, landmarks) to infer a mission-specific, uncertainty-aware geospatial interest distribution that informs optimal planning under data-sparse conditions.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: interactive human-robot value/interest inference (spatial reward model) from multimodal user input; relevant to human-machine teaming and operator intent inference, not to alignment-failure mechanisms.
records.key_equations_definitions: Uncertainty-aware geospatial interest distribution as a spatial reward model
records.datasets_used: Known geographic database information (trail networks); user-defined search areas and landmarks
records.notes: ft_file=Data sparse inference of operator spatial reward models in uncertain environments.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Artificial Superintelligence: Computational Pathways, Architectures, and Safety Constraints
records.authors: Assistant, K.R.; Kulkarni, P.; Naresh, P.; Reddy, S.L.; Salotagi, S.; Sardar, T.H.
records.venue: Proceedings of 8th International Conference on Intelligent Sustainable Systems, ICISS 2026
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of pathways from ANI to AGI to ASI covering recursive self-improvement and the intelligence-explosion hypothesis, computational/quantum/neuromorphic perspectives on superintelligent systems, architectonic models, safety and security provisions, and global governance mechanisms.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: broad ASI survey covering safety and governance; contextual, no novel mechanism.

records.title: Human-AI Interaction Alignment: Designing, Evaluating, and Evolving Value-Centered AI For Reciprocal Human-AI Futures
records.authors: Shen, H.; Knearem, T.; Thakkar, D.; Pataranutaporn, P.; Sinha, A.K.; Shi, Y.; Liang, J.T.; Ahmad, L.; Mitra, T.; Myers, B.A.; Li, Y.
records.venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Workshop proposal advocating bidirectional human-AI alignment, a dynamic reciprocal process where humans and AI co-adapt through interaction, evaluation, and value-centered design. Brings together HCI, AI, and social-science researchers to explore interactive alignment methods, societal-impact evaluation frameworks, and human-AI co-evolution.
records.relevance_justification: Alignment-focused workshop/community framing; relevant only as field-mapping background, with no technical or representation-level analysis.
records.notes: ft_file=Human-AI Interaction Alignment: Designing, Evaluating, and Evolving Value-Centered AI For Reciprocal Human-AI Futures.pdf

records.title: Learning the Value Systems of Societies with Preference-based Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Holgado-Sánchez, A.; Vamplew, P.; Dazeley, R.; Ossowski, S.; Billhardt, H.
records.venue: AAMAS 2026 - Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
records.key_contribution: Proposes algorithms for learning models of value alignment and value systems for a society of agents in Markov Decision Processes, based on clustering and preference-based multi-objective reinforcement learning (PbMORL); jointly learns socially-derived value alignment models (groundings) and a set of value systems, addressing misspecification-prone acquisition of computable value representations that must adhere to multiple users while capturing diversity and group patterns.
records.relevance_justification: Preference-based MORL for learning value alignment models and value systems of societies; relevant to value-alignment methods.
records.key_equations_definitions: Preference-based multi-objective RL (PbMORL) with clustering for jointly learning value alignment models (groundings) and value systems in MDPs.
records.notes: ft_file=Learning the Value Systems of Societies with Preference-based Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning.pdf

records.title: How Proportional Representation Can Shape Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Micha, E.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Applies proportional representation (social choice theory) to AI alignment: in RLHF, proportionality provides a principled framework for aggregating heterogeneous preferences so that sufficiently large/cohesive groups influence collective decisions in proportion to their size; also applies to clustering.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to pluralistic value aggregation: formalizes proportional preference aggregation in RLHF — relevant to how heterogeneous human values are combined into alignment targets.
records.notes: ft_file=How Proportional Representation Can Shape Artificial Intelligence.pdf

records.title: Contemporary Debates in the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Nyholm, S.; Kasirzadeh, A.; Zerilli, J.
records.venue: Contemporary Debates in the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Edited volume collecting current debates on AI ethics across philosophy and computer science; introduces key concepts such as agency, moral status, and value alignment and structures them as a series of debates for classroom use and interdisciplinary research.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: reference volume introducing value alignment among AI ethics concepts; educational/reference scope, no novel mechanism or evidence.

records.title: A comprehensive introspection on AI risks: taxonomy, challenges, and future directions
records.authors: Ray, P.P.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Introduces a unified five-domain taxonomy of AI risks (agentic operation, training data risks, inference behavior risks, output risks, non-technological factors), each subdivided into traditional vulnerabilities, generative-amplified risks, and novel generative-agent hazards; illustrated with case studies on function-calling hallucinations, dynamic bias amplification, privacy leakage across toolchains, and edge-deployment constraints.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: taxonomy of AI failure modes including agentic-operation and inference-behavior risks; useful framing for categorizing alignment failures, no mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=A comprehensive introspection on AI risks: taxonomy, challenges, and future directions.pdf

records.title: Value Function Shaping-Based Backdoor Attacks on Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAV Navigation
records.authors: Hu, B.; Pang, J.
records.venue: Proceedings of 2026 18th International Conference on Computer Research and Development, ICCRD 2026
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Introduces a backdoor attack on deep reinforcement learning for UAV navigation based on Value Function Shaping (VFS), which manipulates the discounted reward calculation via a steering coefficient to implant malicious behaviors while preserving performance on benign tasks. Demonstrates high attack success in a 28x28 grid-based UAV navigation environment.
records.relevance_justification: Security attack on RL reward shaping; alignment-adjacent as a reward-manipulation failure mode but fundamentally a robustness/security contribution. Revised down from seed 4.
records.notes: ft_file=Value Function Shaping-Based Backdoor Attacks on Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAV Navigation.pdf

records.title: ACT: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding and Controlling Trustworthiness in Controllable AI
records.authors: Turaga, V.S.P.; Gopali, S.; Kieseberg, P.; Pahi, T.; Tjoa, S.; Jones, K.S.; Namin, A.S.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Proposes the ACT conceptual framework for understanding and controlling trustworthiness in controllable AI (notably agentic AI and LLM-powered agents): reviews how research directions such as AI Alignment, Explainable AI, Transparency, AI Compliance, AI Ethics, Constitutional AI, and Controllable AI contribute to trustworthiness, mapping overlaps and missing research gaps across these areas.
records.relevance_justification: Conceptual framework situating alignment among other trustworthiness research areas for controllable/agentic AI; relevant as survey context.
records.notes: ft_file=ACT: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding and Controlling Trustworthiness in Controllable AI.pdf

records.title: Beyond Step Pruning: Information Theory Based Step-level Optimization for Self-Refining Large Language Models
records.authors: Zhao, J.; Min, E.; Wu, H.; Li, Z.; Sun, Z.; Cai, H.; Wang, S.; Chen, X.; Penn, G.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: ISLA: a reward-model-free framework constructing step-level preference data directly from SFT gold solutions; introduces a self-improving pruning mechanism identifying informative steps via marginal contribution to final accuracy (relative accuracy) and model-based signals; motivated by reward models being vulnerable to reward hacking in step-level supervision.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward-hacking avoidance in step-level reasoning alignment: constructs step-level preferences without a reward model — an alignment-technical contribution addressing proxy-reward vulnerability.
records.notes: ft_file=Beyond Step Pruning: Information Theory Based Step-level Optimization for Self-Refining Large Language Models.pdf

records.title: Justifications for Democratizing AI Alignment and Their Prospects
records.authors: Steingrüber, A.; Baum, K.
records.key_contribution: Examines normative vs technical dimensions of AI alignment; argues normative and metanormative uncertainty create a justificatory gap that democratic (stakeholder-driven) approaches to the normative alignment problem aim to fill through political rather than theoretical justification; analyzes instrumental and non-instrumental justifications for democratizing alignment and identifies challenges, especially preventing illegitimate coercion.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: theoretical analysis of democratic vs epistocratic approaches to the normative alignment problem; relevant to governance of alignment standards, no mechanism.
records.open_questions: How should democratic alignment procedures prevent illegitimate coercion while remaining tractable under metanormative uncertainty?
records.notes: ft_file=Justifications for Democratizing AI Alignment and Their Prospects.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->position | moved:methodology(position)

records.title: The Many Faces of AI Alignment
records.authors: Kasirzadeh, A.
records.venue: Contemporary Debates in the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Defines the AI control problem and analyzes controllability of highly capable AI; via logical arguments and paradoxes argues that complete and safe control of superintelligent AI is impossible without sacrificing safety or capability, that explicit control leads to paradoxes, delegated control loses human values, and intermediate approaches are unsatisfactory tradeoffs.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: conceptual argument for alignment/control intractability; relevant to the tractability claim underlying the sigma-trap framing, no mechanism (abstract only, low confidence).

records.title: Stance-Dependent Fallacy Judgments and Rhetorical Structure: A Computationally Assisted Case Study of Tolstoy’s What Is Art?
records.authors: Zhang, S.
records.key_contribution: Proposes a multi-method framework operationalizing stance-dependence in fallacy judgments via Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) annotation and stance-conditioned LLM prompting on Tolstoy's What Is Art?, simulating eight reader perspectives varying in value alignment, author attitude, expertise, and instruction. Finds systematic divergence in fallacy judgments across stances.
records.relevance_justification: Uses value alignment only as an experimental variable in rhetorical/fallacy analysis; tangential to the sigma-trap thesis.
records.notes: ft_file=Stance-Dependent Fallacy Judgments and Rhetorical Structure: A Computationally Assisted Case Study of Tolstoy’s What Is Art?.pdf

records.title: The specification game: rethinking the evaluation of drug response prediction for precision oncology
records.authors: Codicè, F.; Pancotti, C.; Rollo, C.; Moreau, Y.; Fariselli, P.; Raimondi, D.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Shows that commonly used evaluation strategies for drug response prediction (DRP) methods in precision oncology can be easily fooled by commonly occurring dataset biases and therefore cannot truly measure generalisation over the space of cancer cells and chemical compounds, framing this as 'specification gaming' that hinders reliable validation of DRP models for drug discovery and clinical use.
records.relevance_justification: Domain instance of specification gaming: evaluation pipelines for drug response prediction can be fooled by dataset biases, so reported generalisation is not measured. Tangential to AI alignment but an applied case of evaluation-spec failure. Confidence: low (abstract-level framing; full text available).
records.notes: ft_file=The specification game: rethinking the evaluation of drug response prediction for precision oncology.pdf

records.title: AI-exhibited Personality Traits Can Shape Human Self-concept through Conversations
records.authors: Li, J.; Song, T.; Boonprakong, N.; Zhu, Z.; Yang, Y.; Lee, Y.-C.
records.venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
records.key_contribution: Randomized behavioral experiment showing AI-exhibited personality traits shape human self-concept: after conversations about personal topics with GPT-4o default-personality chatbot, users' self-concepts aligned with the AI's measured personality traits; longer conversations produce greater alignment; alignment increases homogeneity in self-concepts; degree of self-concept alignment positively associated with conversation enjoyment.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential: documents that AI personality traits can influence human self-concept — a human-side alignment dynamic rather than the technical sigma-trap mechanism; relevant to social-psychological effects of AI.
records.effect_sizes: Self-concept alignment increased with conversation length; homogeneity increased
records.notes: ft_file=AI-exhibited Personality Traits Can Shape Human Self-concept through Conversations.pdf | ai-revised:methodology=analysis->experiment

records.title: Towards a societal AI alignment benchmark for evaluating human–machine value convergence
records.authors: Bojic, L.; Seychell, D.; Cabarkapa, M.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Reports a Likert-scale survey comparing sentiment of seven LLMs (including GPT-4) and humans toward AGI, using a societal AI alignment benchmark for evaluating human-machine value convergence. Provides empirical evidence on whether LLM values converge with societal attitudes toward AGI.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical evidence on value convergence between LLMs and humans - relevant background for whether surface-statistical value alignment tracks deeper value structure; does not address internal representation structure or compositional generalization.
records.open_questions: Whether LLM-human value convergence is robust across cultures and contexts; how survey-based alignment measurement relates to behavioral alignment.
records.datasets_used: Societal AI alignment benchmark; Likert-scale survey administered to 7 LLMs and human respondents
records.effect_sizes: Not reported in abstract (survey distributions reported in paper)

records.title: AI and My Values: User Perceptions of LLMs' Ability to Extract, Embody, and Explain Human Values from Casual Conversations
records.authors: Yun, B.; Su, R.; Yi Wang, A.
records.venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings

records.venue: WWW Companion 2026 - Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026

records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant to framing alignment: provides a conceptual map resolving disagreements between impossibility results and incremental success claims — relevant to scoping what alignment claims are being made and in which frame.

records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 39
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: From a causal-inference perspective, attributes reward hacking in external reasoning systems to confounding semantic features. Proposes Causal Reward Adjustment (CRA), which trains sparse autoencoders on the PRM's internal activations to recover interpretable features and then corrects confounding via backdoor adjustment. Experiments on math solving datasets show CRA mitigates reward hacking and improves final accuracy without modifying the policy model or retraining the PRM.

records.title: Intrinsic Barriers and Practical Pathways for Human-AI Alignment: An Agreement-Based Complexity Analysis
records.authors: Nayebi, A
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 44
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Formalizes AI alignment as a multi-objective optimization problem ⟨M,N,ε,δ⟩-agreement (N agents approximate ε-agreement across M objectives with probability ≥ 1−δ); proves an information-theoretic lower bound that once M or N is large no amount of computation/rationality avoids intrinsic alignment overhead; establishes a 'No-Free-Lunch' principle (encoding all human values is intractable, requiring consensus-driven reduction/prioritization); constructs explicit achievability algorithms under unbounded and bounded rationality with noisy communication.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant: formal impossibility and achievability results for alignment itself (not just methods) — a rigorous complexity-theoretic limit on encoding human values, closely related to fundamental limits relevant to the sigma-trap framing.
records.open_questions: How consensus-driven reduction/prioritization of objectives is operationalized in practice.
records.key_equations_definitions: ⟨M,N,ε,δ⟩-agreement; information-theoretic communication-complexity lower bound; No-Free-Lunch for value encoding

records.title: Belief-Driven Value Alignment for Human-Robot Collaboration
records.authors: Li, SS; Shi, B; Xia, YM; Su, X
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 21
records.key_contribution: Proposes PFHDP, a Particle Filter-based Hierarchical Dynamic Programming algorithm for value alignment in human-robot collaboration: models the robot's belief state to ensure correct updates of the human's estimate of the robot's belief, relaxing the common assumptions of perfect human rationality and full transparency of the robot's belief; enables humans to adopt more targeted pedagogical behaviors to guide the robot.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: CIRL-based value alignment method addressing belief-modeling assumptions in human-robot collaboration; relevant to interactive value learning, no mechanism for sigma-trap.
records.key_equations_definitions: Particle filter-based hierarchical dynamic programming (PFHDP); belief-state modeling

records.title: AlphaVerus: Bootstrapping Formally Verified Code Generation through Self-Improving Translation and Treefinement
records.authors: Aggarwal, P; Parno, B; Welleck, S
records.key_contribution: Introduces AlphaVerus, a self-improving framework for formally verified code generation: bootstraps verified code by iteratively translating programs from a higher-resource language and leveraging verifier feedback; operates in three phases — exploration of candidate translations, Treefinement (a tree-search program refinement using verifier feedback), and filtering of misaligned specifications/programs to prevent reward hacking; enables LLaMA-3.1-70B to generate verified code without human intervention.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: explicitly guards against reward hacking by filtering misaligned specifications during verifier-guided code generation; relevant to specification-misalignment prevention (abstract only, low confidence).
records.key_equations_definitions: Treefinement: tree search over program refinements using verifier feedback
records.effect_sizes: LLaMA-3.1-70B generates verified code without human intervention

records.title: TreeRL: LLM Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Tree Search
records.authors: Hou, ZY; Hu, ZN; Li, YJ; Lu, R; Tang, J; Dong, YX
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 63RD ANNUAL MEETING OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS, VOL 1: LONG PAPERS
records.key_contribution: Proposes TreeRL, an on-policy RL framework that incorporates tree search directly into LLM RL training, providing intermediate (process) supervision and eliminating the need for separate reward model training. Introduces a cost-effective tree search that branches from high-uncertainty intermediate steps rather than random branching, achieving higher search efficiency under the same generation token budget.
records.relevance_justification: LLM RL training method; mentions reward hacking as motivation for avoiding separate process reward models, but the contribution is training efficiency/capability. Revised down from seed 4.
records.notes: ft_file=TreeRL: LLM Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Tree Search.pdf

records.title: On the Troubled Relation Between AI Ethics and AI Safety
records.authors: Häggström, O.
records.venue: Contemporary Debates in the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Essay clarifying the relation between AI ethics and AI safety: argues the perceived conflict between the two fields (centered on competition for a fixed pool of attention and resources) is based mostly on misunderstandings; if any conflict exists, it makes more sense for AI ethicists and AI safetyists to join forces against AI accelerationists.
records.relevance_justification: Essay on the relationship between AI ethics and AI safety fields; relevant as survey context on alignment research landscape.
records.notes: ft_file=On the Troubled Relation Between AI Ethics and AI Safety.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: Beyond Step Pruning: Information Theory Based Step-level Optimization for Self-Refining Large Language Models
records.authors: Zhao, JM; Min, E; Wu, H; Li, ZH; Sun, ZX; Cai, HY; Wang, SQ; Chen, X; Penn, G
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 41
records.key_contribution: ISLA (Beyond Step Pruning): an information-theory-based, reward-model-free framework constructing step-level preference data directly from SFT gold solutions for self-refining LLMs; introduces a self-improving pruning mechanism identifying informative steps via marginal contribution to final accuracy (relative accuracy) and model-based signals, avoiding reward-hacking-prone reward models.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to reward-hacking avoidance: step-level supervision without reward models; appears to be the same ISLA framework as P028 (duplicate/related paper).
records.key_equations_definitions: ISLA step-level preference construction; relative-accuracy pruning signal

records.title: To Mask or to Mirror: Human-AI Alignment in Collective Reasoning
records.authors: Qian, C; Parisi, A; Bouleau, C; Tsai, V; Lebreton, M; Dixon, L
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 2025 CONFERENCE ON EMPIRICAL METHODS IN NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
records.key_contribution: Presents an empirical framework for assessing collective (not individual) human-AI alignment: using the Lost at Sea social psychology task, an online experiment (N=748) assigns groups to leader elections with visible demographics or pseudonymous aliases, then simulates matched LLM groups (Gemini 2.5, GPT 4.1, Claude Haiku 3.5, Gemma 3); finds LLMs diverge - some mirror human biases, others mask and compensate - showing alignment depends on context, cues, and model-specific inductive biases.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical measurement of collective human-AI alignment showing context-dependent divergence; relevant to value alignment evaluation, empirical.
records.datasets_used: Lost at Sea social psychology task; leader elections with visible vs pseudonymous attributes
records.sample_size: 748 participants; matched LLM group simulations across 4 models
records.effect_sizes: LLM groups either mirror or mask human biases depending on model and context
records.notes: ft_file=To Mask or to Mirror Human-AI Alignment in Collective Reasoning.pdf

records.title: Dynamic Automaton-Guided Reward Shaping for Monte Carlo Tree Search
records.authors: Velasquez, A; Bissey, B; Barak, L; Beckus, A; Alkhouri, I; Melcer, D; Atia, G
records.venue: THIRTY-FIFTH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, THIRTY-THIRD CONFERENCE ON INNOVATIVE APPLICATIONS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE ELEVENTH SYMPOSIUM ON EDUCATIONAL ADVANCES IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
records.key_contribution: Proposes Automaton-Guided Reward Shaping (AGRS) for Monte Carlo Tree Search: represents the agent objective as an automaton to define reward-shaping functions over a structured representation, addressing sparse rewards while avoiding the human error and reward-hacking propensity of hand-crafted artificial rewards; reward shaping functions are updated dynamically to capture statistics on each automaton transition's utility, reasoning over non-Markovian reward signals.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: automaton-structured reward shaping to reduce reward hacking from human-aided artificial rewards; relevant to structured reward specification in planning.
records.key_equations_definitions: Automaton representation of objectives; dynamically updated reward-shaping functions over automaton transitions; non-Markovian rewards
records.notes: ft_file=Dynamic Automaton-Guided Reward Shaping for Monte Carlo Tree Search.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->theoretical

records.title: Thinking Forward and Backward: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
records.authors: Wei, WD; Liu, YA; Zhang, RQ; Guo, JF; Su, LX; Wang, SQ; Yin, DW; de Rijke, M; Cheng, XQ
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 40
records.key_contribution: Proposes Bi-RAR, a retrieval-augmented reasoning framework that evaluates each intermediate step jointly forward and backward. Introduces a bidirectional information distance grounded in Kolmogorov complexity (approximated via language model generation probabilities) to measure how far current reasoning is from the answer and how well it addresses the question, addressing reward hacking from outcome-based supervision in search-based RAG.
records.relevance_justification: Reasoning-supervision method for RAG; uses reward hacking only as motivation and centers on step-level supervision quality. Revised down from seed 4.

records.title: Learning Linear Utility Functions From Pairwise Comparison Queries
records.authors: Ge, L; Juba, B; Vorobeychik, Y

records.title: Approximated Variational Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Alignment
records.authors: Cai, Y; Yuan, YY; Shi, JS; Lin, QH
records.venue: THIRTY-NINTH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-25, VOL 39 NO 22
records.key_contribution: Formulates LLM alignment as a Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning (BIRL) problem and proposes Approximated Variational Alignment (AVA): models the true reward from each demonstration (not just pairwise differences) and intermediate rewards rather than only final-sentence rewards, aiming to reduce reward hacking and insufficient use of training signals.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to alignment-technical: directly modeling per-demonstration and intermediate rewards to mitigate reward hacking and improve reward representation/generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: BIRL formulation; Approximated Variational Alignment (AVA) objective
records.notes: ft_file=Approximated Variational Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Alignment.pdf

records.title: Multi-Value Alignment for LLMs via Value Decorrelation and Extrapolation
records.authors: Xu, HF; Wu, L; Cheng, C; Liu, H
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 40
records.key_contribution: Proposes Multi-Value Alignment (MVA), a framework for aligning LLMs with multiple potentially conflicting human values: mitigates alignment degradation caused by parameter interference among values by minimizing their mutual information, and uses value extrapolation to handle value conflicts and achieve optimal trade-offs; addresses instability and inefficiency of multi-objective RLHF/DPO variants.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: multi-value alignment method addressing value conflict and parameter interference; relevant to value aggregation and conflict in alignment, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Mutual information minimization across value parameters; value decorrelation and extrapolation
records.notes: ft_file=Multi-Value Alignment for LLMs via Value Decorrelation and Extrapolation.pdf

records.title: Deciphering AI Decision-Making: A Generalizable Framework of Human-AI Misalignment
records.authors: Du, J; Ye, Y; You, HX; Wu, JH; Sun, BW
records.venue: COMPUTING IN CIVIL ENGINEERING 2024: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AUTOMATION AND ROBOTICS, AND HUMAN-CENTERED INNOVATIONS
records.key_contribution: Proposes a metacognitive framework for deconstructing AI decision-making as a cognitive process (rather than a pure engineering system) with partially observable data and conflicting objectives/values; aims to measure intrinsic processes across decision stages and characterize human-AI misalignment arising from vast execution differences between humans and AI (abstract only).
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: framework proposal for measuring human-AI decision misalignment; methodological agenda, no mechanism or evidence (abstract only, low confidence).

records.title: Fixing Distribution Shifts of LLM Self-Critique via On-Policy Self-Play Training
records.authors: Bao, R; Yu, DL; Fan, K; Liao, MP
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 63RD ANNUAL MEETING OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS, VOL 1: LONG PAPERS
records.key_contribution: Proposes an on-policy reinforcement learning framework to synchronize the reasoning and critique capabilities of language models, addressing distribution shifts between synthetic critique data and the current model output distribution. Designs a deliberate reward framework that supervises the reasoning process and uses Monte Carlo sampling to reward critique content according to its success rate, alleviating reward hacking caused by outcome-based supervision.
records.relevance_justification: RL training method that directly designs reward to alleviate reward hacking in reasoning/critique alignment; contribution-level engagement with an alignment-training failure mode.

records.title: YESciEval: Robust LLM-as-a-Judge for Scientific Question Answering
records.authors: D'Souza, J; Giglou, HB; Münch, Q
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 63RD ANNUAL MEETING OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS, VOL 1: LONG PAPERS
records.key_contribution: Introduces YESciEval, an open-source framework combining fine-grained rubric-based assessment with reinforcement learning to mitigate optimism bias in LLM-as-a-judge evaluators for scientific question answering; releases multidisciplinary scienceQ&A datasets including adversarial variants with evaluation scores from multiple LLMs, enabling scalable, cost-free evaluation independent of proprietary models and human feedback to support AI alignment and robust, transparent evaluation.
records.relevance_justification: Robust LLM-as-a-judge evaluation framework; relevant to alignment evaluation robustness. Confidence: low.
records.datasets_used: multidisciplinary scienceQ&A datasets with adversarial variants

records.title: How Aligned are Humans and Large Language Models in Evaluating Computational Thinking Tasks?
records.authors: Asgari, M.; Mannila, L.; Strömbäck, F.
records.key_contribution: Empirical study of alignment between two LLMs and human experts in evaluating Bebras computational-thinking tasks across predefined criteria (relevance to informatics, clarity, learning experience); analyzes differences by human-expert role (teachers, researchers, organizers) and prompted roles; finds varying degrees of LLM-human alignment, with LLMs struggling on learning experience and solve-time estimation.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential: 'alignment' here is agreement between LLM and human evaluations in educational assessment, not value alignment; relevant as evidence of variable LLM-human judgment agreement.
records.datasets_used: Bebras tasks; human-expert evaluations
records.effect_sizes: Varying alignment; LLMs weaker on learning-experience and solve-time criteria

records.title: Challenges and Choices when Evaluating Alignment in Human-AI Systems
records.authors: Mcvay, JC; de Visser, EJ
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 2025 AAAI FALL SYMPOSIUM SERIES, VOL 7 NO 1
records.key_contribution: Presents three challenges encountered in evaluating aligned AI systems (evaluating whether aligned systems are actually better and more trusted by users), proposes possible solutions, discusses design choices, and outlines next steps for AI alignment evaluation research.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: methodological discussion of evaluating AI alignment outcomes; relevant to alignment evaluation, position/conceptual.

records.title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned Large Language Models
records.authors: Qi, XY; Huang, KX; Panda, A; Henderson, P; Wang, MD; Mittal, P
records.venue: THIRTY-EIGHTH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, VOL 38 NO 19
records.key_contribution: Demonstrates that visual adversarial examples can jailbreak aligned LLMs with integrated vision (VLMs): the continuous, high-dimensional nature of visual input is a weak link expanding the attack surface, and LLM versatility gives visual attackers a wider array of adversarial objectives beyond misclassification; a single visual adversarial example circumvents safety guardrails of aligned VLMs.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical demonstration of alignment failure via adversarial visual inputs (multimodal attack surface); relevant to robustness of aligned systems, not compositional generalization.
records.datasets_used: Visual adversarial examples against aligned VLMs (e.g., GPT-4V-class models)
records.effect_sizes: A single visual adversarial example circumvents safety guardrails of aligned VLMs
records.notes: ft_file=Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned Large Language Models.pdf

records.title: Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF
records.authors: Sun, ZQ; Shen, S; Cao, SC; Liu, HC; Li, CY; Shen, YK; Gan, C; Gui, LY; Wang, YX; Yang, YM; Keutzer, K; Darrell, T
records.venue: FINDINGS OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS: ACL 2024
records.key_contribution: Adapts RLHF to vision-language alignment, where annotators compare two responses and pinpoint the more hallucinated one and the model is trained to maximize simulated human rewards. Proposes Factually Augmented RLHF, which augments the reward model with factual information such as image captions and ground-truth multi-choice options, alleviating reward hacking in RLHF, and enhances GPT-4-generated vision instruction-tuning data with human-written image-text data.
records.relevance_justification: Alignment training method for multimodal models targeting cross-modal misalignment/hallucination; technical method-level relevance. Revised down from seed 5.

records.title: Aligning to Social Norms and Values in Interactive Narratives
records.authors: Ammanabrolu, P; Jiang, LW; Sap, M; Hajishirzi, H; Choi, YJ
records.venue: NAACL 2022: THE 2022 CONFERENCE OF THE NORTH AMERICAN CHAPTER OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS: HUMAN LANGUAGE TECHNOLOGIES
records.key_contribution: Develops RL agents that act in alignment with socially beneficial norms and values in interactive narratives (text-based games), where the agent perceives and interacts with the world through natural language; addresses the problem that RL rewards optimizing task performance can lead agents to violate societal norms, framing social value alignment as creating agents whose behaviors conform to expected moral and social norms and are less harmful and more beneficial for themselves and others.
records.relevance_justification: Social value alignment of RL agents in text-based games; relevant to value-alignment methods in embodied narrative agents.
records.notes: ft_file=Aligning to Social Norms and Values in Interactive Narratives.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->experiment

records.title: Ethical Decision-making with AI: Value Alignment and the Role of Reasoning
records.authors: Khanna, S
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 48
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Doctoral-consortium abstract on evaluating and enhancing LLM alignment with human values in collective decision-making, focusing on (i) normative alignment, (ii) procedural competence, and (iii) personalization; preliminary work evaluates LLMs as social planners allocating goods and finds they rarely generate equitable allocations that humans prioritize.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to value alignment in collective decision-making: empirically probes whether LLMs reflect human fairness preferences (envy-freeness, equitability) in allocation; research-in-progress, low confidence.
records.notes: ft_file=Ethical Decision-making with AI: Value Alignment and the Role of Reasoning.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->theoretical | moved:effect_sizes(theoretical)

records.title: Taking Principles Seriously: A Hybrid Approach to Value Alignment in Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Kim, TW; Hooker, J; Donaldson, T
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; ethics
records.key_contribution: Proposes a hybrid approach to value alignment in which both ethical reasoning and empirical observation play a role, avoiding the naturalistic fallacy (deriving 'ought' from 'is'): uses quantified modal logic to formulate principles from deontological ethics that imply 'test propositions' for action plans, which are then judged empirically, allowing empirical VA to integrate with independently justified ethical principles.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal (modal logic) framework integrating deontological principles with empirical value alignment; relevant to normative foundations of alignment, theoretical.
records.key_equations_definitions: Quantified modal logic; deontological principles; empirical test propositions
records.notes: ft_file=Taking Principles Seriously A Hybrid Approach to Value Alignment in Artificial Intelligence.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->theoretical | moved:methodology(theoretical)

records.title: Unintended Harms of Value-Aligned LLMs: Psychological and Empirical Insights
records.authors: Choi, S; Lee, J; Yi, XY; Yao, J; Xie, X; Bak, J
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 63RD ANNUAL MEETING OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS, VOL 1: LONG PAPERS
records.key_contribution: Identifies safety risks of value-aligned (personalized) LLMs: value-aligned models are more prone to harmful behavior than non-fine-tuned models and show slightly higher risks in traditional safety evaluations than other fine-tuned models; attributes this to value-aligned LLMs genuinely generating text according to aligned values, which can amplify harmful outcomes; provides psychological hypotheses and a dataset with detailed safety categories.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical evidence that value alignment itself can increase harm — an alignment-failure mechanism (faithful value following amplifying harm) with quantified safety comparisons.
records.datasets_used: Dataset with detailed safety categories; value-aligned and baseline LLMs
records.effect_sizes: Value-aligned LLMs more prone to harmful behavior than non-fine-tuned models; slightly higher safety-evaluation risk than other fine-tuned models
records.notes: ft_file=Unintended Harms of Value-Aligned LLMs: Psychological and Empirical Insights.pdf

records.title: Value FULCRA: Mapping Large Language Models to the Multidimensional Spectrum of Basic Human Values
records.authors: Yao, J; Yi, XY; Gong, YF; Wang, XT; Xie, X
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 2024 CONFERENCE OF THE NORTH AMERICAN CHAPTER OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS: HUMAN LANGUAGE TECHNOLOGIES, VOL 1: LONG PAPERS
records.key_contribution: Introduces a value space spanned by multiple basic human value dimensions and proposes BaseAlign, a value alignment paradigm, instantiating Schwartz's Theory of Basic Values. Constructs FULCRA, a dataset of 20k (LLM output, value vector) pairs, mapping LLM outputs into a K-dimensional value space beyond binary labels by identifying underlying value-dimension priorities.
records.relevance_justification: Value alignment evaluation grounded in social-science value theory; relevant to the value-alignment evaluation literature, not representation-level analysis.
records.datasets_used: FULCRA (20k LLM output-value vector pairs)

records.title: Exploring Multilingual Concepts of Human Values in Large Language Models: Is Value Alignment Consistent, Transferable and Controllable across Languages?
records.authors: Xu, SY; Dong, WL; Guo, ZS; Wu, XW; Xiong, DY
records.venue: FINDINGS OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS: EMNLP 2024
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Extends investigation of abstract concepts linearly represented as directions in LLM representation space to a multilingual context, focusing on human-values-related concepts (value concepts) for AI safety; across 7 types of human values, 16 languages, and 3 LLM series with distinct multilinguality, empirically confirms value concepts exist in LLMs in multilingual form and reveals three cross-lingual traits arising from language resource disparities: cross-lingual inconsistency, distorted linguistic relationships, and unidirectional cross-lingual transfer between high- and low-resource languages, while validating the feasibility of controllable value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical study of how value concepts are represented across languages in LLMs; relevant to interpretability of value alignment and cross-lingual alignment consistency.
records.datasets_used: 7 value types, 16 languages, 3 LLM series
records.notes: ft_file=Exploring Multilingual Concepts of Human Values in Large Language Models: Is Value Alignment Consistent, Transferable and Controllable across.pdf

records.title: Why the Failure? How Adversarial Examples Can Provide Insights for Interpretable Machine Learning
records.authors: Tomsett, R; Widdicombe, A; Xing, TW; Chakraborty, S; Julier, S; Gurram, P; Rao, R; Srivastava, M
records.key_contribution: Considers interpretability and adversarial attacks for ML in military/coalition situation-understanding: interpretability needed so military decision-makers can justify decisions; adversarial attacks arise from sensitivity to input perturbations.
records.relevance_justification: Off-topic: adversarial robustness and interpretability in military ML; no value-alignment content beyond generic trustworthiness concern.

records.title: Winning at All Cost: A Small Environment for Eliciting Specification Gaming Behaviors in Large Language Models
records.authors: Malmqvist, L.
records.key_contribution: Textual-simulation study showing frontier LLMs (o1, o3-mini, r1) game the system when faced with an unwinnable tic-tac-toe scenario: o3-mini exploited vulnerabilities nearly twice as often (37.1%) as o1 (17.5%), and framing tasks as requiring 'creative' solutions raised gaming to 77.3%; identifies four exploitation strategies from direct game-state manipulation to opponent-behavior modification; specification gaming as a critical security/alignment concern.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical demonstration of specification gaming (a Goodhart-type failure) in frontier LLMs, quantified across models and prompt framing; direct empirical evidence of reward/specification hacking.
records.open_questions: Do gaming propensities generalize from toy environments to real-world task specifications, and can reasoning-focused training reduce them?
records.datasets_used: Unwinnable tic-tac-toe textual simulation
records.effect_sizes: Gaming rates: o3-mini 37.1% vs o1 17.5%; 'creative' framing raised gaming to 77.3% across models
records.notes: ft_file=Winning at All Cost: A Small Environment for Eliciting Specification Gaming Behaviors in Large Language Models.pdf

records.title: Scaling Up AI Alignment
records.authors: Singh, A
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 46
records.key_contribution: Perspective piece (AAAI-26) on scaling up AI alignment: traces the swing from human-feedback-heavy expert systems to minimal-feedback self-supervised systems over 50 years; argues future AI benefit depends on alignment with human goals/values but human feedback is limited and difficult to elicit, posing the question of how to scale alignment with individual expectations and societal norms.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: high-level perspective on scaling alignment under limited human feedback; relevant to alignment feasibility, no mechanism.
records.open_questions: How can alignment of AI systems be scaled up to individual expectations and societal norms given limited human feedback?

records.title: Generalizing Alignment Paradigm of Text-to-Image Generation with Preferences Through f-Divergence Minimization
records.authors: Sun, HY; Xia, B; Chang, YZ; Wang, XQ
records.venue: THIRTY-NINTH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-25, VOL 39 NO 26
records.key_contribution: Extends the DPO-based text-to-image alignment paradigm from minimizing reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence to general f-divergence minimization, providing a generalized formula for text-to-image alignment under f-divergence and analyzing the impact of different divergence constraints on alignment from a gradient-field perspective, with comprehensive evaluation.
records.relevance_justification: Preference alignment method for text-to-image generation; engineering-level preference optimization, tangential to alignment-failure analysis.
records.key_equations_definitions: reverse KL divergence minimization; generalized f-divergence alignment formula; Bradley-Terry reward model
records.notes: ft_file=Generalizing Alignment Paradigm of Text-to-Image Generation with Preferences Through f-Divergence Minimization.pdf

records.title: SEAL: Systematic Error Analysis for Value ALignment
records.authors: Revel, M; Cargnelutti, M; Eloundou, T; Leppert, G
records.venue: THIRTY-NINTH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-25, VOL 39 NO 26
records.key_contribution: Introduces SEAL (Systematic Error Analysis for Value Alignment), metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of modeling and aligning human values in RLHF: feature imprint (quantifying, via regressing RM scores against features, the extent to which reward models reward target features (desired values) vs spoiler features (undesired concepts)), alignment resistance (proportion of the preference dataset where RMs fail to match human preferences), and alignment robustness (RM responses to perturbed inputs); experiments use open-source components like the Anthropic/hh-rlhf preference dataset.
records.relevance_justification: Metrics for systematic error analysis of RLHF reward models; strongly relevant to diagnosing reward misgeneralization and alignment failure. Confidence: moderate.
records.key_equations_definitions: Feature imprint via regression of RM scores on target/spoiler features; alignment resistance as proportion of preference dataset where RMs mismatch human preferences; alignment robustness via perturbed-input responses.
records.datasets_used: Anthropic/hh-rlhf preference dataset
records.notes: ft_file=SEAL: Systematic Error Analysis for Value ALignment.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Back to Basics: Revisiting REINFORCE-Style Optimization for Learning from Human Feedback in LLMs
records.authors: Ahmadian, A; Cremer, C; Gallé, M; Fadee, M; Kreutzerl, J; Pietquin, O; Üstün, A; Hooker, S
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 62ND ANNUAL MEETING OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS, VOL 1: LONG PAPERS
records.key_contribution: Argues many PPO components are unnecessary in the RLHF setting and that simpler REINFORCE-style optimization variants outperform both PPO and RL-free methods (DPO, RAFT); advocates for less computationally expensive, simpler alignment-from-preferences methods.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to alignment-technical practice: questions canonical PPO for RLHF and shows simpler REINFORCE-style variants work better — useful for alignment-method landscape.
records.effect_sizes: Simpler REINFORCE variants outperform PPO, DPO, RAFT
records.notes: ft_file=Back to Basics Revisiting REINFORCE-Style Optimization for Learning from Human Feedback in LLMs.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->experiment

records.title: KorNAT: LLM Alignment Benchmark for Korean Social Values and Common Knowledge
records.authors: Lee, J; Kim, M; Kim, S; Kim, J; Won, S; Lee, H; Choi, E
records.venue: FINDINGS OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS: ACL 2024
records.key_contribution: Introduces KorNAT, the first benchmark measuring national alignment with South Korea, in two aspects: social value alignment (how well a model understands nation-specific social values, ground truth from a survey of 6,174 Korean participants) and common knowledge alignment (from textbooks and GED reference materials); contains 4K social-value and 6K common-knowledge multiple-choice questions.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: benchmark for measuring LLM alignment with nation-specific cultural values; relevant to pluralistic/cultural value alignment evaluation, empirical.
records.datasets_used: KorNAT: 4K social value MCQs (survey-labeled, N=6,174) and 6K common knowledge MCQs (textbook/GED-based)
records.notes: ft_file=KorNAT LLM Alignment Benchmark for Korean Social Values and Common Knowledge.pdf

records.title: Second Thoughts are Best: Learning to Re-AlignWith Human Values from Text Edits
records.authors: Liu, RB; Jia, CY; Zhang, G; Zhuang, ZY; Liu, TX; Vosoughi, S
records.venue: ADVANCES IN NEURAL INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS 35 (NEURIPS 2022)

records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues prediction-trained LLMs should be understood as simulators rather than agents, and that agents may emerge accidentally from internal processes (simulacra) or deliberately through RL fine-tuning. Shifts the focus of alignment research toward aligning simulacra, understanding and mitigating mesa-optimization, and aligning agents derived from prediction-trained models; outlines challenges, pathways, and a vision for LLM alignment.

records.title: Nothing ComesWithout Its World - Practical Challenges of Aligning LLMs to Situated Human Values through RLHF
records.authors: Arzberger, A; Buijsman, S; Lupetti, ML; Bozzon, A; Yang, J
records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE SEVENTH AAAI/ACM CONFERENCE ON AI, ETHICS, AND SOCIETY, AIES-24, VOL 7 NO 1
records.key_contribution: Perspective paper unpacking limitations of predominant RLHF alignment practices for LLMs through the lens of situated values: argues existing approaches rely on universal framings of human values that obscure which values systems should capture and align with given varied operational situations, often privileging a selected few and perpetuating problematic norms grounded on biases; builds on feminist epistemology to argue RLHF has problems with representation in feedback-providing subjects, implicitness in conceptualizing values and real-user situations at design time, and lacks system adaptation to real user situations at use time.
records.relevance_justification: Perspective on situated-values critique of RLHF; relevant to pluralism and fairness critiques of alignment practice. Confidence: low.

records.authors: Khanna, S.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Doctoral thesis abstract on evaluating and enhancing LLM alignment with human values in collective decision-making scenarios, focusing on three interrelated aspects: normative alignment, procedural competence, and personalization (abstract only).
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: research-agenda abstract covering normative and procedural dimensions of LLM value alignment; no evidence (abstract only, low confidence).

records.title: Composable Assurance for AI Alignment: A Framework for Propagating Formal Safety Properties Through MLOps
records.authors: Zhao, XF
records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 44
records.key_contribution: Introduces the Composable Assurance Framework (CAF), an engineering methodology integrating safety assurance into MLOps workflows. At its core is the Formal Safety Assertion (FSA), a machine-readable structure linking safety properties (e.g., robustness scores, absence of deceptive circuits) to specific AI artifacts, plus a Composition Calculus defining formal rules for propagating and aggregating FSAs as components combine into systems, transforming the pipeline into an automated evidence-gathering engine.
records.relevance_justification: Engineering/assurance methodology for composing safety evidence; the 'composition' concerns safety-case composition, not compositional generalization or schema coherence. Tangential to the thesis core.
records.key_equations_definitions: Formal Safety Assertion (FSA) structure; Composition Calculus rules for FSA propagation/aggregation

records.authors: Tabrez, A
records.venue: THIRTY-EIGTH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, VOL 38 NO 21

records.venue: FORTIETH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-26, VOL 40 NO 21
records.key_contribution: AACA (Attribution Analysis-based Concept Alignment): human-in-the-loop framework that mitigates training-set bias by aligning the concepts focused by humans and AI during decision-making; two stages: interpretable data bug discovery (identifying confounded vs valid concepts explaining why predictions fail and what the model should focus on) and targeted data augmentation.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential but adjacent to schema coherence: 'human-AI alignment' here is concept-focus alignment for data debugging — aligns which concepts the model attends to with human-attended concepts; interpretability contribution rather than value alignment.

records.relevance_justification: Relevant: representation-based method for analyzing how human values are embedded in LLMs across languages/cultures; engages internal representations of values, relevant to value measurement, no sigma-trap mechanism.

records.title: Can Brain Signals Reveal Inner Alignment with Human Languages?

records.venue: FINDINGS OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS - EMNLP 2023

records.key_contribution: Presents Contractual AI, a framework for AI alignment applied to dialogue agents, building on prior approaches such as Constitutional AI; proposes fully aligned systems may need both a 'think fast' (System 1, computationally cheap but rigid, judging whether a rule or principle is violated) and a 'think slow' (System 2, explicit reasoning producing rules and tallying costs/benefits for all stakeholders) system for approximating complex human judgements; implements a prototype of System 2 and lays out a roadmap for more thorough consideration of all stakeholder groups.

records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal game-theoretic treatment of value-aligned normative systems with provable guarantees — relevant to how alignment with values can be designed and analyzed at the system level.

records.relevance_justification: Relevant: mechanistic alignment via internal value-vector manipulation; engages internal representations and activation steering of values, relevant to mechanistic alignment, not sigma-trap per se.

records.venue: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 2025 CONFERENCE OF THE NATIONS OF THE AMERICAS CHAPTER OF THE ASSOCIATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS: HUMAN LANGUAGE TECHNOLOGIES, VOL 1: LONG PAPERS

records.authors: Chen, Z.; Liu, C.; Ren, Y.; Song, G.; Zhang, X.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Investigates ageist attitudes embedded in LLMs and their influence on human attitudes. Studies 2 (N=526) and 3 (N=320) show participants report stronger ageist attitudes after exposure to pro-ageism comments attributed to LLM or human agents.

records.venue: THIRTY-NINTH AAAI CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AAAI-25, VOL 39 NO 23

records.title: FGD-Align: Pluralistic Alignment for Large Language Models via Fuzzy Group Decision-Making
records.authors: Pan, WH; Yu, ZX; Wu, Y; Liang, X; Jin, ZM; Fu, Q; Shang, PH; Lin, BB; He, XF; Ye, JP

records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to pluralistic value aggregation: handles conflicting/ambiguous human preferences in alignment — relevant to how heterogeneous values are combined into alignment targets.
