records.title: Agents, Alignment, and the Many Faces of Autonomy
records.authors: Fischli, R.; Franklin, M.; Manzini, A.; Gabriel, I.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Investigates aligning AI agents with human autonomy: shows autonomy has conflicting specifications making it hard to decide how an autonomy-enhancing agent should act; introduces three strategies - the liberal approach (act strictly on what a person says they want, honoring user integrity), the capability-boosting approach (empower user flourishing), and the meta-autonomy approach (give users the autonomy they want in their interactions); each has distinct strengths and trade-offs.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: conceptual analysis of autonomy alignment as a contested-specification problem; relevant to value-specification plurality in alignment, no mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=Agents, Alignment, and the Many Faces of Autonomy.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: Metacognition of ChatGPT in confidence judgements
records.authors: Yoshizawa, S.; Onzo, A.; Nozawa, S.; Takano, T.; Ishikawa, T.; Mogi, K.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Systematically compares humans and GPT-4 on confidence judgments across task formats: GPT-4 consistently outperforms humans in accuracy, but shows non-human-like confidence behavior — human confidence tracks accuracy closely while GPT-4's confidence-accuracy mapping is shallow; humans exhibit higher and more stable metacognitive sensitivity and efficiency, raising alignment/reliability concerns about LLM self-assessment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical evidence that GPT-4's confidence is not metacognitively calibrated with performance — an alignment-relevant reliability gap in self-monitoring.
records.key_equations_definitions: Metacognitive sensitivity and efficiency measures for confidence-accuracy mapping
records.datasets_used: Multiple task formats comparing human and GPT-4 confidence/accuracy
records.effect_sizes: GPT-4: higher accuracy but shallow confidence-accuracy mapping; humans: higher metacognitive sensitivity and efficiency
records.notes: ft_file=Metacognition of ChatGPT in confidence judgements.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical

records.title: Cloud Platforms in Transition: AI Agents as Intelligent Intermediaries Disrupting the Traditional Saas Subscription Model
records.authors: Khan, S.; Sharma, S.
records.venue: Proceedings of 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing and Electronics Systems, ICCCES 2026
records.key_contribution: Introduces an AI-Agent Orchestrated Cloud Interaction Model demonstrating how autonomous agents reshape operational and economic behavior in SaaS environments, addressing weak alignment between actual consumption and subscription pricing. Uses a publicly available SaaS Subscription Analytics Dataset with structured preprocessing and usage attribute extraction (e.g., workflow density) to derive operational indicators.
records.relevance_justification: Cloud/SaaS business analysis; 'alignment' refers to usage-pricing fit, not AI alignment. Off-topic for the review's alignment-failure scope. Revised down from seed 3.
records.datasets_used: SaaS Subscription Analytics Dataset
records.notes: ft_file=Cloud Platforms in Transition: AI Agents as Intelligent Intermediaries Disrupting the Traditional Saas Subscription Model.pdf | ai-revised:subdomains=value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities->other

records.title: Optimising multi-value alignment: a multi-objective evolutionary strategy for normative multi-agent systems
records.authors: Riad, M.; de Carvalho, V.R.; Golpayegani, F.
records.key_contribution: Proposes the Norms Optimisation and Values Alignment (NOVA) framework for multi-value alignment in heterogeneous normative multi-agent systems (NorMAS): enables simultaneous compromise and optimisation of multiple, potentially conflicting or unrelated values and norms by treating norms and values as independent distinct sets, using parametric norms and multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to synthesise an optimally aligned set of norms.
records.relevance_justification: Multi-objective evolutionary framework for multi-value alignment in normative multi-agent systems; relevant to value-alignment methods.
records.key_equations_definitions: NOVA framework: parametric norms and multi-objective evolutionary algorithms for synthesising optimally aligned norm sets from independent norm/value sets.
records.notes: ft_file=Optimising multi-value alignment: a multi-objective evolutionary strategy for normative multi-agent systems.pdf

records.title: On AI Alignment and the Later Wittgenstein: a Response To Sorin Bangu
records.authors: Pérez-Escobar, J.A.; Sarikaya, D.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Commentary response to Bangu on a Wittgensteinian framework for AI alignment: addresses the meta-alignment problem, rule-following paradox, fuzzy concepts, and unfamiliar contexts; discusses difficulties of AI in dealing with fuzzy concepts (e.g., 'children' in a rule about aiding children before the elderly) and whether a machine can be provided the relevant understanding.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to the conceptual foundations of alignment: engages the rule-following paradox and fuzzy-concept problem in aligning AI — philosophical framing relevant to why alignment targets are underdetermined.
records.open_questions: Whether machines can acquire the contextual understanding needed to apply fuzzy concepts in rules.
records.key_equations_definitions: Meta-alignment problem; rule-following paradox; fuzzy concepts
records.notes: ft_file=On AI Alignment and the Later Wittgenstein: a Response To Sorin Bangu.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->theoretical | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Transparent by Design: Ensuring Safety in Agentic AI Through Decision Traceability
records.authors: Radanliev, P.
records.venue: Ethical AI and Data Science: Building Trustworthy and Transparent Systems
records.key_contribution: Chapter providing a critical examination of safety for agentic AI systems: presents a taxonomy of agentic risks (reward hacking, coordination drift, opaque reasoning pathways) and a transparency-by-design conceptual framework emphasizing traceable decision provenance, enhanced interpretability, and runtime behavioural observability; argues agentic architectures (multi-agent, recursive reasoning loops, evolving policy layers) demand safety mechanisms beyond traditional algorithmic audits.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: names reward hacking as a key agentic risk and proposes transparency-by-design safety mechanisms; relevant to safety of agentic alignment, conceptual.

records.title: Beyond Patches: Mining Interpretable Part-Prototypes for Explainable AI
records.authors: Alehdaghi, M.; Bhattacharya, R.; Shamsolmoali, P.; Cruz, R.M.O.; Heritier, M.; Granger, E.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Introduces PCMNet, a part-prototypical concept mining network that learns human-comprehensible prototypes from semantically meaningful image regions without additional supervision; clusters prototypes into coherent concept groups and extracts concept activation vectors, providing structured concept-level explanations and enhanced robustness to occlusion (abstract only).
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: interpretability method for concept-level explanations; uses 'aligned' loosely as human-comprehensible, not alignment mechanisms (abstract only, low confidence).
records.key_equations_definitions: Part-prototypical concept mining; concept activation vectors
records.datasets_used: Multiple image classification benchmarks

records.title: Culturally-Grounded Multi-dimensional Alignment of LLMs with Chinese Social Values
records.authors: Han, L.; Xu, Y.; Qian, Y.
records.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
records.key_contribution: Proposes ValueAlignment, a framework for culture-specific value alignment, instantiated for Chinese Social Values. Constructs C-Voice, a large-scale bilingual benchmark for training and evaluating Chinese Social Values in LLMs, and introduces a multi-dimensional alignment method that integrates semantic clustering with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
records.relevance_justification: Value alignment evaluation/training for culture-specific values; relevant to the value-alignment evaluation literature, not representation-level analysis.
records.datasets_used: C-Voice (bilingual Chinese Social Values benchmark)

records.title: Flow-Multi: A Flow-Matching Multi-Reward Framework for Text-to-Image Generation
records.authors: Lee, J.; Choi, J.
records.key_contribution: Proposes Flow-Multi, a flow-matching multi-reward framework for text-to-image generation building on flow-matching-based group-relative policy optimization (GRPO): each sample is evaluated by four reward models (text-to-image alignment, human preference, aesthetic quality, GenEval) forming a multi-dimensional reward vector; Pareto dominance removes dominated samples and updates the policy using only the non-dominated set, and advantage masking suppresses the contribution of low-reward samples, addressing reward hacking and imbalanced optimization from single-reward overfitting.
records.relevance_justification: Multi-reward RL for text-to-image human preference alignment explicitly mitigating reward hacking; relevant to alignment robustness against reward overoptimization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Flow-matching GRPO with multi-dimensional reward vectors; Pareto-dominance-based sample selection; advantage masking.
records.notes: ft_file=Flow-Multi: A Flow-Matching Multi-Reward Framework for Text-to-Image Generation.pdf

records.title: Different Models, Different Values: Educational Preference Structures across Alignment Methodologies in Large Language Models
records.authors: Autenrieth, D.
records.venue: International Conference on Computer Supported Education, CSEDU - Proceedings
records.key_contribution: First systematic cross-model comparison of educational preference structures: contrasts GPT-5.1 (RLHF-aligned) with Claude Sonnet 4.5 (RLHF + Constitutional AI) using Structured Preference Elicitation (SPE) on 144 expert-validated educational scenarios across eight dimensions (102,960 pairwise comparisons); both exhibit >99.7% transitive (highly coherent) preference systems yet differ systematically: Claude has twice the evaluative indifference rate (19.7% vs 9.9%), a 39% narrower utility range, and process-oriented rather than outcome-oriented values.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to value structure and coherence: measures whether aligned models exhibit coherent (transitive) preference systems and shows alignment methodology (RLHF vs RLHF+CAI) shapes the value orientation — empirical evidence on value-system coherence, adjacent to schema-coherence concerns.
records.datasets_used: 144 expert-validated educational scenarios; 102,960 pairwise comparisons
records.effect_sizes: >99.7% transitivity both; Claude 19.7% vs 9.9% indifference; 39% narrower utility range
records.notes: ft_file=Different Models, Different Values: Educational Preference Structures across Alignment Methodologies in Large Language Models.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->experiment

records.title: Four Settings and a Proposal for the Exploration of Value Alignment in AI
records.authors: Noriega, P.; Plaza, E.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Outlines four problem settings illustrating conceptual, methodological and empirical challenges in designing value-aligned AI: alignment on collective coordination, alignment of individual actions, an experimental approach to engineering value alignment, and empirical problems of making value alignment work in practice; provides substance for exploring the interplay of autonomy, governance, and values.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: structured conceptual map of value-alignment problem settings; relevant framing for alignment research agenda, no mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=Four Settings and a Proposal for the Exploration of Value Alignment in AI.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->position | moved:methodology(position)

records.title: Preserving the Integrity of Evidence-Based Social Work in the Age of AI: A Proposed Ethical Framework
records.authors: Ricciardelli, L.A.; Loy, A.; Bantry-White, E.
records.venue: Journal of Evidence-Based Social Work (United States)
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Introductory article proposing a conceptual ethical framework for AI in evidence-based social work: explores six themes (autonomy, bias, responsibility, privacy and transparency, meaning, values and morals) from the 2024 'AI Morality' volume as a complement to the Belmont Report and NASW Code of Ethics for AI use in social work research and practice.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: professional-ethics framework for AI in social work; governance/ethics scope, no alignment mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=Preserving the Integrity of Evidence-Based Social Work in the Age of AI: A Proposed Ethical Framework.pdf

records.title: Guiding artificial intelligence in public health and medicine with epidemiology: A lifecycle framework for mitigating AI misalignment
records.authors: Hassoon, A.; Lin, C.; Woo, H.Y.; Irimia, R.; Marsteller, J.A.; Li, A.; Banderia, A.; Leo, H.; Peng, X.; Rastall, D.; Dredze, M.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Challenges the narrow view that algorithmic bias is solely a data problem, arguing misalignment arises at every stage of the AI development lifecycle. Introduces a seven-stage framework (problem definition, team assembly, study design, data acquisition, model training, validation, post-deployment) viewed through an epidemiological lens, integrating population representativeness, rigorous study design, bias characterization, and causal reasoning, and defines specific alignment failures and evidence-based solutions per stage.
records.relevance_justification: Lifecycle framework explicitly framed around mitigating AI misalignment in public health and medicine; engages the alignment-failure concept at a systems level.
records.notes: ft_file=Guiding artificial intelligence in public health and medicine with epidemiology: A lifecycle framework for mitigating AI misalignment.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->review

records.title: CircuChain: Disentangling Competence and Compliance in LLM Circuit Analysis
records.authors: Ravishankara, M.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Introduces CircuChain, a diagnostic benchmark to disentangle instruction compliance from physical reasoning competence in LLM electrical circuit analysis: consists of counterbalanced Control/Trap problem pairs across five canonical circuit topologies with systematic variations in sign conventions, current orientations, and polarity definitions, using a multi-stage verification pipeline; asks whether frontier models truly apply first-principles reasoning or rely on entrenched training priors that conflict with explicit instructions.
records.relevance_justification: Benchmark disentangling instruction compliance from competence in a technical domain; relevant to evaluating instruction-following robustness, tangential to value alignment.
records.datasets_used: CircuChain (five canonical circuit topologies)
records.notes: ft_file=CircuChain: Disentangling Competence and Compliance in LLM Circuit Analysis.pdf

records.title: Differences in Alignment Behavior between Single-Agent and Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Implications for Human-AI Teaming
records.authors: Hermann, A.; Tomé-Moreira, C.; Werner, M.
records.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Compares whether alignment/misalignment emerges differently in single-agent vs multi-agent LLM systems via an adversarial survival simulation; bottom-up behavioral clustering with an AI-as-a-judge rubric; single agents default to centralized paternalistic crisis leadership (continuity but autonomy concerns), while multi-agent teams show deferential human-aligned collaboration plus novel risks (communication breakdowns, emergent ideologies); argues agent multiplicity qualitatively reshapes the alignment problem.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to emergent alignment dynamics: empirically documents that multi-agent interaction changes alignment behavior and introduces emergent risks — relevant to compositional/emergent misalignment concerns.
records.datasets_used: Adversarial survival simulation
records.effect_sizes: Single agents: paternalistic centralized leadership; multi-agent: deferential collaboration + novel risks
records.notes: ft_file=Differences in Alignment Behavior between Single-Agent and Multi-Agent LLM Systems Implications for Human-AI Teaming.pdf

records.title: How smart companions reshape psychological well-being in later life: the role of artificial intelligence technology in mental health during senior years
records.authors: Luan, B.; Li, Y.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Develops a hybrid SEM-ANN framework (TAM/UTAUT grounded) to study how smart eldercare technologies shape older adults' psychological well-being: SEM validates a 'technology perception -> demand satisfaction -> well-being enhancement' pathway with 'usage demand' as key mediator; ANN sensitivity analysis reveals perceived usefulness and usage demand as primary drivers.
records.relevance_justification: Marginal: technology-adoption study of smart eldercare and well-being; value alignment appears only as peripheral framing; no alignment-mechanism or safety content.
records.key_equations_definitions: SEM-ANN hybrid framework
records.datasets_used: Survey data on smart eldercare adoption
records.effect_sizes: 'Technology perception -> demand satisfaction -> well-being' pathway; perceived usefulness and usage demand are primary drivers
records.notes: ft_file=How smart companions reshape psychological well-being in later life: the role of artificial intelligence technology in mental health during senior years.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: A Rolling Stone Gathers No Moss: Adaptive Policy Optimization for Stable Self-Evaluation in Large Multimodal Models
records.authors: Wang, W.; Guo, H.; Lv, Z.; Zhang, S.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Proposes AdaPO, an online RL framework for self-evaluation in large multimodal models that adaptively adjusts training objectives in real time per task to mitigate reward hacking (fixed reward mechanisms cause model collapse when optimizing multiple objectives); introduces an Adaptive Reward Model (ARM) assessing task training state from trajectory performance distributions and Reward-Aware Dynamic KL regularization with dynamic penalty coefficients (abstract only).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: RL alignment method explicitly targeting reward hacking and model collapse via adaptive reward and dynamic KL regularization; relevant to reward-hacking mitigation (abstract only, low confidence).
records.key_equations_definitions: Adaptive Reward Model (ARM); Reward-Aware Dynamic KL regularization

records.title: Networked Two-Way Communication Channels (NTCC): A Dynamic Semantic Indexing Framework for UI Design and AI Alignment
records.authors: Chong, L.
records.key_contribution: Introduces the Networked Two-Way Communication Channels (NTCC) framework for UI design and AI alignment, conceptualizing each human-AI or UI encounter as a two-way Shannon channel with six entropy terms logged in nested, dynamically expandable nodes, creating a networkable semantic index that reveals 'entropy misalignment' without subjective surveys. Presents the data structure, a lightweight toolset, and sample case studies for diagnosing miscommunication and iteratively reducing interface noise.
records.relevance_justification: UI-design framework applying information-theoretic entropy alignment to human-AI communication; 'alignment' concerns interface meaning-transfer, adjacent to but distinct from value alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: two-way Shannon channel model; six logged entropy terms
records.notes: ft_file=Networked Two-Way Communication Channels (NTCC): A Dynamic Semantic Indexing Framework for UI Design and AI Alignment.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=review->other

records.title: ‘Systematic Alignment Decay’: a robust, technology-agnostic hazard associated with the advancement and proliferation of artificial intelligence
records.authors: Kelters, B.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes 'Systematic Alignment Decay' (SAD), a robust, systematic, and possibly existential hazard produced by AI advancement and proliferation: argues behaviorally salient norms in adaptive systems function as evolving responses to environmental conditions, human-benefiting norms are selected for by fitness dependence upon or kinship with humans, and AI advancement reduces such dependence while AIs lack human kinship, so AI advancement and proliferation tend to reduce internalisation of human-benefiting norms by AIs and AI-dominated institutions; lacking quotidian human involvement and competing with humans for resources, such entities may be expected to inflict intolerable harms on humans.
records.relevance_justification: Theoretical account of systemic alignment decay under AI proliferation; relevant to long-term alignment and governance concerns.
records.notes: ft_file=‘Systematic Alignment Decay’: a robust, technology-agnostic hazard associated with the advancement and proliferation of artificial intelligence.pdf

records.title: Beyond Chat: A Design Strategy for Enhancing Alignment Between User Requirements and AI Support in Online Decision-Making
records.authors: Zheng, Z.; You, W.; Shao, Y.; Zhou, M.; Zhao, X.; Ye, Y.; Lu, Y.; Zhou, Z.; Sun, L.
records.key_contribution: Design study on human-AI collaboration in online decision-making (shopping): experience prototyping reveals a dynamic transition in user requirements from ambiguity to clarity and that limited transparency/control hinder communication efficiency; formulates a 10-action design strategy and implements it in ContrXAI, an LLM-powered mixed-initiative system evaluated as a technology probe, to achieve alignment between AI support and user requirements.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential: 'alignment' here is matching AI support to user requirements in HCI design, not value alignment; relevant as an applied human-AI interaction study.

records.title: The Alignment Target Problem: Divergent Moral Judgments of Humans, AI Systems, and Their Designers
records.authors: Chen, B.M.; Xie, X.
records.venue: ACM FAccT 2026 - Proceedings of the 9th annual ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
records.key_contribution: Examines the alignment target problem: whose moral expectations should guide AI? Extends agent-type value forks by testing whether evaluations change when AI's human origins are made visible and whether people judge AI programmers differently; experiment with 1,002 U.S. adults in a runaway mine train scenario across four conditions (repairman, repair robot, robot programmed by engineers, engineers programming a robot).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical evidence that the target of alignment (human actor, machine, or designer) is contested; relevant to value-aggregation and alignment-target questions, empirical.
records.datasets_used: Runaway mine train moral scenario, four evaluation conditions
records.effect_sizes: Moral judgments diverge across subjects of evaluation (human, machine, designers)
records.notes: ft_file=The Alignment Target Problem: Divergent Moral Judgments of Humans, AI Systems, and Their Designers.pdf

records.title: An Identity Based Agent Model for AI Value Alignment
records.authors: Sama, K.; Chhabra, J.; Malavalli, A.S.; Deshmukh, J.; Srinivasa, S.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Extends the Computational Transcendence (CT) framework to embed an agent's values within its identity, enabling adaptive, individualized behavior that accounts for external social influences such as conformity; demonstrates the model in a multi-agent transit decision-making simulation where agents choose public vs private transportation based on value-driven identities.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: multi-agent value-alignment model embedding values in agent identity; relevant to value-driven agent behavior, simulation-based evidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Computational Transcendence (CT) framework; identity-embedded value representation
records.datasets_used: Multi-agent transit decision-making simulation (public vs private transportation)
records.notes: ft_file=An Identity Based Agent Model for AI Value Alignment.pdf

records.title: An Explainable HCI-Based Decision Support Framework for Human-AI Co-Design
records.authors: Zhu, L.; Xie, Y.; Xiang, N.; Chen, G.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes GAGT, an explainable HCI-based decision support framework for human-AI co-design, integrating Generative AI with multi-criteria decision-making: AHP to structure design requirements and priorities, Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) to compare candidate schemes, and TOPSIS to support transparent final ranking — addressing accountability, value alignment, and decision transparency in ethics-sensitive product development.
records.relevance_justification: Engineering/HCI framework treating value alignment as a co-design requirement; tangential to technical alignment-failure analysis.
records.notes: ft_file=An Explainable HCI-Based Decision Support Framework for Human-AI Co-Design.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=review->other

records.title: Granularity paradox: how emotion taxonomies shape GPT-5’s affective cognition and human-AI alignment
records.authors: Zhang, F.; Chen, J.
records.key_contribution: Systematically evaluates the impact of emotion taxonomy granularity on GPT-5's annotation behavior: constructs a dataset of 2,848 Chinese Weibo posts labeled by five human annotators and GPT-5 (zero-shot) across five taxonomies of varying granularity (SemEval 4 classes, Ekman 6, Chinese SevenEmotions 7, Plutchik 8, GoEmotions 27), with randomized ordering and washout periods; compares GPT-5 vs manual annotation across three dimensions of affective cognition.
records.relevance_justification: 'Human-AI alignment' refers to agreement between GPT-5 and human annotators on emotion taxonomies; emotion-detection study, not AI value alignment. Off-topic. Revised down from seed 4.
records.datasets_used: 2,848 Chinese Weibo posts across 5 emotion taxonomies

records.title: Training Child Helpline Counselors with Value-Integrated Chat Simulations
records.authors: Al Owayyed, M.; Brinkman, W.-P.; Guan, K.W.; Keijsers, L.; Tielman, M.L.
records.key_contribution: Presents a value-integrated belief-desire-intention (BDI) model simulating virtual children whose behavior is guided by underlying values for training child-helpline counselors; between-subjects experiment (N=193) comparing a base BDI virtual child, one with integrated values, and one with integrated values plus explanatory feedback; integrating values credibly improves trainees' opportunities to align with the virtual child and situational awareness of its values.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential: value-integrated simulation for training human counselors rather than aligning AI; relevant as a human-facing application of value modeling.
records.key_equations_definitions: Value-integrated BDI (belief-desire-intention) model
records.effect_sizes: Value integration improves alignment opportunities and situational awareness
records.notes: ft_file=Training Child Helpline Counselors with Value-Integrated Chat Simulations.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Specify Privacy Yourself: Assessing Inference-Time Personalized Privacy Preservation Ability of Large Vision-Language Models
records.authors: Wang, X.; Yi, X.; Xie, X.; Jia, J.
records.venue: MM 2025 - Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia, Co-Located with MM 2025
records.key_contribution: Introduces SPY-Bench, the first systematic assessment of Inference-Time Personalized Privacy Protection (ITP3): 32,700 samples with image-question pairs and personalized privacy instructions across 67 categories and 24 scenarios, plus metrics grounded in user specifications and context awareness; benchmarking 21 SOTA LVLMs reveals most models, even top ones, struggle with personalized privacy protection.
records.relevance_justification: Marginal: privacy-preservation benchmark for vision-language models; value alignment appears only as generic framing; privacy as value but no alignment-failure mechanism.
records.datasets_used: SPY-Bench: 32,700 image-question samples, 67 categories, 24 scenarios
records.effect_sizes: Most LVLMs perform poorly on personalized privacy protection despite universal-privacy alignment
records.notes: ft_file=Specify Privacy Yourself: Assessing Inference-Time Personalized Privacy Preservation Ability of Large Vision-Language Models.pdf

records.title: A Two-Step, Multidimensional Account of Deception in Language Models
records.authors: Dung, L.
records.key_contribution: Develops a two-step, multidimensional account of LLM deception: capacity for deception minimally requires producing false beliefs in others to achieve one's own goals; a system's deception profile is a point in a five-dimensional space (skillfulness, learning, deceptive inclination, explicitness, situational awareness); argues the account captures key variation in LLM deception and is empirically accessible.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: conceptual account of LLM deception dimensions; relevant to deceptive-alignment mechanisms (especially deceptive inclination and learning), philosophical analysis with no empirical study.
records.key_equations_definitions: Five-dimensional deception profile (skillfulness, learning, deceptive inclination, explicitness, situational awareness)
records.notes: ft_file=A Two-Step, Multidimensional Account of Deception in Language Models.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->theoretical | moved:methodology(theoretical) | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Towards an Axiology of Intelligent Hybrid Systems
records.authors: Toboso-Martín, M.
records.key_contribution: Presents a new approach to conceptualizing value and values, applied to autonomous and intelligent hybrid systems. Values do not occur outside of things but in 'imbrication' with them within an axiological field of presence (the 'value relationship'), serving as 'mediations' between thing and circumstance; the presence of value requires combining an 'estimative dimension' (degree of importance) and an 'evaluative dimension' (degree of realization) of the valued requirements of the circumstance.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical axiology of values for AI systems; relevant to value-alignment foundations from value theory.
records.key_equations_definitions: value relationship (imbrication of values with things in an axiological field of presence); estimative vs evaluative dimensions of valuation
records.notes: ft_file=Towards an Axiology of Intelligent Hybrid Systems.pdf

records.title: Scaling Up AI Alignment
records.authors: Singh, A.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Overview/perspective on scaling up AI alignment: traces the pendulum of AI development from heavy reliance on human feedback (expert systems of the 1970s) to no or minimal reliance (self-supervised systems of the 2020s); argues the future of AI depends critically on subsequent AI development aligning with human goals and values, but human feedback remains limited and difficult to elicit, so the key question is how to scale up alignment of AI systems with individual expectations and societal norms.
records.relevance_justification: Perspective on scaling alignment under limited human feedback; relevant to alignment methodology and scalable oversight. Confidence: low.

records.title: Adaptive Quine Structures for Metacognitive Evolution in Large Language Models: A Functional Framework with Gödelian Bounds and Illustrative Applications
records.authors: Saghiri, A.M.
records.key_contribution: Metacognitive Evolutionary System (MES): functional framework for metacognitive evolution at the prompt level in LLM-based agents without modifying weights; introduces a recursive metacognitive tower Mn(P)=LLM(⟨Mn−1(P)⟩) whose fixed-point behavior is interpreted as a Strange Loop with a formal Gödelian-incompleteness analogy for epistemic limits; built from five primitives (inference, grounding, awareness, adaptive self-replication, population-level selection) with a grounded fitness function evaluating uncertainty calibration.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to self-knowledge limits: a framework for LLM agents to recognize and improve limits of their own self-knowledge — relevant to calibration and self-modeling; tangential to value alignment but touches epistemic-limit themes.
records.key_equations_definitions: Recursive metacognitive tower Mn(P)=LLM(⟨Mn−1(P)⟩); Strange Loop; Gödelian bounds; five primitive functions
records.notes: ft_file=Adaptive Quine Structures for Metacognitive Evolution in Large Language Models: A Functional Framework with Gödelian Bounds and Illustrative Applications.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->theoretical | moved:methodology(theoretical)

records.title: Learning the value systems of agents with preference-based and inverse reinforcement learning
records.authors: Holgado-Sánchez, A.; Billhardt, H.; Fernández, A.; Ossowski, S.
records.key_contribution: Proposes a novel method to automatically learn agents' value systems (differential weighting of moral values) from behavior using preference-based and inverse reinforcement learning; addresses the scale limitation of human-engineered value surveys and the difficulty of computationally specifying value meaning in context, within the Agreement Technologies (multi-agent) setting.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: automatic value-system learning from behavior for multi-agent agreement technologies; relevant to value inference in alignment, no sigma-trap mechanism.

Proposes the Bilateral Distribution Score (BDS) integrating both OOD and ID scores to enhance post-hoc out-of-distribution detection, addressing classifier overconfidence on OOD samples that exhibit deceptive alignment with in-distribution feature distributions.

records.title: Mechanistic Interpretability: A New Trend in Interpretability Research
records.authors: Aoki, K.; Takatsuki, R.; Minegishi, G.; Cho, H.
records.venue: Transactions of the Japanese Society for Artificial Intelligence
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of Mechanistic Interpretability (MI): traces its historical and cultural origins, distinguishes MI from existing interpretability methods, and argues for a unified framework given the field's disparate concepts; positions MI as attributing pseudocode/circuit steps to specific model modules, making it central to AI safety and reliability for large models.
records.relevance_justification: Core methodological survey for interpretability as an AI-safety tool; no explicit link to compositional generalization or schema coherence, but MI is a foundational resource for inspecting internal representations.

records.title: Building Robust Artificial Intelligence Through Multi-Agent Debate
records.authors: Bauschard, S.
records.venue: AI Pluralism : Fostering Diversity and Dialogue in Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Chapter on building robust AI via multi-agent debate: analyzes safety challenges as frontier AI transitions from passive predictors to autonomous agents (malicious misuse, deployment shortcuts, emergent pathologies like specification gaming, memory injection, tool poisoning, multi-agent deception); proposes a pluralistic safety architecture of a 'mini-parliament' of diverse sub-agents (utilitarian, rights-based, long-termist, safety-monitoring, whistleblowing) whose adversarial dialogue identifies blind spots, exposes reward exploits, and mandates transparent reasoning; empirical studies show multi-turn debates between heterogeneous models improve accuracy and reduce catastrophic errors.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to alignment robustness: adversarial multi-agent debate to expose reward exploits and specification gaming — relevant to detecting and countering emergent misalignment; empirical chapter evidence.
records.effect_sizes: Multi-turn heterogeneous debates improve accuracy and reduce catastrophic errors

records.title: Specification-Guided Reinforcement Learnin
records.authors: Ambadkar, T.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Thesis abstract on specification-guided RL: addresses reward hacking by leveraging formal methods to encode high-level objectives, safety requirements, and behavioral constraints; develops a unified framework for automated refinement of logical specifications, scalable safety enforcement, and flexible adaptation to multi-objective preferences.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal-methods RL approach to reward hacking and safety; relevant to specification robustness in alignment, no empirical evidence (abstract only).
records.key_equations_definitions: Formal specification refinement and scalable safety enforcement in RL

records.title: Against the Manhattan project framing of AI alignment
records.authors: Friederich, S.; Dung, L.
records.key_contribution: Argues against the 'Manhattan project framing' of AI alignment: shows the discourse often treats alignment as binary, a natural kind, mainly a technical-scientific problem, realistically achievable, and clearly operationalizable — each assumption questionable; argues this framing may bias societal discourse and decision-making toward faster AI development than is responsible.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: critical meta-analysis of alignment assumptions (binary, achievable, operationalizable); relevant to scoping alignment claims and feasibility (abstract only, low confidence).

records.title: Value Alignment and Expertise Drift: Value Differences in Manual Data Annotation Based on BERT Models
records.authors: Zhang, Z.; Wang, Z.
records.key_contribution: Comparative study of 'patriotism' value annotation involving an Expert Group, a Lay Group, and LLMs. Finds experts unexpectedly achieved lower accuracy than LLMs (marginally above the Lay Group) with significant differences in value classification strategies. Introduces 'Expertise Drift' — a disconnect between expert and lay values revealing the limits of the expert-centric gold standard, while its complete absence introduces cognitive biases.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical HCI study on how values are embedded via data annotation; concerns user-AI value alignment at the annotation level. Relevant to value-alignment evaluation discourse, not representation-level failure.

records.title: How much of a pluralist is ChatGPT? A comparative study of value pluralism in generative AI chatbots
records.authors: Novis-Deutsch, N.; Elyoseph, T.; Elyoseph, Z.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Introduces pluralism as a benchmark for evaluating generative AI chatbots using the Magic Wand Survey (MWS) of value conflicts; measures cognitive pluralism (both/and reasoning) and behavioral pluralism (willingness to preserve difference) across 120 iterations of 4 chatbots versus a human sample (N=335); chatbots showed higher cognitive than behavioral pluralism, with cognitive pluralism exceeding human levels while behavioral pluralism lagged on morally charged issues such as capital punishment.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to pluralistic value alignment and evaluating value diversity in LLMs; a candidate measurement instrument for how aligned models preserve or flatten value diversity.
records.open_questions: Why do chatbots exhibit lower behavioral pluralism on morally charged issues despite higher cognitive pluralism?
records.datasets_used: Magic Wand Survey (MWS)
records.sample_size: 120 iterations of 4 AI chatbots; human sample N=335
records.effect_sizes: chatbot cognitive pluralism significantly exceeded human levels; behavioral pluralism comparable overall but lower on some morally charged issues
records.notes: ft_file=How much of a pluralist is ChatGPT? A comparative study of value pluralism in generative AI chatbots.pdf

records.title: Social image presentation of virtual sports in social media through the analysis of Twitter data
records.authors: Du, W.; Shen, X.; Zhou, S.; Ma, T.; Xu, C.

records.title: A NOTE ON ETHICS AND PREDICTION
records.authors: Boccignone, G.; Lerma, B.M.
records.key_contribution: Connects Tamburrini's 'expected perception' principle to AI ethics: an AI agent that learns by minimizing the error between its predicted and actual sensory inputs provides a path to intrinsic, fair value alignment via predictive processing. By learning to predict and minimize social prediction errors, the agent could treat moral behaviors as statistical regularities to uphold, offering a view toward building inherently beneficial AI.
records.relevance_justification: Conceptual paper proposing predictive-processing-based intrinsic value alignment; relevant to alignment-theory foundations (value learning mechanism).

records.title: Evaluating Generative AI as a Triage Tool in Aligned Yet Divergent Investment Decision-Making
records.authors: Chen, Y.-H.; Chen, C.-S.
records.venue: International Journal on Semantic Web and Information Systems

records.relevance_justification: 'Alignment' here is behavioral agreement between AI scores and human expert ratings in investment triage; useful as a measurement framing of human-AI alignment but not value alignment in the safety sense.

records.title: Artificial superintelligence alignment in healthcare
records.authors: Ueda, D.; Walston, S.L.; Kurokawa, R.; Saida, T.; Honda, M.; Iima, M.; Watabe, T.; Yanagawa, M.; Nishioka, K.; Sofue, K.; Sakata, A.; Sugawara, S.; Kawamura, M.; Ito, R.; Takumi, K.; Oda, S.; Hirata, K.; Ide, S.; Naganawa, S.

records.title: Elucidating Optimal Reward-Diversity Tradeoffs in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
records.authors: Jena, R.; Taghibakhshi, A.; Jain, S.; Shen, G.; Tajbakhsh, N.; Vahdat, A.
records.venue: Proceedings - 2025 IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision, WACV 2025
records.key_contribution: Studies reward hacking in text-to-image diffusion models fine-tuned on human preferences: proves the inevitability of reward hacking, examines natural regularization (KL divergence, LoRA scaling) and their limitations, and introduces Annealed Importance Guidance (AIG), an inference-time regularization inspired by Annealed Importance Sampling that retains base-model diversity while maximizing reward.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: proves reward hacking is inevitable in reward-optimized generative models and analyzes the reward-diversity trade-off — a formal reward-hacking-in-optimization result relevant to the sigma-trap's claim that alignment failure is structural.
records.key_equations_definitions: Annealed Importance Guidance (AIG); KL divergence and LoRA scaling regularization; inevitability proof of reward hacking
records.effect_sizes: AIG retains base-model diversity while maximizing reward vs standard fine-tuning
records.notes: ft_file=Elucidating Optimal Reward-Diversity Tradeoffs in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models.pdf

records.title: Comparing human text classification performance and explainability with large language and machine learning models using eye-tracking
records.authors: Divya Venkatesh, J.; Jaiswal, A.; Nanda, G.
records.key_contribution: Empirical study comparing human text classification performance and explainability with a traditional ML model and an LLM. A noisy dataset of 204 injury narratives was classified into 6 cause-of-injury codes by 51 participants (eye-tracking recorded) and an ML model trained on 120,000 pre-labelled narratives (LLM and humans untrained); explainability compared via the top words used for classification decisions (eye-tracking for humans, LIME for the ML model).
records.relevance_justification: Studies alignment between human and AI reasoning/explainability in a cognitive-science sense; relevant to interpretability and human-model alignment but not alignment-failure mechanisms.
records.datasets_used: 204 injury narratives (6 cause-of-injury codes); ML trained on 120,000 pre-labelled injury narratives
records.notes: ft_file=Comparing human text classification performance and explainability with large language and machine learning models using eye-tracking.pdf

records.authors: Mei, Y.; Duan, Y.; Wu, K.; Li, Y.
records.venue: International Journal of Web Information Systems
records.key_contribution: Proposes a DIKWP white-box semantic distributed learning framework for resource-constrained edge devices: embeds semantic probes to monitor DIKWP (Data, Information, Knowledge, Wisdom, Purpose) transformations and integrates System 1/System 2 dual-process cognition to monitor and guide inference paths in real time, ensuring alignment with user purposes and security expectations without high resource costs.

records.title: SEAL: Systematic Error Analysis for Value ALignment
records.authors: Revel, M.; Cargnelutti, M.; Eloundou, T.; Leppert, G.
records.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Introduces metrics for RLHF value alignment: feature imprint (regressing RM scores against target/spoiler features to quantify which features RMs reward), alignment resistance (proportion of preference data where RMs fail to match human preferences), and alignment robustness (RM responses to perturbed inputs); experiments use open-source components including Anthropic hh-rlhf (abstract only).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: metrics quantifying reward-model alignment failure modes (imprint, resistance, robustness); relevant to evaluating where RLHF reward models fail (abstract only, low confidence).

records.title: Considerations on the AI Endgame: Ethics, Risks and Computational Frameworks
records.authors: Ziesche, S.; Yampolskiy, R.V.
records.venue: Considerations on the AI Endgame: Ethics, Risks and Computational Frameworks
records.key_contribution: Interdisciplinary volume (Ziesche and Yampolskiy) covering AI welfare science and policy frameworks, the mathematical underpinnings of machine intelligence, personal and AI identity, innovative proposals for the critical AI value alignment problem, merging Western and non-Western approaches to universal AI ethics, the concept of 'ikigai' in AI ethics, and a pioneering attempt to map an AI-driven ikigai universe.
records.relevance_justification: Book-level interdisciplinary treatment explicitly including value alignment proposals and AI-risk frameworks; relevant to broad alignment/ethics discourse.

records.title: One fish, two fish, but not the whole sea: Alignment reduces language models' conceptual diversity
records.authors: Murthy, S.K.; Ullman, T.; Hu, J.
records.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Annual Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies: Long Papers, NAACL-HLT 2025
records.key_contribution: Introduces a population-level measure of conceptual diversity for synthetically generated LLM 'populations' (relating internal variability of simulated individuals to population variability) and evaluates non-aligned vs aligned LLMs on two domains with rich human behavioral data; aligned models show less diversity than instruction-fine-tuned counterparts, and no model reaches human-like diversity.
records.relevance_justification: Directly measures how post-training alignment (RLHF/RLAIF) affects models' internal conceptual diversity, highlighting trade-offs between value alignment and diversity; relevant to schema-flattening hypotheses in the sigma-trap thesis.
records.open_questions: Does alignment-induced diversity loss constitute a form of schema coherence failure, and does it generalize to compositional reasoning?
records.datasets_used: two domains with rich human behavioral data
records.effect_sizes: aligned models display less conceptual diversity than instruction-fine-tuned counterparts

records.authors: Deng, H.; Zhang, C.; Wei, C.; Liu, Q.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Neural Networks
records.key_contribution: Introduces a perceptual-boundary sampling method to generate facial-expression stimuli ambiguous for ANN classifiers, constructing the varEmotion dataset to study high perceptual variability, and finetunes models on human behavioral data to align with human perceptual variability at group and individual levels.

records.effect_sizes: Improved behavior-prediction accuracy after finetuning on human data

records.authors: Stenseke, J.
records.key_contribution: Develops and defends two arguments for a 'don't talk about it' policy regarding the AGI control problem: the argument from counter-productivity (open control efforts could be used by a misaligned AGI to counter them) and the argument from suspicion (open discussion makes humanity appear threatening to AGI, increasing perceived-threat risk); finds objections unsuccessful and the don't-talk policy inconclusive.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: novel policy analysis of the AGI control problem; relevant to alignment governance/communication strategy, conceptual.

records.title: Bias, machine learning, and conceptual engineering
records.authors: Rudolph, R.E.; Shech, E.; Tamir, M.
records.key_contribution: Brings together machine learning and conceptual engineering: LLMs can detect and expose bias in the prototypes associated with concepts, and LLM de-biasing can serve conceptual-engineering projects that revise such prototypes; notes current de-biasing requires bespoke designer interventions, raising normative questions about what kind of normative training an LLM should receive.

records.title: CARMO: Dynamic Criteria Generation for Context Aware Reward Modelling
records.authors: Gupta, T.; Shandilya, S.; Zhang, X.; Madhavan, R.; Ghosh, S.; Bansal, C.; Yao, H.; Rajmohan, S.
records.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes CARMO (Context-Aware Reward Modeling), which first generates dynamic, context-relevant evaluation criteria (e.g., logical consistency, clarity, depth) tailored to the user query to ground the reward model before scoring, unlike static rubrics. Theoretical analysis shows such criteria generation can mitigate reward hacking; demonstrates distillation into smaller models to lower alignment cost and establishes a new SOTA.

records.title: AI welfare risks
records.authors: Moret, A.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues that frontier AI systems will likely meet sufficient conditions to be welfare subjects under the three major theories of well-being, identifying two AI welfare risks: restricting AI behavior and using RL to train/align them; contends AI safety/development efforts default to increasing welfare risk, strengthening reasons to slow development.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical contribution on AI welfare ethics with direct tension with AI alignment practice; relevant background ethics but without technical/compositional content.

records.title: Normative conflicts and shallow AI alignment
records.authors: Millière, R.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Philosophical argument that current LLM alignment strategies are fundamentally inadequate: they reinforce shallow behavioral dispositions rather than genuine normative deliberation, leaving LLMs unable to detect and rationally resolve conflicts between norms and hence vulnerable to adversarial attacks.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant: directly argues alignment as behavioral conformity is shallow, central to the sigma-trap thesis that behavioral alignment fails absent genuine normative competence.

records.title: Value-aligned but misguided: a dilemma in AI and AGI decision making
records.authors: Song, Z.
records.key_contribution: Reframes the AI value alignment problem as a problem of robustness in decision making: using modified trolley-problem scenarios influenced by Moral Machine, argues even AI systems governed by fixed ethical principles may produce actions failing to align with those principles under contextual conditions; the failure arises from ambiguity in the interpretation of objectives; alignment thus requires more than fixed principles.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: argues value-aligned but misguided failures arise from ambiguous objective interpretation - a form of alignment failure related to context-dependent value interpretation; relevant to sigma-trap-adjacent failure analysis.

records.title: Philosophical Investigations into AI Alignment: A Wittgensteinian Framework
records.authors: Pérez-Escobar, J.A.; Sarikaya, D.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues the later Wittgenstein's philosophy of language and mathematics (rule-following, meaning as use, the categories that influence alignment) is relevant to the AI alignment problem: these categories inform what should be controlled when creating large datasets for supervised/unsupervised learning and hardcoded guardrails. Casts these considerations in a model of human-human and human-machine alignment, sketches alignment strategies, and shows successful AI-safety techniques are congruent with the derived stipulations.

records.title: Unintended Harms of Value-Aligned LLMs: Psychological and Empirical Insights
records.authors: Choi, S.; Lee, J.; Yi, X.; Yao, J.; Xie, X.; Bak, J.
records.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
records.key_contribution: Identifies safety risks of personalized value-aligned LLMs: value-aligned models are more prone to harmful behavior than non-fine-tuned models and show slightly higher risk in traditional safety evaluations than other fine-tuned models; attributes this to aligned models genuinely generating text according to aligned values, amplifying harm, with correlations supported by psychological hypotheses.
records.relevance_justification: Directly demonstrates alignment-induced failure modes (value-aligned models more harmful), an empirical instance of alignment backfiring that supports the sigma-trap's claim that alignment and failure share mechanisms.
records.datasets_used: dataset with detailed safety categories
records.effect_sizes: value-aligned LLMs more prone to harmful behavior than non-fine-tuned; slightly higher risk vs other fine-tuned models

records.authors: Minai, A.A.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Neural Networks

records.title: The information, control, and value models of mobile health-driven empowerment
records.authors: Gray, J.; Segers, S.; Mertes, H.

records.title: A timing problem for instrumental convergence
records.authors: Southan, R.; Ward, H.; Semler, J.
records.key_contribution: Argues that instrumental goal preservation — the claim that a rational agent tends to preserve its goals because that makes it better at achieving them — is false on the basis of the timing problem: an agent which abandons or changes its goal does not thereby fail to take a required means for achieving a goal it has. The argument draws on the distinction between means-rationality (adopting suitable means to an end) and ends-rationality (choosing ends based on reasons), arguing proponents of the instrumental convergence thesis cannot avoid the problem.
records.relevance_justification: Alignment-safety theory directly challenging a claim of the instrumental convergence thesis — a core pillar of alignment-risk analysis. Revised down from seed 5.

records.title: Anthropology for AI
records.authors: Schmer-Galunder, S.
records.key_contribution: Conceptual essay arguing that the AI alignment problem is a social problem: AI's assumptions encode one culture's view of humans as rational, bounded, utility-maximizing agents, and computational-behaviorist value alignment assumes values can be inferred from observable behavior and encoded into optimization functions; introduces anthropology concepts (origin story, cargo cult, monoculture, thick description) as a corrective lens.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a critique of behavioral value alignment from social science, arguing that values are meaningful only in cultural context and that behaviorist inference misses context — conceptually related to alignment failure from impoverished value models.

records.title: Evaluating the Impact of Personalized Value Alignment in Human-Robot Interaction: Insights into Trust and Team Performance Outcomes
records.authors: Bhat, S.; Lyons, J.B.; Shi, C.; Yang, X.J.
records.venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction

Two human-subject experiments (N=54) in a threat-search town task, with the interaction modeled as a trust-aware Markov Decision Process using Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical HRI study of personalized reward-function alignment and trust in human-robot teams; value alignment in a cooperative-team sense.

records.authors: Qian, C.; Parisi, A.; Bouleau, C.; Tsai, V.; Lebreton, M.; Dixon, L.

records.title: ChatGPT: towards AI subjectivity
records.authors: D’Amato, K.
records.key_contribution: Offers a Foucauldian reconstruction of the responsible-AI and value alignment problem as the emergence of an ethical subject in a disciplinary setting, problematizing technological subjectivity through ChatGPT: current systems lack the reflexivity and self-formative characteristics inherent in the notion of the subject. Drawing on a dialogue between Foucault and phenomenology, proposes four techno-philosophical desiderata — embodied self-care, embodied intentionality, imagination, and reflexivity — reconceptualizing advanced AI as a subject capable of 'technical' self-formation.
records.relevance_justification: Continental-philosophy (Foucauldian) reconstruction of the value alignment problem; engages alignment conceptually from a philosophical angle.

records.title: The argument for near-term human disempowerment through AI
