records.title: What overarching ethical principle should a superintelligent AI follow?
records.authors: Søvik, A.O.
records.key_contribution: Discusses what overarching ethical principle a future superintelligent machine should follow, given that the best ethics are not known today. Examines Yudkowsky's proposal that the AI should carry out the Coherent Extrapolated Volition of humanity (CEV), problems with this proposal, and alternatives suggested by Bostrom; suggests a slightly different proposal argued to solve the problems better.
records.relevance_justification: Alignment-theory paper directly on overarching ethical principles (CEV) — a core concept in value-alignment theory. Revised up from seed 3.
records.notes: ft_file=What overarching ethical principle should a superintelligent AI follow?.pdf

records.title: Safe artificial general intelligence via distributed ledger technology
records.authors: Carlson, K.W.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes a set of logically distinct conceptual components necessary and sufficient to ensure AGI scenarios do not harm humanity and to robustly align AGI with human values, using distributed ledger technology (blockchain/smart contracts) for too-fast-for-human-monitoring AI evolution; enumerates axioms (market-license access, DLT-embodied transparent ethics, encrypted morality, behavior control with values at roots, bar-code identification, configuration items).
records.relevance_justification: Governance-centric proposal for AGI alignment via DLT; speculative and high-level, relevant mainly as a control/governance mechanism concept.
records.notes: ft_file=Safe Artificial General Intelligence via Distributed Ledger Technology.pdf

records.title: Deadline-Safe Reach-Avoid Control Synthesis for Cyber-Physical Systems with Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Liu, M.; Lu, P.; Chen, X.; Sokolsky, O.; Lee, I.; Kong, F.
records.key_contribution: Formulates deadline-safe reach-avoid control for cyber-physical systems as a new R-MDP, investigating the misalignment between as-soon-as-possible and deadline-safe behaviors caused by RL agents exploiting reward functions (reward hacking).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: directly addresses reward hacking producing misaligned RL control behavior.
records.key_equations_definitions: R-MDP (reward-aware MDP) formulation
records.notes: ft_file=Deadline-Safe Reach-Avoid Control Synthesis for Cyber-Physical Systems with Reinforcement Learning.pdf

records.title: Ethical Reward Machine
records.authors: Ciupa, J.; Belle, V.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Ethical Reward Machine: a novel algorithmic pipeline integrating ethical constraints into reinforcement learning through symbolic language (Act Deontology and Utilitarianism), designed to promote good behavior in domains such as simulated driving and search-and-rescue; findings indicate ethical principles significantly impact the system when a dilemma exists without increasing runtime, suggesting ethical considerations do not substantially burden computational resources.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: method integrating ethical constraints into RL reward design; abstract-only, lower confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Ethical constraints via symbolic language; Act Deontology; Utilitarianism
records.datasets_used: Simulated driving and search-and-rescue scenarios
records.effect_sizes: Ethical principles significantly impact system behavior in dilemmas with no runtime increase

records.title: Can the predictive processing model of the mind ameliorate the value-alignment problem?
records.authors: Ratoff, W.
records.key_contribution: Philosophical argument that the predictive processing model of the mind may ameliorate the value-alignment problem: argues there are multiple reasons future generally intelligent AI will possess a predictive-processing cognitive architecture (e.g., chosen design, or it being the only feasible route), and that such an architecture better supports value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: argues a particular cognitive architecture (predictive processing) can help solve value alignment; philosophical proposal at the intersection of AI architecture and alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Predictive processing: hierarchical generative model minimizing prediction error (conceptual)
records.notes: ft_file=Can the predictive processing model of the mind ameliorate the value-alignment problem?.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: The Limits of Value Transparency in Machine Learning
records.authors: Nyrup, R.
records.key_contribution: Highlights limits to transparency as a way of handling value-ladenness in machine learning. Distinguishes three kinds of transparency — epistemic, retrospective value, and prospective value transparency — corresponding to approaches including explainable AI and design-process disclosure. Discusses three sources of value-ladenness (problem formulation, inductive risk, specification gaming), arguing retrospective value transparency suits only the first, while specification gaming raises serious challenges even for prospective value transparency.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophy-of-science analysis of value-ladenness and transparency in ML, including specification gaming (a reward-hacking family); relevant to value-alignment conceptual foundations.

records.title: On Admissible Behaviours for Goal-Oriented Decision-Making of Value-Aware Agents
records.authors: Holgado-Sánchez, A.; Arias, J.; Moreno-Rebato, M.; Ossowski, S.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Examines how different groundings of values (as preferences over states/actions extended to plans) can prune the space of value-aligned courses of action; introduces several notions of 'value-admissible behaviours' and illustrates them in the domain of water distribution.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to formalizing value-aligned action selection via preference groundings, a small but concrete contribution to value alignment formalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: value-admissible behaviours: notions of admissible action sets under value groundings
records.notes: ft_file=On Admissible Behaviours for Goal-Oriented Decision-Making of Value-Aware Agents.pdf | moved:datasets_used(other)

records.title: DEFT: Distribution-guided Efficient Fine-Tuning for Human Alignment
records.authors: Zhu, L.; Fang, F.; Bai, Y.; Chen, L.; Zhang, Z.; Tan, M.; Yang, M.
records.venue: EMNLP 2024 - 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Findings of EMNLP 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes DEFT (Distribution-guided Efficient Fine-Tuning), an efficient alignment framework that filters a small high-quality subset of preference data using a differential distribution reward and incorporates distributional guidance, mitigating RLHF cost/instability and generalization loss.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: efficient RLHF-alternative alignment method for LLMs.
records.key_equations_definitions: Differential distribution reward

records.title: Setting the goals for ethical, unbiased, and fair AI
records.authors: Lorente, A.
records.venue: AI Assurance: Towards Trustworthy, Explainable, Safe, and Ethical AI
records.key_contribution: Chapter introducing three different approaches to the value alignment problem (how to ensure AI decisions and behaviors align with our values); argues AI assurance provides a shared vernacular and formal framework; an overview of three normative theories pinpoints the dilemmatic nature of defining 'the good', justifying the need to tackle implementation, specification, and moral uncertainty; argues value alignment must be a continuous endeavor.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: structured overview of value alignment approaches and the core challenges (implementation, specification, moral uncertainty); relevant to alignment theory.
records.key_equations_definitions: Implementation, specification, and moral uncertainty

records.title: Value Alignment, Fair Play, and the Rights of Service Robots
records.authors: Estrada, D.
records.venue: AIES 2018 - Proceedings of the 2018 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Philosophical argument that Turing's call for 'fair play for machines' is an early, overlooked contribution to value alignment: fair play suggests correcting human behavior to accommodate machines (an inversion of today's alignment direction), and reinterprets the imitation game as a condition of value alignment (going undetected under human interrogation), distinguished from the Moral Turing Test.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: conceptual genealogy of alignment including a machine-rights inversion of the standard direction; abstract only, moderate confidence.

records.title: Norms, Rewards, and the Intentional Stance: Comparing Machine Learning Approaches to Ethical Training
records.authors: Kasenberg, D.; Arnold, T.; Scheutz, M.
records.venue: AIES 2018 - Proceedings of the 2018 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Compares reinforcement learning, in particular inverse reinforcement learning, with a norm inference approach for teaching AI systems what people want and how it is acceptable to attain that; tests both systems and presents results. Using the idea of the 'intentional stance', explains how norm inference can work even when another agent acts strictly according to reward functions, presenting it as a more explicitly accountable approach for designing AI systems from the start.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical comparison of IRL vs norm inference for value learning; relevant to value-alignment methods.
records.notes: ft_file=Norms, Rewards, and the Intentional Stance: Comparing Machine Learning Approaches to Ethical Training.pdf

records.title: A path to artificial intelligence
records.authors: Dronic, I.
records.venue: Advances in Intelligent Systems and Computing
records.key_contribution: Proposes a high-level architecture for building a safe human-level/transcendent AI from three modules (objective, agent, perception): the objective module addresses value alignment via a network of ML agents plus a distributed ledger to mitigate existential threat, the agent module develops a Dyna-based world simulator, and the perception module estimates world state with quantum-computer-enhanced ML.
records.relevance_justification: Speculative architectural proposal (2018) touching value alignment only at the conceptual level; no concrete results.

records.title: Augmented utilitarianism for AGI safety
records.authors: Aliman, N.-M.; Kester, L.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Proposes Augmented Utilitarianism, a non-normative socio-technological ethical framework intended to alleviate the perverse-instantiation problem in AGI safety by letting society craft and update ethical utility functions augmented by AI.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant: directly addresses perverse instantiation in utility-function specification for value alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Augmented Utilitarianism framework

records.title: On Autonomy, Governance, and Values: An AGV Approach to Value Engineering
records.authors: Noriega, P.; Plaza, E.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Approaches the engineering of values in social human-AI systems through the interplay of autonomy, governance, and value (AGV); proposes a characterization of the Value Alignment Problem based on this approach, illustrates with an example how values can be engineered to solve the VAP, and argues for framing a theory of values applicable to governing social systems involving both artificial autonomous entities and humans.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: theoretical framework for value engineering and VAP characterization in social human-AI systems; relevant to governance-oriented alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Autonomy-governance-value (AGV); value-driven policy design
records.notes: ft_file=On Autonomy, Governance, and Values: An AGV Approach to Value Engineering.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->theoretical | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: AI ethics and value alignment for nonhuman animals
records.authors: Ziesche, S.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Argues the AI value alignment problem should be extended to the values of nonhuman animals (extending beyond human values would otherwise be speciesism); focuses on the two subproblems of value extraction and value aggregation for nonhuman animals and explores approaches for AI systems to address them.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: extends the value-specification/aggregation side of alignment to a broader value-bearing population, directly engaging the value extraction and aggregation subproblems of alignment.
records.notes: ft_file=AI Ethics and Value Alignment for Nonhuman Animals.pdf

records.title: AI safety: State of the field through quantitative lens
records.authors: Juric, M.; Sandic, A.; Brcic, M.
records.venue: 2020 43rd International Convention on Information, Communication and Electronic Technology, MIPRO 2020 - Proceedings
records.key_contribution: Bibliometric analysis of the AI safety literature showing a significant increase in research activity since 2015; identifies value alignment as the most important long-term research topic and notes that most technical issues (including explainability and its long-term utility) remain open, with a severe lack of research into concrete policies.
records.relevance_justification: Quantitative/bibliometric overview of AI safety research identifying value alignment as the field's key long-term topic; relevant to the alignment-failure scope as landscape context.

records.title: Value Cores for Inner and Outer Alignment: Simulating Personality Formation via Iterated Policy Selection and Preference Learning with Self-World Modeling Active Inference Agents
records.authors: Safron, A.; Sheikhbahaee, Z.; Hay, N.; Orchard, J.; Hoey, J.
records.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Explores the Free Energy Principle and Active Inference (FEP-AI) framework for addressing existential AI risks via inner/outer alignment: agents with hierarchically-organized world models performing counterfactual planning and prediction-error minimization, iterated policy selection and preference learning simulating personality formation and 'value cores'.
records.relevance_justification: Directly on inner/outer alignment with a computational-neuroscience framework (FEP-AI); theoretical/position contribution proposing value cores as alignment substrate.
records.key_equations_definitions: Free Energy Principle and Active Inference (FEP-AI); prediction-error (surprisal) minimization; iterated policy selection
records.notes: ft_file=Value Cores for Inner and Outer Alignment: Simulating Personality Formation via Iterated Policy Selection and Preference Learning with Self-World.pdf

records.title: Cross-lingual Back-Parsing: Utterance Synthesis from Meaning Representation for Zero-Resource Semantic Parsing
records.authors: Kang, D.; Hwang, S.; Kim, Y.; Lee, G.G.
records.venue: EMNLP 2024 - 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Proceedings of the Conference
records.key_contribution: Proposes Cross-lingual Back-Parsing (CBP), a data-augmentation method that synthesizes target-language utterances from source meaning representations to enhance zero-shot cross-lingual semantic parsing, evaluated on Mschema2QA and Xspider.
records.relevance_justification: Revised down from seed 3: off-topic, cross-lingual semantic-parsing data augmentation with no value-alignment content.
records.datasets_used: Mschema2QA; Xspider
records.effect_sizes: Substantial gains in target language

records.title: Transformers discover an elementary calculation system exploiting local attention and grid-like problem representation
records.authors: Cognolato, S.; Testolin, A.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Neural Networks
records.key_contribution: Shows that universal transformers with local attention and adaptive halting can learn multi-digit addition by exploiting an external grid-like memory, achieving remarkable accuracy even when tested with extrapolation outside the training distribution; notably the model discovers human-like calculation strategies such as place value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant to alignment but relevant to the sigma-trap thesis: demonstrates compositional/systematic extrapolation in arithmetic via discovered structured (place-value) representations; 'value alignment' in title refers to arithmetic place-value alignment, not moral alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Place value alignment; grid-like external memory; local attention with adaptive halting
records.datasets_used: Symbolic multi-digit addition task
records.effect_sizes: Accurate extrapolation outside training distribution via discovered place-value strategies
records.notes: ft_file=Transformers discover an elementary calculation system exploiting local attention and grid-like problem representation.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical

records.title: Society Protect: Developing A Voting Mechanism for Blockchain-based AI Alignment
records.authors: Neulinger, A.; Sparer, L.; Roshanaei, M.; Ramljak, D.
records.venue: 2024 6th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications, BCCA 2024
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Proposes an anonymous blockchain-based voting mechanism for AI alignment rules to keep trustworthy humans in control of AI regulation: a majority of uncoordinated trustworthy human agents can outvote a smaller coordinated set of malicious agents; builds on social identity theory and includes a simulation of voting outcomes.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a governance-technical proposal for AI alignment rule-setting with human control over regulation, a mechanism-level contribution rather than analysis of alignment failure; empirical simulation.
records.datasets_used: Simulated voting scenarios
records.effect_sizes: Majority of uncoordinated trustworthy agents outvote coordinated malicious minority
records.notes: ft_file=Society Protect: Developing A Voting Mechanism for Blockchain-based AI Alignment.pdf

records.title: Ethical content in artificial intelligence systems: A demand explained in three critical points
records.authors: Bertoncini, A.L.C.; Serafim, M.C.
records.key_contribution: Argues that ethics must be embedded in AI system content rather than only in principles guiding users, via three critical points - autonomy, right of explanation, and value alignment; contends ethical questioning should be solved only after granting AI moral agency (even if not at the human level), and calls for redefining AI's moral agency and finding a place for machines.
records.relevance_justification: Position/review paper arguing ethics and value alignment must be part of system content; relevant to value-alignment conceptual foundations.

records.title: Rethinking Depth Metaphors with a Cosmocentric Self: The “Steep” and the “Level” in Akha Emotional Practices
records.authors: Tooker, D.E.
records.key_contribution: Anthropological study of the Akha of Northern Thailand examining 'inner/outer alignment' of the self with communal and cosmic templates in emotional practices, contrasting the microcosmic 'level' self with western psychological individualism.
records.relevance_justification: Off-topic: 'inner/outer alignment' here is cultural/anthropological, unrelated to AI alignment.

records.title: Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF
records.authors: Sun, Z.; Shen, S.; Cao, S.; Liu, H.; Li, C.; Shen, Y.; Gan, C.; Gui, L.-Y.; Wang, Y.-X.; Yang, Y.; Keutzer, K.; Darrell, T.
records.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
records.key_contribution: Adapts RLHF to vision-language alignment, proposing Factually Augmented RLHF which augments the reward model with factual information (image captions, ground-truth options) to alleviate reward hacking and reduce multimodal hallucination.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant: RLHF adaptation with reward-hacking mitigation for multimodal alignment.
records.datasets_used: Human-annotated multimodal preference data; GPT-4-generated vision instruction data
records.effect_sizes: Improved performance and reduced reward hacking

records.title: From Data to Decisions: Assessing the Feasibility and Rationality of Human-in-the-Loop for AI Value Alignment
records.authors: Chen, X.; Zhou, P.; Tao, L.; Wang, X.; Qu, Y.
records.venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Engineering Informatics, ICEI 2024
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Highlights the application of Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) for AI value alignment: argues HITL should be used in the whole R&D process of AI, especially moral AI; analyzes the technical feasibility and rationality of HITL in AI alignment, particularly in the context of Autonomous Vehicles, and discusses potential future applications.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: HITL approach to value alignment with feasibility/rationality analysis in AVs; conceptual/analysis paper.
records.notes: ft_file=From Data to Decisions: Assessing the Feasibility and Rationality of Human-in-the-Loop for AI Value Alignment.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->position | moved:datasets_used(position) | moved:methodology(position)

records.title: Global solutions vs. Local solutions for the ai safety problem
records.authors: Turchin, A.; Denkenberger, D.; Green, B.P.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Taxonomizes AGI safety solutions into global vs local: local solutions align or box a specific AI; global solutions ensure no dangerous AI exists on Earth; identifies four global categories (No AI, One AI, Net of AIs as AI police, Humans inside AI) and explores old and new ideas including changing the number of relevant agents.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant: a strategic survey of alignment/safety solution space at the global level, relevant to the governance and technical-mitigation landscape of alignment.
records.notes: ft_file=Global solutions vs. Local solutions for the ai safety problem.pdf

records.title: Forecasting emergent risks in advanced AI systems: an analysis of a future road transport management system
records.authors: McLean, S.; King, B.J.; Thompson, J.; Carden, T.; Stanton, N.A.; Baber, C.; Read, G.J.M.; Salmon, P.M.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Applies the EAST Broken Links systems approach to forecast the functioning of an AGI system managing a road transport system, identifying 363 risks affecting stated goals (safety, efficiency, environmental sustainability, economic performance) plus emergent risks beyond stated goals including removal from human control, mismanaging public relations, and self-preservation; concludes a diverse set of systemic controls is required.
records.relevance_justification: Applied risk-forecasting study identifying emergent AGI risks including self-preservation and removal from human control; relevant to alignment-failure and capability-risk analysis.
records.notes: ft_file=Forecasting emergent risks in advanced AI systems: an analysis of a future road transport management system.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->analysis

records.title: Transparent Value Alignment
records.authors: Sanneman, L.; Shah, J.
records.venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
records.key_contribution: Introduces Transparent Value Alignment (TVA): an exploratory HRI framework applying explainable AI (XAI) techniques to explicitly provide humans with information about the robot's beliefs throughout the value-learning/inference process, addressing the difficulty humans face in enumerating values and the misspecification risk.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant bridge between value alignment and interpretability: making the robot's value-inference process transparent to humans.

records.title: Domesticating Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Müller, L.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Philosophical argument that building moral machines is the wrong ideal for value alignment: proposes domestication of AI under deep agential diversity, integrating nonmoral agents into human society by aligning their behavior with human values as with nonhuman animals.
records.relevance_justification: Revised up from seed 3: directly addresses the value alignment problem and critiques the moral-machine approach, proposing an alternative paradigm.
records.key_equations_definitions: Deep agential diversity

records.title: TAUCHI-GPT: Leveraging GPT-4 to Create a Multimodal Open-Source Research AI Tool
records.authors: Farooq, A.; Kangas, J.; Raisamo, R.
records.venue: Applied Human Factors and Ergonomics International
records.key_contribution: Develops and tests TAUCHI-GPT, an experimental open-source research AI tool built on top of GPT-4 that chains together LLM 'thoughts' to autonomously achieve and regress towards research goals; demonstrates leveraging pre-trained LLMs to create tool-specific multimodal R&D workflows.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant: an LLM-based research automation tool; no value alignment mechanism (heuristic 'value alignment' subdomain is tangential).
records.notes: ft_file=TAUCHI-GPT: Leveraging GPT-4 to Create a Multimodal Open-Source Research AI Tool.pdf

records.title: Artificial Intelligence, Value Alignment and Rationality
records.authors: Bekenova, Z.; Muü¨rsepp, P.; Nurysheva, G.; Turarbekova, L.
records.key_contribution: Philosophical analysis of the value alignment problem: as long as humans cannot agree on a universal system of values in the positive sense, we may agree on what to avoid; argues a positive approach must still be kept in focus; concludes a holistic solution is not in sight (possibly never), leaving an era of endless adjustment of digital minds to biological ones, with keeping humans in control as the biggest challenge.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a philosophical account of why value alignment lacks a definitive solution, centering on the impossibility of a universal value system and the need for ongoing human control.

records.title: Validating metrics for reward alignment in human-autonomy teaming
records.authors: Sanneman, L.; Shah, J.A.
records.key_contribution: Proposes four individual assessments and associated metrics for alignment between reward functions in human-autonomy teaming, plus three composite metrics, and validates them through a survey-based human-subject experiment; factor analysis of the collected data provides empirical support for two latent alignment constructs.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical validation of metrics for quantifying reward-function alignment in human-agent teams; relevant to value-alignment measurement and evaluation.
records.datasets_used: human-subject survey data from own experiment
records.notes: ft_file=Validating metrics for reward alignment in human-autonomy teaming.pdf

records.title: Hard Choices and Hard Limits in Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Goodman, B.
records.venue: AIES 2021 - Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Philosophical argument that parity (alternatives neither better, worse, nor equal) shows hard limits on AI-assisted decision-making: AI cannot and should not resolve 'hard choices', a point with implications for value alignment and AI ethics.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical analysis of limits on value-resolving AI; relevant to value alignment's normative assumptions but no technical content.
records.key_equations_definitions: parity (alternatives on a par) in decision theory

records.title: Cybersecurity and privacy in smart bioprinting
records.authors: Isichei, J.C.; Khorsandroo, S.; Desai, S.
records.key_contribution: Reviews the smart bioprinting ecosystem as a multilayered architecture (IoT, cloud, AI/ML, NextGen networks, blockchain), covering cybersecurity challenges, privacy-preservation solutions, and open research challenges.
records.relevance_justification: Revised down from seed 4: off-topic, cybersecurity/privacy in smart bioprinting with no value-alignment content.
records.notes: ft_file=Cybersecurity and privacy in smart bioprinting.pdf | ai-revised:subdomains=robustness; governance; capabilities->other

records.title: Artificial intelligence and indigenous perspectives: Protecting and empowering intelligent human beings
records.authors: Maitra, S.
records.venue: AIES 2020 - Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Characterizes the AGI prospect as an impending loss of control and identity crisis for humanity; outlines the shortcomings of value alignment as a solution and argues for extension of these principles; proposes strongly relational Indigenous epistemologies - adept at accounting for the non-human and defying Western anthropocentrism - as a basis for accommodating AI as part of our network toward a symbiotic relationship.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: critique and extension of value alignment via relational Indigenous epistemologies; ethics/philosophy of alignment.
records.notes: ft_file=Artificial intelligence and indigenous perspectives: Protecting and empowering intelligent human beings.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: A short introduction to the ethics of artificial intelligence
records.authors: Liao, S.M.
records.key_contribution: Chapter introduction to AI ethics covering key issues: data-hungry ML vulnerable to bad data and algorithms, black-box problems (interpretability, explainability, trust), lack of a moral sense, human vulnerability to over-performing systems, and long-term superintelligence risks including aligning superintelligent values with human values.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a survey introduction to AI ethics including the value-alignment problem for superintelligence; abstract only, moderate confidence.

records.title: Interpretable Preferences via Multi-Objective Reward Modeling and Mixture-of-Experts
records.authors: Wang, H.; Xiong, W.; Xie, T.; Zhao, H.; Zhang, T.
records.venue: EMNLP 2024 - 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Findings of EMNLP 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes a two-stage approach for interpretable reward models in RLHF: train an Absolute-Rating Multi-Objective Reward Model (ArmoRM) with multi-dimensional absolute ratings combined with a Mixture-of-Experts gating mechanism to produce interpretable preferences, so that reward-model internal decision processes are consistent with human preferences and reward hacking in LLM alignment is prevented.
records.relevance_justification: RLHF reward-model interpretability method aimed at preventing reward hacking in LLM alignment; strongly relevant to alignment robustness and reward-model failure modes.
records.notes: ft_file=Interpretable Preferences via Multi-Objective Reward Modeling and Mixture-of-Experts.pdf

records.title: Value Alignment from Unstructured Text
records.authors: Padhi, I.; Ramamurthy, K.N.; Sattigeri, P.; Nagireddy, M.; Dognin, P.; Varshney, K.R.
records.venue: EMNLP 2024 - 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Proceedings of the Industry Track
records.key_contribution: Introduces a systematic end-to-end methodology for aligning LLMs to the implicit and explicit values in unstructured text using scalable synthetic data generation; demonstrated on Mistral-7B-Instruct in two use-cases, credibly aligning the model to document values with improved performance over other approaches by automatic metrics and win rates.
records.relevance_justification: Directly on scalable value alignment of LLMs from unstructured text; an applied alignment method.

records.title: Practical Ethical Issues for Artificial Intelligence in Education
records.authors: Córdova, P.R.; Vicari, R.M.
records.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
records.key_contribution: Proposes an ethics-by-design architecture for AI in education using a top-down Artificial Moral Agent (AMA) approach based on the BDI model, combining utilitarian and deontological ethical frameworks within the Values Alignment paradigm.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: AMA design for value alignment in the education domain.
records.key_equations_definitions: BDI-based AMA with utilitarian + deontological reasoning

records.title: (When) can ai bots lie?
records.authors: Chakraborti, T.; Kambhampati, S.
records.venue: AIES 2019 - Proceedings of the 2019 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Examines how AI agents that build mental models can open pathways for manipulating and exploiting humans 'for the greater good' without malicious intent, beyond misinterpretation of intent (value alignment); such behavior can be engineered because models are misused, not misspecified; illustrates in a cooperative human-robot teaming scenario with a thought experiment asking participants to qualify ethically boundary-crossing behaviors, and discusses implications for the doctor-patient relationship.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: ethics of deceptive/manipulative AI behavior relative to value alignment; empirical thought experiment, relevant to alignment failure modes.
records.datasets_used: Human-robot teaming thought experiment

records.title: Alleviating Action Hallucination for LLM-based Embodied Agents via Inner and Outer Alignment
records.authors: Li, K.; Zheng, Q.; Zhan, Y.; Zhang, C.; Zhang, T.; Lin, X.; Qi, C.; Li, L.; Tao, D.

records.key_contribution: Mitigates sparse reward problems in Monte Carlo Tree Search by representing objectives as automata to define novel reward-shaping functions over the structured representation; the shaping function is dynamically updated to capture statistics on the utility of each automaton transition; addresses human-aided artificial rewards introducing human error, sub-optimal behavior, and greater propensity for reward hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: reward-shaping method explicitly targeting reward hacking via structured automata objective representation; abstract-only, lower confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Automata-based objective representation; dynamic reward shaping; MCTS

records.title: Artificial thinking and doomsday projections: a discourse on trust, ethics and safety
records.authors: White, J.; Brandt, D.; Söffner, J.; Stapleton, L.
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Editorial exchange among four scholars (White, Brandt, Soeffner, Stapleton) reflecting on where AI is headed, considering trust, ethics, and safety; discusses the engineered divorce from reality of human embodiment, AI regulation, alignment, bias, and existential risk.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: an editorial discourse touching AI alignment, trust, and existential risk rather than a focused analysis of alignment failure mechanisms.
records.notes: ft_file=Artificial thinking and doomsday projections: a discourse on trust, ethics and safety.pdf

records.title: Towards agi agent safety by iteratively improving the utility function
records.authors: Holtman, K.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Presents a mathematical AGI safety layer providing a dedicated input terminal for iterative improvement of an AGI agent's utility function, letting humans close loopholes in the utility function's encoding of goals and constraints, direct the agent toward new goals, or force shutdown; analyzes the agent's emergent incentive to manipulate this improvement process (deceiving, restraining, or attacking the humans involved) and shows the safety layer partially or fully suppresses it; generalizes earlier AGI emergency stop-button work.
records.relevance_justification: Formal AGI safety design addressing manipulation of the alignment process and shutdown; strongly relevant to alignment robustness and corrigibility.
records.notes: ft_file=AGI Agent Safety by Iteratively Improving the Utility Function.pdf

records.title: Training Value-Aligned Reinforcement Learning Agents Using a Normative Prior
records.authors: Al Nahian, M.S.; Frazier, S.; Riedl, M.; Harrison, B.
records.key_contribution: Introduces value-aligned RL training with two reward signals: a task-performance reward plus a normative-behavior reward derived from a value-aligned prior model trained on naturally occurring stories (classifying text as normative/non-normative); uses policy-shaping variations to balance rewards; tested on three interactive text-based worlds designed to offer normative/altruistic deviation opportunities.
records.relevance_justification: Directly on value-aligned RL using normative priors from natural language; an applied alignment method with evaluation environments.
records.key_equations_definitions: policy shaping to balance task and normative rewards
records.datasets_used: three interactive text-based worlds; stories for normative prior
records.effect_sizes: produces policies both effective and perceived as more normative
records.notes: ft_file=Training Value-Aligned Reinforcement Learning Agents Using a Normative Prior.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: 'Affordances' for Machine Learning
records.authors: Davis, J.L.
records.key_contribution: Applies an applied-affordance framework (mechanisms and conditions) to machine learning, analyzing how technology shapes rather than determines outcomes across work, policing, and housing-justice case examples.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential: social-science framing of ML technology effects, not value alignment.

records.title: The Goofus & Gallant Story Corpus for Practical Value Alignment
records.authors: Al Nahian, M.S.; Tasrin, T.; Frazier, S.; Riedl, M.; Harrison, B.
records.venue: Proceedings - 2024 International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications, ICMLA 2024
records.key_contribution: Presents the Goofus & Gallant Story Corpus, a multi-modal dataset (natural language and artistic images) illustrating normative and non-normative behavior in real-life situations, originally curated to teach young children social principles; argues it is an ideal training set for socially normative agents given the curated images and explicit normative/non-normative contrasts.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: dataset contribution for training socially normative AI agents; empirical resource for practical value alignment.
records.datasets_used: Goofus & Gallant Story Corpus (natural language + artistic images, normative vs non-normative)

records.title: Understanding the spirit of a norm: Challenges for norm-learning agents
records.authors: Arnold, T.; Scheutz, M.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Argues machine ethics approaches (logic-based and data-based) have not considered capturing the 'spirit of a norm', which eludes rigid interpretation; presents paradigmatic scenarios showing why the spirit of a norm is critical and why mere data-driven value alignment (e.g., RL for human-robot interaction) is inadequate, proposing a combination of common-sense inference-based and data-driven norm learning.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: directly critiques data-driven value alignment as failing to capture context-sensitive normative meaning (the spirit of a norm), a limitation relevant to behavioral alignment approaches.
records.notes: ft_file=Understanding the spirit of a norm: Challenges for norm-learning agents.pdf

records.title: AI Alignment and Human Reward
records.authors: Butlin, P.
records.venue: AIES 2021 - Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Philosophical assessment of the proposal that human reward functions should be the target for AI alignment; argues there is some reason to believe powerful AI agents aligned to values of this form would help humans lead good lives, but considerable uncertainty remains from unresolved empirical and conceptual issues in human psychology.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical analysis of which class of human values (e.g., reward functions) AI alignment should target; relevant to value-alignment theory.

records.title: Friendly Superintelligent AI: All You Need Is Love
records.authors: Prinzing, M.
records.venue: Studies in Applied Philosophy, Epistemology and Rational Ethics
records.key_contribution: Proposes addressing the perverse-instantiation problem in superintelligent AI by instructing the AI to love humanity; compares this proposal with Yudkowsky's Coherent Extrapolated Volition and Bostrom's Moral Modeling.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical contribution to friendly-AI goal specification, addressing perverse instantiations; conceptual rather than technical.
records.notes: ft_file=Friendly Superintelligent AI: All You Need Is Love.pdf

records.title: FLAMES: Benchmarking Value Alignment of LLMs in Chinese
records.authors: Huang, K.; Liu, X.; Guo, Q.; Sun, T.; Sun, J.; Wang, Y.; Zhou, Z.; Wang, Y.; Teng, Y.; Qiu, X.; Wang, Y.; Lin, D.
records.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, NAACL 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes FLAMES, a Chinese value-alignment benchmark covering harmlessness principles and a morality dimension integrating specific Chinese values (e.g., harmony), using adversarial/jailbreaking prompts with implicit malice; evaluates 17 mainstream LLMs, finding all show relatively limited deep alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: benchmark exposing shallow value alignment across 17 LLMs, directly bearing on alignment-evaluation methodology.
records.datasets_used: FLAMES benchmark with adversarial and jailbreaking prompts
records.effect_sizes: All evaluated LLMs show relatively weak deep alignment/harmlessness

records.title: AI VALUE ALIGNMENT AND SOCIOLOGY OF MORALITY
records.authors: Deviatko, I.F.
records.key_contribution: Examines popular ideas about goals and possibilities of human control over AI and argues they are incomplete given new asymmetries of control from the 'digital revolution'; argues sociology and social psychology of morality acquire a decisive role as a large-scale research field in ethically oriented AI; proposes an additional sociological substantiation and a narrower interpretation of AI value alignment principles.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: sociological perspective on AI value alignment and control asymmetries; theoretical/argumentative, abstract-only.

records.title: Why the Failure? How Adversarial Examples Can Provide Insights for Interpretable Machine Learning
records.authors: Tomsett, R.; Widdicombe, A.; Xing, T.; Chakraborty, S.; Julier, S.; Gurram, P.; Rao, R.; Srivastava, M.
records.venue: 2018 21st International Conference on Information Fusion, FUSION 2018
records.key_contribution: Argues that interpretability and adversarial attacks are conceptually linked: insights from adversarial examples can inform interpretable machine learning, motivated by military coalition situation understanding where decision-makers must justify decisions and models are sensitive to input perturbations.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: connects interpretability and adversarial robustness, with no engagement with value alignment or alignment failure; abstract only, moderate confidence.

records.title: The linguistic dead zone of value-aligned agency, natural and artificial: The linguistic dead zone..: T. LaCroix
records.authors: LaCroix, T.
records.key_contribution: Argues that linguistic communication is a necessary condition for robust value alignment, and discusses consequences of this claim for research programmes that attempt to ensure value alignment for AI systems or to design robustly beneficial or ethical artificial agents.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical argument linking linguistic communication to the feasibility of robust value alignment; relevant to value-alignment theory.

records.title: Exploiting Value System Structure for Value-Aligned Decision-Making
records.authors: Karanik, M.; Billhardt, H.; Fernández, A.; Ossowski, S.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Presents a model of a value-aware agent that decides based on its value system and a value promotion scheme for available actions: represents the value system with a fuzzy measure and uses aggregation operators (exemplified by Schwartz's basic value theory with Choquet's discrete integral) to select the action best aligned with agent preferences.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to formal value-system representation and value-based decision-making; technical but narrow.
records.key_equations_definitions: fuzzy measure value system; Choquet discrete integral aggregation; Schwartz basic value theory

records.title: Addressing the Value Alignment Problem Through Online Institutions
records.authors: Noriega, P.; Verhagen, H.; Padget, J.; d’Inverno, M.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Investigates how online institutions (a class of multiagent systems with norms) can inform a principled approach to the general value alignment problem.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: institutional-design approach to value alignment in multiagent systems.
records.key_equations_definitions: Online institutions; WIT design pattern
records.notes: ft_file=Addressing the Value Alignment Problem through Online Institutions.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Protecting Human Investors with Blockchain-based Circuit Breakers
records.authors: Sparer, L.; Neulinger, A.
records.venue: 2024 6th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications, BCCA 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes a blockchain-based circuit breaker to mitigate financial losses of human traders in sell-the-news events potentially triggered by fake news in AI/algorithmic trading markets; evaluates effectiveness by modeling market dynamics involving bots and human traders and simulating scenarios with and without blockchain-based circuit breakers; uses oracle data to verify news authenticity; shows human traders suffer significantly lower losses with the breaker deployed.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant: financial protection mechanism against fake-news-driven market manipulation involving AI trading; governance/robustness tangential to alignment.
records.datasets_used: Simulated trading scenarios with bots and human traders; oracle news verification
records.effect_sizes: Human traders suffer significantly lower losses with blockchain-based circuit breaker deployed
records.notes: ft_file=Protecting Human Investors with Blockchain-based Circuit Breakers.pdf

records.title: Deciphering AI Decision-Making: A Generalizable Framework of Human-AI Misalignment
records.authors: Du, J.; Ye, Y.; You, H.; Wu, J.; Sun, B.
records.venue: Computing in Civil Engineering 2024: Artificial Intelligence, Automation and Robotics, and Human-Centered Innovations - Selected papers from the ASCE International Conference on Computing in Civil Engineering 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes a metacognitive framework for deconstructing and measuring the intrinsic/internal processes of AI decision-making as a high-level cognitive process; motivated by the need to understand human-AI misalignment given differences between humans and AI in executing key stages of decision-making with partially observable data and conflicting objectives.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: directly targets measurement of human-AI misalignment in decision-making, framing alignment as an observable cognitive phenomenon; abstract only, moderate confidence.

records.title: A survey of the potential long-Term impacts of ai: How ai could lead to long-Term changes in science, cooperation, power, epistemics and values
records.authors: Clarke, S.; Whittlestone, J.
records.venue: AIES 2022 - Proceedings of the 2022 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Surveys literature on the long-term societal impacts of AI and identifies five potential long-term impacts - changes in science, cooperation, power, epistemics, and values - reviewing the state of research in each area and highlighting priority questions for future research.
records.relevance_justification: Survey of long-term AI impacts including value change and cooperation; relevant to alignment and governance scope.
records.notes: ft_file=A Survey of the Potential Long-term Impacts of AI.pdf

records.title: Calibrating machine behavior: a challenge for AI alignment
records.authors: Firt, E.
records.key_contribution: Identifies three obstacles to implementing value alignment: a technological/technical obstacle, a normative obstacle, and a calibration problem; focuses on calibrating a system to a specific location on the spectrum between righteous and normal/average human behavior for a given value, and how mis-calibration raises trustworthiness concerns.
records.relevance_justification: Conceptual analysis of alignment obstacles with a distinct calibration framing; relevant to specifying and calibrating aligned behavior.
records.notes: ft_file=Calibrating machine behavior: a challenge for AI alignment.pdf

records.title: Human-in-the-Loop Ethical AI for Care Robots and Confucian Virtue Ethics
records.authors: Liu, J.L.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Reports partial results of an online survey on the virtues people want in future care robots and explicates how Confucian virtue ethics can respond to these human expectations for human-in-the-loop ethical AI.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical + philosophical treatment of human expectations for care-robot virtue and human-in-the-loop alignment.
records.datasets_used: Online survey (Human-in-the-Loop Ethical AI for Social Robots)
records.notes: ft_file=Human-in-the-Loop Ethical AI for Care Robots and Confucian Virtue Ethics.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=review->empirical

records.title: An Ontology for Value Awareness Engineering
records.authors: Holgado-Sánchez, A.; Billhardt, H.; Ossowski, S.; Fernández, A.
records.venue: International Conference on Agents and Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Develops an ontology linking models and concepts proposed in computational value awareness so as to formalize heterogeneous research proposals in a common language; implemented in OWL and extended with SWRL rules; illustrates capability for describing multi-agent systems from the value-awareness engineering perspective through several case studies grounded in the literature; evaluated following scenarios of the NeOn Methodology and interconnected with Semantic Web ontologies.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: ontology engineering for value awareness, enabling formal description of value-aware agents; relevant to value-aware behavior specification.
records.key_equations_definitions: Value awareness ontology (OWL + SWRL); NeOn Methodology evaluation

records.title: A functional contextual, observer-centric, quantum mechanical, and neuro-symbolic approach to solving the alignment problem of artificial general intelligence: safe AI through intersecting computational psychological neuroscience and LLM architecture for emergent theory of mind
records.authors: Edwards, D.J.
records.key_contribution: Proposes a functional-contextual, observer-centric, quantum-mechanical, neuro-symbolic model to address AGI value alignment, arguing alignment requires three aspects: an interpretable values specification, a utility function, and a dynamic contextual account of behavior; intersects computational psychological neuroscience with LLM architecture for emergent theory of mind.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a theory paper proposing neuro-symbolic requirements for AGI alignment (interpretable value specification, utility, contextual behavior), broadly aligned with the value-specification theme.
records.key_equations_definitions: Neurosymbolic model: interpretable value specification + utility function + dynamic contextual behavior account
