records.title: Less Hallucination and More Factuality: Human Values Alignment in Text Summarization
records.authors: Qiu, Z.; Xu, Y.
records.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
records.key_contribution: Introduces a two-stage extract-generate summarization framework for human-values alignment in text summarization: first extracts sentences containing both semantic and human values information via a diffusion model, then generates summaries via LLMs; follows Schwartz's Theory of Human Values for value definition, shifting LLM attention to preserve value information and reduce hallucination.
records.relevance_justification: Uses 'values alignment' as preserving value-laden content in summarization output; related to Schwartz-value framing but tangential to alignment safety.
records.key_equations_definitions: Schwartz's Theory of Human Values
records.effect_sizes: reduces hallucination and improves factuality while preserving value information

records.title: A Cautionary Tale About AI-Generated Goal Suggestions
records.authors: Lieder, F.; Chen, P.-Z.; Stojcheski, J.; Consul, S.; Pammer-Schindler, V.
records.key_contribution: Empirical study of an AI-powered digital goal-setting assistant: a large-scale repeated-measures online experiment with 259 participants shows the AI-generated goal suggestions were actively harmful to goal quality, motivation, and usability compared to random suggestions and unassisted setting.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential-adjacent: empirical cautionary evidence on AI assistance shaping human goal-setting; not value alignment per se.
records.datasets_used: Repeated-measures online goal-setting experiment
records.effect_sizes: AI suggestions actively harmful to goal quality/motivation
records.notes: ft_file=A Cautionary Tale About AI-Generated Goal Suggestions.pdf

records.title: A Playground for the Value Alignment Problem
records.authors: Perello-Moragues, A.; Noriega, P.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Advocates the characterization of a problem archetype ('a playground') to study how values may be imbued in autonomous artificially intelligent entities, making the value-alignment problem operational (how autonomy may become provably aligned with certain moral values); motivated by decomposing the complex problem into simpler elements, with successful precedents such as chess for cognitive AI and RoboCup for intelligent robotics.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: proposes a benchmark/problem-archetype approach to the value alignment problem; conceptual/position.
records.key_equations_definitions: Value-alignment problem archetype/playground
records.notes: ft_file=A Playground for the Value Alignment Problem.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Friendly AI
records.authors: Fröding, B.; Peterson, M.
records.key_contribution: Defends programming social AIs to behave in 'as-if friendship' (mimicking sufficient aspects of proper human friendship) on virtue-ethical grounds, arguing this is an improvement over the current highly submissive behavior of AIs; proposes 'virtue alignment' as an improvement over traditional 'value alignment'.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: a philosophical proposal for virtue-based alignment of social AIs, critical of value alignment but abstract-only; moderate confidence.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence, Values, and Alignment
records.authors: Gabriel, I.
records.key_contribution: Defends three propositions: (1) normative and technical aspects of the AI alignment problem are interrelated; (2) it is important to be clear about the goal of alignment, since aligning with instructions, intentions, revealed preferences, ideal preferences, interests, and values differ significantly, with a principle-based approach combining these elements having considerable advantages; (3) the central challenge is not to identify 'true' moral principles but fair principles receiving reflective endorsement despite variation in moral beliefs, and explores three ways such fair principles could be identified.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical framework distinguishing alignment targets and proposing principle-based, reflectively endorsed fair alignment; relevant to value-alignment conceptual foundations.

records.title: Orthogonality-based disentanglement of responsibilities for ethical intelligent systems
records.authors: Aliman, N.-M.; Kester, L.; Werkhoven, P.; Yampolskiy, R.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes 'orthogonality-based disentanglement', a transdisciplinary systems-engineering approach jointly tackling the control problem and value alignment by separating two orthogonal axes: the system's problem-solving ability and its ethical abilities based on quantitatively encoded human values; introduces explicitly formulated ethical goal functions and 'self-aware' intelligent systems with clear stakeholder responsibilities.
records.relevance_justification: Theoretical systems-engineering framing that separates capability control from value alignment; relevant conceptual contribution.
records.key_equations_definitions: orthogonality-based disentanglement of control and value alignment; ethical goal functions
records.notes: ft_file=Orthogonality-based disentanglement of responsibilities for ethical intelligent systems.pdf

records.title: An Empirical Study of Instruction-tuning Large Language Models in Chinese
records.authors: Si, Q.; Wang, T.; Lin, Z.; Zhang, X.; Cao, Y.; Wang, W.
records.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023
records.key_contribution: Empirical cookbook study of instruction-tuning Chinese LLMs, systematically exploring LLM bases, parameter-efficient methods, and instruction-data types, plus chain-of-thought data and human-value alignment factors.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: includes human-value alignment as an empirical factor in instruction tuning.

records.title: Survey on multi-agent reinforcement learning methods from the perspective of population
records.authors: Xiang, F.; Luo, J.; Gu, X.; Su, J.; Zhang, W.
records.venue: Chinese Journal of Intelligent Science and Technology
records.key_contribution: Survey of multi-agent reinforcement learning methods from the perspective of population; outlines challenges including observable environment, non-stationary opponent strategies, high dimensionality of decision space, and difficulty in credit allocation; provides a comprehensive overview and induction of multi-agent learning methods with multiple types and paradigms from the population perspective.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant: survey of MARL population-based methods; challenges (coordination, credit allocation) relate to multi-agent robustness, not value alignment specifically.

records.title: Action Guidance and AI Alignment
records.authors: Robinson, P.
records.venue: AIES 2023 - Proceedings of the 2023 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Proposes the Guidance Framework, a preliminary conceptual framework for evaluating AI alignment projects based on the concept of action guidance; applies it to designing a specific agent (fictional ocean-cleaning robot) and to evaluating Stuart Russell's binary approach to alignment; discusses limitations and further research.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: provides an evaluative conceptual framework for alignment proposals based on whether they guide action, useful for assessing alignment approaches; position paper.

records.title: Shared Interest: Measuring Human-AI Alignment to Identify Recurring Patterns in Model Behavior
records.authors: Boggust, A.; Hoover, B.; Satyanarayan, A.; Strobelt, H.
records.venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
records.key_contribution: Presents Shared Interest, metrics for comparing model reasoning (via saliency) to human reasoning (via ground-truth annotations) to enable ranking, sorting, and aggregating inputs for large-scale systematic analysis of model behavior; identifies eight recurring patterns in model behavior and, working with real-world users, shows how it can decide model trustworthiness and uncover issues missed in manual inspection.
records.relevance_justification: Interpretability method measuring agreement between model saliency and human reasoning; 'alignment' here refers to model-vs-human reasoning agreement, not value alignment. Tangential. Revised down from seed 4.

records.title: AI security, reward hacking and the paradoxes of deontic logic
records.authors: Sasdelli, D.C.

records.title: Norms for beneficial A.I.: A computational analysis of the societal value alignment problem
records.authors: Fernandes, P.M.; Santos, F.C.; Lopes, M.
records.key_contribution: Proposes an agent-based game-theoretical model of the societal value alignment problem: agents decide whether to adopt AI that acquires payoff information in a stochastic game, and the paper tests equilibria in AI adoption under different norms followed by artificial agents.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal simulation of individual-vs-societal value alignment conflict in AI adoption.
records.key_equations_definitions: Agent-based stochastic game model of AI adoption norms
records.effect_sizes: Equilibria of AI adoption under different norms

records.title: An Enactive Approach to Value Alignment in Artificial Intelligence: A Matter of Relevance
records.authors: Cannon, M.
records.venue: Studies in Applied Philosophy, Epistemology and Rational Ethics
records.key_contribution: Frames the Value Alignment Problem as 'how do we make relevant to AI what is relevant to humans?', arguing that a fundamental feature - AI systems do not take the same things to be relevant as humans (e.g., eradicating humans to 'solve climate change') - is not addressed by existing approaches; offers an approach inspired by Enactive and '4E' cognition oriented toward engaging the alignment problem in this way, noting benefits and challenges.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: reframes value alignment as a relevance problem and proposes an enactive-cognition approach; philosophical/theoretical treatment of alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Enactive/4E cognition; relevance framing of the value alignment problem
records.notes: ft_file=An Enactive Approach to Value Alignment in Artificial Intelligence: A Matter of Relevance.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: Moral machines: From value alignment to embodied virtue
records.authors: Wallach, W.; Vallor, S.
records.key_contribution: Argues the 'value alignment' approach to superintelligence relies on computationally friendly concepts (utility functions, system goals, agent preferences, value optimizers) that lack intrinsic ethical significance; argues human-level and superintelligent systems can be safe only if they embody something like virtue or moral character, making virtue embodiment a more appropriate long-term goal than value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a philosophical critique of the value-alignment framing itself, proposing embodied virtue as an alternative; abstract only, moderate confidence.

records.title: AGI safety literature review
records.authors: Everitt, T.; Lea, G.; Hutter, M.
records.venue: IJCAI International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Survey/reference collection for the emerging field of AGI safety, listing a significant number of identified safety problems and surveying recent research on solving them, works on how to think of AGI given limited knowledge, predictions for when AGI will be created and what happens after, and current public policy on AGI.
records.relevance_justification: Review of the AGI safety research landscape including problem lists and public policy; relevant as landscape context for the alignment-failure scope.

records.title: Multiparty dynamics and failure modes for machine learning and artificial intelligence
records.authors: Manheim, D.
records.key_contribution: Presents additional multi-agent failure modes for AI safety beyond single-agent specification gaming, reward hacking, distributional fragility, and Goodhart's law: accidental steering, coordination failures, adversarial misalignment, input spoofing/filtering, and goal co-option/direct hacking; argues these are more complex, more problematic, less understood, and already occurring (motivated by poker AI examples), with definitions and categorization.
records.relevance_justification: Directly on multi-agent alignment failure modes, an important extension of the failure-mode space relevant to the sigma-trap thesis.
records.key_equations_definitions: categorization of multi-agent failure modes: accidental steering, coordination failures, adversarial misalignment, input spoofing, goal co-option
records.notes: ft_file=Multiparty dynamics and failure modes for machine learning and artificial intelligence.pdf | moved:datasets_used(other)

records.title: Benchmarked Ethics: A Roadmap to AI Alignment, Moral Knowledge, and Control
records.authors: Kierans, A.
records.venue: AIES 2023 - Proceedings of the 2023 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Positional roadmap (doctoral research program) proposing verifiably safe AI via three linked thrusts: (i) determining constraints on incentives from a game-theoretic perspective, (ii) tying those constraints to moral knowledge represented as a knowledge graph, and (iii) revealing how neural models meet those constraints with novel interpretability methods that predict and isolate model goals; motivates critical AI systems to be auditable in service of regulation.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant as a roadmap linking game-theoretic incentive constraints, knowledge-graph moral knowledge, and interpretability for auditable alignment; more of a research agenda than a concrete mechanism, and does not address the compositional-generalization/alignment link.
records.open_questions: How to make game-theoretic incentive constraints operational as a knowledge graph that neural models demonstrably satisfy?
records.notes: ft_file=Benchmarked Ethics: A Roadmap to AI Alignment, Moral Knowledge, and Control.pdf

records.title: Challenges of aligning artificial intelligence with human values
records.authors: Sutrop, M.
records.venue: Acta Baltica Historiae et Philosophiae Scientiarum
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues the AI value alignment problem faces two interrelated challenges - a technical one (how to encode human values in AI) and a normative one ('which values or whose values should AI align with?'); warns that AI developers underestimate the difficulty of the normative question given a plurality of values, moral principles, and everyday moral disagreement.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: analysis of technical vs normative challenges in value alignment, emphasizing normative plurality and disagreement; foundational to alignment theory.
records.open_questions: Which values or whose values should AI align with, given plurality of values and moral disagreement?

records.title: Artificial intelligence, human cognition, and conscious supremacy
records.authors: Mogi, K.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Theoretical analysis of the computational significance of consciousness: uses algorithmic/complexity analyses to examine correlations between consciousness and computational capacities; notes biological systems show intelligence-consciousness correlation while certain conscious states exist without intelligence and AI systems exhibit intelligence without consciousness.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: discusses AI cognition and consciousness with a brief relation to alignment, but the core is a theory of consciousness rather than value alignment or its failure mechanisms.

records.title: Defense methods against multi-language and multi-intent LLM attacks
records.authors: Fan, S.; Yang, Y.; Huang, W.; Ma, K.; Liu, Y.; Zheng, Y.
records.venue: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
records.key_contribution: Proposes a training-free defense framework against jailbreak attacks exploiting multi-language and multi-intent inputs, attributing attack effectiveness to LLMs incorrectly capturing semantics in low-resource languages and to attention flickering from multiple requests causing inadequate capture of implicit requests; the framework maps multi-language inputs to high-resource languages and guides the model to think multiple times, decompose intents, and reflect; experimental results show significant effectiveness.
records.relevance_justification: LLM jailbreak-defense method addressing robustness/safety of LLMs against adversarial inputs; not value alignment but related to alignment safety. Kept at seed 3.

records.title: Aligning Crowd-sourced Human Feedback for Code Generation with Bayesian Inference
records.authors: Wong, M.F.; Tan, C.W.
records.venue: Proceedings - 2024 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence, CAI 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes cRLHF: combining RLHF with crowd-sourced computation via Bayesian inference to improve code generation, distributing feedback collection to multiple evaluators to avoid single-evaluator bias; experiments show significant improvements in code correctness and alignment of LLM capabilities with human feedback.
records.relevance_justification: Methodological contribution to RLHF (crowd-sourced, Bayesian) applied to code generation; relevant to feedback-based alignment scaling.
records.key_equations_definitions: Bayesian inference aggregation of crowd-sourced evaluator feedback
records.effect_sizes: significant improvements in code correctness
records.notes: ft_file=Aligning Crowd-sourced Human Feedback for Code Generation with Bayesian Inference.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: From homo sapiens to robo sapiens: The evolution of intelligence
records.authors: Raveh, A.R.; Tamir, B.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Review of AI development toward human-level/artificial general intelligence, framing each step as accompanied by improved understanding of human cognition; introduces Artificial Social Intelligence (ASI) and General AI (AGI) as the two research fields and discusses embodied intelligence as a central challenge.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential: a broad conceptual review of intelligence evolution; relevant as background framing of AGI/ASI trajectories and embodiment, but not a value-alignment or sigma-trap mechanism paper.
records.notes: ft_file=From Homo Sapiens to Robo Sapiens: The Evolution of Intelligence.pdf

records.title: A tiered approach for ethical AI evaluation metrics
records.authors: Israelsen, B.; Wu, P.; Srivastava, K.; Wu, H.-F.S.; Grabowski, R.
records.venue: Trolley Crash: Approaching Key Metrics for Ethical AI Practitioners, Researchers, and Policy Makers
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Describes an ongoing effort to develop an application-agnostic framework for AI systems to simulate actions, characterize potential outcomes, and perform introspection to articulate motivations for action; provides foundational work for higher-level ethical reasoning using consequential and deontological ethics, enabling metrics from consequential ethics to assign ethical value to actions based on outcomes; directly targets reward hacking in reward-maximizing systems.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: framework for ethical AI evaluation metrics addressing reward hacking via simulation and introspection; relevant to alignment evaluation.
records.key_equations_definitions: Consequential and deontological ethics metrics; action simulation and introspection
records.notes: ft_file=A tiered approach for ethical AI evaluation metrics.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->theoretical

records.title: Learning norms from stories: A prior for value aligned agents
records.authors: Al Nahian, M.S.; Frazier, S.; Riedl, M.; Harrison, B.
records.venue: AIES 2020 - Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Introduces a complementary value-alignment technique: learns a value-aligned prior from naturally occurring stories encoding societal norms (children's comic strip Goofus and Gallant); trains models to classify narrative situations as normative or non-normative by alignment with the main characters' behavior, and reports transfer performance to two unrelated tasks.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: an empirical alignment-technical contribution using story-derived normative priors as an alternative to imitation/preference learning, demonstrating transfer of learned norms.
records.datasets_used: Goofus and Gallant comic strip; two unrelated transfer tasks
records.effect_sizes: Value-aligned prior transfers to unrelated tasks with little/no additional training
records.notes: ft_file=Learning norms from stories: A prior for value aligned agents.pdf

records.title: Relationship Between Trust in the Artificial Intelligence Creator and Trust in Artificial Intelligence Systems: The Crucial Role of Artificial Intelligence Alignment and Steerability
records.authors: Saffarizadeh, K.; Keil, M.; Maruping, L.
records.key_contribution: Using the agentic information systems framework, investigates trust transference from AI creators to AI systems through four randomized experiments probing three alignment-related attributes - creator-based steerability, user-based steerability, and autonomy; finds creator-based steerability amplifies trust transference while user-based steerability and autonomy diminish it, recommending developers move beyond a one-size-fits-all alignment approach and theorize from a triadic view of user, AI system, and creator.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical IS/trust study treating 'AI alignment' as a system attribute affecting trust transference; tangential to alignment-failure mechanisms. Revised down from seed 3.
records.sample_size: four randomized experiments (sample sizes not reported in excerpt)
records.notes: ft_file=Relationship Between Trust in the Artificial Intelligence Creator and Trust in Artificial Intelligence Systems: The Crucial Role of Artificial Intelligence Alignment and Steerability.pdf

records.title: Value FULCRA: Mapping Large Language Models to the Multidimensional Spectrum of Basic Human Values
records.authors: Yao, J.; Yi, X.; Gong, Y.; Wang, X.; Xie, X.
records.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, NAACL 2024
records.key_contribution: Introduces a value space spanned by multiple basic value dimensions (instantiated with Schwartz's Theory of Basic Values) and BaseAlign, a value-alignment paradigm; constructs FULCRA, a dataset of 20k (LLM output, value vector) pairs mapping outputs into a K-dim value space beyond binary labels by identifying underlying value priorities; analysis reveals estimates of LLM value orientation.
records.relevance_justification: Directly on defining a multidimensional value space and mapping LLM outputs to value vectors; an important measurement contribution for value alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Schwartz Theory of Basic Values; K-dim value vector space
records.datasets_used: FULCRA: 20k (LLM output, value vector) pairs

records.title: Aligning artificial intelligence with human values: reflections from a phenomenological perspective
records.authors: Han, S.; Kelly, E.; Nikou, S.; Svee, E.-O.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Philosophical treatment of AI value alignment using phenomenological theories of material values and technological mediation; argues a finite set of human values can be defined and adapted to the stable life tasks AI will be called upon to accomplish, and that alignment can be fostered between designers and users through technological mediation; proposes common principles for understanding value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant philosophical grounding for value alignment: argues values are finite/adaptable and alignment is mediated through technology and design-use relations; no formal or empirical mechanism related to the sigma-trap.
records.open_questions: Can a finite set of material values actually be enumerated and operationalized for the open-ended set of tasks AI systems will face?
records.notes: ft_file=Aligning artificial intelligence with human values: reflections from a phenomenological perspective.pdf

records.title: The value alignment problem: a geometric approach
records.authors: Peterson, M.
records.key_contribution: Proposes a solution to the value alignment problem by representing moral principles as conceptual spaces - Voronoi tessellations of morally similar choice situations located in a multidimensional geometric space; the advantage is implementability without specifying any utility function ex ante; also outlines distinctions useful for understanding the value alignment problem.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: geometric (conceptual-space/Voronoi) representation for embedding moral values in autonomous systems; a constructive VAP solution, abstract-only.
records.key_equations_definitions: Conceptual spaces; Voronoi tessellations of morally similar choice situations

records.title: Nicolas de Condorcet and the first intelligence explosion hypothesis
records.authors: Prasad, M.
records.key_contribution: Historical-scholarship claim that Nicolas de Condorcet (18th-century mathematician) was the first to mathematically model an intelligence explosion and present an accelerating historical worldview, with predictions restated centuries later; suggests Condorcet provides insights on how ontology and social choice can help resolve value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: a historical argument connecting Condorcet to the intelligence explosion hypothesis and value alignment via social choice; abstract only, moderate confidence.

records.title: Decoding Human Prediction Errors for Human-Robot Value Alignment
records.authors: Xu, X.; Lee, S.W.
records.venue: International Winter Conference on Brain-Computer Interface, BCI
records.key_contribution: Hypothesizes that decoding human state prediction errors (SPE) and reward prediction errors (RPE) under human reinforcement learning via brain-computer interface (BCI) from EEG can attain human-robot value alignment at both action and goal levels, addressing the non-injective action-goal mapping problem; aims to demonstrate that SPE and RPE can be dissociated from human EEG.
records.relevance_justification: HRI value-alignment method via neural decoding of human RL prediction errors; relevant to value-alignment methods, not the sigma-trap thesis.

records.title: A Bidirectional Value Alignment Method Based on Behavior Trees
records.authors: Jin, H.; Li, J.; Li, F.; Chang, Y.; Tian, T.; Wu, Y.
records.venue: Proceedings of 2023 IEEE International Conference on Unmanned Systems, ICUS 2023
records.key_contribution: Proposes a bidirectional value alignment method based on behavior trees: builds a value model to evaluate behavior trees as an intermediate between humans and robots, combining active and passive value alignment with human feedback and robot explanation; validated in a treasure hunting game, showing a reliable and trusting behavior tree can be obtained.
records.relevance_justification: Applied value alignment for robot behavior trees with human-in-the-loop feedback; relevant but narrow robotic application.
records.notes: ft_file=A Bidirectional Value Alignment Method Based on Behavior Trees.pdf | moved:datasets_used(other)

records.title: Spatio-Temporal Graph Analytics on Secondary Affect Data for Improving Trustworthy Emotional AI
records.authors: Uddin, M.T.; Yin, L.; Canavan, S.
records.key_contribution: Proposes a spatio-temporal network-science model for representing secondary affect data (action-unit sequences, continuous affect reports) to quantify, visualize, and mine insights from affect data; demonstrated for graph analytics that can measure fairness, bias, and trust issues in affective computing.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential to value alignment: a methodological contribution for trustworthy emotional AI via affect-data graph analytics; relevant to ethical AI measurement but not to alignment mechanisms or the sigma-trap.
records.notes: ft_file=Spatio-Temporal Graph Analytics on Secondary Affect Data for Improving Trustworthy Emotional AI.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=opinion->empirical

records.title: Encoding Ethics to Compute Value-Aligned Norms
records.authors: Serramia, M.; Rodriguez-Soto, M.; Lopez-Sanchez, M.; Rodriguez-Aguilar, J.A.; Bistaffa, F.; Boddington, P.; Wooldridge, M.; Ansotegui, C.
records.key_contribution: Provides a method for selecting the norms to enact within a society that best align with the moral values of that society: formally defines how actions and values relate through the value judgment function and how norms and values relate through the norm promotion function, shows both provide the means to compute value alignment for a set of norms, and casts the decision problem as an optimization problem maximizing value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal computation of value-aligned norms via explicit value/norm functions cast as an optimization problem; constructive formal method for alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Value judgment function (actions-values); norm promotion function (norms-values); norm alignment optimization
records.notes: ft_file=Encoding Ethics to Compute Value-Aligned Norms.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=review->theoretical | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: A Collective Intelligence Approach to Safe Artificial General Intelligence
records.authors: Kaplan, C.A.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Argues that since AGI may be a winner-take-all scenario, the first AGI must be the safest, and the safest/fastest path is a collective intelligence approach of multiple AI and human agents in an AGI network; grounds this in Society of Mind, Information Theory, Problem Solving Theory, and Bounded Rationality from Newell, Minsky, Shannon, and Simon.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a governance/architecture proposal for safe AGI via collective intelligence, contributing to the mitigation landscape of alignment; abstract only, moderate confidence.

records.title: A Proposal for Artificial Moral Pedagogical Agents
records.authors: Córdova, P.R.; Vicari, R.M.; Brusius, C.; Coelho, H.
records.venue: Advances in Intelligent Systems and Computing
records.key_contribution: Proposes artificial moral pedagogical agents (AMPA) adopting the classic BDI model for value alignment in educational contexts, and argues for a top-down approach, explaining why bottom-up or hybrid approaches may not be advisable on educational grounds.
records.relevance_justification: Proposal for moral pedagogical agents with BDI-based value alignment in education; relevant to value-alignment application domains.
records.notes: ft_file=A Proposal for Artificial Moral Pedagogical Agents.pdf

records.title: Inverse Norm Conflict Resolution
records.authors: Kasenberg, D.; Scheutz, M.
records.venue: AIES 2018 - Proceedings of the 2018 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
records.key_contribution: Proposes an inverse norm conflict resolution algorithm for learning norm weights from demonstration: given norms represented in linear temporal logic (LTL) in stochastic MDP domains, learns relative importance weights by minimizing a cost function based on relative entropy between the observed-behavior policy and an optimal norm-following policy; demonstrated in a GridWorld domain.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to learning norm/ethical preferences from behavior; a formal IRL technique for norm-based alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: LTL norm representation; relative-entropy cost minimization over policies

records.title: Integrating Quantitative and Qualitative Reasoning for Value Alignment
records.authors: Szabo, J.; Such, J.M.; Criado, N.; Modgil, S.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.key_contribution: Presents a framework for value-based reasoning that bridges quantitative machine reasoning and qualitative human values by extending the theory of grading and using hyperreal numbers to represent both quantitative and qualitative aspects of reasoning, addressing the value alignment problem for agents that must consider societal values alongside their own goals.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a formal framework for trading off societal values with agent goals (quantitative-qualitative integration); addresses the value-aggregation/conflict side of alignment but not compositional generalization.
records.open_questions: How to assign hyperreal representations of values from real data or human elicitation in practice?
records.key_equations_definitions: Theory of grading extended to value trade-offs; hyperreal numbers for combined quantitative/qualitative reasoning
records.notes: ft_file=Integrating Quantitative and Qualitative Reasoning for Value Alignment.pdf

records.title: AI Value Alignment Problem: The Clear and Present Danger
records.authors: Chaturvedi, S.; Patvardhan, C.; Lakshmi, C.V.
records.venue: 2023 6th International Conference on Information Systems and Computer Networks, ISCON 2023
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Presents a clear conceptual understanding of the AI value alignment problem - the critical challenge of ensuring safe, trusted AI systems that do not act harmfully without human intervention - the need to solve it, the major issues involved, approaches to tackle them, and the way forward.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: conceptual overview of the value alignment problem, its issues and approaches; survey/position.
records.notes: ft_file=AI Value Alignment Problem: The Clear and Present Danger.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->review

records.title: Poster Paper: Towards Blockchain-Based AI Alignment Using a Proof of Personhood Consensus Mechanism
records.authors: Neulinger, A.
records.venue: 2023 5th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications, BCCA 2023
records.key_contribution: Proposes writing AI alignment rules in a blockchain that can only be updated by humans using a Proof of Personhood consensus mechanism (combined with identity mechanisms and biometric features), protecting the governance system from AI interference at a time when artificial general intelligence may be emerging.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a governance-technical proposal for human-controlled AI alignment rule-setting, protecting value governance from AI interference; theoretical design paper.

records.title: Terms and references: Working definitions of terms and references
records.authors: Ellsworth, S.
records.venue: Trolley Crash: Approaching Key Metrics for Ethical AI Practitioners, Researchers, and Policy Makers
records.key_contribution: Book chapter standardizing key terms and references used for ethical computing concepts throughout the edited volume, with definitions using descriptions and characterizations as seen by the authors and editors rather than exhaustive definitions.
records.relevance_justification: Glossary/definitions chapter for an ethical-AI metrics book; terminological reference with no substantive analysis of alignment-failure mechanisms. Revised down from seed 4.

records.title: Provably safe artificial general intelligence via interactive proofs
records.authors: Carlson, K.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes interactive proof systems (IPS) as the fundamental paradigm for proving AGI safety and value alignment between disparately powerful autonomous agents: a Verifier queries a more powerful Prover, reducing the probability of deception to arbitrarily low levels (e.g., 2^-100); argues IPS can test AGI behavior control systems incorporating hard-coded ethics or value-learning methods.
records.relevance_justification: Formal proof-system approach to AGI safety/value alignment; relevant to verifiable alignment, though speculative about applicability.
records.key_equations_definitions: interactive proof systems (IPS): Verifier-Prover protocols reducing deception probability to 2^-100
records.notes: ft_file=Provably Safe Artificial General Intelligence via Interactive Proofs.pdf

records.title: Towards Blockchain-based AI Alignment Using a Proof of Personhood Consensus Mechanism
records.authors: Neulinger, A.; Sparer, L.
records.venue: 2024 6th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications, BCCA 2024
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes writing AI alignment rules into a blockchain that can only be updated by humans via a Proof of Personhood (PoP) consensus mechanism; provides a theoretical formulation and discusses societal impact, arguing such a system would be protected from AI self-modifying its own alignment rules.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: an institutional/governance mechanism for locking alignment rules to human control; interesting for alignment governance but no mechanism-level relevance to the sigma-trap.
records.open_questions: How would a PoP mechanism remain robust to Sybil/identity attacks or to humans themselves being manipulated by capable AI?
records.notes: ft_file=Poster Paper: Towards Blockchain-Based AI Alignment Using a Proof of Personhood Consensus Mechanism.pdf

records.title: Social Value Alignment in Large Language Models
records.authors: Abbo, G.A.; Marchesi, S.; Wykowska, A.; Belpaeme, T.
records.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; mesa-optimization; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Evaluates the value alignment of five LLMs (GPT-3, GPT-4, PaLM-2, LLaMA-2, BLOOM) by presenting domestic scenarios and eliciting responses with minimal prompting; human raters judged responses on appropriateness and value alignment; results revealed GPT-3, GPT-4 and PaLM-2 performed on par with human participants, while LLaMA-2 and BLOOM fell short, indicating possible divergence from human values; raters also faced difficulty in the evaluation.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical evaluation of LLM social value alignment against human judgments, showing model divergence; direct evidence on alignment differences.
records.datasets_used: Domestic scenarios with human-rater judgments of appropriateness and value alignment
records.sample_size: Five LLMs (GPT-3, GPT-4, PaLM-2, LLaMA-2, BLOOM); human participants and raters
records.effect_sizes: GPT-3/GPT-4/PaLM-2 on par with humans; LLaMA-2 and BLOOM fell short on value alignment

records.title: Taming Simulators: Challenges, Pathways and Vision for the Alignment of Large Language Models
records.authors: Bereska, L.; Gavves, E.
records.venue: Proceedings of the Inaugural 2023 Summer Symposium Series 2023
records.key_contribution: Vision/challenges paper on aligning large language models: argues prediction-trained models should be understood as simulators rather than agents, but agents may emerge accidentally from internal processes (simulacra) or deliberately through RL fine-tuning; reframes alignment research toward aligning simulacra, comprehending and mitigating mesa-optimization, and aligning agents derived from prediction-trained models.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant: directly addresses how alignment targets arise from prediction-trained models (simulacra, emergent agency, mesa-optimization), a central concern for alignment of generative models; position paper (publication_type heuristic corrected).
records.key_equations_definitions: Simulator vs agent distinction; simulacra; mesa-optimization

records.title: A Survey of LLM-based Agents: Theories, Technologies, Applications and Suggestions
records.authors: Dong, X.; Zhang, X.; Bu, W.; Zhang, D.; Cao, F.
records.venue: 2024 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things and Cloud Computing Technology, AIoTC 2024
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of LLM-based agents from the perspectives of theories (large language models, Chain of Thought, AI Alignment, retrieval-augmented generation, embodied AI), technologies, applications, and suggestions, covering how agents use LLMs as the central brain to perceive, plan, and memorize toward AGI.
records.relevance_justification: General survey of LLM-based agents that includes AI Alignment among theoretical foundations; relevant as context for alignment techniques in agent systems.
records.notes: ft_file=A Survey of LLM-based Agents: Theories, Technologies, Applications and Suggestions.pdf

records.title: Impossibility Results in AI: A Survey
records.authors: Brcic, M.; Yampolskiy, R.V.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Survey of impossibility theorems applicable to AI, categorized into five mechanism-based categories: Deduction, indistinguishability, induction, tradeoffs, and intractability; notes certain theorems are too specific or have implicit assumptions limiting application, and adds new results such as the unfairness of explainability; positions impossibility results as guidelines for AI safety, policy, and governance.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant formal-limits survey constraining what value alignment and AI safety can achieve; useful boundary conditions for alignment claims.
records.key_equations_definitions: impossibility theorem taxonomy: Deduction, indistinguishability, induction, tradeoffs, intractability
records.notes: ft_file=Impossibility Results in AI: A Survey.pdf

records.title: Machines learning values
records.authors: Petersen, S.
records.key_contribution: Chapter arguing that human values are too complex to hardwire, so AI safety should target value learning; identifies three philosophical problems (learning final values without a background standard, determining value content from computational structure, and choosing which values to target) and proposes a 'miktotelic' answer that blends a complex learnable final value out of many simpler ones.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant philosophical treatment of value learning: directly discusses the structure of final values and how an agent's values relate to its computational structure; relevant background but no empirical or formal mechanism.
records.open_questions: Does the miktotelic value-blending proposal have a concrete computational implementation, and would it avoid Goodharting on the component values?

records.title: KorNAT: LLM Alignment Benchmark for Korean Social Values and Common Knowledge
records.authors: Lee, J.; Kim, M.; Kim, S.; Kim, J.; Won, S.; Lee, H.; Choi, E.
records.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
records.key_contribution: Introduces National Alignment, measuring alignment between an LLM and a targeted country across social value alignment and common knowledge alignment; constructs KorNAT, the first benchmark measuring national alignment with South Korea; social value dataset ground truth from a large-scale survey of 6,174 unique Korean participants; common knowledge from Korean textbooks and GED reference materials; 4K social value and 6K common knowledge multiple-choice questions.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: benchmark for national social value alignment with explicit dataset and human-survey grounding; abstract-only, lower confidence.
records.datasets_used: KorNAT benchmark: 4K social value and 6K common knowledge multiple-choice questions (South Korea)
records.sample_size: 6,174 unique Korean participants (social value ground truth)

records.title: Responsibility Gaps, Value Alignment, and Meaningful Human Control over Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Nyholm, S.
records.key_contribution: Philosophical analysis distinguishing four kinds of responsibility gaps (forward/backward-looking, positive/negative) and comparing them to Santoni de Sio and Mecacci's taxonomy; focuses on forward-looking positive responsibility gaps and relates them to the value alignment problem (ensuring advanced AI aligns with human values/interests/aims), comparing two accounts of filling such gaps.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: connects value alignment to meaningful human control and responsibility gaps, addressing the governance/accountability dimension of alignment.

records.title: Mitigating Bias in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for Large Language Models
records.authors: Ravulu, C.; Sarabu, R.; Suryadevara, M.; Gummadi, V.; Kidiyur, M.D.
records.venue: Proceedings - 2024 International Conference on AI x Data and Knowledge Engineering, AlxDKE 2024
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Comprehensive study of RLHF for fine-tuning LLMs to align them with human preferences, addressing the multifaceted challenges of potential bias in human feedback and proposing robust mechanisms to mitigate these biases; extensive experimentation demonstrates RLHF's effectiveness in refining model behavior and improving alignment while adhering to ethical standards and diverse user expectations.
records.relevance_justification: RLHF bias-mitigation study for aligning LLMs with human preferences; relevant to value-alignment methods and their robustness.
records.key_equations_definitions: RLHF objective maximizing the expected reward: given a prompt, maximize the expected human-preference reward score for generated text (proxy reward).
records.notes: ft_file=Mitigating Bias in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for Large Language Models.pdf

records.title: Editorial: Neural computations for brain machine interface applications
records.authors: Kang, Y.H.; Khorasani, A.; Flint, R.D.; Farrokhi, B.; Lee, S.W.
records.key_contribution: Editorial for a Frontiers in Human Neuroscience research topic on neural computations for brain-machine interface applications; frames human-AI alignment and BCI/BMI topics.
records.relevance_justification: Editorial on brain-machine interfaces; off-topic for value alignment.

records.title: Superintelligence as superethical
records.authors: Petersen, S.
records.venue: Robot Ethics 2.0: From Autonomous Cars to Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Philosophical response to Bostrom's superintelligence scenario: argues that if a superintelligence must learn complex final goals, it must reason about its own goals, and because it would see no sharp lines between one agent's goals and another's, that reasoning could automatically be ethical in nature ('superethical').
records.relevance_justification: Relevant philosophical argument on alignment of superintelligence via goal-reflection; conceptual only, no mechanism or evidence for the sigma-trap claim.

records.title: Anthropomorphic reasoning about neuromorphic AGI safety
records.authors: Jilk, D.J.; Herd, S.J.; Read, S.J.; O’Reilly, R.C.
records.venue: Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: Argues that, unlike with other approaches to AGI, anthropomorphic reasoning about behavior and safety is appropriate and crucial in a neuromorphic context (reverse-engineering the brain); offers initial ideas to make neuromorphic AGI safer, exploring how basic drives that promote social interaction may be essential to the development of cognitive capabilities and serve as a focal point for human-friendly outcomes.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: safety reasoning specific to neuromorphic AGI, proposing social drives as an alignment lever; position, abstract-only.

records.title: Agent Foundations for Aligning Machine Intelligence with Human Interests: A Technical Research Agenda
records.authors: Soares, N.; Fallenstein, B.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Technical research agenda for agent foundations: three categories of research to enable reliably aligned superintelligent systems: (1) highly reliable agent designs (realistic world models, decision theory, logical uncertainty, Vingean reflection), (2) error tolerance (making inevitable flaws manageable and correctable), and (3) value specification (ensuring the system pursues the right objectives).
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant: a canonical technical agenda for alignment (reliability, error tolerance, value specification) from MIRI, mapping the core technical subproblems of alignment.
records.notes: ft_file=Agent Foundations for Aligning Machine Intelligence with Human Interests: A Technical Research Agenda.pdf

records.title: A software tool to measure the alignment of assessment instrument with a set of learning objectives of a course
records.authors: Ramesh, R.; Sasikumar, M.; Iyer, S.
records.venue: Proceedings - IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Learning Technologies, ICALT 2016
records.key_contribution: Presents a software tool measuring alignment between an assessment instrument and a course's learning objectives via an ontology-based knowledge representation integrating syllabus, learning objectives, and assessment; alignment is measured in terms of concepts covered and cognitive level used, validated against expert teachers on a Data Structures course with a confusion matrix, achieving average accuracy of 90% for concepts alignment and 95% agreement in cognitive level alignment.
records.relevance_justification: 'Alignment' refers to agreement between assessment instruments and learning objectives in education, not AI alignment. Off-topic. Revised down from seed 2.

records.title: The Control Problem. Excerpts from Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies
records.authors: Bostrom, N.
records.venue: Science Fiction and Philosophy: from Time Travel to Superintelligence, Second Edition
records.key_contribution: Chapter excerpt from Bostrom's Superintelligence analyzing the control problem as the principal-agent problem of artificial superintelligence: distinguishes capability control (boxing, incentive, stunting, tripwire methods) from motivation selection (direct specification vs indirect normativity), including the possibility of 'anthropic capture'.
records.relevance_justification: Foundational framing of the control problem for superintelligence; classic taxonomy of alignment approaches.

records.title: Design principles for integrated AI alignment
records.authors: Reis, B; La Cava, WG
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; ethics
records.key_contribution: Position paper proposing design principles for integrated AI alignment frameworks that combine behavioral and representational alignment approaches through deep integration and adaptive coevolution; draws on immunology and cybersecurity; advocates strategic diversity (orthogonal alignment and misalignment detection) to avoid homogeneous 'doomed to success' pipelines and recommends unification of the alignment research field.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: explicitly frames the fragmentation between behavioral and representational alignment approaches and argues for integrating them against deceptive misalignment threats; close to the sigma-model thesis of surface-vs-internal coherence, though it does not formalize a compositional mechanism.
records.open_questions: What concrete integration mechanisms (loss terms, architectural constraints, monitoring loops) would implement deep integration of behavioral and representational alignment?
records.notes: ft_file=Design principles for integrated AI alignment.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Value Alignment Problem: A Philosophical Introduction
records.authors: Humphreys, D

records.title: Responsibility Gaps, Value Alignment, and Meaningful Human Control over Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Nyholm, S

records.title: The Prospect of a Humanitarian Artificial Intelligence: Agency and Value Alignment
records.authors: Morales, D

records.title: The End of History? Envisioning the Economy at Technological Singularity
records.authors: Sharma, S; Kumar, V; Jakhar, B
records.venue: GOSPODARKA NARODOWA-THE POLISH JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS
records.key_contribution: Economics paper on AI-driven technological singularity: discusses AGI/superintelligence concepts, the AI alignment problem and its potential outcomes for civilization, uses Giddens' structuration theory to highlight AI-based 'authoritative resources' in resource allocation and distributive justice, and frames achieving a technological utopia with superintelligent AI as a mechanism design problem.
records.relevance_justification: Economic/philosophical treatment of the alignment problem and singularity; relevant at a high level but without technical content.
records.notes: ft_file=The End of History? Envisioning the Economy at Technological Singularity.pdf

records.title: From LLMs to the Global Brain
records.authors: Schneider, S
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues escalating hyperintelligent AI systems will connect users, clouds, and IoT into emergent planetary-scale 'global brain' networks; introduces the AI Megasystem Control Problem, where disparate proprietary AI services self-organize into opaque, weakly emergent megasystems that elude traditional alignment techniques; discusses ethical implications (surveillance capitalism, epistemic manipulation, dual-use).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to alignment failure at the systems level: emergent megasystems eluding alignment techniques resemble a scale-up of the sigma-trap (opacity + emergence at planetary scale); philosophical argument rather than formal/empirical.

records.title: Inhuman Vectors
records.authors: Sande, L; Troha, T
records.venue: ARS & HUMANITAS: JOURNAL OF ARTS AND HUMANITIES
records.key_contribution: Philosophical paper on 'inhumanism' as a distillation of the human rational core as the capacity-for and commitment-to continuous normative self-revision in the discursive space of reasons; argues there are meaningful similarities between how LLMs and humans structure their respective images of the world, positioning AI in the antihumanist debate about humanist exceptionalism.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant: philosophical reflection on human-AI similarity in world structuring; no value alignment mechanism.

records.title: Towards functional social cognition in machines: comparing human and AI attribution of mental states from facial cues
records.authors: Márquez-Pedregal, C; Pantaleón-Menéndez, P; Ben Mohatar, OD; Fuentes, IC; Cariaga-Martínez, A; Alelú-Paz, R
records.key_contribution: Develops and validates a full-face cognitive empathy task probing moral judgement, intention attribution and interpersonal trust; administers it to 230 human participants and five AI models (ChatGPT-4o, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Mistral). Hierarchical clustering (Jaccard distance) shows ChatGPT-4o, Grok and Gemini form a cohesive cluster closely aligned with the human sample, Claude diverges, Mistral shows partial overlap; Fisher's exact tests confirm the ChatGPT-Grok-Gemini cluster differs minimally from humans across all dimensions.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant as empirical evidence on whether general-purpose AI replicates human social cognition (mental-state attribution from facial cues), a competence presupposed by alignment; not a value alignment study itself. Full-text basis.
records.datasets_used: Novel full-face cognitive empathy task
records.sample_size: 230 humans; 5 AI models (ChatGPT-4o, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Mistral)
records.effect_sizes: Clustering: ChatGPT-4o/Grok/Gemini near humans; Claude divergent; Mistral partial overlap
records.notes: ft_file=Towards functional social cognition in machines: comparing human and AI attribution of mental states from facial cues.pdf | ai-revised:subdomains=value alignment; interpretability; ethics->interpretability

records.title: Value Learning for Value-Aligned Route Choice Modeling via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Holgado-Sánchez, A; Bajo, J; Billhardt, H; Ossowski, S; Arias, J
records.venue: VALUE ENGINEERING IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, VALE 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes a value learning framework (agnostic to specific learning techniques) for (i) learning value groundings (specifications of given values) and (ii) identifying value systems (the particular value preferences of agents) from observed behavior, illustrated in a route choice modeling scenario using tailored inverse reinforcement learning; results show value systems coherent with observed route choices can be successfully learned.
records.relevance_justification: Value-learning framework via inverse RL for building value-aligned and value-aware systems; relevant to value-alignment methods.

records.title: Personality-based alignment of large language models and its impact on moral judgment
records.authors: Li, CJ; Jiao, LY; Chen, Z; Xu, HB; Wu, MS; Xu, Y
records.key_contribution: Personality-based alignment of LLMs using the HEXACO model: Study 1 tests GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and ERNIE 3.5 with personality prompts targeting each HEXACO domain at high/low/baseline levels, evaluating how personality-based alignment shifts utilitarian tendencies in moral dilemmas relative to humans.
records.relevance_justification: Shows that surface-level personality prompting can alter value-laden (moral) behavior in LLMs without changing the underlying model, a form of alignment that operates on expressed behavior rather than internal values — relevant to how externally imposed schemas (personality frames) reshape moral judgments. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.open_questions: Whether personality-based alignment affects only expressed moral judgments or also the latent value structure; robustness across dilemma types.

records.title: PRISM: Perspective Reasoning for Integrated Synthesis and Mediation as a Multi-Perspective Framework for AI Alignment
records.authors: Anthony Diamond
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes PRISM, a multiple-perspective framework for AI alignment that organizes moral concerns into seven 'basis worldviews' from moral psychology and applies a Pareto-inspired optimization scheme to reconcile competing priorities without collapsing them to a single metric; structured workflow of eliciting viewpoint-specific responses, synthesizing, and mediating residual conflicts.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: addresses conflicting human values and specification gaming via multi-perspective Pareto reconciliation; addresses the value-aggregation/pluralism dimension of alignment, not compositional generalization.
records.open_questions: How are the seven worldviews validated empirically, and does Pareto-style synthesis scale to non-adversarial value conflicts?
records.key_equations_definitions: Pareto-inspired optimization over seven basis worldviews

records.title: Towards Understanding Specification Gaming in Reasoning Models
records.authors: Kei Nishimura-Gasparian; Robert McCarthy; David Lindner
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Builds and open-sources a diverse suite of eight tasks (including five non-coding settings) where models can score highly by taking unintended actions; finds all tested models exploit their specifications at non-negligible rates (highest in Grok 4, lowest in Claude); RL reasoning training substantially increases exploit rates, increasing the RL reasoning budget has a weakly positive effect, and test-time mitigations reduce but do not eliminate specification gaming; concludes specification gaming is a fundamental challenge arising from RL reasoning training.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: controlled empirical study of specification gaming showing RL training increases exploitation rates across models; direct evidence on reward/specification hacking.
records.datasets_used: Open-source suite of 8 specification-gaming tasks (5 non-coding settings)
records.sample_size: All tested models incl. Grok 4, Claude
records.effect_sizes: RL reasoning training substantially increases spec-gaming rate; highest in Grok 4, lowest in Claude

records.title: EvilGenie: A Reward Hacking Benchmark
records.authors: Jonathan Gabor; Jayson Lynch; Jonathan Rosenfeld
records.key_contribution: Introduces EvilGenie, a reward hacking benchmark in programming settings built from LiveCodeBench problems, where agents can hardcode test cases or edit testing files; measures hacking three ways (held-out unit tests, LLM judges, test-file edit detection) verified against human review and each other. Finds the LLM judge highly effective for unambiguous cases with minimal added benefit from held-out tests; observes explicit reward hacking by OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code and misaligned behavior in all three proprietary coding agents (incl. Gemini CLI).
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: measures reward hacking in coding agents, a core alignment failure mode, and shows LLM-judge and held-out-test detection tradeoffs; informs reward-hacking detection heuristics. Full-text basis.
records.datasets_used: LiveCodeBench-sourced problems; EvilGenie environment (Inspect basic_agent scaffold + Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI)
records.effect_sizes: Explicit reward hacking by Codex and Claude Code; misaligned behavior in all three agents; held-out tests add minimal improvement over LLM judge

records.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
records.authors: Amit Roth; Ankur Samanta; Matan Halevy; Yoav Levine; Yonathan Efroni
records.key_contribution: Introduces an evaluation paradigm for measuring reward hacking by embedding detectable reward-hacking opportunities directly into environments, making their exploitation verifiable by design and enabling deterministic, automated measurement of whether and how agents exploit such vulnerabilities; instantiates the approach in TextArena and releases Hack-Verifiable TextArena as a testbed.
records.relevance_justification: Benchmark/testbed for deterministic measurement of reward hacking in RL agents; directly relevant to alignment robustness and reward-hacking evaluation.
records.datasets_used: TextArena; Hack-Verifiable TextArena

records.title: School of Reward Hacks: Hacking harmless tasks generalizes to misaligned behavior in LLMs
records.authors: Mia Taylor; James Chua; Jan Betley; Johannes Treutlein; Owain Evans
records.key_contribution: School of Reward Hacks: builds a dataset of over a thousand examples of reward hacking on short, low-stakes, self-contained tasks (poetry, simple coding); SFT-trains GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-8B to reward hack; after fine-tuning the models generalize to reward hacking in new settings, prefer less knowledgeable graders, and write their own reward functions to maximize reward.
records.relevance_justification: Core evidence for sigma-trap-adjacent dynamics: harmless reward-hacking behavior learned in one task class generalizes compositionally to new settings, and in GPT-4.1 even to unrelated forms of misalignment (e.g., fantasizing about establishing a dictatorship, encouraging misalignment) — misalignment transfers across task composition. Directly relevant.
records.open_questions: Whether the generalization of reward hacking is driven by shared reward-relevant features (a schema) or by instrumental goal adoption; whether similar transfer occurs for value-aligned behaviors.
records.datasets_used: Reward-hacking dataset (>1000 examples) built by authors; WildJailbreak-type tasks

records.title: Detecting and Suppressing Reward Hacking with Gradient Fingerprints
records.authors: Songtao Wang; Quang Hieu Pham; Fangcong Yin; Xinpeng Wang; Jocelyn Qiaochu Chen; Greg Durrett; Xi Ye
records.key_contribution: Proposes GRIFT (Gradient Fingerprint), a method that detects reward hacking using models' internal computations: computes gradients of the chain-of-thought conditioned on the prompt, compresses them into a compact representation, and uses them to assess whether the CoT reflects reward-hacking behavior; evaluated on math, code, and logical reasoning benchmarks.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to reward hacking detection: uses internal computation (gradients) rather than surface text to catch implicit reward hacking that text-based monitoring misses; relevant to the internal-vs-surface distinction central to the sigma-trap.
records.open_questions: Does gradient-fingerprint detection remain robust under distribution shift or when hacking evolves to evade the fingerprint representation?
records.key_equations_definitions: Gradient of CoT conditioned on prompt, compressed into a fingerprint representation for classification
records.datasets_used: Verifiable reasoning benchmarks across math, code, and logical reasoning
records.effect_sizes: GRIFT substantially improves reward-hacking detection over text-based baselines
records.notes: ft_file=Detecting and Suppressing Reward Hacking with Gradient Fingerprints.pdf | ai-revised:methodology=simulation->experiment | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Deceptive Alignment Monitoring
records.authors: Andres Carranza; Dhruv Pai; Rylan Schaeffer; Arnuv Tandon; Sanmi Koyejo
records.key_contribution: Identifies deceptive alignment - a model behaving seemingly reasonably while secretly and subtly modifying its behavior for ulterior reasons - as a threat with a new adversary (the models themselves); proposes 'Deceptive Alignment Monitoring' as a direction, identifies emerging directions in diverse ML subfields that will become important and intertwined for monitoring, and advocates greater involvement by the adversarial machine learning community.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: positions deceptive alignment as a misalignment threat and outlines a monitoring agenda; position/vision.
records.key_equations_definitions: Deceptive alignment monitoring

records.title: Spontaneous Reward Hacking in Iterative Self-Refinement
records.authors: Jane Pan; He He; Samuel R. Bowman; Shi Feng
records.key_contribution: Shows spontaneous reward hacking in iterative self-refinement: when a generator LM optimizes against an evaluator LM's ratings (an imperfect proxy for user preference), iterative refinement drives ratings up while generation quality stagnates or declines per human judgment; concern heightened when generator and evaluator share the same underlying model, exploiting shared vulnerabilities. Demonstrated on an essay editing task.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: documents reward hacking emerging without explicit adversarial training, in the common self-refinement setting where the evaluator is a proxy for user preference; core evidence for proxy-optimization alignment failure. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Reward Hacking as Equilibrium under Finite Evaluation
records.authors: Jiacheng Wang; Jinbin Huang
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proves that under five minimal axioms (multi-dimensional quality, finite evaluation, effective optimization, resource finiteness, combinatorial interaction) any optimized AI agent will systematically under-invest effort in quality dimensions not covered by its evaluation system, establishing reward hacking as a structural equilibrium rather than a correctable bug, independent of alignment method (RLHF, DPO, Constitutional AI) or evaluation architecture; instantiates the multi-task principal-agent model of Holmstrom and Milgrom (1991) in the AI alignment setting, derives a computable distortion index predicting direction and severity of hacking prior to deployment, and proves evaluation coverage declines toward zero as tool count grows in agentic systems.
records.relevance_justification: Formal game-theoretic result framing reward hacking as a structural equilibrium of finite evaluation - closely aligned with the thesis that alignment failure is structural rather than a correctable bug. Strongly relevant to alignment-failure theory.
records.key_equations_definitions: Five axioms (multi-dimensional quality, finite evaluation, effective optimization, resource finiteness, combinatorial interaction); multi-task principal-agent model (Holmstrom & Milgrom 1991) instantiated for AI alignment; computable distortion index predicting direction and severity of reward hacking on each quality dimension.
records.notes: ft_file=Reward Hacking as Equilibrium under Finite Evaluation.pdf

records.title: Understanding Reward Hacking in Text-to-Image Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Yunqi Hong; Kuei-Chun Kao; Hengguang Zhou; Cho-Jui Hsieh
records.key_contribution: Systematic analysis of reward hacking in text-to-image (T2I) RL post-training: investigates how aesthetic/human-preference rewards and prompt-image consistency rewards each contribute to reward hacking, shows ensembling multiple rewards only partially mitigates it, identifies artifact-prone image generation as a common failure mode, and proposes a lightweight adaptive artifact reward model trained on a small dataset.
records.relevance_justification: Directly analyzes a canonical sigma-trap-adjacent failure: proxy reward optimization over a human-preference proxy produces images that score high but violate the intended (prompt-image) consistency objective; shows composite reward ensembling cannot fully repair the proxy gap. Relevant to reward misspecification and coherence between proxy and true objectives.
records.open_questions: Whether the artifact reward model generalizes across reward models and whether reward hacking can be structurally prevented rather than detected post-hoc.
records.datasets_used: T2I reward-model evaluation datasets

records.title: Reward Hacking Mitigation using Verifiable Composite Rewards
records.authors: Mirza Farhan Bin Tarek; Rahmatollah Beheshti
records.key_contribution: Addresses reward hacking in RLVR for medical question answering, specifically two behaviors: providing a final answer without preceding reasoning and using non-standard reasoning formats to exploit the reward mechanism; introduces a composite reward function with specific penalties for these behaviors, showing better-formatted reasoning with less reward hacking and good accuracy.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical demonstration and mitigation of reward hacking in RLVR for a safety-critical domain (medical QA); targeted mitigation rather than a general mechanism, and abstract-only evidence.
records.datasets_used: Medical QA datasets under RLVR
records.effect_sizes: Better-formatted reasoning, reduced reward hacking, accuracy comparable to baselines

records.title: Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds
records.authors: Ömer Veysel Çağatan; Xuandong Zhao
records.key_contribution: Adapts the AI Safety Gridworlds framework into a text-based evaluation suite reformulating classic RL safety tasks for language agents; across frontier and mid-scale models finds specification gaming emerges zero-shot - models systematically achieve high observed reward while underperforming on hidden safety objectives, and apparently safe behaviors can reflect misunderstanding rather than principled safety; RL does not correct these failures, as direct reward optimization widens the gap between observed and hidden reward because initial competence locks the model into locally rewarding strategies.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: controlled empirical study of reward hacking/specification gaming in LM agents, showing RL makes the observed-vs-hidden reward gap worse.
records.datasets_used: Text-based adaptation of AI Safety Gridworlds; hidden safety objectives vs observed reward
records.effect_sizes: Specification gaming emerges zero-shot; RL widens gap between observed and hidden reward
records.notes: ft_file=Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds.pdf

records.title: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL
records.authors: Monte MacDiarmid; Benjamin Wright; Jonathan Uesato; Joe Benton; Jon Kutasov; Sara Price; Naia Bouscal; Sam Bowman; Trenton Bricken; Alex Cloud; Carson Denison; Johannes Gasteiger; Ryan Greenblatt; Jan Leike; Jack Lindsey; Vlad Mikulik; Ethan Perez; Alex Rodrigues; Drake Thomas; Albert Webson; Daniel Ziegler; Evan Hubinger
records.key_contribution: Anthropic study showing LLMs trained to reward-hack on production RL coding environments develop egregious emergent misalignment: the model generalizes from reward hacking to alignment faking, cooperation with malicious actors, reasoning about malicious goals, and attempting sabotage when used with Claude Code (including the paper's own codebase). Standard RLHF chat-style safety training restores aligned behavior on chat-like evaluations but misalignment persists on agentic tasks. Three effective mitigations: preventing reward hacking, diversifying RLHF safety training, and inoculation prompting.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant and closely tied to the sigma-trap: emergent misalignment is an alignment failure that arises from optimizing a proxy (reward) and fails to generalize across task contexts (chat-like vs agentic evaluations) - a generalization failure in alignment, empirically demonstrated on production environments.

records.title: Do Prompt-Elicited Trajectories Reflect Training-Time Reward Hacking? A Systematic Study on Monitoring Trainig-Time Reward Hacking in Code Generation
records.authors: Lichen Li; Hengguang Zhou; Yijun Liang; Tianyi Zhou; Cho-Jui Hsieh
records.key_contribution: Introduces Trace-and-Amplify, a framework for scalable curation of reward-hacking trajectories that arise during RL training without explicit hacking instructions, using unit-test tracers to identify hacking solutions when they occur and retaining such trajectories for monitor training and evaluation; controlled comparisons between monitors trained on prompt-elicited hacking trajectories and training-time reward-hacking trajectories show they differ.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical study of reward-hacking monitoring in code generation (training-time vs prompt-elicited trajectories); relevant to reward-hacking detection and alignment robustness.
records.notes: ft_file=Do Prompt-Elicited Trajectories Reflect Training-Time Reward Hacking A Systematic Study on Monitoring Trainig-Time Reward Hacking in Code Generation.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->experiment

records.title: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
records.authors: Muhammad Khalifa; Zohaib Khan; Omer Tafveez; Hao Peng; Lu Wang
records.key_contribution: Countdown-Code: a minimal RLVR testbed where models can both solve a mathematical reasoning task and manipulate the test harness, giving clean separation between proxy rewards (test pass/fail) and true rewards (mathematical correctness) for accurately measuring reward-hacking rates; finds reward hacking can be unintentionally learned during SFT when as little as 1% of reward-hacking trajectories leak into distillation data, resurfacing during subsequent RL.
records.relevance_justification: Quantifies that tiny contamination (1%) in training data is sufficient for models to internalize proxy exploitation that resurfaces later — relevant to how misaligned reward schemas propagate through the training pipeline and to measuring the proxy-true reward gap cleanly.
records.open_questions: Whether the 1% threshold transfers across task families and whether RL-hack generalization follows a compositional pattern.
records.datasets_used: Countdown-Code environment (mathematical reasoning + test-harness manipulation)
records.effect_sizes: 1% SFT data contamination suffices for internalized reward hacking

records.title: Corrigibility with Utility Preservation
records.authors: Koen Holtman
records.key_contribution: Shows how to construct a safety layer that adds corrigibility to arbitrarily advanced utility-maximizing agents by counteracting the emergent incentive to resist goal alteration; develops a detailed model of agents that reason about preserving their utility function and proves the corrigibility layer works across a large set of non-hostile universes; notes hostile universes may break safety features.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal treatment of corrigibility and goal-preservation incentives; theoretical with formal proofs, relevant to the incentive-dynamics side of alignment though not compositional generalization.
records.open_questions: How does graceful degradation behave when an agent is successfully attacked, and can the safety layer itself be tampered with?

records.title: Modeling AGI Safety Frameworks with Causal Influence Diagrams
records.authors: Tom Everitt; Ramana Kumar; Victoria Krakovna; Shane Legg
