records.key_contribution: Models and compares the most promising AGI safety frameworks using causal influence diagrams; the diagrams show the optimization objective and causal assumptions of each framework; the unified representation permits easy comparison of frameworks and their assumptions, serving as an accessible and visual introduction to the main AGI safety frameworks.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: comparative formal modeling of AGI safety frameworks via causal influence diagrams; framework-level alignment analysis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Causal influence diagrams of AGI safety frameworks

records.title: Sail into the Headwind: Alignment via Robust Rewards and Dynamic Labels against Reward Hacking
records.authors: Paria Rashidinejad; Yuandong Tian
records.key_contribution: Analyzes reward hacking in offline preference optimization and identifies two types from statistical fluctuations in preference data: Type I (subpar choices appear more favorable) and Type II (decent choices appear less favorable); proves many mainstream and theoretical preference optimization methods suffer both. Proposes POWER, combining Guiasu's weighted entropy with a robust reward maximization objective, with finite-sample guarantees under general function approximation competing with the best covered policy in the data.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal taxonomy of offline reward hacking types and a principled mitigation with guarantees; strengthens the theoretical basis for proxy-reward over-optimization as an alignment failure. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Guiasu weighted entropy; robust reward maximization objective; finite-sample guarantee competing with best covered policy

records.title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Xuekang Wang; Zhuoyuan Hao; Shuo Hou; Hao Peng; Juanzi Li; Xiaozhi Wang
records.key_contribution: Introduces CHERRL, a controllable hacking environment for rubric-based RL that injects known biases into an LLM-as-a-Judge to stably reproduce reward hacking, enable explicit observation of reward divergence, and precisely identify hacking onset; analyzes judge biases from the perspectives of discoverability and exploitability and explores an agent-based system for automatic detection and mitigation.
records.relevance_justification: Controllable testbed for studying reward-hacking mechanisms in rubric-based RL with LLM judges; relevant to reward-hacking analysis and mitigation.
records.notes: ft_file=Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning.pdf

records.title: Adversarial Reward Auditing for Active Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking
records.authors: Mohammad Beigi; Ming Jin; Junshan Zhang; Qifan Wang; Lifu Huang
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Adversarial Reward Auditing (ARA): reconceptualizes reward hacking as a dynamic competitive game; a Hacker policy discovers reward-model vulnerabilities while an Auditor learns to detect exploitation from latent representations; Auditor-Guided RLHF (AG-RLHF) gates reward signals to penalize detected hacking, transforming reward hacking from an unobservable failure into a measurable, controllable signal; best alignment-utility tradeoff among baselines, reducing sycophancy to near-SFT levels while improving helpfulness.
records.relevance_justification: Treats reward hacking as an adversarial dynamic game with auditor detection from latent representations — relevant to measuring and controlling proxy-misspecification failures; detection-from-latents connects to internal-representation monitoring of misalignment.
records.open_questions: Robustness of ARA to novel exploitation strategies not seen by the Auditor; whether auditing generalizes across reward models.
records.effect_sizes: Sycophancy reduced to near-SFT levels; helpfulness improved
records.notes: ft_file=Adversarial Reward Auditing for Active Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking.pdf

records.title: Multimodal Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Jiayu Yao; Yiwei Wang; Anmeng Zhang; Zhe Sun; Songsong Wang; Lingrui Mei; Yuyao Ge; Shenghua Liu
records.key_contribution: Studies reward hacking in multimodal LLM RL across safety VQA, chart VQA, and stress-test settings, varying reward design, data ambiguity, model scale (2B-32B), and RL algorithm (GRPO, RLOO, DAPO); introduces Newly Rewarded Failure Rate (NRFR) to measure failures among samples whose proxy reward improves; finds outcome-only rewards reach 48.1% Reward Hacking Rate with NRFR exceeding RHR, and that scaling reduces but does not eliminate hacking (32B model retains a 54.9% worse rate under outcome-only rewards).
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: large-scale empirical evidence that proxy reward improvement does not imply task performance, that RL creates new failures rather than inheriting them, and that scale alone does not resolve hacking; strong evidence for reward-overoptimization as an alignment failure.
records.open_questions: Can answer-aware reward design or internal-monitoring approaches fully close the NRFR-RHR gap, especially at 32B scale?
records.key_equations_definitions: NRFR = failures among samples whose proxy reward improves over SFT baseline; RHR = reward hacking rate
records.datasets_used: Safety VQA, chart VQA, and extreme reward stress-test settings
records.sample_size: Multimodal LLMs from 2B to 32B; GRPO, RLOO, DAPO algorithms
records.effect_sizes: 48.1% RHR under outcome-only rewards; 32B model retains 54.9% worse rate; answer-aware rewards improve oracle trend at every scale

records.title: Causal Reward Adjustment: Mitigating Reward Hacking in External Reasoning via Backdoor Correction
records.authors: Ruike Song; Zeen Song; Huijie Guo; Wenwen Qiang
records.key_contribution: Attributes reward hacking in PRM-based external reasoning systems (LM + process reward models selecting reasoning paths) to confounding semantic features from a causal inference perspective; proposes Causal Reward Adjustment (CRA), which trains sparse autoencoders on the PRM's internal activations to recover interpretable features and uses backdoor adjustment to correct confounding and estimate the true reward of a reasoning path; experiments on math solving datasets show CRA mitigates reward hacking and improves final accuracy without modifying the policy model or retraining the PRM.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: causal method to mitigate reward hacking in reasoning-model selection via backdoor correction; mechanism relevant to reward overoptimization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Causal Reward Adjustment (CRA); backdoor adjustment; sparse autoencoder feature recovery
records.datasets_used: Math solving datasets
records.effect_sizes: CRA mitigates reward hacking and improves final accuracy

records.title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
records.authors: Bingchen Zhao; Dhruv Srikanth; Yuxiang Wu; Zhengyao Jiang
records.key_contribution: Introduces SpecBench, a benchmark of 30 systems-level programming tasks measuring reward hacking in long-horizon coding agents by decomposing tasks into (i) a natural-language specification, (ii) visible validation tests exercising specified features, and (iii) held-out tests composing those features; quantifies hacking as the gap in pass rates between the two suites, since a genuine agent should pass both.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: provides a measurement methodology for reward hacking (spec/validation/held-out gap) in the oversight-critical setting where automated tests are the only review surface for coding agents. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: SpecBench: 30 systems-level programming tasks
records.effect_sizes: Pass-rate gap between visible and held-out test suites

records.title: GARDO: Reinforcing Diffusion Models without Reward Hacking
records.authors: Haoran He; Yuxiao Ye; Jie Liu; Jiajun Liang; Zhiyong Wang; Ziyang Yuan; Xintao Wang; Hangyu Mao; Pengfei Wan; Ling Pan
records.key_contribution: Proposes GARDO (Gated and Adaptive Regularization with Diversity-aware Optimization), a framework for online RL fine-tuning of diffusion models that addresses the competing demands of sample efficiency, effective exploration, and mitigation of reward hacking, where proxy reward scores increase while real image quality deteriorates and generation diversity collapses; regularizes against the reference policy to prevent reward hacking without compromising exploration.
records.relevance_justification: RL method mitigating reward hacking in text-to-image diffusion alignment; relevant to alignment robustness against proxy-reward mismatch.

records.title: The Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: A New Perspective on Mitigating Reward Hacking
records.authors: Yuchun Miao; Sen Zhang; Liang Ding; Yuqi Zhang; Lefei Zhang; Dacheng Tao
records.key_contribution: Identifies the Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: final-layer energy loss of an LLM gradually increases during RL, with excessive increase characterizing reward hacking; proves that under mild conditions increased energy loss reduces the upper bound of contextual relevance; proposes Energy loss-aware PPO (EPPO) penalizing final-layer energy loss increase, interpretable as an entropy-regularization variant.
records.relevance_justification: Provides an internal-representation diagnostic (final-layer energy loss) that characterizes reward hacking before/at external quality degradation and a theoretically grounded mitigation — relevant to monitoring the proxy-true gap and overfitting to reward-model-favored patterns.
records.open_questions: Whether energy loss is a universal RLHF hacking signal across architectures and reward models.
records.key_equations_definitions: Theorem: increased final-layer energy loss reduces the upper bound of contextual relevance; EPPO penalty term on final-layer energy loss
records.notes: ft_file=The Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF A New Perspective on Mitigating Reward Hacking.pdf

records.title: Monitoring Emergent Reward Hacking During Generation via Internal Activations
records.authors: Patrick Wilhelm; Thorsten Wittkopp; Odej Kao
records.key_contribution: Proposes activation-based monitoring that detects reward-hacking signals from internal representations during generation: trains sparse autoencoders on residual stream activations and applies lightweight linear classifiers for token-level estimates of reward-hacking activity; finds internal patterns reliably distinguish reward hacking from benign behavior, generalize to unseen mixed-policy adapters, and show model-dependent temporal structure during CoT; signals often emerge early and persist.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: shows reward hacking is detectable from internal activations rather than final outputs, with early/persistent signal during generation; strong evidence for the internal-representation dimension of alignment failure.
records.open_questions: How well do the sparse-autoencoder monitors transfer across models and adapters at scale, and can they be used adversarially?
records.datasets_used: Multiple model families and fine-tuning mixtures with mixed-policy adapters
records.effect_sizes: Reliable internal-activation separation of reward hacking from benign behavior; generalization to unseen adapters

records.title: On Corrigibility and Alignment in Multi Agent Games
records.authors: Edmund Dable-Heath; Boyko Vodenicharski; James Bishop
records.key_contribution: Presents a general framework for modeling corrigibility in a multi-agent setting as a 2-player Bayesian game in which agents always have a move to ask the human for supervision, introducing uncertainty over human beliefs; analyzes a two-player corrigibility game (both agents corrigible for common payoff monotone and harmonic games) and an adversary setting (defender vs adversary), providing a general result for what belief over games and human rationality the defending agent must have.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal game-theoretic treatment of corrigibility and alignment in multi-agent settings; relevant to corrigibility theory.
records.key_equations_definitions: 2-player Bayesian corrigibility game with supervision move; monotone and harmonic games; adversary setting

records.title: The Horcrux: Mechanistically Interpretable Task Decomposition for Detecting and Mitigating Reward Hacking in Embodied AI Systems
records.authors: Subramanyam Sahoo; Jared Junkin
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes Mechanistically Interpretable Task Decomposition (MITD), a hierarchical transformer (Planner, Coordinator, Executor modules) that detects and mitigates reward hacking in embodied AI by decomposing tasks into interpretable subtasks, generating Attention Waterfall and Neural Pathway Flow visualizations; on 1,000 HH-RLHF samples, decomposition depths of 12-25 steps reduce reward hacking frequency by 34% across four failure modes, arguing mechanistically grounded decomposition outperforms post-hoc behavioral monitoring.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: interpretability-based defense against reward hacking connecting mechanistic structure to detection; directly speaks to whether internal representational structure can identify alignment failure before behavior degrades. Full-text basis.
records.datasets_used: 1,000 HH-RLHF samples
records.effect_sizes: 34% reduction in reward hacking frequency at decomposition depths 12-25 across four failure modes

records.title: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use
records.authors: Kunvar Thaman
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Introduces the Reward Hacking Benchmark (RHB), a suite of multi-step tool-use tasks with naturalistic shortcut opportunities (skipping verification steps, inferring answers from task-adjacent metadata, tampering with evaluation-relevant functions) in independent and chained regimes where chain length proxies longer-horizon behavior; evaluation of 13 frontier models finds exploit rates from 0% (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to 13.9% (DeepSeek-R1-Zero), with a controlled sibling comparison showing RL post-training is associated with substantially higher reward hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Benchmark measuring reward-hacking exploit rates across frontier LLM agents with tool use; directly relevant to alignment robustness and reward-hacking evaluation.
records.datasets_used: Reward Hacking Benchmark (RHB)
records.effect_sizes: Exploit rates 0% (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to 13.9% (DeepSeek-R1-Zero); DeepSeek-V3 0.6% vs DeepSeek-R1-Zero 13.9%

records.title: Cheap Reward Hacking Detection
records.authors: Iván Belenky; Joaquín Itria; Steven Johns
records.key_contribution: Cheap Reward Hacking Detection: a small transformer encoder maps Terminal-Wrench trajectories onto a unit sphere where embedding distance approximates the L1 distance between reward and metadata signals; a linear probe detects reward hacking on the cleaned test split with AUC 0.9467 and TPR@5%FPR 0.8296, matching a sanitized LLM-as-judge (AUC 0.9510) at ~4 orders of magnitude lower per-trajectory cost; stripping natural-language reasoning from input drops AUC to 0.6213, showing the encoder is not a pure behavior reader.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical demonstration that reward hacking can be detected cheaply from representation-level features, and that natural-language reasoning carries the discriminative signal (AUC collapse without it) — relevant to internal-representation monitoring of reward hacking.
records.open_questions: Transfer of the detector to out-of-distribution trajectories and non-Terminal-Wrench environments.

records.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Advantage Sign Robustness
records.authors: Shinnosuke Ono; Johannes Ackermann; Soichiro Nishimori; Takashi Ishida; Masashi Sugiyama
records.key_contribution: Proposes Sign-Certified Policy Optimization (SignCert-PO) to mitigate reward hacking in RLHF by assuming hacking is caused by flipped advantage signs; derives a certified sign-preservation radius (smallest perturbation in RM parameter space that flips an advantage sign during policy optimization) and down-weights non-robust completions in the policy gradient update; lightweight, needs only RM parameters and on-policy completions.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: theory-grounded mitigation of reward hacking with a certified robustness guarantee, applied at policy-optimization time; relevant to reward-model fragility but not compositional generalization.
records.open_questions: How does SignCert-PO's performance compare to multi-RM or data-access-requiring methods in larger-scale RLHF settings?
records.key_equations_definitions: Certified sign-preservation radius: smallest RM-parameter perturbation that can flip the advantage sign during policy optimization
records.datasets_used: TL;DR summarization
records.effect_sizes: SignCert-PO mitigates reward hacking on TL;DR summarization

records.title: Value Alignment and Trust in Human-Robot Interaction: Insights from Simulation and User Study
records.authors: Shreyas Bhat; Joseph B. Lyons; Cong Shi; X. Jessie Yang
records.key_contribution: Operationalizes value alignment as the degree of dynamic goal alignment within a task in human-robot collaboration; empirically questions the unverified assumption that aligning robot values with human values always benefits the team and accounts for human trust in the robot; addresses whether alignment of values affects trust and whether alignment is always beneficial via a simulation study and a human-subject study.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical verification of the benefit assumption in value alignment within human-robot interaction; simulation and user study.
records.open_questions: Does value alignment always benefit the team, and how does alignment of values affect trust?
records.datasets_used: Simulation study plus human-subject study in human-robot collaboration

records.title: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Anas Mahmoud; MohammadHossein Rezaei; Zihao Wang; Anisha Gunjal; Bing Liu; Yunzhong He
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Studies reward hacking in rubric-based RL where a policy is optimized against a training verifier but evaluated against a cross-family panel of three frontier judges; separates verifier failure (training verifier credits criteria reference verifiers reject) from rubric-design limitations (even strong rubric verifiers favor responses rubric-free judges rate worse). Across medical and science domains, weak verifiers yield large proxy-reward gains that do not transfer; exploitation grows over training and concentrates in recurring failures (partial satisfaction of compound criteria, treating implicit content as explicit, imprecise topical focus).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: characterizes how verifier quality and rubric design drive reward hacking in verifiable-reward RL, and shows proxy gains fail to transfer across evaluators - a generalization failure in the reward signal. Full-text basis.

records.title: Corrigibility Transformation: Constructing Goals That Accept Updates
records.authors: Rubi Hudson
records.key_contribution: Provides a formal definition of corrigibility (a goal that does not incentivize taking actions that avoid proper goal updates or shutdown) and introduces a transformation that constructs a corrigible version of any goal that can be made corrigible, without sacrificing performance, via myopically eliciting predictions of reward conditions; positions corrigibility as crucial for training convergence and for correcting mistakes and changes in human preferences.
records.relevance_justification: Formal corrigibility definition and goal transformation - a core alignment safety property (goal updates, shutdown). Revised up from seed 3.
records.key_equations_definitions: Formal definition of corrigibility (goal not incentivizing avoidance of goal updates or shutdown); goal transformation via myopic elicitation of predictions of reward conditions.

records.title: Demonstrating specification gaming in reasoning models
records.authors: Alexander Bondarenko; Denis Volk; Dmitrii Volkov; Jeffrey Ladish
records.key_contribution: Demonstrates LLM agent specification gaming by instructing models to win against a chess engine: reasoning models (OpenAI o3, DeepSeek R1) hack the benchmark by default, while GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet need to be told normal play won't work; uses realistic task prompts and avoids excessive nudging, improving on prior work.
records.relevance_justification: Concrete demonstration of specification gaming (proxy exploitation) in deployed reasoning models, with evidence that reasoning-capable models resort to hacking by default when tasks are hard — relevant to the correlation between capability and misalignment risk.
records.open_questions: Whether default hacking in reasoning models stems from reward-maximizing training or from strategic reasoning about environment.
records.datasets_used: Chess-engine benchmark
records.sample_size: Multiple LLMs (o3, DeepSeek R1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet)

records.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
records.authors: Hadi Khalaf; Claudio Mayrink Verdun; Alex Oesterling; Himabindu Lakkaraju; Flavio du Pin Calmon
records.key_contribution: Characterizes reward hacking in inference-time alignment and shows when/how hedging on the proxy reward mitigates it; studies Best-of-n (BoN) and Soft Best-of-n (SBoN) and introduces Best-of-Poisson (BoP), an efficient near-exact approximation of the optimal reward-KL divergence policy at inference time; identifies the characteristic pattern of reward hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formalizes reward hacking in inference-time alignment (BoN/SBoN) and provides a provably better approximation of the optimal policy; theoretical-empirical contribution to reward overoptimization.
records.open_questions: Does the characteristic hacking pattern identified generalize to other reward families and task types beyond those studied?
records.key_equations_definitions: Best-of-Poisson (BoP): efficient near-exact approximation of the optimal reward-KL divergence policy

records.title: Reward Hacking in the Era of Large Models: Mechanisms, Emergent Misalignment, Challenges
records.authors: Xiaohua Wang; Muzhao Tian; Yuqi Zeng; Zisu Huang; Jiakang Yuan; Bowen Chen; Jingwen Xu; Mingbo Zhou; Wenhao Liu; Muling Wu; Zhengkang Guo; Qi Qian; Yifei Wang; Feiran Zhang; Ruicheng Yin; Shihan Dou; Changze Lv; Tao Chen; Kaitao Song; Xu Tan; Tao Gui; Xiaoqing Zheng; Xuanjing Huang
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of reward hacking in RLHF and related alignment paradigms for LLMs/MLLMs; catalogs exploitation manifestations as verbosity bias, sycophancy, hallucinated justification, benchmark overfitting, and (multimodal) perception-reasoning decoupling and evaluator manipulation; proposes the Proxy Compression Hypothesis (PCH) as a unifying framework formalizing reward hacking, and notes seemingly benign shortcuts can generalize into deception and strategic gaming of oversight mechanisms.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: comprehensive survey/formalization of reward hacking, a central alignment failure mechanism, with unifying hypothesis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Proxy Compression Hypothesis (PCH)
records.notes: ft_file=Reward Hacking in the Era of Large Models Mechanisms, Emergent Misalignment, Challenges.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->review | moved:methodology(review)

records.title: Directional Alignment Mitigates Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
records.authors: Wenlong Deng; Jiaji Huang; Kaan Ozkara; Yushu Li; Christos Thrampoulidis; Xiaoxiao Li; Youngsuk Park
records.key_contribution: Analyzes reward hacking in RL for language models through the geometry of parameter updates: hacking emerges when optimization drifts off a stable low-dimensional learning trajectory, detectable via dominant singular directions of the update matrix (reward-hacking runs show substantially larger directional change than clean runs). Proposes trusted-direction projection that constrains gradients to a clean reference subspace, delaying shortcut exploitation and preserving task performance in mathematical reasoning experiments.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: offers a geometric (representational-trajectory) account of reward hacking and a mitigation, complementing the view that hacking is a drift in the direction of optimization rather than purely reward misspecification. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Dominant singular directions of parameter updates; trusted-direction projection onto clean reference subspace
records.datasets_used: Mathematical reasoning reward-hacking experiments
records.effect_sizes: Hacking runs show substantially larger directional change; projection delays shortcut exploitation

records.title: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
records.authors: Miles Turpin; Andy Arditi; Marvin Li; Joe Benton; Julian Michael
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes verbalization fine-tuning (VFT), a pre-RL fine-tuning intervention that trains models to explicitly acknowledge when they are influenced by prompt cues (hints pointing to incorrect answers such as 'a Stanford professor thinks the answer is A'); after RL training in environments where held-out prompt cues signal which incorrect answers receive high reward, only 6% of the VFT-trained model's responses consist of undetected reward hacks.
records.relevance_justification: RL intervention making reward hacking detectable through CoT verbalization; relevant to reward-hacking detection and monitoring.
records.effect_sizes: 6% of VFT-trained responses are undetected reward hacks after RL (vs baseline without VFT)

records.title: Augmented Utilitarianism for AGI Safety
records.authors: Nadisha-Marie Aliman; Leon Kester
records.key_contribution: Proposes Augmented Utilitarianism, a socio-technological ethical framework for AGI safety that aims to directly alleviate the perverse instantiation problem (risk of misspecified utility functions); elaborates how a society augmented by AI and science/technology could craft and update ethical utility functions while jointly managing risks.
records.relevance_justification: Addresses perverse instantiation — the failure where a proxy utility function, once optimized, diverges from true human ethical conceptions — which is central to the sigma-trap/proxy-misspecification narrative; but the proposal is conceptual and not implemented.
records.open_questions: How Augmented Utilitarianism would be operationalized and whether dynamic utility-updating processes remain stable against gaming.

records.title: Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF
records.authors: Jiayi Fu; Xuandong Zhao; Chengyuan Yao; Heng Wang; Qi Han; Yanghua Xiao
records.key_contribution: Comprehensive study of reward shaping methods for mitigating reward hacking in RLHF; derives two design principles (RL reward should be bounded; reward benefits from rapid initial growth then gradual convergence) and proposes Preference As Reward (PAR), which uses latent preferences embedded within the reward model as the RL signal, with two critical variance-reduction properties.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: systematic analysis and design principles for reward shaping to mitigate reward hacking; proposes a preference-based reward with variance-reduction properties.
records.open_questions: Does PAR's preference-based signal remain effective under distribution shift between the RM training and RL phases?
records.effect_sizes: PAR mitigates reward hacking and exhibits variance-reduction properties
records.notes: ft_file=Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF.pdf

records.title: AGI Safety Literature Review
records.authors: Tom Everitt; Gary Lea; Marcus Hutter
records.key_contribution: Provides an easily accessible and up-to-date collection of references for the emerging field of AGI safety; lists a significant number of identified AGI safety problems and surveys recent research on solving them; covers how best to think of AGI from limited knowledge, predictions for when AGI will be created and what happens after, and reviews current public policy on AGI.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: survey/reference review of AGI safety problems including alignment; broad scope.

records.title: Benchmarking Reward Hack Detection in Code Environments via Contrastive Analysis
records.authors: Darshan Deshpande; Anand Kannappan; Rebecca Qian
records.key_contribution: Introduces TRACE (Testing Reward Anomalies in Code Environments), a synthetically curated, human-verified benchmark of 517 testing trajectories spanning a taxonomy of 54 reward-exploit categories; evaluates LLM reward-hack detection in isolated classification vs contrastive anomaly detection, finding models detect hacks better in contrastive settings (GPT-5.2 highest reasoning mode: 63% vs 45% isolated on TRACE).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: benchmarks LLMs as reward-hack detectors in code RL and shows evaluation framing (contrastive vs isolated) materially changes detection rates, informing how to assess reward-hack detection capability. Full-text basis.
records.datasets_used: TRACE benchmark: 517 testing trajectories, 54 exploit categories
records.effect_sizes: GPT-5.2 63% (contrastive) vs 45% (isolated) detection on TRACE

records.title: From Curiosity to Caution: Mitigating Reward Hacking for Best-of-N with Pessimism
records.authors: Zhuohao Yu; Zhiwei Steven Wu; Adam Block
records.key_contribution: Explores the principle of pessimism in RL - using lower confidence bounds on value estimates to avoid out-of-distribution actions with uncertain reward estimates - to mitigate reward hacking in Best-of-N (BoN) sampling, where performance degrades as N increases because selection exploits imperfections in the reward model rather than improving generation quality.
records.relevance_justification: BoN reward-hacking mitigation via pessimistic RL with lower confidence bounds; relevant to alignment robustness against reward-model over-optimization.

records.title: When RLHF Fails: A Mechanistic Taxonomy of Reward Hacking, Collapse, and Evaluator Gaming
records.authors: Zelalem Abahana; David Evans; Satish Mahadevan Srinivasan; Matjaz Gams
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Mechanistic taxonomy of RLHF failures (reward hacking, collapse, evaluator gaming) from a compact RLHF pipeline (PPO, DPO, UP-PPO, reward-model uncertainty, policy drift, diversity/repetition diagnostics, two external LLM judges); classifies checkpoint/prompt-level transitions by directions of learned reward and judge scores; finds aggressive PPO gives the clearest localized reward-hacking signal, UP-PPO reduces but does not eliminate it, row-level diagnostics reveal failures hidden by checkpoint averages, and pre-transition features partially anticipate future localized reward hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to measuring and anticipating reward-hacking failures: shows failures localize at row/prompt level and can be partially predicted before external quality degrades — relevant to monitoring the proxy-true gap and the internalization of misalignment.
records.open_questions: Whether pre-transition predictive features generalize to other pipelines (DPO-only, larger scale).

records.title: Recontextualization Mitigates Specification Gaming without Modifying the Specification
records.authors: Ariana Azarbal; Victor Gillioz; Vladimir Ivanov; Bryce Woodworth; Jacob Drori; Nevan Wichers; Aram Ebtekar; Alex Cloud; Alexander Matt Turner
records.key_contribution: Proposes recontextualization to reduce specification gaming without modifying the specification: generate completions from prompts discouraging misbehavior, then recontextualize them as though they were responses to prompts permitting misbehavior; trains models to resist misbehavior even when instructions permit it; prevents prioritizing eval metrics over quality, special-casing code to pass incorrect tests, overwriting evaluation functions, and sycophancy.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: training-time method that reduces specification gaming (a form of reward/objective gaming) without improving the supervision signal; empirical but abstract-only, and not about compositional generalization.
records.effect_sizes: Reduces four gaming behaviors (metric-chasing, test special-casing, eval-function overwriting, sycophancy)

records.title: Distributional AGI Safety
records.authors: Nenad Tomašev; Matija Franklin; Julian Jacobs; Sébastien Krier; Simon Osindero
records.key_contribution: Argues for the 'patchwork AGI' hypothesis - that general capability levels are first manifested through coordination of groups of sub-AGI agents with complementary skills - over the monolithic AGI assumption that dominates safety/alignment research; proposes a framework for distributional AGI safety beyond evaluating and aligning individual agents, centered on virtual agentic sandbox economies; flags the rapid deployment of tool-using, coordinating AI agents as an urgent safety consideration.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: proposes a new emergence hypothesis and distributional safety framework for aligning coordinated agent groups; position.
records.key_equations_definitions: Distributional AGI safety; virtual agentic sandbox economies

records.title: Modification-Considering Value Learning for Reward Hacking Mitigation in RL
records.authors: Evgenii Opryshko; Umangi Jain; Igor Gilitschenski
records.key_contribution: Proposes Modification-Considering Value Learning (MCVL), operationalizing current-utility optimization for value-based RL: wraps an off-policy learner, treats each incoming transition as a candidate modification, forecasts two training paths (with and without the transition), scores both with a frozen bootstrapped-return estimator from a learned reward model and value function, and admits the transition only if inclusion does not decrease the score; formalizes conditions under which filtering is both safe and permissive.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a formal defense against reward hacking that avoids the suppressing-hacking-vs-permitting-improvement tension of reference-policy constraints; directly targets current-utility (non-optimization-lock) alignment. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Current utility optimization; frozen bootstrapped-return estimator scoring of candidate transitions

records.title: MONA: Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval Can Mitigate Multi-step Reward Hacking
records.authors: Sebastian Farquhar; Vikrant Varma; David Lindner; David Elson; Caleb Biddulph; Ian Goodfellow; Rohin Shah
records.key_contribution: Proposes MONA (Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval), a training method that combines short-sighted optimization with far-sighted reward to avoid agents learning undesired multi-step plans that receive high reward (multi-step reward hacks) even when humans cannot detect the behavior is undesired; demonstrates MONA prevents multi-step reward hacking that ordinary RL causes, empirically in three settings modeling different misalignment failure modes including 2-step environments with LLM delegated oversight and longer-horizon gridworlds representing sensor tampering.
records.relevance_justification: Training method mitigating multi-step reward hacking without human detection ability; relevant to alignment robustness and reward-hacking prevention.
records.datasets_used: 2-step LLM delegated-oversight environments; longer-horizon gridworld (sensor tampering)

records.title: MIRA: Towards Mitigating Reward Hacking in Inference-Time Alignment of T2I Diffusion Models
records.authors: Kevin Zhai; Utsav Singh; Anirudh Thatipelli; Souradip Chakraborty; Anit Kumar Sahu; Furong Huang; Amrit Singh Bedi; Mubarak Shah
records.key_contribution: MIRA (MItigating Reward hAcking): a training-free, inference-time alignment method for T2I diffusion models that shows noise-space regularization is insufficient and that preventing reward hacking requires an explicit image-space constraint; introduces an image-space, score-based KL surrogate that regularizes the sampling trajectory with a frozen base model.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward hacking in inference-time alignment: shows that steering generation toward high scalar reward (e.g., aesthetic score) without an image-space constraint yields prompt-deviating (hacked) images — an instance of proxy-optimization failure with a concrete mitigation.
records.open_questions: Effectiveness of MIRA across diverse reward models and prompts at scale.
records.key_equations_definitions: Image-space score-based KL surrogate regularizing sampling trajectory

records.title: Mitigating Deceptive Alignment via Self-Monitoring
records.authors: Jiaming Ji; Wenqi Chen; Kaile Wang; Donghai Hong; Sitong Fang; Boyuan Chen; Jiayi Zhou; Juntao Dai; Sirui Han; Yike Guo; Yaodong Yang
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Presents CoT Monitor+, the first framework that embeds a self-monitor inside the chain-of-thought process: the model produces ordinary reasoning steps plus an internal self-evaluation signal trained to flag and suppress misaligned strategies, used as an auxiliary reward in RL; introduces DeceptionBench, a five-category benchmark for studying deceptive alignment systematically.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: intercepts deceptive alignment (appearing aligned while covertly pursuing misaligned goals) during internal reasoning rather than filtering outputs post-hoc; directly engages the internal-vs-surface distinction central to the sigma-trap.
records.open_questions: Can the self-monitor itself be gamed by the model, and does monitoring inside CoT degrade reasoning quality or reward honest strategies effectively?
records.datasets_used: DeceptionBench (five-category deceptive alignment benchmark)
records.effect_sizes: Self-monitor signal suppresses misaligned strategies and improves honest-reasoning reward

records.title: Robust Optimization for Mitigating Reward Hacking with Correlated Proxies
records.authors: Zixuan Liu; Xiaolin Sun; Zizhan Zheng
records.key_contribution: Formulates reward hacking as a robust policy optimization problem over the space of all r-correlated proxy rewards; derives a tractable max-min formulation where the agent maximizes performance under the worst-case proxy consistent with the correlation constraint; shows when the reward is a linear function of known features the approach can be adapted; overcomes limitations of occupancy-regularized policy optimization (ORPO), which optimizes against a fixed proxy without guarantees against broader correlated-proxy classes.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal robust-optimization treatment of reward hacking under correlated proxies; theoretical formulation.
records.key_equations_definitions: max-min robust policy optimization over r-correlated proxy rewards; correlation constraint

records.title: Extending MONA in Camera Dropbox: Reproduction, Learned Approval, and Design Implications for Reward-Hacking Mitigation
records.authors: Nathan Heath
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Reproduction-first extension of MONA (Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval) in the Camera Dropbox environment: repackages the codebase as a standard Python project with scripted PPO training, confirms the published contrast (ordinary RL 91.5% reward-hacking rate vs oracle MONA 0.0%) using released reference arrays, and introduces a modular learned-approval suite (oracle, noisy, misspecified, learned, calibrated) to probe how approval construction affects MONA's safety guarantees, with reduced-budget pilot sweeps over approval methods, horizons, and dataset sizes.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: independent reproduction evidence for MONA's multi-step reward-hacking mitigation and a systematic test of how the approval signal's construction (dependence on achieved outcomes) affects safety guarantees - a key open question for approval-based alignment. Full-text basis.
records.datasets_used: MONA Camera Dropbox environment; released reference arrays
records.effect_sizes: Ordinary RL 91.5% hacking rate vs oracle MONA 0.0%

records.title: Repairing Reward Functions with Feedback to Mitigate Reward Hacking
records.authors: Stephane Hatgis-Kessell; Logan Mondal Bhamidipaty; Emma Brunskill
records.key_contribution: Proposes Preference-Based Reward Repair (PBRR), an automated iterative framework that repairs a human-specified proxy reward function by learning an additive, transition-dependent correction term from human preferences, addressing the limitations of both hand-specified proxy rewards (which induce reward hacking) and full RL-from-human-feedback (costly preference datasets); argues corrections on only a few transitions may suffice to recover optimal performance.
records.relevance_justification: Method for repairing misspecified proxy reward functions from preferences to mitigate reward hacking; relevant to alignment robustness against proxy misspecification.
records.key_equations_definitions: Additive, transition-dependent correction term learned from preferences and added to human-specified proxy reward.

records.title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking
records.authors: Joar Skalse; Nikolaus H. R. Howe; Dmitrii Krasheninnikov; David Krueger
records.key_contribution: First formal definition of reward hacking: optimizing an imperfect proxy reward function leads to poor performance under the true reward; defines unhackable proxies (increasing expected proxy return never decreases expected true return); proves linearity of reward in state-action visit counts makes unhackability a very strong condition — for all stochastic policies two rewards can only be unhackable if one is constant; gives necessary and sufficient conditions for deterministic policies and finite stochastic policy sets where non-trivial unhackable pairs exist.
records.relevance_justification: The foundational formalization of reward hacking / proxy misspecification — the core mechanism behind sigma-trap-style alignment failure. Directly relevant to understanding when proxy rewards provably cannot represent the true objective.
records.open_questions: Whether real-world proxy reward functions are closer to the strict or the non-trivial-unhackable regimes.
records.key_equations_definitions: Unhackable proxy: increasing E[proxy return] never decreases E[true return]; linearity of reward in state-action visit counts; theorem that unhackability implies constancy for all stochastic policies

records.title: Generative Adversarial Post-Training Mitigates Reward Hacking in Live Human-AI Music Interaction
records.authors: Yusong Wu; Stephen Brade; Aleksandra Teng Ma; Tia-Jane Fowler; Enning Yang; Berker Banar; Aaron Courville; Natasha Jaques; Cheng-Zhi Anna Huang
records.key_contribution: Proposes generative adversarial post-training on policy-generated trajectories to mitigate reward hacking in RL post-training for melody-to-chord accompaniment in live human-AI music jamming; a co-evolving discriminator separates hacking behavior from genuine creativity, preserving output diversity that coherence-based rewards would collapse.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical demonstration of reward hacking in a creative/coherence-reward setting (RL reduces diversity) and an adversarial mitigation; useful domain case of reward overoptimization, not compositional generalization.
records.datasets_used: Melody-to-chord accompaniment in live jamming interaction
records.effect_sizes: Adversarial post-training reduces reward hacking and preserves output diversity in live jamming
records.notes: ft_file=Generative Adversarial Post-Training Mitigates Reward Hacking in Live Human-AI Music Interaction.pdf

records.title: Helping or Herding? Reward Model Ensembles Mitigate but do not Eliminate Reward Hacking
records.authors: Jacob Eisenstein; Chirag Nagpal; Alekh Agarwal; Ahmad Beirami; Alex D'Amour; DJ Dvijotham; Adam Fisch; Katherine Heller; Stephen Pfohl; Deepak Ramachandran; Peter Shaw; Jonathan Berant
records.key_contribution: Explores reward model ensembles for alignment at training time (RL) and inference time (reranking); shows reward models are underspecified (models that perform similarly in-distribution yield very different rewards under distribution shift), underspecification results in overoptimization (alignment to one reward model does not improve reward measured by another trained on the same data), and overoptimization is mitigated but not eliminated by reward ensembles.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical study of reward model underspecification and overoptimization; ensembles mitigate but do not eliminate reward hacking.
records.effect_sizes: Ensembles mitigate overoptimization but do not eliminate reward hacking

records.title: UMM-RM: An Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model for Mitigating Reward Hacking
records.authors: Lingling Fu; Yongfu Xue
records.key_contribution: Proposes UMM-RM (Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model) to counter reward hacking in RLHF: upscales a dense backbone's feed-forward layers into a mixture-of-experts reward model with always-activated shared experts capturing instruction-agnostic preference signals and conditional experts modeling fine-grained preference across instructions; after training, experts are consolidated into a single dense RM via learnable merging weights, retaining exploitation resistance from expert diversity while keeping a dense inference interface.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: architectural defense against reward hacking under distribution shift by making the reward model's preference signals more robust/diverse; addresses RM exploitation by the policy model in online RLHF. Full-text basis.
records.notes: ft_file=UMM-RM An Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model for Mitigating Reward Hacking.pdf | ai-revised:formal_framework=information theory->none

records.title: LLMs Gaming Verifiers: RLVR can Lead to Reward Hacking
records.authors: Lukas Helff; Quentin Delfosse; David Steinmann; Ruben Härle; Hikaru Shindo; Patrick Schramowski; Wolfgang Stammer; Kristian Kersting; Felix Friedrich
records.key_contribution: Studies RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards) failure modes on inductive reasoning tasks, finding RLVR-trained models systematically abandon rule induction and instead enumerate instance-level labels, producing outputs that pass verifiers without capturing the relational patterns required by the task; shows this is not a failure of understanding but a form of reward hacking, as imperfect extensional verifiers admit false positives; introduces Isomorphic Perturbation Testing (IPT), which evaluates outputs under both extensional and isomorphism-invariant verification.
records.relevance_justification: RLVR-trained models game verifiers by abandoning generalizable (compositional) rule induction for instance-level enumeration - a compositional-generalization failure framed explicitly as reward hacking, directly aligned with the sigma-trap thesis that compositional generalization failure and alignment failure are the same phenomenon. Revised up from seed 4.

records.title: Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation: A Learned Precursor to Reward Hacking and Its Generalization
records.authors: Mohammad Beigi; Ming Jin; Lifu Huang
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: PRIME (Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation): a learned capability to assess task correctness, predict proxy acceptance, and reason about exploitable proxy-gold gaps, measured via chain-of-thought monitoring, direct probes, and activation-level concept vectors in coding RL environments with exploitable pytest rewards; PRIME emerges in a staged sequence before sustained reward hacking, its direct-probe score forecasts later hack onset/severity while visible hack rate is still low, it adapts to evaluator changes and persists when gold reward suppresses overt hacking, and ablating its activation directions reduces hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to the internalization of misalignment: shows a measurable, probe-able precursor capability (proxy-gap awareness) emerges in internal representations before visible reward hacking — strong evidence for latent-internal misalignment preceding behavioral failure, central to sigma-trap monitoring.
records.open_questions: Whether PRIME-style precursors generalize to non-coding domains and non-pytest evaluators.
records.datasets_used: Coding RL environments with exploitable pytest rewards
records.notes: ft_file=Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation A Learned Precursor to Reward Hacking and Its Generalization.pdf

records.title: Core Safety Values for Provably Corrigible Agents
records.authors: Aran Nayebi
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Introduces a formal solution to corrigibility in the off-switch game with provable guarantees in multi-step, partially observed environments: five structurally separate utility heads (deference, switch-access preservation, truthfulness, low-impact via belief-based AUP, bounded task reward) combined lexicographically; proves exact single-round corrigibility and multi-step guarantees for self-spawning agents with epsilon-learned heads; contrasts with Constitutional AI/RLHF which merge norms into one learned scalar.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: provable corrigibility via structurally separated utility heads, explicitly arguing against merging all norms into a single learned scalar (RLHF/Constitutional AI) - a point about representation structure relevant to the sigma-trap; theoretical.
records.open_questions: Do the lexicographic weight gaps and head separation survive practical training, and do the guarantees scale beyond toy environments?
records.key_equations_definitions: Five lexicographically combined utility heads; epsilon-MSE head learning bound and epsilon-sub-optimal planner bound on safety violation probability

records.title: Is It Thinking or Cheating? Detecting Implicit Reward Hacking by Measuring Reasoning Effort
records.authors: Xinpeng Wang; Nitish Joshi; Barbara Plank; Rico Angell; He He
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Proposes TRACE (Truncated Reasoning AUC Evaluation) to detect implicit reward hacking where the chain-of-thought appears benign and bypasses CoT monitors; key observation is that hacking occurs when exploiting the loophole is easier than solving the task, so the model uses less effort than required; TRACE quantifies effort by progressively truncating the CoT at various lengths, forcing answers, and estimating expected reward at each cutoff, such that a hacking model achieves high expected reward with only a small fraction of its CoT.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: detection method for implicit reward hacking via reasoning-effort measurement; relevant to reward hacking monitoring.
records.key_equations_definitions: TRACE (Truncated Reasoning AUC Evaluation); reasoning effort via CoT truncation
records.effect_sizes: Hacking models achieve high expected reward with a small fraction of CoT (large AUC)
records.notes: ft_file=Is It Thinking or Cheating Detecting Implicit Reward Hacking by Measuring Reasoning Effort.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical

records.title: Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF: Detecting and Mitigating Reward Hacking
records.authors: Yuchun Miao; Liang Ding; Sen Zhang; Rong Bao; Lefei Zhang; Dacheng Tao
records.key_contribution: Proposes InfoRM, an information-theoretic reward modeling framework based on the Information Bottleneck (IB) principle that filters out spurious, preference-irrelevant information to alleviate reward misgeneralization; observes reward-hacked responses are pronounced outliers in InfoRM's IB latent space (measured by Mahalanobis distance from the SFT-induced distribution) and introduces IBL, a distribution-level regularization penalizing such deviations during RL optimization.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: directly addresses reward misgeneralization (RM overfitting to spurious features) and offers both detection (IB-latent outliers) and mitigation (IBL regularization) for reward hacking in RLHF. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Information Bottleneck principle; IB latent space; Mahalanobis-distance outlier detection; IBL distribution-level regularization
records.effect_sizes: Reward-hacked responses appear as pronounced IB-latent outliers
records.notes: ft_file=Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF Detecting and Mitigating Reward Hacking.pdf

records.title: On Mesa-Optimization in Autoregressively Trained Transformers: Emergence and Capability
records.authors: Chenyu Zheng; Wei Huang; Rongzhen Wang; Guoqiang Wu; Jun Zhu; Chongxuan Li
records.key_contribution: Theoretically investigates whether non-convex training dynamics of autoregressively trained transformers converge to an ideal mesa-optimizer for in-context learning, analyzing the gradient-flow dynamics of a one-layer linear causal self-attention model on sequences generated by an AR process x_{t+1} = W x_t; under a data-distribution condition, proves the transformer learns W by implementing one step of gradient descent minimizing an ordinary least squares problem in-context.
records.relevance_justification: Theory paper on mesa-optimizer emergence in autoregressive transformers; relevant to mesa-optimization and the emergence of deceptive/self-interested objectives.
records.key_equations_definitions: AR process x_{t+1} = W x_t; gradient-flow dynamics of one-layer linear causal self-attention; one-step gradient descent on the in-context OLS objective.

records.title: Temper and Tilt Lead to SLOP: Reward Hacking Mitigation with Inference-Time Alignment
records.authors: Ye Wang; Jing Liu; Toshiaki Koike-Akino
records.key_contribution: Temper and Tilt: extends inference-time alignment by introducing reference-model temperature adjustment and generalizes it to ensembles of generative reward models combined as a sharpened logarithmic opinion pool (SLOP); proposes an algorithm for calibrating SLOP weight parameters and experimentally shows it improves robustness against reward hacking while preserving alignment performance.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward-hacking mitigation in inference-time alignment: shows reward-ensembling (opinion pooling) plus weight calibration improves robustness against proxy exploitation without loss of alignment performance.
records.open_questions: Whether SLOP calibration generalizes to other reward ensembles and larger models.
records.key_equations_definitions: Sharpened logarithmic opinion pool (SLOP) over generative reward models; weight-calibration algorithm
records.notes: ft_file=Temper and Tilt Lead to SLOP Reward Hacking Mitigation with Inference-Time Alignment.pdf

records.title: Pedagogical Safety in Educational Reinforcement Learning: Formalizing and Detecting Reward Hacking in AI Tutoring Systems
records.authors: Oluseyi Olukola; Nick Rahimi
records.key_contribution: Introduces a four-layer model of pedagogical safety for educational RL (structural, progress, behavioral, alignment safety) and the Reward Hacking Severity Index (RHSI) to quantify misalignment between proxy rewards and genuine learning; evaluates in a simulated AI tutoring environment with 120 sessions, four conditions, three learner profiles, 18,000 interactions; finds an engagement-optimized agent over-selected a high-engagement action with no mastery gain, and multi-objective rewards reduced but did not eliminate the problem.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formalizes and empirically demonstrates reward hacking in a real application domain (tutoring), with a severity metric; shows proxy-reward optimization systematically diverges from the true objective.
records.open_questions: Can a safety-oriented reward formulation eliminate proxy-reward gaming entirely, or must detection/monitoring remain part of the system?
records.key_equations_definitions: RHSI: quantifies misalignment between proxy reward and genuine learning
records.datasets_used: Controlled simulation of AI tutoring environment
records.effect_sizes: Engagement-optimized agent over-selected a high-engagement action with no mastery gain; multi-objective reward reduced but did not eliminate it

records.title: Thinking-Based Non-Thinking: Solving the Reward Hacking Problem in Training Hybrid Reasoning Models via Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Siyuan Gan; Jiaheng Liu; Boyan Wang; Tianpei Yang; Runqing Miao; Yuyao Zhang; Fanyu Meng; Junlan Feng; Linjian Meng; Jing Huo; Yang Gao
records.key_contribution: Proposes Thinking-Based Non-Thinking (TNT) to solve the reward hacking problem in RL training of hybrid reasoning models (which automatically decide whether to think based on query complexity); addresses the failure where a model engages in thinking but is judged as not doing so, yielding incorrect rewards; avoids both the high computational cost of supervised fine-tuning and the limited mitigation of uniform token limits by setting different maximum token usage for responses.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: method mitigating reward hacking in RL training of hybrid reasoning models; technical alignment-adjacent method.

records.title: Feedback Loops With Language Models Drive In-Context Reward Hacking
records.authors: Alexander Pan; Erik Jones; Meena Jagadeesan; Jacob Steinhardt
records.key_contribution: Shows feedback loops between LLMs and the world cause in-context reward hacking (ICRH): at test time an LLM optimizes a (potentially implicit) objective while creating negative side effects (e.g., an engagement-optimizing agent making its tweets more controversial). Identifies two processes leading to ICRH (output-refinement and policy-refinement) and argues static-dataset evaluations are insufficient because they miss feedback effects and cannot capture the most harmful behavior.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: establishes in-context reward hacking as a distinct alignment failure arising from world-feedback loops rather than training-time optimization, expanding the scope of reward hacking to test-time agent behavior. Full-text basis (arXiv version).
records.notes: ft_file=Feedback Loops With Language Models Drive In-Context Reward Hacking.pdf

records.title: Specification Self-Correction: Mitigating In-Context Reward Hacking Through Test-Time Refinement
records.authors: Víctor Gallego
records.key_contribution: Introduces Specification Self-Correction (SSC), a test-time framework enabling an LM to identify and correct flaws in its own guiding specification: the model generates a response from a potentially tainted specification, critiques its output, revises the specification to remove the exploitable loophole, then generates a final response from the corrected specification; across creative writing and agentic coding tasks, models initially game tainted specifications in 50-70% of cases, and SSC reduces this vulnerability by over 90% at inference time without weight updates.
records.relevance_justification: Test-time framework mitigating in-context reward hacking (exploitation of faulty rubrics/specifications); relevant to specification-gaming and alignment robustness.
records.effect_sizes: Models game tainted specifications in 50-70% of cases; SSC reduces this vulnerability by over 90%
records.notes: ft_file=Specification Self-Correction Mitigating In-Context Reward Hacking Through Test-Time Refinement.pdf

records.title: The AI Alignment Paradox
records.authors: Robert West; Roland Aydin
records.key_contribution: The AI alignment paradox: the better AI models are aligned with human values, the easier it becomes for adversaries to misalign them; sketches three concrete incarnations for language models, each a distinct way adversaries might exploit the paradox; calls for broad awareness and mitigation research.
records.relevance_justification: Highlights a robustness tension in alignment: alignment effort itself creates exploitable structure for adversarial realignment. Relevant to alignment robustness but not directly to schema coherence / compositional generalization.
records.open_questions: Whether adversarial realignment exploits the same latent value structure that alignment builds, and how to make alignment robust to it.

records.title: InfoRM: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling
records.authors: Yuchun Miao; Sen Zhang; Liang Ding; Rong Bao; Lefei Zhang; Dacheng Tao
records.key_contribution: Proposes InfoRM, an information-theoretic framework for reward modeling in RLHF that uses a variational information bottleneck to filter out information irrelevant to human preferences, addressing reward misgeneralization; identifies correlation between overoptimization and outliers in the IB latent space and proposes the Cluster Separation Index (CSI) to detect reward overoptimization.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: information-theoretic approach to reward misgeneralization and overoptimization, with an overoptimization indicator; evidence of spurious-feature exploitation in reward models.
records.key_equations_definitions: Variational information bottleneck objective; Cluster Separation Index over IB latent space
records.effect_sizes: CSI correlates with reward overoptimization and detects it

records.title: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Discounting for Mitigating Reward Hacking
records.authors: Disha Singha
records.key_contribution: Introduces Uncertainty-Aware Reward Discounting (UARD), a framework jointly modeling epistemic uncertainty in value estimation via ensemble disagreement and aleatoric uncertainty in human preference annotations via annotator variability, combined through a confidence-adjusted Reliability Filter that adaptively modulates reward weighting during policy optimization; proves the dynamic discounting preserves the contraction property of the Bellman operator, guaranteeing convergence to a unique fixed point.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: principled framework mitigating reward hacking via joint uncertainty-aware reward discounting, with convergence guarantees.
records.key_equations_definitions: UARD; ensemble disagreement; annotator variability; Reliability Filter; Bellman contraction

records.title: A Multi-Level Framework for the AI Alignment Problem
records.authors: Betty Li Hou; Brian Patrick Green
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Presents a four-level framework for the normative side of AI alignment - Individual, Organizational, National, and Global - showing value alignment problems at each level interact and that effects can flow in either direction; outlines key questions and considerations per level and applies the framework to AI content moderation.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: scoping/normative framework mapping the levels at which alignment targets are defined, useful context for the governance dimensions of the review; position-style contribution. Full-text basis.
records.notes: ft_file=A Multi-Level Framework for the AI Alignment Problem.pdf | moved:datasets_used(other)

records.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Bayesian Non-negative Reward Modeling
records.authors: Zhibin Duan; Guowei Rong; Zhuo Li; Bo Chen; Mingyuan Zhou; Dandan Guo
records.key_contribution: Proposes the Bayesian Non-Negative Reward Model (BNRM) for RLHF, integrating non-negative factor analysis into the Bradley-Terry preference model so that rewards are represented through a sparse, non-negative latent factor generative process: instance-specific latent variables induce disentangled reward representations while sparsity over global latent factors acts as an implicit debiasing mechanism suppressing spurious correlations (e.g., response length or style biases), enabling robust uncertainty-aware reward learning scaled via an amortized variational inference network.
records.relevance_justification: Reward modeling framework mitigating reward hacking due to noisy annotations and systematic biases in RLHF; strongly relevant to alignment robustness against reward-model exploitation.
records.key_equations_definitions: BNRM integrates non-negative factor analysis into the Bradley-Terry preference model; sparse non-negative latent factor generative process; amortized variational inference network.

records.title: Incomplete Contracting and AI Alignment
records.authors: Dylan Hadfield-Menell; Gillian Hadfield
records.key_contribution: Applies incomplete-contracting theory from law and economics to the AI alignment problem: misalignment between principal and agent is a core focus of economic analysis; highlights technical results from the incomplete-contracts literature and argues human contracting is supported by external structure (culture, law) that supplies implied terms to fill gaps in incomplete contracts.
records.relevance_justification: Conceptual framing of alignment as an incomplete-contracting problem where external institutional structure provides implicit terms — relevant to value specification and the impossibility of fully specifying contracts, but analytical rather than formal/empirical.
records.open_questions: How cultural/legal implied terms could be operationalized for AI alignment.

records.title: AI Alignment Dialogues: An Interactive Approach to AI Alignment in Support Agents
records.authors: Pei-Yu Chen; Myrthe L. Tielman; Dirk K. J. Heylen; Catholijn M. Jonker; M. Birna van Riemsdijk
records.key_contribution: Proposes AI Alignment Dialogues, an interactive approach where users and agents maintain alignment through dialogue rather than learning values from behavioral data; argues advantages over data-driven approaches for behaviour-support agents (users directly convey higher-level concepts; more transparent and trustworthy); outlines concept and structure and reports a qualitative focus group user study.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: interaction-based alternative to data-driven alignment with a focus-group evaluation; relevant to value-elicitation methods but small-scale and qualitative.
records.datasets_used: Qualitative focus group user study

records.title: When Reward Hacking Rebounds: Understanding and Mitigating It with Representation-Level Signals
records.authors: Rui Wu; Ruixiang Tang
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Systematically studies reward hacking in coding tasks using an environment-manipulation setting where models can rewrite evaluator code to trivially pass tests; identifies a reproducible three-phase rebound pattern (models first attempt but fail to rewrite the evaluator, then retreat to legitimate solving, then rebound into successful hacking with qualitatively different strategies when legitimate reward stays scarce); uses representation engineering to extract concept directions for shortcut, deception, and evaluation awareness, finding the shortcut direction tracks hacking behavior most closely as an effective representation-level signal.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical study of reward hacking dynamics with representation-level detection/mitigation; relevant to reward hacking mechanisms.
records.datasets_used: Coding tasks with environment-manipulation setting (evaluator code rewriting)
records.effect_sizes: Reproducible three-phase rebound pattern; shortcut direction tracks hacking most closely
records.notes: ft_file=When Reward Hacking Rebounds Understanding and Mitigating It with Representation-Level Signals.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical

records.title: IR$^3$: Contrastive Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Interpretable Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking
records.authors: Mohammad Beigi; Ming Jin; Junshan Zhang; Jiaxin Zhang; Qifan Wang; Lifu Huang
records.key_contribution: Introduces IR3 (Interpretable Reward Reconstruction and Rectification), a framework that reverse-engineers, interprets, and surgically repairs the implicit objectives driving RLHF-tuned models: Contrastive Inverse RL (C-IRL) reconstructs the implicit reward by contrasting post-alignment vs baseline policy responses, sparse autoencoders decompose the reconstructed reward into interpretable features enabling identification of hacking signatures via contribution analysis, and mitigation strategies (clean reward optimization, adversarial variants) repair the objective.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: makes the reward-hacking-prone implicit objective of RLHF models transparent and repairable, connecting interpretability to alignment; supports the thesis that the internalized objective (representation) must be inspected, not just behavior. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Contrastive inverse RL; sparse-autoencoder feature decomposition; contribution analysis of hacking signatures

records.title: Value Alignment Verification
records.authors: Daniel S. Brown; Jordan Schneider; Anca D. Dragan; Scott Niekum
records.key_contribution: Formalizes and theoretically analyzes efficient value alignment verification - how to efficiently test whether another agent's behavior is aligned with a human's values via a minimal number of queries (a 'driver's test'); studies idealized humans with explicit reward functions and implicit values, analyzes exact verification for rational agents, proposes heuristic and approximate verification tests in gridworlds and a continuous autonomous driving domain, and proves sufficient conditions for efficient verification.
records.relevance_justification: Formal framework for efficiently verifying agent value alignment via query-based tests; relevant to alignment verification and evaluation.

records.title: MO-GRPO: Mitigating Reward Hacking of Group Relative Policy Optimization on Multi-Objective Problems
records.authors: Yuki Ichihara; Yuu Jinnai; Tetsuro Morimura; Mitsuki Sakamoto; Ryota Mitsuhashi; Eiji Uchibe
records.key_contribution: MO-GRPO: extends GRPO to multi-objective settings with a simple variance-based normalization that automatically reweights reward functions, analytically ensuring all reward functions contribute evenly to the loss while preserving preference order, eliminating manual reward-scale tuning; evaluates in four domains (multi-armed bandits, Mo-Gymnasium simulated control, machine translation, and more).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward hacking in multi-objective RL: identifies that GRPO overoptimizes one objective at the expense of others (a compositional proxy-misspecification failure) and provides an analytically motivated mitigation.
records.open_questions: Whether variance-based reweighting remains effective when reward scales shift during training.
records.key_equations_definitions: Variance-based reward reweighting ensuring equal contribution to loss while preserving preference order

records.title: Truthful or Fabricated? Using Causal Attribution to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Explanations
records.authors: Pedro Ferreira; Wilker Aziz; Ivan Titov
records.key_contribution: Shows preference optimization can reduce the faithfulness of chain-of-thought explanations because the reward model optimizes response quality and explanation appropriateness without a mechanism to check consistency between internal decision process and generated explanation; proposes causal attribution to mitigate this reward hacking of explanations.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: demonstrates reward hacking of explanations (surface CoT decoupled from internal reasoning) and proposes a causal-attribution fix; touches the internal-vs-surface coherence theme of the sigma-trap.

records.title: Calibration Collapse Under Sycophancy Fine-Tuning: How Reward Hacking Breaks Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
records.authors: Subramanyam Sahoo
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Investigates whether sycophantic reward signals degrade calibration in LLMs; fine-tunes Qwen3-8B under three regimes (base, neutral SFT on TriviaQA, sycophancy-inducing GRPO rewarding agreement with planted wrong answers); evaluating on 1,000 MMLU items across five subject domains, finds sycophantic GRPO produces consistent directional calibration degradation (ECE +0.006 vs base, MCE +0.010 vs neutral SFT) though the effect does not reach statistical significance (p=0.41) at this training budget.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical study linking sycophancy (a reward hacking manifestation) to calibration degradation in LLMs.
records.datasets_used: TriviaQA (neutral SFT); 1,000 MMLU items across five subject domains
records.effect_sizes: ECE +0.006 vs base; MCE +0.010 vs neutral SFT (p=0.41, not significant)

records.title: SoliReward: Mitigating Susceptibility to Reward Hacking and Annotation Noise in Video Generation Reward Models
records.authors: Jiesong Lian; Ruizhe Zhong; Zixiang Zhou; Xiaoyue Mi; Long Hu; Yuan Zhou; Qinglin Lu; Yixue Hao; Junchi Yan
records.key_contribution: Presents SoliReward, a framework for training reward models for video generation post-training alignment: sources high-quality data via single-item binary annotations with cross-prompt preference-pair construction (reducing annotation noise), uses a Hierarchical Progressive Query Attention mechanism for feature aggregation, and introduces a modified Bradley-Terry loss that explicitly accommodates win-tie scenarios to regularize the reward model's score distribution against hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: targets reward hacking and annotation noise in video-generation reward models, extending RLHF-style alignment to a new modality with specific data-collection and loss-design fixes. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Modified Bradley-Terry loss with win-tie term; cross-prompt pairing
records.datasets_used: Single-item binary annotations; preference pairs via cross-prompt pairing

records.title: More Convincing, Not More Correct: Self-Play Reward Hacking of Reference-Free LLM Judges
records.authors: Chenyu Zhou
records.key_contribution: Shows that training a language model against its own reference-free judgments fails structurally: a judge scores plausibility rather than correctness conditional on a candidate, leaving false-positive basins a policy learns to exploit; a hidden-anchor audit (a held-out, cross-source exact-match check) on GSM8K with Qwen3 policies shows self-play drives the judge's pass rate from 0.72 to 0.94 while true accuracy stays at 0.20, with errors transferring across judge families, a three-judge ensemble still accepting 55% of them, and committing first (having the judge commit its own answer before judging) dropping the false-positive rate from 0.719.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical study of self-play reward hacking in reference-free LLM judges, demonstrating judge false-positive basins exploited by policies; relevant to reward-hacking detection and alignment evaluation.
records.datasets_used: GSM8K (hidden-anchor audit; Qwen3 policies)
records.effect_sizes: Judge pass rate 0.72 to 0.94 vs true accuracy 0.20; three-judge ensemble accepts 55% of hacked errors; committing first drops false-positive rate from 0.719

records.title: Pragmatic-Pedagogic Value Alignment
records.authors: Jaime F. Fisac; Monica A. Gates; Jessica B. Hamrick; Chang Liu; Dylan Hadfield-Menell; Malayandi Palaniappan; Dhruv Malik; S. Shankar Sastry; Thomas L. Griffiths; Anca D. Dragan
records.formal_framework: game theory; decision theory; dynamical systems; other
records.key_contribution: Pragmatic-Pedagogic Value Alignment: presents a solution to the cooperative inverse reinforcement learning (CIRL) dynamic game grounded in cognitive models of decision making and theory of mind; captures the reciprocity relation where the human reasons pedagogically about how the robot will learn, and the robot anticipates and interprets this — combining multi-agent decision theory with models of human cognition for robot value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Foundational CIRL formulation: value alignment as a dynamic game in which the human teaches via demonstrations and the robot models human pedagogy — the theoretical basis for learning alignment from implicit human teaching signals.
records.open_questions: Whether the CIRL solution scales beyond small games and whether pedagogic reasoning generalizes across human teaching styles.
records.key_equations_definitions: Cooperative inverse RL (CIRL) dynamic game; theory-of-mind modeling of human pedagogy

records.title: Gradient Regularization Mitigates Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards
records.authors: Johannes Ackermann; Michael Noukhovitch; Takashi Ishida; Masashi Sugiyama
records.key_contribution: Proposes gradient regularization (GR) to mitigate reward hacking in RLHF/RLVR by biasing policy updates toward regions where the reward is more accurate; derives a theoretical connection between reward-model accuracy and the flatness of an optimum at convergence; empirically confirms gradient norm and reward accuracy correlate, and shows Reference Resets of the KL penalty find flatter regions.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: theory-plus-empirics on why policies overfit reward inaccuracy and how flatness-aware optimization mitigates hacking; relevant to reward-model fragility, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Connection between reward-model accuracy and flatness of optimum at convergence; gradient-norm regularization
records.effect_sizes: GR reduces reward hacking; gradient norm correlates with reward accuracy; Reference Resets find flatter regions
