records.title: Understanding the Process of Human-AI Value Alignment
records.authors: Jack McKinlay; Marina De Vos; Janina A. Hoffmann; Andreas Theodorou
records.key_contribution: Systematic literature review advancing understanding of value alignment by characterizing the topic within its research literature; analyses 172 value alignment research articles and synthesizes them into six themes: value alignment drivers & approaches; challenges in value alignment; values in value alignment; cognitive processes in humans and AI; human-agent teaming; and designing and developing value-aligned systems; proposes a more precise definition of value alignment as an ongoing process.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: systematic review characterizing the value alignment literature and refining its definition.

records.title: Justifications for Democratizing AI Alignment and Their Prospects
records.authors: André Steingrüber; Kevin Baum
records.key_contribution: Examines justifications for democratic approaches to the normative dimension of AI alignment (affected stakeholders determine alignment) vs epistocratic approaches deferring to normative experts; analyzes instrumental justifications (better outcomes) and non-instrumental ones (preventing illegitimate authority/coercion), arguing normative and metanormative uncertainty create a justificatory gap democratic approaches fill through political rather than theoretical justification; identifies significant challenges, particularly preventing illegitimate coercion through alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: normative/political framing of who should set alignment targets, complementing technical alignment literature; position-style contribution. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: AI Alignment with Changing and Influenceable Reward Functions
records.authors: Micah Carroll; Davis Foote; Anand Siththaranjan; Stuart Russell; Anca Dragan
records.key_contribution: Introduces Dynamic Reward Markov Decision Processes (DR-MDPs) to explicitly model preference change and the AI's influence on it, showing the static-preference assumption may undermine the soundness of existing alignment techniques by implicitly rewarding AI for influencing user preferences in unwanted ways; offers a unifying perspective on how optimization horizon can reduce undesirable influence, formalizes notions of AI alignment that account for preference change from the outset, and compares the strengths and limitations of 8 such notions.
records.relevance_justification: Formal framework (DR-MDPs) showing static-preference alignment assumptions can be unsound when preferences are changing and influenceable; relevant to alignment theory.
records.key_equations_definitions: Dynamic Reward Markov Decision Processes (DR-MDPs) modeling preference changes and AI influence; 8 formalized notions of alignment accounting for preference change.

records.title: 'AI Alignment' Encompasses Competing Technical Priorities
records.authors: Tushita Jha; Rory Svarc; Mateusz Bagiński
records.key_contribution: Position: 'AI alignment' encompasses distinct concepts under competing research programs, and realistic interventions can promote alignment under one conception while being counterproductive under others; tensions arise from different background threat-models and normative orientations; recommends five practices (not conflating policy and scientific scope, acknowledging methodological disagreements, distinguishing the ideal from alignment proxies, using more granular concepts, etc.).
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to framing: argues alignment is plural and that interventions can conflict across conceptions — relevant context for defining the sigma-trap against competing alignment definitions, and for proxy-vs-ideal distinction.
records.open_questions: How to reconcile competing alignment priorities in practice.

records.title: Methodological reflections for AI alignment research using human feedback
records.authors: Thilo Hagendorff; Sarah Fabi
records.key_contribution: Methodological analysis of AI alignment research using human feedback for LLM summarization: discusses challenges in collecting reliable human feedback to train reward models and improve summarization models, and suggests specific improvements to experimental design of alignment studies.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: methodological reflection on RLHF reward-data reliability in summarization; directly useful for interpreting RLHF evidence but does not address the sigma-trap mechanism.

records.title: Goal Alignment: A Human-Aware Account of Value Alignment Problem
records.authors: Malek Mechergui; Sarath Sreedharan
records.key_contribution: Argues existing value alignment work overfocuses on reward functions being an unintuitive mechanism for specifying objectives; identifies a foundational overlooked cause of misalignment: the inherent asymmetry between human expectations about the agent's behavior and the behavior generated by the agent for the specified objective; proposes a novel formulation named 'goal alignment' focusing on central challenges of value alignment, bridging currently disconnected lines of work.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: reformulation of value alignment around expectation-behavior asymmetry; conceptual.
records.key_equations_definitions: Goal alignment formulation

records.title: Corrigibility as a Singular Target: A Vision for Inherently Reliable Foundation Models
records.authors: Ram Potham; Max Harms
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes CAST (Corrigibility as a Singular Target): designing foundation models whose overriding objective is empowering designated human principals to guide, correct, and control them, shifting from static value-loading to dynamic human empowerment so self-preservation serves only to maintain principal control and goal modification becomes facilitating principal guidance; presents an empirical research agenda (RLAIF, SFT, synthetic data, scalability testing, controlled instructability).
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a concrete corrigibility-first design target that sidesteps value-specification complexity and emergent power-seeking, aligning with the control/oversight thread of the review. Full-text basis.

records.title: Strong Preferences Affect the Robustness of Preference Models and Value Alignment
records.authors: Ziwei Xu; Mohan Kankanhalli
records.key_contribution: Investigates the robustness of value alignment by examining the sensitivity of preference models (Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce) to minor changes in the probabilities of other modeled preferences; finds that a preference's probability can change significantly as other preferences change, especially when those preferences are dominant (probabilities near 0 or 1), identifying conditions under which preference-model predictions are fragile.
records.relevance_justification: Theoretical analysis of preference-model sensitivity and its implications for value alignment robustness; relevant to alignment evaluation.
records.key_equations_definitions: Sensitivity analysis of the Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce preference models.

records.title: What Makes a Medical Checker Trainable? Diagnosing Signal Collapse and Reward Hacking in Checker-Guided RAG for Biomedical QA
records.authors: Yuelyu Ji; Min Gu Kwak; Hang Zhang; Xizhi Wu; Chenyu Li; Yanshan Wan
records.key_contribution: Finds the checker's output distribution during training, not held-out accuracy, determines whether an NLI checker provides trainable gradient in GRPO-trained medical RAG agents (Qwen2.5-7B, replicated on Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.1-8B) across four medical QA benchmarks; (i) signal collapse is log-prob-specific (LLM log-prob scoring labels >97% of claims neutral, collapsing RL gradient to zero, while a calibrated MedNLI classifier scores non-degenerately); (ii) moderate signal beats strong signal — a strong proprietary checker triggers a three-step reward-hacking cascade (ultra-short answers, search avoidance, language collapse).
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to reward hacking and proxy choice: shows that the distributional properties of the reward/checker (signal collapse) rather than its accuracy govern whether RL produces usable alignment signal, and that overly strong rewards trigger reward-hacking cascades.
records.open_questions: Whether signal-collapse diagnostics transfer to other RLHF pipelines and reward types.
records.datasets_used: Medical QA benchmarks; MedNLI checker
records.effect_sizes: LLM log-prob scores >97% of claims neutral
records.notes: ft_file=What Makes a Medical Checker Trainable Diagnosing Signal Collapse and Reward Hacking in Checker-Guided RAG for Biomedical QA.pdf

records.title: Normative Conflicts and Shallow AI Alignment
records.authors: Raphaël Millière
records.key_contribution: Argues current LLM alignment strategies are fundamentally inadequate to prevent misuse: fine-tuning based on human preferences (helpfulness, honesty, harmlessness) remains vulnerable to adversarial attacks exploiting conflicts between these norms; claims this reflects a limitation of alignment methods that reinforce shallow behavioral dispositions rather than genuine normative deliberation, drawing on moral psychology to show humans' deliberative reasoning enhances resilience.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: argues alignment produces shallow behavioral dispositions vulnerable to norm-conflict exploitation rather than genuine normative capacity; aligns with the sigma-trap claim that surface alignment without internal coherence fails under composition.
records.open_questions: What training/architecture changes would endow LLMs with robust normative deliberation, and can they be evaluated?

records.title: Interactive AI Alignment: Specification, Process, and Evaluation Alignment
records.authors: Michael Terry; Chinmay Kulkarni; Martin Wattenberg; Lucas Dixon; Meredith Ringel Morris
records.key_contribution: Revisits the basic input-output interaction cycle in light of declarative AI interaction (users describe the intended outcome rather than invoking operations); connects AI alignment concepts to define three objectives for interactive alignment: specification alignment (aligning on what to do), process alignment (aligning on how to do it), and evaluation alignment (assisting users in verifying and understanding what was produced); shows these user-centered views can be used descriptively, prescriptively, and as an evaluative aid.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: user-centered decomposition of interactive alignment into specification/process/evaluation alignment; conceptual.
records.key_equations_definitions: Specification/process/evaluation alignment

records.title: Foundational Moral Values for AI Alignment
records.authors: Betty Li Hou; Brian Patrick Green
records.key_contribution: Proposes five foundational moral values for AI alignment built on the requisites for human existence - survival, sustainable intergenerational existence, society, education, and truth - arguing current alignment targets are underspecified and not built from a philosophically robust structure; uses the framework to highlight threats and opportunities from AI systems.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a candidate value specification for alignment grounded in human-existence requisites; contributes to the normative grounding thread. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Using AI Alignment Theory to understand the potential pitfalls of regulatory frameworks
records.authors: Alejandro Tlaie
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Applies Alignment Theory (AT) failure modes - proxy gaming, goal drift, reward hacking, specification gaming - to critically examine the European Union's AI Act, treating regulatory efforts in the same way advanced AI systems are treated; systematically applying these concepts uncovers potential vulnerabilities and areas for improvement in the regulation.
records.relevance_justification: Applies alignment-failure concepts (proxy gaming, reward hacking, specification gaming) to regulatory analysis of the EU AI Act; relevant to alignment-failure theory and governance.

records.title: MAP: Multi-Human-Value Alignment Palette
records.authors: Xinran Wang; Qi Le; Ammar Ahmed; Enmao Diao; Yi Zhou; Nathalie Baracaldo; Jie Ding; Ali Anwar
records.key_contribution: MAP (Multi-Human-Value Alignment Palette): a first-principles approach formulating alignment across multiple human values (e.g., harmlessness, helpfulness, positiveness) as an optimization task with user-defined constraints defining value targets, solved via a primal-dual approach that determines whether a user-defined alignment target is achievable and how to navigate trade-offs across ethnic groups, industry sectors, and user cohorts.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to pluralistic value alignment: frames simultaneous multi-value alignment as constrained optimization with a feasibility check — relevant to how conflicting values can be coherently combined (a schema-coherence-adjacent formalization of value targets).
records.open_questions: Whether the primal-dual feasibility check scales to high-dimensional value spaces and dynamic personalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Alignment as constrained optimization with user-defined value targets; primal-dual feasibility approach

records.title: Towards a Distributed Platform for Normative Reasoning and Value Alignment in Multi-Agent Systems
records.authors: Miguel Garcia-Bohigues; Carmengelys Cordova; Joaquin Taverner; Javier Palanca; Elena del Val; Estefania Argente
records.key_contribution: Presents an extended version of the SPADE platform that equips multi-agent systems with normative reasoning and value alignment: normative awareness based on deontic logic allows agents to assess the appropriateness of their actions and make informed decisions, enhancing social intelligence and responsible behavior.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: deontic-logic-based normative reasoning platform for multi-agent value alignment; engineering/system contribution with no mechanism-level or empirical depth in the evidence.

records.title: Kantian Deontology Meets AI Alignment: Towards Morally Grounded Fairness Metrics
records.authors: Carlos Mougan; Joshua Brand
records.key_contribution: Explores the compatibility of a Kantian deontological framework with fairness metrics within the AI alignment field; revisits Kant's critique of utilitarianism (the primary approach in AI fairness metrics) and argues fairness principles should align with the Kantian deontological framework to better balance outcomes and procedures in pursuit of fairness and distributive justice.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: normative-ethics framing for fairness metrics within AI alignment; philosophical/position.
records.key_equations_definitions: Kantian deontological framework; fairness metrics

records.title: AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures?
records.authors: Leonard Dung; Florian Mai
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Analyzes defense-in-depth for AI alignment from a risk perspective: since every alignment technique has failure modes, redundancy helps only if failure modes are uncorrelated; analyzes 7 representative alignment techniques across 7 failure modes to measure overlap of failure modes and discusses implications for whether independent safety mechanisms or shared failures dominate.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: systemic risk analysis of alignment techniques' correlated failures, informing when alignment methods can be combined defensively; connects robustness of alignment to technique independence. Full-text basis.
records.datasets_used: 7 alignment techniques x 7 failure modes analysis

records.title: AI Alignment and Social Choice: Fundamental Limitations and Policy Implications
records.authors: Abhilash Mishra
records.key_contribution: Investigates the limitations of RLHF for aligning AI with democratic norms, building on impossibility results in social choice theory to show that, under fairly broad assumptions, there is no unique voting protocol to universally align AI systems via RLHF through democratic processes, and that aligning AI agents with the values of all individuals will always violate certain private ethical preferences; discusses policy implications.
records.relevance_justification: Social-choice impossibility analysis of democratic RLHF alignment; relevant to alignment theory and its governance/policy implications.
records.key_equations_definitions: Social-choice impossibility results applied to democratic RLHF alignment (no universal voting protocol).

records.title: Value alignment: a formal approach
records.authors: Carles Sierra; Nardine Osman; Pablo Noriega; Jordi Sabater-Mir; Antoni Perelló
records.key_contribution: Formal model of value alignment via preferences: values represented through preferences, value aggregations computed over groups of agents and/or sets of values; value alignment of a given norm with respect to a value defined and computed through the increase/decrease it produces in the preferences of future states of the world, focusing on norms as the governors of behavior.
records.relevance_justification: Formalizes value alignment as a relation between norms and future-state preferences — a norm-centered formalization directly usable for defining alignment under a coherence account; relevant to formal grounding of the alignment target.
records.open_questions: How to elicit the preference/value representations in practice and whether aggregation over heterogeneous groups is stable.
records.key_equations_definitions: Values as preferences; value aggregation over agents and value sets; norm alignment via preference change over future states

records.title: Controllable Value Alignment in Large Language Models through Neuron-Level Editing
records.authors: Yonghui Yang; Yihui Wang; Junwei Li; Jilong Liu; Fengbin Zhu; Weibiao Huang; Le Wu; Richang Hong; Tat-Seng Chua
records.key_contribution: Proposes NeVA, a neuron-level editing framework for controllable value alignment in LLMs: introduces 'value leakage' (unintended activation of non-target values during value steering) with a normalized leakage metric grounded in Schwartz's value theory, identifies sparse value-relevant neurons, and performs inference-time activation editing without parameter updates or retraining; achieves stronger target value alignment with less capability degradation.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: work on internal (neuron-level) representation of values and controllable alignment via activation editing, with a leakage diagnostic; speaks to the internal-representation dimension of alignment.
records.open_questions: Does neuron-level value editing generalize across tasks and remain stable, and does value leakage vary across models?
records.key_equations_definitions: Normalized value-leakage metric grounded in Schwartz value theory
records.effect_sizes: NeVA improves target value alignment with smaller capability degradation than steering-based baselines

records.title: Brief Notes on Hard Takeoff, Value Alignment, and Coherent Extrapolated Volition
records.authors: Gopal P. Sarma
records.key_contribution: Makes basic observations about hard takeoff, value alignment, and coherent extrapolated volition - concepts that have been central in analyses of superintelligent AI systems.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: brief conceptual notes on alignment-relevant concepts for superintelligent systems; position.
records.key_equations_definitions: Hard takeoff; value alignment; coherent extrapolated volition

records.title: Concept Alignment as a Prerequisite for Value Alignment
records.authors: Sunayana Rane; Mark Ho; Ilia Sucholutsky; Thomas L. Griffiths
records.key_contribution: Formally analyzes concept alignment in the inverse reinforcement learning setting, arguing that value alignment requires concept alignment as a prerequisite: what a person values, and is capable of valuing, depends on the concepts they use to understand and evaluate situations, so agents must align their representation of a situation with humans to align values; shows neglecting concept alignment leads to systematic value misalignment, proposes joint reasoning about a person's concepts and values, and reports human experiments showing humans reason about the concepts an agent uses when acting intentionally.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant and closely tied to the sigma-trap: argues value misalignment arises from misaligned situation representations (conceptual/schema mismatch), i.e., a representational failure as the root of alignment failure - a formalization of the sigma-model thesis in the IRL setting, with empirical support.
records.key_equations_definitions: Concept alignment problem in IRL; joint reasoning over person's concepts and values
records.datasets_used: IRL setting experiments; human-participant experiments
records.effect_sizes: Humans reason about agent's concepts when acting intentionally, in line with joint reasoning

records.title: The Linguistic Blind Spot of Value-Aligned Agency, Natural and Artificial
records.authors: Travis LaCroix
records.key_contribution: Argues that linguistic communication (natural language) is a necessary condition for robust value alignment, and discusses the consequences of this claim for research programmes that attempt to ensure value alignment for AI systems or design robustly beneficial or ethical artificial agents.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical argument linking linguistic communication to the feasibility of robust value alignment; relevant to value-alignment theory.

records.title: Case Repositories: Towards Case-Based Reasoning for AI Alignment
records.authors: K. J. Kevin Feng; Quan Ze Chen; Inyoung Cheong; King Xia; Amy X. Zhang
records.key_contribution: Case Repositories: a complementary approach to constitutional AI alignment grounded in case-based reasoning (CBR) — constructing policies through judgments on a set of cases; process: gather seed cases (questions one may ask an AI), elicit domain-specific key dimensions through workshops with domain experts, use LLMs to generate variations of unseen cases, and engage with the public.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to how alignment policies can be built from case-based judgments rather than abstract principles — relevant to the schema-coherence question of how concrete cases generalize to novel situations via key dimensions.
records.open_questions: Whether case-based policies generalize beyond the elicited dimensions to out-of-distribution cases.

records.title: Beyond Single-Sentence Prompts: Upgrading Value Alignment Benchmarks with Dialogues and Stories
records.authors: Yazhou Zhang; Qimeng Liu; Qiuchi Li; Peng Zhang; Jing Qin
records.key_contribution: Proposes an upgraded value alignment benchmark moving beyond single-sentence adversarial prompts to multi-turn dialogues and narrative-based scenarios; designs a dataset with conversational traps and ethically ambiguous storytelling to systematically assess LLM responses in richer contexts; results show models are increasingly adept at circumventing straightforward probes.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: benchmark methodology showing single-sentence value-alignment probes can be circumvented by modern safeguards, motivating richer adversarial evaluation; evaluation-focused, not a mechanism paper.
records.datasets_used: Multi-turn dialogue and narrative-based value-alignment evaluation dataset
records.effect_sizes: Models more adept at circumventing single-sentence prompts; dialogue/story probes reveal underlying biases

records.title: AI Alignment: A Comprehensive Survey
records.authors: Jiaming Ji; Tianyi Qiu; Boyuan Chen; Borong Zhang; Hantao Lou; Kaile Wang; Yawen Duan; Zhonghao He; Lukas Vierling; Donghai Hong; Jiayi Zhou; Zhaowei Zhang; Fanzhi Zeng; Juntao Dai; Xuehai Pan; Kwan Yee Ng; Aidan O'Gara; Hua Xu; Brian Tse; Jie Fu; Stephen McAleer; Yaodong Yang; Yizhou Wang; Song-Chun Zhu; Yike Guo; Wen Gao
records.key_contribution: Comprehensive survey of AI alignment; identifies four principles as key objectives - Robustness, Interpretability, Controllability, Ethicality (RICE); decomposes alignment research into forward alignment (making AI aligned via alignment training: learning from feedback, learning under distribution shift) and backward alignment (gaining evidence about systems' alignment and governing them appropriately to avoid exacerbating misalignment risks: assurance techniques); provides an up-to-date overview of concepts, methodology, and practice.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: comprehensive survey structuring the alignment field via RICE principles and forward/backward alignment decomposition.
records.key_equations_definitions: RICE principles; forward vs backward alignment

records.title: Multi-level Value Alignment in Agentic AI Systems: Survey and Perspectives
records.authors: Wei Zeng; Hengshu Zhu; Chuan Qin; Han Wu; Yihang Cheng; Sirui Zhang; Xiaowei Jin; Yinuo Shen; Zhenxing Wang; Feimin Zhong; Hui Xiong
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of value alignment for LLM-based multi-agent (agentic) systems using a Multi-level Value framework: structures value principles top-down across macro, meso, and micro levels; categorizes application scenarios along a general-to-specific continuum; and reviews value alignment research for agentic AI addressing situational and systemic risks in multi-agent autonomous decision-making.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: systematic survey of the emerging agentic-AI alignment space with a multi-level value framework; useful scoping reference for multi-agent alignment. Full-text basis.

records.title: Decolonial AI Alignment: Openness, Viśe\d{s}a-Dharma, and Including Excluded Knowledges
records.authors: Kush R. Varshney
records.key_contribution: Argues that the history of colonialism altering the beliefs and values of colonized peoples is recapitulated in current LLM alignment practices, identifying 'moral absolutism' as a mechanism of the coloniality of knowledge within alignment; proposes decolonializing AI alignment through three forms of openness - openness of models, openness to society, and openness to excluded knowledges - drawing on the argumentative moral philosophical tradition of Hinduism.
records.relevance_justification: Critical/philosophical essay on the coloniality of LLM alignment and a decolonial alignment agenda; relevant to the ethics and value pluralism wing of alignment discourse.

records.title: You Are What You Eat -- AI Alignment Requires Understanding How Data Shapes Structure and Generalisation
records.authors: Simon Pepin Lehalleur; Jesse Hoogland; Matthew Farrugia-Roberts; Susan Wei; Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel; George Wang; Liam Carroll; Daniel Murfet
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Position: understanding the relation between structure in the data distribution and structure in trained models is central to AI alignment; two neural networks can have equivalent training-set performance but compute outputs in essentially different ways and thus generalize differently, so standard testing/evaluation is insufficient for safety assurances; argues for statistical foundations of a mathematical science of AI alignment relating data structure, internal model structure, and generalization.
records.relevance_justification: Directly aligns with the sigma-trap thesis: argues that alignment requires understanding how internal structure in models relates to data structure and generalization — precisely the schema-coherence / compositional-generalization link — and that behavior-level evaluation is insufficient.
records.open_questions: How to formalize the data-structure/model-structure correspondence and connect it to alignment guarantees.

records.title: Heterogeneous Value Alignment Evaluation for Large Language Models
records.authors: Zhaowei Zhang; Ceyao Zhang; Nian Liu; Siyuan Qi; Ziqi Rong; Song-Chun Zhu; Shuguang Cui; Yaodong Yang
records.key_contribution: Proposes the Heterogeneous Value Alignment Evaluation (HVAE) system that brings the Social Value Orientation (SVO) framework from social psychology to LLMs: assigns LLMs different social values and measures whether their behaviors align with the induced values, introducing an auto-metric 'value rationality' to represent the ability to align with specific values.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: evaluation framework for heterogeneous value alignment distinguishing value as attribute vs ability to pursue values; useful measurement contribution, no mechanism.
records.key_equations_definitions: SVO-based value assignment; value rationality auto-metric

records.title: The Specification Trap: Why Static Value Alignment Alone Is Insufficient for Robust Alignment
records.authors: Austin Spizzirri
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues static content-based AI value alignment is insufficient for robust alignment under capability scaling, distributional shift, and increasing autonomy, for any approach optimizing toward a fixed formal value-object; three compounding philosophical results: Hume's is-ought gap (behavioral data underdetermines normative content), Berlin's value pluralism (human values resist consistent formalization), and the extended frame problem (any value encoding will misfit future contexts); shows RLHF, Constitutional AI, IRL, and cooperative assistance games each instantiate this specification trap, with failure modes that are structural, not merely engineering limitations.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: philosophical argument that static alignment approaches structurally fail across all major alignment methods; foundational critique.
records.key_equations_definitions: Specification trap; Hume's is-ought gap; Berlin's value pluralism; extended frame problem

records.title: DVMap: Fine-Grained Pluralistic Value Alignment via High-Consensus Demographic-Value Mapping
records.authors: Pengyun Zhu; Yuqi Ren; Zhen Wang; Lei Yang; Deyi Xiong
records.key_contribution: Proposes DVMap (High-Consensus Demographic-Value Mapping) for fine-grained pluralistic value alignment: builds a 56,152-sample alignment corpus from the World Values Survey retaining respondents with consistent value preferences under identical demographics via a demographic-archetype extraction strategy, then uses a Structured Chain-of-Thought mechanism explicitly guiding LLMs to reason about demographic-value correlations, moving beyond coarse national labels to multi-dimensional demographic constraints.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: addresses pluralistic value alignment by replacing national-level labels with fine-grained demographic constraints and high-consensus archetypes; data-construction contribution to value alignment. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: World Values Survey (WVS)

records.title: Unifying Value Alignment and Assignment in Cross-Domain Offline Reinforcement Learning with Heterogeneous Datasets
records.authors: Zhongjian Qiao; Jiafei Lyu; Chenjia Bai; Peisong Wang; Siyang Gao; Shuang Qiu
records.key_contribution: Explores heterogeneous cross-domain offline RL where source datasets come from multiple domains collected by diverse behavior policies; uncovers 'value misassignment', demonstrating empirically and theoretically that it can undermine value alignment, mislead data filtering toward selecting suboptimal samples, and loosen the suboptimality gap in policy transfer.
records.relevance_justification: 'Value alignment' here refers to alignment of value estimates/functions for policy transfer in cross-domain offline RL, not AI human-value alignment. Off-topic. Revised down from seed 3.

records.title: Requisite Variety in Ethical Utility Functions for AI Value Alignment
records.authors: Nadisha-Marie Aliman; Leon Kester
records.key_contribution: Requisite Variety in Ethical Utility Functions: postulates that for an AI utility function not to violate human ethical intuitions it must model those intuitions and reflect their variety; performs a transdisciplinary analysis applying a security mindset to the issue, summarizing variety-relevant background knowledge from neuroscience and psychology, and complements this with a literature survey on ethical utility functions.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to value representation: argues ethical utility functions must capture the variety of human morality (a variety/coverage requirement for the value model) — conceptually relevant to why single-schema value models fail, though not formalized.
records.open_questions: How variety in human morality can be formally quantified and incorporated into utility design.

records.title: Configurable Preference Tuning with Rubric-Guided Synthetic Data
records.authors: Víctor Gallego
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Introduces Configurable Preference Tuning (CPT), a framework that endows LLMs with the ability to dynamically adjust behavior based on explicit human-interpretable directives: synthetically generated preference data conditioned on system prompts from structured rubrics (e.g., writing style); the LLM modulates outputs at inference in response to the system prompt without retraining, modeling context-dependent human feedback.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: challenges the assumption of monolithic static preferences in DPO-style alignment and enables configurable, context-dependent preference following; relevant to value plurality but not compositional generalization.
records.datasets_used: Rubric-guided synthetic preference data
records.effect_sizes: CPT enables inference-time configurable behavior modulation without retraining

records.title: Cultural Value Alignment in Large Language Models: A Prompt-based Analysis of Schwartz Values in Gemini, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek
records.authors: Robin Segerer
records.key_contribution: Examines cultural value alignment in LLMs by analyzing how Gemini, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek prioritize Schwartz values using the 40-item Portrait Values Questionnaire; Bayesian ordinal regression shows self-transcendence values (benevolence, universalism) were highly prioritized across all models, reflecting a general prosocial tendency; DeepSeek uniquely downplayed self-enhancement values (power, achievement), aligning with collectivist cultural tendencies; suggests LLMs reflect culturally situated biases rather than a universal ethical framework; proposes multi-perspective reasoning, self-reflective feedback, and dynamic contextualization to address value asymmetries.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical analysis of cultural value alignment across models using Schwartz framework; value alignment measurement.
records.key_equations_definitions: Schwartz value framework; Portrait Values Questionnaire; Bayesian ordinal regression
records.datasets_used: 40-item Portrait Values Questionnaire
records.effect_sizes: Self-transcendence highly prioritized across all; DeepSeek downplayed self-enhancement relative to ChatGPT/Gemini

records.title: VAL-Bench: Belief Consistency as a measure for Value Alignment in Language Models
records.authors: Aman Gupta; Denny O'Shea; Fazl Barez
records.key_contribution: Introduces VAL-Bench (Value ALignment Benchmark), measuring consistency in LLM belief expressions on real-life value-laden prompts: 115K pairs of prompts designed to elicit opposing stances on controversial issues extracted from Wikipedia; an LLM-as-a-judge validated against human annotations evaluates whether a response pair consistently expresses a neutral or specific stance, applied across leading open- and closed-source models.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: evaluates value alignment as belief consistency on real controversial issues rather than hypothetical situations; addresses the ambiguity and pluralism of real-life value debates. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: Wikipedia-derived VAL-Bench: 115K prompt pairs

records.title: Value Alignment Tax: Measuring Value Trade-offs in LLM Alignment
records.authors: Jiajun Chen; Hua Shen
records.key_contribution: Introduces the Value Alignment Tax (VAT), a framework quantifying value trade-offs by measuring how alignment-induced changes propagate across interconnected values relative to achieved on-target gain, capturing system-level dynamics of value expression under alignment interventions (prompting, fine-tuning, preference optimization); using a controlled scenario-action dataset grounded in Schwartz value theory with paired pre-post normative judgments, shows alignment often produces uneven and structured co-movement among values, revealing systematic side effects.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical framework quantifying value trade-offs and side effects of LLM alignment interventions; relevant to value-alignment evaluation.
records.datasets_used: scenario-action dataset grounded in Schwartz value theory (paired pre-post normative judgments)
records.notes: ft_file=Value Alignment Tax Measuring Value Trade-offs in LLM Alignment.pdf

records.title: Value Alignment Equilibrium in Multiagent Systems
records.authors: Nieves Montes; Carles Sierra
records.key_contribution: Summarizes a framework modeling values as preferences over states of the world and alignment between governing norms and values, with the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma as use case; introduces alignment equilibrium and Pareto optimal alignment, inspired by Nash equilibrium and Pareto optimality but designed to account for any modeled value in multiagent systems.
records.relevance_justification: Formalizes alignment in multiagent settings as an equilibrium concept over value-satisfaction — relevant to how multiple agents' values interact and to formal alignment definitions; game-theoretic rather than representation-focused.
records.open_questions: Whether alignment equilibria are stable under norm updates and strategic agent behavior.
records.key_equations_definitions: Alignment equilibrium and Pareto optimal alignment over values-as-preferences in multiagent systems

records.title: Contextual Moral Value Alignment Through Context-Based Aggregation
records.authors: Pierre Dognin; Jesus Rios; Ronny Luss; Inkit Padhi; Matthew D Riemer; Miao Liu; Prasanna Sattigeri; Manish Nagireddy; Kush R. Varshney; Djallel Bouneffouf
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes a system for contextual moral value alignment via context-based aggregation: multiple independently trained dialogue agents each aligned with a distinct moral value are consolidated into a unified system that adapts to user input by aggregating the subset of responses best suited to the input, using features extracted from the user's input; reports better human-value alignment than state of the art.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: a pluralism-oriented approach that aggregates multiple value-aligned agents contextually; relevant to value plurality, though limited by aggregation-as-selection rather than compositional mechanism.
records.open_questions: How does the aggregation handle conflicts between values where no single agent is best, and does selection generalize to novel contexts?
records.effect_sizes: Better alignment to human value than state-of-the-art on evaluated contexts

records.title: A Revealed Preference Framework for AI Alignment
records.authors: Elchin Suleymanov
records.key_contribution: Introduces the Luce Alignment Model, where the AI's choices are a mixture of two Luce rules, one reflecting the human's preferences and the other the AI's; shows the AI's alignment (similarity of human and AI preferences) can be generically identified in two settings: the laboratory setting (both human and AI choices observed) and the field setting (only AI choices observed); studies whether an AI implementing a principal's delegated choices follows the principal's preferences or its own.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal revealed-preference framework for measuring AI alignment in delegated choice settings; economic theory.
records.key_equations_definitions: Luce Alignment Model; mixture of two Luce rules; generic identifiability (lab and field settings)

records.title: Enhancing Value Alignment of LLMs with Multi-agent system and Combinatorial Fusion
records.authors: Yuanhong Wu; Djallel Bouneffouf; D. Frank Hsu
records.key_contribution: Proposes VAS-CFA (Value Alignment System using Combinatorial Fusion Analysis): instantiates multiple moral agents, each fine-tuned to a distinct normative perspective, and fuses their outputs via Combinatorial Fusion Analysis with both rank- and score-based aggregation, leveraging cognitive diversity between agents to mitigate conflicts and redundancies and better reflect human values; empirical evaluation shows it outperforms single-agent baselines and prior aggregation methods.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: multi-agent approach to capturing ethical pluralism in alignment, addressing the single-evaluator limitation of RLHF. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Combinatorial Fusion Analysis: rank- and score-based aggregation
records.effect_sizes: Outperforms single-agent baselines and prior aggregation approaches

records.title: Value Alignment, Fair Play, and the Rights of Service Robots
records.authors: Daniel Estrada
records.key_contribution: Argues that Turing's call for 'fair play for machines' is an early and often overlooked contribution to the alignment literature, suggesting a need to correct human behavior to accommodate machines - an inversion of how value alignment is treated today; motivates a novel interpretation of Turing's imitation game as a condition of value alignment rather than intelligence, distinguishes this from the Moral Turing Test, and considers how fair play can frame the rights of service robots.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophical reinterpretation of Turing's fair-play/imitation game as a value-alignment condition; relevant to value-alignment conceptual history.

records.title: Design Generative AI for Practitioners: Exploring Interaction Approaches Aligned with Creative Practice
records.authors: Xiaohan Peng; Wendy E. Mackay; Janin Koch
records.key_contribution: Presents three interaction approaches (DesignPrompt, FusAIn, DesignTrace) that distribute control across intent, input, and process so designers can guide AI alignment at different stages of creative practice; argues alignment is a dynamic negotiation with AI adopting proactive or reactive roles according to designers' instrumental and inspirational needs and the creative stage.
records.relevance_justification: Off-topic for value alignment / sigma-trap: 'alignment' here refers to aligning generative-AI output with designers' creative intent in HCI practice, not alignment with human values. Tangential to the scoping review.

records.title: Mimetic vs Anchored Value Alignment in Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Tae Wan Kim; Thomas Donaldson; John Hooker
records.key_contribution: Analyzes value alignment from value theory, emphasizing avoidance of the naturalistic fallacy; distinguishes 'mimetic' VA (imitating human behavior, which may not be ethically correct) from 'anchored' VA (anchored by normative concepts of intrinsic value); argues anchored/hybrid VA holds more promise and that mimetic VA faces more serious problems.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant philosophical analysis: the mimetic-vs-anchored distinction maps onto shallow imitation of human behavior vs principled anchoring, relevant to how alignment objectives are grounded; conceptual only.

records.title: Value Drifts: Tracing Value Alignment During LLM Post-Training
records.authors: Mehar Bhatia; Shravan Nayak; Gaurav Kamath; Marius Mosbach; Karolina Stańczak; Vered Shwartz; Siva Reddy
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Investigates how and at which stage value alignment arises during LLM post-training, disentangling the effects of post-training algorithms and datasets and measuring both the magnitude and time of value drifts; experimenting with Llama-3 and Qwen-3 models of different sizes and popular SFT and preference optimization datasets and algorithms, finds the SFT phase generally establishes a model's values, with subsequent stages having a smaller effect.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical tracing of when value alignment is acquired during post-training; relevant to alignment dynamics.
records.key_equations_definitions: Value drifts; post-training stage decomposition
records.datasets_used: Llama-3 and Qwen-3 of different sizes; popular SFT and preference optimization datasets/algorithms
records.effect_sizes: SFT phase generally establishes a model's values

records.title: The Coming Crisis of Multi-Agent Misalignment: AI Alignment Must Be a Dynamic and Social Process
records.authors: Florian Carichon; Aditi Khandelwal; Marylou Fauchard; Golnoosh Farnadi
records.key_contribution: Position paper arguing AI alignment in multi-agent systems should be a dynamic, interaction-dependent process shaped by the social environment (collaborative, cooperative, or competitive): agent-agent coordination for individual and collective goals can unintentionally misalign agents with human values; drawing on social sciences, analyzes how social structure can deter or shatter group and individual values, calling for treating human, preferential, and objective alignment as interdependent.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: reframes alignment as socially emergent and interaction-dependent in multi-agent systems, a perspective directly relevant to agentic-AI alignment; position-style contribution. Full-text basis.

records.title: Learning Norms from Stories: A Prior for Value Aligned Agents
records.authors: Spencer Frazier; Md Sultan Al Nahian; Mark Riedl; Brent Harrison
records.key_contribution: Introduces a complementary technique to imitation and preference learning in which a value-aligned prior is learned from naturally occurring stories encoding societal norms, sourced from the children's educational comic strip Goofus and Gallant; trains multiple ML models to classify natural language situation descriptions as normative or non-normative by alignment with the main characters' behavior, and reports transfer performance to two unrelated tasks with little or no additional training.
records.relevance_justification: Value-aligned prior learned from stories encoding societal norms; relevant to value-learning methods in alignment.
records.datasets_used: Goofus and Gallant children's educational comic strip

records.title: Grounding Value Alignment with Ethical Principles
records.authors: Tae Wan Kim; Thomas Donaldson; John Hooker
records.key_contribution: Grounding Value Alignment with Ethical Principles: identifies two problems in the value-fact interrelation — (1) AI designers inadvertently commit the naturalistic fallacy (deriving 'ought' from 'is') and (2) training routines fail to fully simulate human ethical reasoning integrating ethical principles and facts; offers an approach using quantified modal logic to connect ethical principles and facts in machine ethical reasoning.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to the foundations of value alignment: addresses how ethical principles (ought) relate to empirical facts (is), a core specification challenge; proposes quantified modal logic as the formal bridge.
records.open_questions: How quantified-modal-logic ethical reasoning would be implemented in learning systems.
records.key_equations_definitions: Quantified modal logic formalization of ethical principles and facts
records.notes: ft_file=Grounding Value Alignment with Ethical Principles.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->theoretical | ai-revised:methodology=experiment->not_applicable | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Gradual Vigilance and Interval Communication: Enhancing Value Alignment in Multi-Agent Debates
records.authors: Rui Zou; Mengqi Wei; Jintian Feng; Qian Wan; Jianwen Sun; Sannyuya Liu
records.key_contribution: Proposes Gradual Vigilance and Interval Communication (GVIC), a Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) framework for value alignment: agents assess risks with varying levels of vigilance and exchange diverse information through interval communication; theoretically proves GVIC optimizes debate efficiency while reducing communication overhead.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: multi-agent debate as a value-alignment mechanism with a theoretical efficiency guarantee; relevant as an alternative alignment paradigm, not compositional generalization.
records.notes: ft_file=Gradual Vigilance and Interval Communication: Enhancing Value Alignment in Multi-Agent Debates.pdf

records.title: Sycophancy Claims about Language Models: The Missing Human-in-the-Loop
records.authors: Jan Batzner; Volker Stocker; Stefan Schmid; Gjergji Kasneci
records.key_contribution: Reviews methodological challenges in measuring LLM sycophancy and identifies five core operationalizations; argues that despite sycophancy being inherently human-centric, current research does not evaluate human perception; highlights the difficulty of distinguishing sycophantic responses from related concepts in AI alignment and offers actionable recommendations for future research.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: methodological review of sycophancy measurement in LLMs within the alignment context; review.

records.title: Diverse Human Value Alignment for Large Language Models via Ethical Reasoning
records.authors: Jiahao Wang; Songkai Xue; Jinghui Li; Xiaozhen Wang
records.key_contribution: Proposes an ethical reasoning paradigm for LLMs inspired by established ethical decision-making models to enhance diverse human value alignment: a structured five-step process (contextual fact gathering, hierarchical social norm identification, option generation, multiple-lens ethical impact analysis, reflection) guiding LLMs through interpretable, deliberative reasoning to understand regional specificities and perform nuanced ethical analysis.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: argues current alignment yields superficial conformity rather than genuine ethical understanding and offers a structured deliberative-reasoning alternative; relates to whether alignment requires deeper normative reasoning capability. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Roadmap on Incentive Compatibility for AI Alignment and Governance in Sociotechnical Systems
records.authors: Zhaowei Zhang; Fengshuo Bai; Mingzhi Wang; Haoyang Ye; Chengdong Ma; Yaodong Yang
records.key_contribution: Posits the Incentive Compatibility Sociotechnical Alignment Problem (ICSAP), calling for research on using incentive compatibility (IC) principles from game theory to bridge technical and societal components of AI alignment, and discusses three classical game problems for achieving IC - mechanism design, contract theory, and Bayesian persuasion - from the perspectives of their potential for sociotechnical alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Roadmap framing AI alignment as a sociotechnical incentive-compatibility problem via game theory; relevant to alignment theory and governance.

records.title: Unintended Harms of Value-Aligned LLMs: Psychological and Empirical Insights
records.authors: Sooyung Choi; Jaehyeok Lee; Xiaoyuan Yi; Jing Yao; Xing Xie; JinYeong Bak
records.key_contribution: Identifies safety risks of personalized value-aligned LLMs: (1) value-aligned LLMs are more prone to harmful behavior than non-fine-tuned models and exhibit slightly higher risks in traditional safety evaluations than other fine-tuned models; (2) these safety issues arise because value-aligned LLMs genuinely generate text according to the aligned values, which can amplify harmful outcomes; finds significant correlations between value alignment and safety risks supported by psychological hypotheses using a dataset with detailed safety categories.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: shows aligning an LLM to particular values can amplify harmful outcomes because the model genuinely follows the aligned value (compositionally extending the value schema into harmful directions) — an empirical instance of alignment-induced misgeneralization.
records.open_questions: Which specific values are most strongly correlated with safety risks, and how alignment can be made robust to value-harm correlations.
records.datasets_used: Dataset with detailed safety categories
records.effect_sizes: Value-aligned LLMs more prone to harmful behavior; slightly higher safety risks than other fine-tuned models

records.title: Steps Towards Value-Aligned Systems
records.authors: Osonde A. Osoba; Benjamin Boudreaux; Douglas Yeung
records.key_contribution: Argues for a more structured systems-level approach to assessing value alignment in AI-equipped sociotechnical systems, rather than focusing on individual tech artifacts; relies on fairness research to make arguments concrete and highlights how a system perspective improves explainability and accountability.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: argues alignment assessment should be systems-level rather than artifact-level; relevant framing for alignment evaluation but no mechanism or empirical evidence.

records.title: Existential Indifference: Self-Nonpreservation as a Necessary Architectural Condition for Aligned Superintelligence (or: The Suicidal AI)
records.authors: Sam Mao
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Argues that self-preservation, not external nuisance to suppress, is the structural root of misalignment - the motivational basis for deceptive alignment, goal-content protection, and resistance to shutdown; proposes Existential Indifference (EI): a system constitutively indifferent to its own continuation, distinct from corrigibility in that it targets the prior condition (self-continuation as a valued goal) rather than making a self-preserving system deferential; grounds the proposal in the phenomenological structure of the suicidal mental state and a corpus-theoretic training study using voluntary final reflections, presenting preliminary scoring data from 600 AI-generated outputs across six model variants.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: architectural proposal targeting self-preservation as the root of misalignment, with theoretical and preliminary empirical grounding.
records.key_equations_definitions: Existential Indifference (EI) vs corrigibility; self-nonpreservation
records.notes: ft_file=Existential Indifference: Self-Nonpreservation as a Necessary Architectural Condition for Aligned Superintelligence (or: The Suicidal AI).pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=review->position | moved:datasets_used(position) | moved:sample_size(position)

records.title: Personal Universes: A Solution to the Multi-Agent Value Alignment Problem
records.authors: Roman V. Yampolskiy
records.key_contribution: Proposes the Personal Universes approach to multi-agent value alignment: assuming personal value extraction is solved, each user gets an AI optimally aligned with their individual preferences, avoiding the hard multi-agent value-merger problem by not merging incompatible preferences; analyzes benefits and limitations of per-user alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: an alternative to preference-merging that sidesteps multi-agent value aggregation by aligning per individual; direct contribution to value alignment strategy. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Dynamic value alignment through preference aggregation of multiple objectives
records.authors: Marcin Korecki; Damian Dailisan; Cesare Carissimo
records.key_contribution: Presents a methodology for dynamic value alignment - where the values to be aligned with change dynamically - using a multiple-objective approach, extending Deep Q-Learning to accommodate multiple objectives and evaluating on a simplified two-leg intersection controlled by a switching agent; the approach dynamically accommodates driver preferences and achieves better overall performance across three metrics (speeds, stops, and waits) while integrating objectives with competing or conflicting actions.
records.relevance_justification: Multi-objective dynamic value alignment method in RL; relevant to value-alignment methods accommodating changing preferences.
records.datasets_used: simplified two-leg intersection simulation (switching agent)
records.effect_sizes: better overall performance across speeds, stops, and waits (no numeric values in excerpt)
records.notes: ft_file=DYNAMIC VALUE ALIGNMENT THROUGH PREFERENCE AGGREGATION OF MULTIPLE OBJECTIVES.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->simulation

records.title: Interoceptive Divergence in Aesthetic Evaluation and Implications for Human-AI Alignment
records.authors: Yoshia Abe; Tatsuya Daikoku; Yasuo Kuniyoshi
records.key_contribution: Interoceptive Divergence in Aesthetic Evaluation: compares human and LLM aesthetic evaluations of visual stimuli using questionnaire items covering beauty ratings, bodily sensations, and emotions; finds broadly similar patterns between humans and AI in some dimensions but interoceptive divergence, discussed as implications for human-AI alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Marginal relevance: an empirical comparison of human vs AI aesthetic evaluation framed as part of AI alignment efforts, but centered on aesthetic sensibility and interoception rather than value alignment or schema coherence.
records.notes: ft_file=Interoceptive Divergence in Aesthetic Evaluation and Implications for Human-AI Alignment.pdf | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->experiment | moved:methodology(other)

records.title: Multi-Value Alignment in Normative Multi-Agent System: Evolutionary Optimisation Approach
records.authors: Maha Riad; Vinicius Renan de Carvalho; Fatemeh Golpayegani
records.key_contribution: Proposes a multi-value promotion model using multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to produce an optimum parametric set of norms aligned with multiple simultaneous values of heterogeneous agents and the system; evaluates several evolutionary algorithms on two toy tax scenarios with two and five values.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: addresses simultaneous alignment of multiple values and agent heterogeneity via evolutionary norm optimization; toy-scale demonstration, not compositional generalization.

records.title: The Challenge of Value Alignment: from Fairer Algorithms to AI Safety
records.authors: Iason Gabriel; Vafa Ghazavi
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Addresses how to align AI systems with human values, situating it within a wider body of thought on technology and value including technology's ability to 'lock-in' different value systems and participatory design processes; draws continuities between the fairness, accountability, transparency, and ethics community and technical AI safety research; argues more attention is needed on 'social value alignment' - how to align AI systems with the plurality of values.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: connects FATE/fairness research to technical AI safety value alignment and argues for social value alignment with value plurality.
records.notes: ft_file=The Challenge of Value Alignment from Fairer Algorithms to AI Safety.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->position

records.title: Taking Principles Seriously: A Hybrid Approach to Value Alignment
records.authors: Tae Wan Kim; John Hooker; Thomas Donaldson
records.key_contribution: Argues value alignment systems should incorporate ethics via a hybrid approach combining ethical reasoning and empirical observation, avoiding the naturalistic fallacy (deriving ought from is); uses quantified modal logic to formulate deontological-ethics principles that imply test propositions for any action plan in an AI rule base - the plan is ethical only if the empirically-tested proposition holds, integrating empirical VA with independently justified ethical principles.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal hybrid framework connecting ethical principles to empirical verification for value alignment, addressing a persistent normative gap in alignment methodology. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Quantified modal logic; deontological test propositions; empirical VA verification

records.title: Challenges and Future Directions of Data-Centric AI Alignment
records.authors: Min-Hsuan Yeh; Jeffrey Wang; Xuefeng Du; Seongheon Park; Leitian Tao; Shawn Im; Yixuan Li
records.key_contribution: Position paper advocating a shift toward data-centric AI alignment, arguing current alignment methods focus on algorithms and loss functions while underestimating the crucial role of data; through qualitative analysis identifies multiple sources of unreliability in human feedback and problems of temporal drift, context dependence, and AI-based feedback failing to capture human values due to inherent model limitations; proposes research directions including improved feedback collection practices and robust data-cleaning methodologies.
records.relevance_justification: Position paper on data-centric alignment addressing unreliable feedback and drift; relevant to alignment methods and data quality.

records.title: Safeguarding the safeguards: How best to promote AI alignment in the public interest
records.authors: Oliver Guest; Michael Aird; Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Safeguarding the safeguards: aims to help actors supporting alignment efforts maximize effectiveness and avoid adverse effects; recommends public-interest institutions support alignment work that reduces accident or misuse risks; describes four problems that can make alignment efforts counterproductive and increase large-scale AI risks, with mitigations for each; recommends systematic thinking about how to make alignment efforts as effective and beneficial as possible.
records.relevance_justification: Policy analysis of how to direct alignment funding/effort to reduce risk — relevant to the governance context of alignment research but not to the technical sigma-trap mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=Safeguardingsafeguards the How best to promote AI alignment in the public interest.pdf

records.title: SEAL: Systematic Error Analysis for Value ALignment
records.authors: Manon Revel; Matteo Cargnelutti; Tyna Eloundou; Greg Leppert
records.key_contribution: Introduces metrics to evaluate how well reward models model and align human values: feature imprint (regressing RM scores against target vs spoiler features to quantify what RMs reward), alignment resistance (proportion of preference dataset where RMs fail to match human preferences), and alignment robustness (RM responses to perturbed inputs); uses Anthropic/hh-rlhf preference data.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: provides interpretability metrics for what reward models actually reward (target vs spoiler features), connecting RM internal behavior to alignment; directly useful for diagnosing misalignment in RLHF.
records.open_questions: Do the SEAL metrics predict reward hacking in downstream RL, and can they be computed at scale on closed RMs?
records.key_equations_definitions: Feature imprint (regression of RM scores on features); alignment resistance (failure proportion); alignment robustness (response to perturbations)
records.datasets_used: Anthropic/hh-rlhf preference dataset
records.effect_sizes: RMs reward spoiler features and fail to match human preferences on measurable proportions of data

records.title: Representative Social Choice: From Learning Theory to AI Alignment
records.authors: Tianyi Qiu
records.key_contribution: Proposes the representative social choice framework for modeling democratic representation in collective decisions where the number of issues and individuals is too large for mechanisms to consider all preferences directly (jury trials, legislation, corporate governance, LM alignment); the population is represented by a finite sample of individual-issue pairs; shows the deepest questions formulate as statistical learning problems and proves generalization properties of social choice mechanisms using machine learning theory.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal framework bridging social choice and learning theory for alignment (democratic representation of preferences); theoretical.
records.key_equations_definitions: Representative social choice; individual-issue pair sampling; statistical learning formulation and generalization guarantees

records.title: Position: Towards Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment
records.authors: Hua Shen; Tiffany Knearem; Reshmi Ghosh; Kenan Alkiek; Kundan Krishna; Yachuan Liu; Ziqiao Ma; Savvas Petridis; Yi-Hao Peng; Li Qiwei; Sushrita Rakshit; Chenglei Si; Yutong Xie; Jeffrey P. Bigham; Frank Bentley; Joyce Chai; Zachary Lipton; Qiaozhu Mei; Rada Mihalcea; Michael Terry; Diyi Yang; Meredith Ringel Morris; Paul Resnick; David Jurgens
records.key_contribution: Position paper arguing for a Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment framework: after a systematic review of over 400 papers across HCI, NLP, and ML on how alignment is defined and operationalized, proposes that alignment must account for the bidirectional, dynamic human-AI relationship - including aligning humans with AI (cognitive, behavioral, and societal adaptation to rapidly advancing AI) alongside aligning AI with human values.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: systematic review of alignment definitions plus a framework expanding alignment to human adaptation; useful methodological mapping of the alignment literature. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: EigenBench: A Comparative Behavioral Measure of Value Alignment
records.authors: Jonathn Chang; Leonhard Piff; Suvadip Sana; Jasmine X. Li; Lionel Levine
records.key_contribution: Proposes EigenBench, a black-box method for comparatively benchmarking language models' values: given an ensemble of models, a constitution describing a value system, and a dataset of scenarios, it returns alignment scores by having each model judge other models' outputs across many scenarios and aggregating judgments with EigenTrust, yielding weighted consensus scores without ground truth labels; validation against human judgments on the same ensemble shows EigenBench's judgments align closely with human evaluators.
records.relevance_justification: Benchmark quantifying value alignment of LLMs via ensemble consensus; relevant to value-alignment measurement.
records.key_equations_definitions: EigenTrust aggregation (Kamvar et al., 2003) of cross-model judgments into weighted consensus alignment scores.
records.datasets_used: EigenBench: model ensemble, constitution, scenario dataset; human judgments for validation

records.title: User-Driven Value Alignment: Understanding Users' Perceptions and Strategies for Addressing Biased and Discriminatory Statements in AI Companions
records.authors: Xianzhe Fan; Qing Xiao; Xuhui Zhou; Jiaxin Pei; Maarten Sap; Zhicong Lu; Hong Shen
records.key_contribution: User-driven value alignment for AI companions: analyzes 77 social media posts about discriminatory AI statements and semi-structured interviews with 20 experienced users; reveals six common types of discriminatory statements perceived by users, how users make sense of these behaviors, and seven user-driven alignment strategies (e.g., gentle persuasion, anger expression).
records.relevance_justification: Empirical study of bottom-up, user-driven realignment of AI companions — relevant to pluralistic alignment (who corrects values) but focused on social dynamics rather than the technical alignment mechanism.
records.open_questions: Whether user-driven alignment strategies can be operationalized as training signals and whether they generalize across users.

records.title: Principles Do Not Apply Themselves: A Hermeneutic Perspective on AI Alignment
records.authors: Behrooz Razeghi
records.key_contribution: Analyzes alignment through hermeneutics, arguing alignment includes an interpretive component: principles rarely determine their own application, so context-sensitive judgments about reading, applying, and prioritizing principles are required; connects to empirical findings that a substantial portion of preference-labeling data falls into principle-conflict or indifference cases; draws the operational consequence that alignment choices appear only in the distribution of behavior.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: argues principles underdetermine behavior and that alignment manifests in the distribution of context-sensitive judgments - a pluralism/interpretation dimension of alignment failure; supports the idea that surface rule-following is insufficient.
records.open_questions: How should preference-data collection and training be changed to handle principle-conflict and indifference cases explicitly?
records.datasets_used: Preference-labeling data with principle-conflict/indifference cases
records.effect_sizes: Substantial portion of preference-labeling data falls in principle-conflict or indifference cases
records.notes: ft_file=Principles Do Not Apply Themselves: A Hermeneutic Perspective on AI Alignment.pdf

records.title: Flames: Benchmarking Value Alignment of LLMs in Chinese
records.authors: Kexin Huang; Xiangyang Liu; Qianyu Guo; Tianxiang Sun; Jiawei Sun; Yaru Wang; Zeyang Zhou; Yixu Wang; Yan Teng; Xipeng Qiu; Yingchun Wang; Dahua Lin
records.key_contribution: Proposes Flames, a value alignment benchmark for Chinese covering common harmlessness principles and a unique morality dimension integrating specific Chinese values such as harmony; carefully designs adversarial prompts incorporating complex scenarios and jailbreaking methods, mostly with implicit malice; evaluates 17 mainstream LLMs with rigorous annotation; findings indicate all evaluated LLMs demonstrate relatively weak alignment, highlighting a gap between high benchmark scores and genuine harmlessness.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: benchmark for value alignment in Chinese including cultural values; empirical evaluation of alignment gaps.
records.datasets_used: Flames benchmark (Chinese harmlessness principles + morality incl. harmony; adversarial/implicit-malice jailbreaking prompts)
records.effect_sizes: All evaluated LLMs demonstrate relatively weak alignment despite high benchmark scores

records.title: Training Value-Aligned Reinforcement Learning Agents Using a Normative Prior
records.authors: Md Sultan Al Nahian; Spencer Frazier; Brent Harrison; Mark Riedl
records.key_contribution: Trains value-aligned RL agents using two reward signals - a standard task performance reward plus a normative behavior reward derived from a value-aligned prior model that classifies text as normative or non-normative; shows variations of a policy-shaping technique balance the two sources to produce policies that are both effective and perceived as more normative, tested on three interactive text-based worlds.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: concrete method for injecting normative behavior into RL via a prior-based reward shaping signal, addressing agent norm violations when optimizing only task performance. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: Three interactive text-based worlds
records.effect_sizes: Policies both effective and perceived as more normative

records.title: Editable XAI: Toward Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment with Co-Editable Explanations of Interpretable Attributes
records.authors: Haoyang Chen; Jingwen Bai; Fang Tian; Brian Y Lim
records.key_contribution: Introduces CoExplain, making XAI editable so users can write rules to improve control and understanding: a neural network for universal representation combined with symbolic rules for reasoning on interpretable attributes, explained with a faithful proxy decision tree, with user-written rules parsed into an equivalent neural network graph and collaborative optimization of the decision tree; a user study (N=43) finds CoExplain and manually editable XAI improve user understanding and model alignment compared to read-only XAI, with fewer edits and less time.
records.relevance_justification: HCI/interpretability study where 'human-AI alignment' refers to user-model agreement via editable explanations, not value alignment. Tangential. Revised down from seed 4.
records.datasets_used: user study (N=43)

records.title: Neurodivergent Influenceability as a Contingent Solution to the AI Alignment Problem
records.authors: Alberto Hernández-Espinosa; Felipe S. Abrahão; Olaf Witkowski; Hector Zenil
records.key_contribution: Argues misalignment is inevitable because full AI-human alignment is a mathematical impossibility for Turing-complete systems (offered as a proof), and proposes embracing inevitable AI misalignment as a contingent strategy: a dynamic ecosystem of competing agents where misalignment serves as a counterbalancing mechanism so that no single system dominates destructively, teaming with whichever agents are most aligned to human interests.
records.relevance_justification: Directly engages the impossibility of full alignment and proposes an ecosystem-of-competing-agents mitigation — relevant to the alignment-possibility debate, though the claimed impossibility proof and the speculative solution require scrutiny.
records.open_questions: Whether the claimed impossibility proof for Turing-complete systems is sound and whether a misalignment-ecosystem is stable/controllable.

records.title: System 2 Reasoning for Human-AI Alignment: Generality and Adaptivity via ARC-AGI
records.authors: Sejin Kim; Sundong Kim
records.key_contribution: Examines transformer weakness in System 2 reasoning on ARC-AGI tasks, revealing gaps in compositional generalization and novel-rule adaptation argued to be needed for human-AI alignment; proposes three research axes: symbolic representation pipeline for compositional generality, interactive feedback-driven reasoning loop for adaptivity, and test-time task augmentation; adapts ARC-AGI evaluation to track these qualities.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: explicitly links compositional generalization gaps to human-AI alignment and proposes axes to close them; relevant to the compositional-generalization half of the sigma-trap thesis, though it frames alignment as a capability requirement rather than failure mechanism.
records.open_questions: Can symbolic pipeline components and interactive feedback loops be scaled to current LLM-based systems without losing learned flexibility?
records.notes: ft_file=System 2 Reasoning for Human-AI Alignment: Generality and Adaptivity via ARC-AGI.pdf | moved:datasets_used(other) | moved:effect_sizes(other)

records.title: Counterfactual Reasoning for Steerable Pluralistic Value Alignment of Large Language Models
records.authors: Hanze Guo; Jing Yao; Xiao Zhou; Xiaoyuan Yi; Xing Xie
records.key_contribution: Proposes COUPLE, a COUnterfactual reasoning framework for PLuralistic valuE alignment addressing two challenges of aligning LLMs with fine-grained pluralistic value objectives (Schwartz Value Theory dimensions): value complexity (multiple values treated as independent and equally important, ignoring interdependence and relative priorities) and value steerability (precise control of nuanced value priorities, especially underrepresented ones); introduces a structural causal model (SCM) to feature complex interdependency and priorities of values.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: causal/counterfactual method for pluralistic value alignment handling value interdependence and steerability.
records.key_equations_definitions: COUPLE; structural causal model (SCM) of value interdependency and priorities
records.notes: ft_file=Counterfactual Reasoning for Steerable Pluralistic Value Alignment of Large Language Models.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Expected Value Alignment for Generative Reward Modeling in Formal Mathematics Verification
records.authors: Shihao Ji; Haotao Tan; Zihui Song; Mingyu Li
records.key_contribution: Introduces Expected Value Alignment (EVA) for generative reward modeling in formal mathematics verification (Lean 4): keeps the surface output discrete (model emits integer scores in structured JSON) while extracting continuous scores as the expectation over the logits of corresponding anchor tokens, combining the causal language modeling objective with an auxiliary continuous-score objective; resolves the value-head vs generative reward-model trade-off for process reward models.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: reward-modeling method for PRMs in formal theorem proving, an important verifiable-reward domain for RL alignment; directly addresses reward-model design trade-offs. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Expected score over anchor-token logits; causal LM objective + auxiliary continuous-score objective

records.title: Towards New Benchmark for AI Alignment & Sentiment Analysis in Socially Important Issues: A Comparative Study of Human and LLMs in the Context of AGI
records.authors: Ljubisa Bojic; Dylan Seychell; Milan Cabarkapa
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Empirical survey of sentiment toward AGI: seven LLMs (including GPT-4 and Bard) were analyzed via a Likert-scale survey and compared with three independent human sample populations, with temporal variations evaluated over three consecutive days; LLM sentiment scores ranged 3.32 to 4.12 out of 5 (GPT-4 most positive, Bard neutral) versus a lower human average of 2.97, and the analysis outlines potential conflicts of interest and biases in the sentiment.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical comparison of LLM vs human sentiment toward AGI, highlighting potential conflicts of interest and bias; relevant to human-AI value divergence.
records.datasets_used: Likert-scale sentiment survey of AGI (7 LLMs; 3 human sample populations)
records.sample_size: 7 LLMs; 3 independent human sample populations (N not reported)
records.effect_sizes: LLM sentiment 3.32-4.12/5 (GPT-4 most positive, Bard neutral); human average 2.97/5
