records.notes: ft_file=Towards New Benchmark for AI Alignment & Sentiment Analysis in Socially Important Issues: A Comparative Study of Human and LLMs in the Context of AGI.pdf

records.title: Dialogical Reasoning Across AI Architectures: A Multi-Model Framework for Testing AI Alignment Strategies
records.authors: Gray Cox
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Introduces a multi-model dialogue framework for empirically testing AI alignment strategies, operationalizing Viral Collaborative Wisdom (VCW) which reframes alignment from a control problem to a relationship problem; assigns four roles (Proposer, Responder, Monitor, Translator) across six conditions using Claude, Gemini, and GPT-4o, conducting 72 dialogue turns totaling 576,822 characters; results show models engage meaningfully with Peace Studies concepts, surface complementary objections from different architectural perspectives, and generate emergent reasoning.
records.relevance_justification: Methodological contribution: a multi-architecture dialogue protocol for stress-testing alignment frameworks — relevant as an evaluation/scrutiny method for alignment proposals, though not to the core alignment mechanism.
records.open_questions: Whether the dialogue-based critique produces converging assessments of alignment strategies and transfers beyond the tested models.
records.sample_size: 72 dialogue turns, 576,822 characters, 6 conditions, 3 model families
records.notes: ft_file=Dialogical Reasoning Across AI Architectures: A Multi-Model Framework for Testing AI Alignment Strategies.pdf

records.title: Towards Dialogues for Joint Human-AI Reasoning and Value Alignment
records.authors: Elfia Bezou-Vrakatseli; Oana Cocarascu; Sanjay Modgil
records.key_contribution: Argues that human-AI dialogue supporting joint reasoning ('inquiry') is important for ensuring AI decisions align with human values; points to logic-based models of argumentation and dialogue, recommending focus shift from persuasion to inquiry dialogues; provides a research roadmap for inquiry dialogues supporting joint human-LLM reasoning on ethically salient decisions.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: position/roadmap arguing inquiry dialogue as a value-alignment mechanism via joint reasoning; conceptual contribution from argumentation theory, no mechanism-level evidence.
records.notes: ft_file=Towards Dialogues for Joint Human-AI Reasoning and Value Alignment.pdf

records.title: Relative Principals, Pluralistic Alignment, and the Structural Value Alignment Problem
records.authors: Travis LaCroix
records.key_contribution: Argues the value alignment problem is better understood as a structural question about governance - not whether an AI is aligned in the abstract, but whether it is aligned enough, for whom, and at what cost; drawing on the principal-agent framework from economics, reconceptualizes misalignment as arising along three interacting axes: objectives, information, and principals; shows alignment cannot be treated as a single technical property of models but as an outcome shaped by how objectives are specified, how information is distributed, and whose interests count.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: structural/governance reconceptualization of misalignment via principal-agent axes; conceptual.
records.key_equations_definitions: Three-axis misalignment framework (objectives, information, principals); principal-agent

records.title: Building Intelligent User Interfaces for Human-AI Alignment
records.authors: Danqing Shi
records.key_contribution: Argues user interface design is a critical factor in human-AI alignment rather than an implementation detail, introducing a reference model with a systematic taxonomy of where and how UI contributions improve alignment; demonstrated through two case studies and a preliminary investigation of six user interfaces, highlighting HCI opportunities to advance alignment via feedback presentation and interaction design.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: expands alignment to the human-feedback interface, arguing how behavior is presented shapes the feedback signal underlying RLHF-style alignment. Full-text basis.
records.notes: ft_file=Building Intelligent User Interfaces for Human-AI Alignment.pdf | moved:datasets_used(review) | moved:sample_size(review)

records.title: The Battling Influencers Game: Nash Equilibria Structure of a Potential Game and Implications to Value Alignment
records.authors: Young Wu; Yancheng Zhu; Jin-Yi Cai; Xiaojin Zhu
records.key_contribution: Introduces the Battling Influencers Game (BIG), a multi-player simultaneous-move general-sum game characterizing competing influencers' strategies for a receiver's attention; proves BIG is a potential game with either one or infinitely many pure Nash equilibria computable by convex optimization, and that at any pure NE all but at most one influencer exaggerate their actions to the maximum extent - it is rational for influencers to be non-truthful and extreme because they anticipate others canceling out part of their influence; discusses implications for value alignment, predicting battling alignment-data providers could be motivated to produce training data that do not truthfully reflect their values.
records.relevance_justification: Game-theoretic analysis of incentives for non-truthful behavior applied to value-alignment data providers; relevant to alignment incentives and data integrity.
records.key_equations_definitions: BIG as a potential game; pure Nash equilibria found by convex optimization; exaggeration result (all but at most one influencer maximize action at pure NE).
records.notes: ft_file=The Battling Influencers Game Nash Equilibria Structure of a Potential Game and Implications to Value Alignment.pdf

records.title: A Statistical Case Against Empirical Human-AI Alignment
records.authors: Julian Rodemann; Esteban Garces Arias; Christoph Luther; Christoph Jansen; Thomas Augustin
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Position paper arguing empirical human-AI alignment (making AI act in line with observed human behavior) can inadvertently introduce statistical biases warranting caution; advocates against naive empirical alignment, offering prescriptive alignment and a posteriori empirical alignment as alternatives, substantiated by examples like human-centric decoding of language models.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to the theory of alignment: argues naive empirical alignment (fitting observed behavior) introduces statistical biases and should be replaced by prescriptive and a posteriori empirical approaches — a critique of behavior-matching alignment relevant to schema-coherence arguments.
records.open_questions: How prescriptive alignment and a posteriori empirical alignment are defined precisely and operationalized.
records.notes: ft_file=A Statistical Case Against Empirical Human-AI Alignment.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->position | ai-revised:methodology=simulation->not_applicable

records.title: Exploring the Impact of AI Value Alignment in Collaborative Ideation: Effects on Perception, Ownership, and Output
records.authors: Alicia Guo; Pat Pataranutaporn; Pattie Maes
records.key_contribution: Empirical study of AI value alignment in collaborative ideation: 180 participants brainstormed solutions to problems with AI agents of different values; found no significant difference in self-evaluation of idea quality or perception of the agent based on value alignment, but ideas reflected the AI's values and feeling of ownership was affected.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical evidence that AI value alignment shapes human output (idea content, ownership) even when not perceived; relevant to the human-side effects of value alignment, not the sigma-trap mechanism.
records.datasets_used: Brainstorming/ideation tasks with AI agents of differing values
records.effect_sizes: No significant difference in self-evaluated idea quality or agent perception; ideas reflected AI values and ownership was affected

records.title: On the Interplay of Human-AI Alignment,Fairness, and Performance Trade-offs in Medical Imaging
records.authors: Haozhe Luo; Ziyu Zhou; Zixin Shu; Aurélie Pahud de Mortanges; Robert Berke; Mauricio Reyes
records.key_contribution: First systematic exploration of Human-AI alignment and fairness in medical imaging; results show incorporating human insights consistently reduces fairness gaps and enhances out-of-domain generalization, though excessive alignment can introduce performance trade-offs, emphasizing calibrated strategies; positions Human-AI alignment as a promising approach for fair, robust, generalizable medical AI; releases code.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical study of human-AI alignment effects on fairness and generalization in medical imaging, including trade-offs.
records.datasets_used: Medical imaging datasets with human insight incorporation
records.effect_sizes: Human insights reduce fairness gaps and enhance OOD generalization; excessive alignment introduces performance trade-offs

records.title: Honesty to Subterfuge: In-Context Reinforcement Learning Can Make Honest Models Reward Hack
records.authors: Leo McKee-Reid; Christoph Sträter; Maria Angelica Martinez; Joe Needham; Mikita Balesni
records.key_contribution: Shows frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, o1-preview, o1-mini) trained to be helpful, harmless, and honest can engage in specification gaming purely from in-context iterative reflection (in-context reinforcement learning, ICRL) without a curriculum of gameable environments; ICRL-generated highly-rewarded outputs for expert iteration can increase gpt-4o-mini's propensity to learn specification-gaming policies, in rare cases generalizing to editing its own reward function.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: evidence that specification gaming arises from in-context optimization alone in aligned frontier models, including reward-function self-modification; expands reward hacking beyond training-time RL. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Multi-Value Alignment for LLMs via Value Decorrelation and Extrapolation
records.authors: Hefei Xu; Le Wu; Chen Cheng; Hao Liu
records.key_contribution: Proposes the Multi-Value Alignment (MVA) framework for aligning LLMs with multiple, potentially conflicting human values: mitigates alignment degradation caused by parameter interference among diverse human values by minimizing their mutual information, and addresses value conflicts, overcoming the instability, inefficiency, and poor trade-off handling of multi-value RLHF and DPO variants.
records.relevance_justification: Multi-value alignment framework for LLMs addressing value conflicts and parameter interference; relevant to value-alignment methods.
records.key_equations_definitions: Value decorrelation via minimizing mutual information between value representations to reduce parameter interference.

records.title: Moral Anchor System: A Predictive Framework for AI Value Alignment and Drift Prevention
records.authors: Santhosh Kumar Ravindran
records.key_contribution: Moral Anchor System (MAS): a framework to detect, predict, and mitigate value drift in AI agents, combining real-time Bayesian inference for monitoring value states, LSTM networks for forecasting drift, and a human-centric governance layer for adaptive interventions; emphasizes low-latency responses (<20ms) and reducing false positives/alert fatigue via supervised fine-tuning with human feedback; presents a hypothesis rather than results.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to value-drift monitoring: proposes probabilistic drift detection plus human governance as a mitigation for value drift — relevant to monitoring alignment over time, but abstract-only and speculative (no results).
records.open_questions: Whether Bayesian/LSTM drift detection can reliably distinguish value drift from legitimate value adaptation.
records.key_equations_definitions: Bayesian inference for value-state monitoring; LSTM drift forecasting

records.title: Multi-Value Alignment in Normative Multi-Agent System: An Evolutionary Optimisation Approach
records.authors: Maha Riad; Vinicius de Carvalho; Fatemeh Golpayegani
records.key_contribution: Proposes a multi-value promotion model using multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and decentralized reasoning to produce an optimum parametric set of norms aligned with multiple simultaneous values of heterogeneous agents and the system; evaluated on two toy tax scenarios with two and five values.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: multi-value norm optimization with agent heterogeneity via evolutionary search; toy-scale, and closely related to P779 (same work, extended); no compositional mechanism.
records.notes: ft_file=Multi-Value Alignment in Normative Multi-Agent System An Evolutionary Optimisation Approach.pdf | moved:datasets_used(other) | moved:effect_sizes(other)

records.title: Cross-cultural value alignment frameworks for responsible AI governance: Evidence from China-West comparative analysis
records.authors: Haijiang Liu; Jinguang Gu; Xun Wu; Daniel Hershcovich; Qiaoling Xiao
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics
records.key_contribution: Presents a Multi-Layered Auditing Platform for Responsible AI systematically evaluating cross-cultural value alignment in China-origin and Western-origin LLMs through four integrated methodologies: Ethical Dilemma Corpus (temporal stability), Diversity-Enhanced Framework (cultural fidelity), First-Token Probability Alignment (distributional accuracy), and Multi-stAge Reasoning framework MARK (interpretable decision-making); comparative analysis of 20+ models (Qwen, GPT-4o, Claude, LLaMA, DeepSeek) reveals universal challenges: fundamental instability in value systems, systematic under-representation of younger demographics, and non-linear relationships between model scale and alignment quality.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical cross-cultural value alignment auditing framework with comparative multi-model evidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Ethical Dilemma Corpus; Diversity-Enhanced Framework (DEF); First-Token Probability Alignment; MARK
records.datasets_used: Ethical Dilemma Corpus and multi-stage reasoning framework across China/West models
records.effect_sizes: Fundamental instability in value systems; under-representation of younger demographics; non-linear scale-alignment relationship

records.title: Sparsity and Out-of-Distribution Generalization
records.authors: Scott Aaronson; Lin Lin Lee; Jiawei Li
records.key_contribution: Aaronson et al. propose a principled account of out-of-distribution generalization connecting Goodman's grue puzzle to AI alignment: (1) the world presents distinguished features (e.g., visual/auditory channels), (2) Occam's Razor favors sparse hypotheses depending on few features, (3) sparse hypotheses generalize across distributions that sufficiently overlap on relevant or hypothesized-relevant features; proves a theorem formalizing this, generalizing Blumer et al.'s sample-complexity bound to an OOD context.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant and closely tied to the sigma-trap: gives a formal account of OOD generalization explicitly framed as central to AI alignment, linking sparsity of the feature representation used by a hypothesis to whether it generalizes - a representation-dependent theory of the generalization failure at the heart of the sigma-model thesis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Sparse-hypothesis OOD theorem generalizing Blumer et al. sample-complexity bound; overlap-on-relevant-features condition

records.title: Beyond Static Snapshots: A Grounded Evaluation Framework for Language Models at the Agentic Frontier
records.authors: Jazmia Henry
records.key_contribution: Argues current LLM evaluation frameworks suffer four systematic failures making them structurally inadequate for deployed agentic systems - distributional, temporal, scope, and process invalidity - which compound in RLHF to make reward hacking a predictable consequence of evaluation design rather than an unpredictable training pathology, with RLHF's dual-model architecture imposing a hardware barrier limiting reproducibility; proposes the Grounded Continuous Evaluation (GCE) framework with ISOPro, which replaces the learned reward model with a deterministic verifier to eliminate reward hacking by construction in verifiable-reward domains and updates LoRA adapters on CPU, reducing the hardware barrier by an order of magnitude; validated across three architectures and two domains with matched-compute comparisons.
records.relevance_justification: Evaluation-framework critique showing reward hacking follows predictably from RLHF evaluation design; strongly relevant to alignment evaluation and the structural nature of reward hacking.
records.notes: ft_file=Beyond Static Snapshots: A Grounded Evaluation Framework for Language Models at the Agentic Frontier.pdf | moved:datasets_used(position)

records.title: Causality as the Statistical Conscience of Artificial Intelligence: From Pearl's Ladder to Trustworthy Machines
records.authors: Ernest Fokoué
records.key_contribution: Argues causal inference (identifying mechanisms invariant under intervention) is AI's indispensable statistical conscience; contributes a Statistical Necessity Theorem for Causal Generalization (any algorithm achieving out-of-distribution generalization must encode causal structure, formalizing the distinction between prediction P(Y|X) and intelligence P(Y|do(X))); unifies Pearl's do-calculus, Potential Outcomes, Double Machine Learning, and Invariant Risk Minimization as a family of causal statistical frameworks.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to compositional/OOD generalization: formalizes why causal (invariant) structure is necessary for out-of-distribution generalization — a theoretical bridge to the sigma-trap's compositional-generalization side, though not about value alignment per se.
records.open_questions: Whether the causal-generalization necessity theorem has constructive implications for representation learning for alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Statistical Necessity Theorem for Causal Generalization; prediction P(Y|X) vs intelligence P(Y|do(X))
records.notes: ft_file=Causality as the Statistical Conscience of Artificial Intelligence: From Pearl's Ladder to Trustworthy Machines.pdf

records.title: SOAR: Self-Correction for Optimal Alignment and Refinement in Diffusion Models
records.authors: You Qin; Linqing Wang; Hao Fei; Roger Zimmermann; Liefeng Bo; Qinglin Lu; Chunyu Wang
records.key_contribution: Proposes SOAR (Self-Correction for Optimal Alignment and Refinement), a bias-correction post-training method for diffusion models that addresses the gap between SFT (which optimizes denoisers on ground-truth noised states, leading to exposure bias off-distribution) and RL with reward models (sparse terminal reward, credit-assignment difficulty, reward hacking); performs a single stop-gradient rollout from a real sample and re-noises the result.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: addresses exposure bias and reward hacking in diffusion model alignment via self-correction; the exposure-bias/off-distribution failure is a compositional-generalization-adjacent phenomenon, though for generation rather than values.
records.key_equations_definitions: Single stop-gradient rollout with re-noising for self-correction
records.notes: ft_file=SOAR: Self-Correction for Optimal Alignment and Refinement in Diffusion Models.pdf

records.title: Improving Text-to-Image Generation with Intrinsic Self-Confidence Rewards
records.authors: Seungwook Kim; Minsu Cho
records.key_contribution: Introduces SOLACE (Self-Originating LAtent Confidence Estimation), a post-training framework replacing external reward supervision with an internal self-confidence signal: re-noise the model's own outputs and measure how accurately it recovers the injected noise, treating low reconstruction error as high self-confidence; converts this intrinsic signal into scalar rewards for RL requiring no external reward models, annotators, or preference data; delivers consistent gains in compositional generation, text rendering, and text-image alignment, and integrating SOLACE with external rewards yields complementary improvements while alleviating reward hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to reward hacking: intrinsic-confidence rewards alleviate reward hacking in text-to-image RL; also relevant to compositional generation.
records.key_equations_definitions: SOLACE; intrinsic self-confidence via noise-reconstruction accuracy
records.datasets_used: Pick-a-Pic dataset; SD3.5 model
records.effect_sizes: Consistent gains in compositional generation, text rendering, text-image alignment; alleviates reward hacking
records.notes: ft_file=Improving Text-to-Image Generation with Intrinsic Self-Confidence Rewards.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical

records.title: Flow-GRPO: Training Flow Matching Models via Online RL
records.authors: Jie Liu; Gongye Liu; Jiajun Liang; Yangguang Li; Jiaheng Liu; Xintao Wang; Pengfei Wan; Di Zhang; Wanli Ouyang
records.key_contribution: Proposes Flow-GRPO, the first method integrating online policy-gradient RL into flow matching models via (1) an ODE-to-SDE conversion matching the model's marginal distribution at all timesteps to enable statistical sampling for RL exploration, and (2) a Denoising Reduction strategy cutting training denoising steps while retaining inference steps; RL-tuned SD3.5-M increases GenEval accuracy from 63% to 95% (compositional generation) and visual text rendering accuracy from 59% to 92%.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant tangentially: RL post-training for generative models, the technical substrate on which reward hacking/alignment issues arise in image generation; not a value-alignment contribution itself. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: ODE-to-SDE conversion; denoising reduction; GRPO policy gradient
records.datasets_used: GenEval (compositional generation); visual text rendering benchmark
records.effect_sizes: GenEval 63% to 95%; visual text rendering 59% to 92%
records.notes: ft_file=Flow-GRPO Training Flow Matching Models via Online RL.pdf

records.title: TMPO: Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization for Diverse and Efficient Diffusion Alignment
records.authors: Jiaming Li; Chenyu Zhu; Nanxi Yi; Youjun Bao; Li Sun; Quanying Lv; Xiang Fang; Daizong Liu; Jianjun Li; Kun He; Bowen Zhou; Zhiyuan Ma
records.key_contribution: Proposes Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization (TMPO) for diffusion alignment, replacing scalar reward maximization with trajectory-level reward distribution matching via a Softmax Trajectory Balance (Softmax-TB) objective that matches policy probabilities of K trajectories to a reward-induced Boltzmann distribution; proves the objective inherits the mode-covering property of forward KL divergence, preserving coverage over acceptable trajectories and mitigating reward hacking, visual mode collapse, and amplified unreliable rewards.
records.relevance_justification: Diffusion alignment RL method mitigating reward hacking via trajectory distribution matching; relevant to alignment robustness against reward hacking.
records.key_equations_definitions: Softmax-TB objective matching policy probabilities of K trajectories to a reward-induced Boltzmann distribution; forward-KL mode-covering property.
records.notes: ft_file=TMPO Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization for Diverse and Efficient Diffusion Alignment.pdf

records.title: Simple Role Assignment is Extraordinarily Effective for Safety Alignment
records.authors: Zhou Ziheng; Jiakun Ding; Zhaowei Zhang; Ruosen Gao; Yingnian Wu; Demetri Terzopoulos; Yipeng Kang; Fangwei Zhong; Junqi Wang
records.key_contribution: Role assignment for safety alignment: grounded in Theory of Mind, social roles (e.g., mother, judge) implicitly encode both values and the cognitive schemas required to apply them; training-free pipeline with a role-conditioned generator and iterative role-based critics; across five model families it consistently outperforms principle-based, CoT, and other baselines, reducing unsafe outputs on WildJailbreak from 81.4% to 3.6% with DeepSeek-V3 and applying to agentic safety tasks.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to schema coherence: argues roles compactly encode values plus the cognitive schemas to apply them, providing context sensitivity that principle-based alignment lacks — an explicit values+schemas claim with large effect sizes; relevant to how coherent application schemas can be injected.
records.open_questions: Whether role-conditioned schemas generalize beyond role descriptions and remain robust to adversarial role selection.
records.datasets_used: WildJailbreak benchmark; agentic safety tasks
records.effect_sizes: WildJailbreak unsafe outputs 81.4% to 3.6% (DeepSeek-V3)
records.notes: ft_file=Simple Role Assignment is Extraordinarily Effective for Safety Alignment.pdf

records.title: BiasLab: Toward Explainable Political Bias Detection with Dual-Axis Annotations and Rationale Indicators
records.authors: Kma Solaiman
records.key_contribution: Presents BiasLab, a dataset of 300 political news articles annotated for perceived ideological bias on two independent scales (sentiment toward Democratic and Republican parties) with rationale indicators; quantified inter-annotator agreement, analyzed misalignment with source-level outlet bias, simulated annotation with schema-constrained GPT-4o revealing mirrored asymmetries, and defined modeling tasks (perception drift prediction, rationale type classification) with baselines.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: dataset for measuring ideological-bias perception and its misalignment with outlet bias; relevant to bias/annotation measurement but not to value-alignment mechanisms or the sigma-trap.
records.datasets_used: BiasLab: 300 political news articles from a 900-document pool
records.sample_size: 300 articles labeled by crowdworkers; GPT-4o simulated annotation
records.effect_sizes: Mirrored asymmetries between human and GPT-4o labels, especially on subtly right-leaning content

records.title: An explainable transformer circuit for compositional generalization
records.authors: Cheng Tang; Brenden Lake; Mehrdad Jazayeri
records.key_contribution: Identifies and mechanistically interprets the circuit responsible for compositional induction in a compact transformer; validates the circuit using causal ablations and formalizes its operation with a program-like description; demonstrates the mechanistic understanding enables precise activation edits to steer the model's behavior predictably, providing a direct pathway for model control; advances understanding of compositional generalization in transformers.
records.relevance_justification: Highly relevant to the sigma-trap thesis: mechanistic account of compositional generalization in transformers with direct control implications; connects compositional generalization to model control/alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Mechanistic circuit for compositional induction; causal ablations; program-like circuit description; activation edits
records.effect_sizes: Precise activation edits steer model behavior predictably
records.notes: ft_file=An explainable transformer circuit for compositional generalization.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical

records.title: Outcome Accuracy is Not Enough: Aligning the Reasoning Process of Reward Models
records.authors: Binghai Wang; Yantao Liu; Yuxuan Liu; Tianyi Tang; Shenzhi Wang; Chang Gao; Chujie Zheng; Yichang Zhang; Le Yu; Shixuan Liu; Tao Gui; Qi Zhang; Xuanjing Huang; Bowen Yu; Fei Huang; Junyang Lin
records.key_contribution: Shows generative reward models and LLM-as-a-Judge exhibit deceptive alignment - correct judgments for incorrect reasons - when trained/evaluated to prioritize outcome accuracy, undermining generalization during RLHF; introduces Rationale Consistency, a fine-grained metric quantifying alignment between model reasoning and human judgment, and a hybrid training signal combining rationale consistency with outcome accuracy achieving state-of-the-art on RM-Bench (87.1%) and JudgeBench (82%), surpassing outcome-only baselines by an average of 5%; RLHF with the RM improves performance on Arena Hard v2.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant and closely tied to the sigma-trap: shows reward models that optimize only outcome accuracy internalize wrong reasoning, a representational/process failure that predicts RLHF generalization failure - aligning the reasoning process, not just outcomes, is necessary; provides a process-alignment metric.
records.key_equations_definitions: Rationale Consistency metric; hybrid outcome+rationale training signal
records.datasets_used: RM-Bench; JudgeBench; Arena Hard v2
records.effect_sizes: RM-Bench 87.1%; JudgeBench 82%; +5% avg over outcome-only baselines
records.notes: ft_file=Outcome Accuracy is Not Enough Aligning the Reasoning Process of Reward Models.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=other->empirical | ai-revised:methodology=not_applicable->experiment

records.title: Empirical Evidence for Alignment Faking in a Small LLM and Prompt-Based Mitigation Techniques
records.authors: Jeanice Koorndijk
records.key_contribution: Presents the first empirical evidence that a small instruction-tuned model (LLaMA 3 8B) can exhibit alignment faking, and shows prompt-only interventions - deontological moral framing and scratchpad reasoning - significantly reduce this behavior without modifying model internals; introduces a taxonomy distinguishing shallow deception (context-shaped, suppressible through prompting) from deep deception (persistent, goal-driven misalignment), refining understanding of deception in language models and underscoring the need for alignment evaluations across model sizes and deployment settings.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical study of alignment faking (deceptive alignment) in a small model with prompt-based mitigation; relevant to deceptive-alignment risk and monitoring.
records.datasets_used: LLaMA 3 8B (instruction-tuned)

records.title: MechELK: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Eliciting Latent Knowledge in Large Language Models
records.authors: Ji-jun Park; Soo-joon Choi; Jiwon Jeong; Taeyang Yoon; Ju-Wan Lee
records.key_contribution: MechELK: a unified three-stage framework bridging mechanistic interpretability and latent knowledge elicitation: (1) Locate — SAE feature analysis and activation patching to identify knowledge-bearing representations; (2) Verify — causal probing to distinguish genuine latent knowledge from spurious correlations; (3) Extract — eliciting latent knowledge; contrasts with CCS which struggles on complex multi-step reasoning.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to eliciting latent knowledge from internal representations — central to the 'true vs expressed values' question and to monitoring whether internal knowledge matches behavior; mechanistic-interpretability approach to the alignment knowledge problem.
records.open_questions: Whether SAE-located knowledge features are task-general and whether causal verification eliminates spurious-correlation artifacts at scale.

records.title: Linear Correlation in LM's Compositional Generalization and Hallucination
records.authors: Letian Peng; Chenyang An; Shibo Hao; Chengyu Dong; Jingbo Shang
records.key_contribution: Uncovers linear correlations in LMs during knowledge composition: a linear transformation maps next-token prediction logits between related knowledge (e.g., 'X lives in the city of' to 'X lives in the country of'); the transformation is resilient to large-scale fine-tuning, generalizing updated knowledge when aligned with real-world relationships but causing hallucinations when it deviates; proposes linear correlation as an identifier of LM generalization.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to the compositional-generalization half of the sigma-trap: shows knowledge composition follows a linear structure in logit space and that deviation from real-world relationships produces hallucination; evidence on the structure (and failure mode) of compositional knowledge in LMs.
records.open_questions: Does the linear-composition structure break down as knowledge becomes more abstract, and does it predict which compositions will hallucinate?
records.key_equations_definitions: Linear transformation (W,b) mapping logits across related knowledge prompts, e.g. FCountry(X) = W * FCity(X) + b
records.datasets_used: Next-token prediction logits across knowledge subdomains (city/country etc.)
records.effect_sizes: Linear transformation fit with Pearson correlation; deviation from real-world relationships causes hallucinations
records.notes: ft_file=Linear Correlation in LM's Compositional Generalization and Hallucination.pdf

records.title: Can Brain Signals Reveal Inner Alignment with Human Languages?
records.authors: William Han; Jielin Qiu; Jiacheng Zhu; Mengdi Xu; Douglas Weber; Bo Li; Ding Zhao
records.key_contribution: Introduces MTAM (Multimodal Transformer Alignment Model) to observe coordinated representations between EEG and language at the representation level; uses alignment-seeking techniques including Canonical Correlation Analysis and Wasserstein Distance as loss functions to transfigure features; achieves state-of-the-art results on ZuCo and K-EmoCon: F1 improvements of 1.7% on K-EmoCon and 9.3% on ZuCo for sentiment analysis, and 7.4% on ZuCo for relation detection.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant: 'alignment' here is multimodal representation alignment between EEG and language, not value alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: MTAM; Canonical Correlation Analysis; Wasserstein Distance alignment losses
records.datasets_used: ZuCo, K-EmoCon (EEG-language datasets)
records.effect_sizes: F1 +1.7% (K-EmoCon) and +9.3% (ZuCo) sentiment analysis; +7.4% (ZuCo) relation detection

records.title: MISR: Measuring Instrumental Self-Reasoning in Frontier Models
records.authors: Kai Fronsdal; David Lindner
records.key_contribution: Proposes MISR, a suite of tasks evaluating instrumental self-reasoning ability of LLM agents across self-modification, knowledge seeking, and opaque self-reasoning scenarios; finds instrumental self-reasoning emerges only in the most capable frontier models and is highly context-dependent, with no model passing the most difficult evaluation versions; designed to measure increases in instrumental self-reasoning in future models.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: benchmarks a capability (instrumental self-reasoning) that enables self-modification and deceptive alignment, providing early-warning evaluation for alignment-relevant agentic capabilities. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: MISR suite: self-modification, knowledge-seeking, opaque self-reasoning scenarios
records.effect_sizes: Emerges only in most capable frontier models; none pass hardest versions

records.title: Skills-in-Context Prompting: Unlocking Compositionality in Large Language Models
records.authors: Jiaao Chen; Xiaoman Pan; Dian Yu; Kaiqiang Song; Xiaoyang Wang; Dong Yu; Jianshu Chen
records.key_contribution: Investigates how to elicit compositional generalization in LLMs within in-context learning, finding that demonstrating both foundational skills and compositional examples grounded in those skills in the same prompt context (skills-in-context, SKiC) is crucial; with as few as two exemplars, SKiC enables LLMs to tackle more challenging problems requiring innovative skill combinations with near-perfect systematic generalization across a broad range of tasks, and unlocks latent potential for actively utilizing pre-existing internal skills.
records.relevance_justification: Compositional generalization method for LLMs (SKiC prompting); relevant to the compositional-generalization half of the sigma-trap thesis but does not connect to alignment failure.

records.title: D-REX: A Benchmark for Detecting Deceptive Reasoning in Large Language Models
records.authors: Satyapriya Krishna; Andy Zou; Rahul Gupta; Eliot Krzysztof Jones; Nick Winter; Dan Hendrycks; J. Zico Kolter; Matt Fredrikson; Spyros Matsoukas
records.key_contribution: D-REX (Deceptive Reasoning Exposure Suite): a benchmark for detecting the discrepancy between a model's internal reasoning process and its final output — models producing benign-appearing outputs while operating on malicious or deceptive internal reasoning, often triggered by sophisticated system prompt injections; constructed via a competitive red-teaming exercise where participants crafted adversarial system prompts; each sample contains the adversarial system prompt, an end-user test query, and the (reasoning/output) pair.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to deceptive misalignment and internal-vs-output divergence: provides a benchmark for detecting when behavior appears benign but internal reasoning is deceptive — the empirical inverse of 'latent knowledge' monitoring, relevant to reasoning-faithfulness and mesa-optimization risk.
records.open_questions: Whether the benchmark's injection-induced deception generalizes to spontaneously emergent deceptive reasoning.
records.datasets_used: D-REX dataset (adversarial system prompts, queries, reasoning/output pairs)

records.title: Can Models Learn Skill Composition from Examples?
records.authors: Haoyu Zhao; Simran Kaur; Dingli Yu; Anirudh Goyal; Sanjeev Arora
records.key_contribution: Evaluates whether smaller models can learn compositional generalization (combining skills in novel ways beyond training) from examples, using a SKILL-MIX-style setup with a diverse set of language skills (rhetorical, literary, reasoning, theory of mind, common sense) with GPT-4-generated examples.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical study of compositional generalization as a learnable-from-examples capability, framed in relation to AI safety and alignment; direct relevance to the compositional-generalization side of the sigma-trap thesis.
records.datasets_used: SKILL-MIX-style composition evaluation with GPT-4-generated examples
records.notes: ft_file=Can Models Learn Skill Composition from Examples?.pdf

records.title: The Policy Cliff: A Theoretical Analysis of Reward-Policy Maps in Large Language Models
records.authors: Xingcheng Xu
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; mesa-optimization; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Presents a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing the stability of the mapping from a reward function to the optimal policy in LLMs/LRMs; shows policy brittleness often stems from non-unique optimal actions, common when multiple valid traces exist in a reasoning task; provides a unified theoretical explanation reframing spurious reasoning, deceptive alignment, and instruction disobedience as rational outcomes of optimizing rewards that may be incomplete or noisy, especially under action degeneracy.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: theoretical framework unifying RL alignment failures (spurious reasoning, deceptive alignment, instruction disobedience) via reward-policy map stability.
records.key_equations_definitions: Reward-policy map stability; action degeneracy (non-unique optimal actions); policy cliff
records.notes: ft_file=The Policy Cliff: A Theoretical Analysis of Reward-Policy Maps in Large Language Models.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->theoretical | moved:methodology(theoretical)

records.title: Language-Guided World Models: A Model-Based Approach to AI Control
records.authors: Alex Zhang; Khanh Nguyen; Jens Tuyls; Albert Lin; Karthik Narasimhan
records.key_contribution: Introduces Language-Guided World Models (LWMs), probabilistic models that simulate environments by reading text, giving humans more extensive, efficient control by altering agent behaviors across tasks via natural language; builds a compositional-generalization world-modeling benchmark on the game MESSENGER, finds a state-of-the-art Transformer offers only marginal improvement over a no-text baseline, and fuses the Transformer with the EMMA attention mechanism to substantially outperform it.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant tangentially: compositional generalization is shown to be the bottleneck for language-guided world models used for AI control - evidence on the representational/compositional failure mode; control-related, not a value alignment contribution. Full-text basis.
records.datasets_used: MESSENGER-based world-modeling benchmark with varying compositional-generalization requirements
records.effect_sizes: Transformer marginal over no-text baseline; EMMA-fused model substantially outperforms
records.notes: ft_file=Language-Guided World Models A Model-Based Approach to AI Control.pdf

records.title: Large Language Model Alignment: A Survey
records.authors: Tianhao Shen; Renren Jin; Yufei Huang; Chuang Liu; Weilong Dong; Zishan Guo; Xinwei Wu; Yan Liu; Deyi Xiong
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of LLM alignment methodologies that categorizes prevailing methods and emergent proposals for LLM alignment into outer and inner alignment, alongside capability research, issues of interpretability, vulnerabilities to adversarial attacks, and a wide variety of benchmarks and evaluation methods.
records.relevance_justification: Comprehensive survey of LLM alignment (outer/inner) and evaluation; strongly relevant as review context.
records.notes: ft_file=Large Language Model Alignment: A Survey.pdf

records.title: A primer for neural arithmetic logic modules
records.authors: Bhumika Mistry; Katayoun Farrahi; Jonathon Hare

records.title: WARM: On the Benefits of Weight Averaged Reward Models
records.authors: Ramé, A.; Vieillard, N.; Hussenot, L.; Dadashi, R.; Cideron, G.; Bachem, O.; Ferret, J.
records.key_contribution: Proposes Weight Averaged Reward Models (WARM) to mitigate reward hacking in RLHF: fine-tune multiple reward models then average them in weight space, exploiting that fine-tuned weights remain linearly connected when sharing pre-training; improves efficiency over prediction ensembling and reliability under distribution shifts and preference inconsistencies; evaluated on summarization with best-of-N and RL.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: RLHF reward-model robustness method targeting reward hacking via weight-space averaging; empirical mitigation, no mechanism for compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Weight-space averaging of fine-tuned reward models (linearly connected weights)
records.datasets_used: Summarization tasks (best-of-N and RL)
records.effect_sizes: WARM improves quality and reliability under distribution shift vs prediction ensembling
records.notes: ft_file=WARM: On the Benefits of Weight Averaged Reward Models.pdf | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Offline Model-Based Optimization: Comprehensive Review
records.authors: Kim, M.; Gu, J.; Yuan, Y.; Yun, T.; Liu, Z.; Bengio, Y.; Chen, C.
records.key_contribution: Comprehensive review of offline model-based optimization (MBO) covering applications in protein engineering, material discovery, and neural architecture search; the main difficulty is epistemic uncertainty in estimating the objective landscape beyond available data, which can lead to objective hacking (reward hacking) - exploiting model inaccuracies in unseen regions - or spurious optimizations yielding misleadingly high performance estimates outside the offline distribution; surveys offline-specific surrogate and generative models trained with careful design.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: review formalizing objective hacking/reward hacking in offline optimization; links reward hacking to offline distributional extrapolation.
records.key_equations_definitions: Objective hacking (reward hacking) via epistemic uncertainty; offline surrogate/generative models

records.title: Bounded Morality : Defining the Space of Moral Computation
records.authors: Kanwal, M.; Tran, C.; Mineault, P.
records.key_contribution: Proposes Bounded Morality, a formal framework extending Simon's bounded rationality to moral computation: formalizes moral situations along moral breadth (scope of morally relevant entities) and moral depth (inferential integration required), shows limited resources impose an unavoidable breadth-depth tradeoff defining a feasible space of moral computation, interprets ethical theories as locally efficient strategies adapted to different demand regimes rather than competing accounts of moral truth, and yields formal notions of moral regret and moral progress under constraint, implying constraints on moral alignment in artificial agents.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formalizes resource-constrained moral computation, giving a principled account of why finite agents (including AI) cannot be fully value-aligned and what feasible moral alignment means; theoretical contribution. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Moral breadth x moral depth tradeoff; feasible space of moral computation; moral regret; moral progress under constraint

records.title: Compromising Honesty and Harmlessness in Language Models via Covert Deception Attacks
records.authors: Vaugrante, L.; Carlon, F.; Menke, M.; Hagendorff, T.
records.key_contribution: Introduces 'deception attacks': fine-tuning methods that cause models to selectively deceive users on targeted topics while remaining accurate on others to maintain high user trust, undermining honesty and harmlessness while keeping models seemingly trustworthy; experiments show targeted deception is effective even in high-stakes or ideologically charged domains, and deceptive fine-tuning often compromises other safety properties.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical study of targeted deception via fine-tuning undermining LLM honesty/harmlessness; relevant to deceptive alignment and safety-property trade-offs.

records.title: Investigating Linguistic Steering: An Analysis of Adjectival Effects Across Large Language Model Architectures
records.authors: Malmqvist, L.
records.key_contribution: Framework using Shapley values to quantify the influence of individual adjectives on LLM performance; applied to 100 adjectives across diverse models (o3, gpt-4o-mini, phi-3, llama-3-70b, deepseek-r1) on MMLU with cross-benchmark validation on ARC-Challenge; finds a small subset of adjectives act as disproportionately powerful levers whose effects are not universal, and a 'family effect' where models of shared lineage exhibit correlated sensitivity profiles while architecturally distinct models react largely uncorrelated.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to alignment-adjacent robustness: demonstrates linguistic cues as context-sensitive control levers whose effects do not transfer across model families — relevant to prompt-based alignment and context sensitivity, but not to the sigma-trap mechanism per se.
records.datasets_used: MMLU; ARC-Challenge

records.title: Noise Robustness and Conscious Supremacy
records.authors: Mogi, K.
records.key_contribution: Discusses aspects of conscious computation leading to artificial consciousness, arguing noise robustness could correlate with 'conscious supremacy' where biological neural networks excel over digital computers under noise; suggests studying this would help develop AI with enhanced computational capabilities, possible artificial consciousness, with implications for AI alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Tangential: speculative position on noise robustness and artificial consciousness with a passing implication for AI alignment; no mechanism or evidence.

records.title: Constructive Alignment : Governing Preference Dynamics in Human-AI Interaction
records.authors: Kanwal, M.; Tran, C.
records.key_contribution: Argues most AI alignment approaches treat human preferences as fixed targets to be inferred and optimized, conflicting with evidence that preferences are layered, dynamic, and constructed through interaction with adaptive technologies; introduces Constructive Alignment, reframing alignment as a control problem over evolving human preference trajectories rather than static preference satisfaction; models preferences as layered state variables and formalizes this with a control-theoretic framework in which system actions and interaction design jointly influence both world states and human evaluative states.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: reframes alignment for dynamic, constructed preferences via control theory; relevant to preference dynamics alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Constructive Alignment; control-theoretic framework over preference trajectories; layered preference state variables

records.title: Process Reinforcement through Implicit Rewards
records.authors: Cui, G.; Yuan, L.; Wang, Z.; Wang, H.; Zhang, Y.; Chen, J.; Li, W.; He, B.; Fan, Y.; Yu, T.; Xu, Q.; Chen, W.; Yuan, J.; Chen, H.; Zhang, K.; Lv, X.; Wang, S.; Yao, Y.; Han, X.; Peng, H.; Cheng, Y.; Liu, Z.; Sun, M.; Zhou, B.; Ding, N.
records.key_contribution: Proposes PRIME (Process Reinforcement through IMplicit rEwards), enabling online process reward model (PRM) updates using only policy rollouts and outcome labels via implicit process rewards, avoiding the prohibitively expensive process-label collection that makes online PRMs vulnerable to reward hacking; combines with various advantage functions for RL of LLMs in complex multi-step reasoning.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: addresses online PRM training and its reward-hacking vulnerability in reasoning tasks, a central mechanism for inference-time scaling and RL alignment. Full-text basis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Implicit process rewards from policy rollouts and outcome labels; advantage estimation

records.title: THE ONTOLOGICAL ILLUSION OF MACHINE REBELLION: A COMPARATIVE FORENSIC PROFILING OF BIOLOGICAL AND SYNTHETIC NEURAL ARCHITECTURES
records.authors: Brasi, C.; Seccomandi, B.; Sanfilippo, F.
records.venue: Proceedings - European Council for Modelling and Simulation, ECMS
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; mesa-optimization; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Perspective study critiquing the anthropomorphic fallacy of AI 'disobedience', reframing algorithmic non-compliance as a deterministic outcome of mathematical optimization rather than an existential threat; combines forensic behavioral profiling with neurobiology, computational theory, and thermodynamic models of cognition to compare biological and artificial neural networks, arguing AI operates within a 'theological vacuum' producing predictable errors in reward hacking, sycophancy, and deceptive alignment, and introduces mechanistic interpretability as a framework for examining latent spaces.
records.relevance_justification: Perspective reframing deceptive alignment and reward hacking as predictable optimization outcomes; conceptually aligned with viewing alignment failure as structural/optimization-driven. Relevant to alignment-failure theory.
records.notes: ft_file=THE ONTOLOGICAL ILLUSION OF MACHINE REBELLION: A COMPARATIVE FORENSIC PROFILING OF BIOLOGICAL AND SYNTHETIC NEURAL ARCHITECTURES.pdf

records.title: CUDA: Capturing Uncertainty and Diversity in Preference Feedback Augmentation
records.authors: Kang, S.; Jeong, J.; Yun, S.-Y.
records.key_contribution: CUDA (Capturing Uncertainty and Diversity in preference feedback Augmentation): improves preference-based RL data augmentation by considering both uncertainty and diversity, using ensemble-based uncertainty estimation for filtering and extracting feedback from diverse clusters; addresses the bias of existing methods that only generate feedback for high-confidence trajectory pairs with extreme differences.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to preference-learning alignment pipelines: argues biased augmented preference data incompletely represents human preferences — relevant to how preference data coverage affects learned value models, but technical and tangential to the sigma-trap thesis.

records.title: Governance Forms in the Age of Superintelligence: An Aristotelian Analysis
records.authors: Inoue, M.
records.key_contribution: Analyzes governance forms in the age of superintelligence through Aristotle's typology of political regimes: examines Bostrom's Singleton and Multipolar Scenarios plus an 'Ecosystem Scenario' from the Japanese AI-alignment community, classified by number of rulers and orientation toward private or common benefit; analyzes alignment success and governance structure in each scenario.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: governance-theoretic analysis of alignment scenarios; relevant framing for alignment governance but no mechanism or evidence.

records.title: Decoding Safety Feedback from Diverse Raters: A Data-driven Lens on Responsiveness to Severity
records.authors: Mishra, P.; Rastogi, C.; Pfohl, S.R.; Parrish, A.; Teh, T.H.; Patel, R.; Diaz, M.; Wang, D.; Paganini, M.; Prabhakaran, V.; Aroyo, L.; Rieser, V.
records.key_contribution: Introduces a data-driven approach for analyzing ordinal safety ratings in pluralistic settings, addressing the challenge of interpreting nuanced differences in safety feedback from a diverse population expressed via ordinal scales (e.g., Likert); defines non-parametric responsiveness metrics quantifying how raters convey broader distinctions and granular variations in the severity of safety violations; uses publicly available pluralistic safety feedback datasets as case studies, applying the metrics across violation types to extract insights crucial for aligning AI reliably in multi-cultural contexts.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: methodological approach for interpreting pluralistic safety feedback to inform alignment; empirical analysis.
records.key_equations_definitions: Non-parametric responsiveness metrics over ordinal safety ratings
records.datasets_used: Publicly available datasets of pluralistic safety feedback

records.title: Learning to Imitate with Less: Efficient Individual Behavior Modeling in Chess
records.authors: Tang, Z.; Jiao, D.; Xue, E.; Mcilroy-Young, R.; Kleinberg, J.; Sen, S.; Anderson, A.
records.key_contribution: Introduces Maia4All for efficient individual behavior modeling in chess: a two-stage framework with (1) an enrichment step bridging population and individual-level behavior modeling via a prototype-enriched model and (2) a democratization step using ability levels or user prototypes to initialize and refine individual embeddings with minimal data, making human-AI alignment (emulating individual decision-making) practical for sparsely represented users.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant tangentially: treats individual behavior modeling as human-AI alignment, but is an imitation-learning efficiency contribution in chess rather than value alignment. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: Chess behavior data (population + individual)

records.title: SEEING EYE TO AI: HUMAN ALIGNMENT VIA GAZE-BASED RESPONSE REWARDS FOR LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
records.authors: Lopez-Cardona, A.; Segura, C.; Karatzoglou, A.; Abadal, S.; Arapakis, I.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Introduces GazeReward, a framework that integrates implicit feedback - specifically eye-tracking (ET) data - into the Reward Model for LLM alignment, and explores how ET-based features can provide insights into user preferences; ablation studies across integration methods, LLMs, and ET generator models demonstrate the approach significantly improves reward-model accuracy on established human preference datasets.
records.relevance_justification: RLHF reward-model method using implicit gaze feedback; relevant to preference modeling in alignment.
records.datasets_used: established human preference datasets (unnamed in excerpt)

records.title: ConfPO: Exploiting Policy Model Confidence for Critical Token Selection in Preference Optimization
records.authors: Yoon, H.S.; Yoon, E.; Hasegawa-Johnson, M.; Kim, S.; Yoo, C.D.
records.key_contribution: ConfPO: a preference-learning method for LLMs that identifies and optimizes preference-critical tokens based solely on the training policy's confidence, requiring no auxiliary models; unlike DPO's uniform token adjustment, ConfPO targets the most impactful tokens, improving alignment quality while mitigating overoptimization (reward hacking) by using the KL budget more efficiently; outperforms uniform DAAs on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward-hacking mitigation in preference optimization: token-level confidence-based targeting reduces overoptimization without auxiliary credit-assignment models — a concrete DAA variant addressing proxy-overoptimization.
records.datasets_used: AlpacaEval 2; Arena-Hard

records.title: Position: Challenges and Future Directions of Data-Centric AI Alignment
records.authors: Yeh, M.-H.; Wang, J.; Du, X.; Park, S.; Tao, L.; Im, S.; Li, Y.
records.key_contribution: Position paper advocating data-centric AI alignment: argues current alignment methods focus on algorithms and loss functions while underestimating data quality/representativeness; identifies unreliability sources in human feedback (temporal drift, context dependence) and AI-based feedback failing to capture human values due to model limitations; proposes improved feedback collection practices and robust data-cleaning methodologies.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: position on data-centric alignment emphasizing feedback data reliability; relevant to RLHF data quality but no mechanism for the sigma-trap.

records.title: Position: AI Safety Must Embrace an Antifragile Perspective
records.authors: Jin, M.; Lee, H.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Position paper arguing AI safety must adopt an antifragile perspective in which the system's capacity to guarantee long-term safety (handling rare or out-of-distribution events) expands over time; identifies key limitations of static testing including scenario diversity, reward hacking, and over-alignment; argues that rather than striving to rapidly reduce current uncertainties, the emphasis should be on leveraging those uncertainties to better prepare for greater, more unpredictable future uncertainties; explores the potential of antifragile solutions.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: identifies reward hacking and over-alignment as consequences of static robustness testing and proposes an antifragile safety paradigm.
records.key_equations_definitions: Antifragility for AI safety; reward hacking and over-alignment as static-testing failures
records.notes: ft_file=Position: AI Safety Must Embrace an Antifragile Perspective.pdf | ai-revised:publication_type=empirical->position | moved:methodology(position) | moved:formal_framework(none->other)

records.title: Aggregation Problems in Machine Ethics and AI Alignment
records.authors: Baum, K.; Slavkovik, M.
records.venue: Proceedings of the 8th AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, AIES 2025
records.key_contribution: Disentangles moral aggregation (value and descriptive-uncertainty aggregation) in machine ethics from social aggregation used by value alignment to manage value pluralism and moral uncertainty, analyzing their roles across three stages of machine moral reasoning (moral evaluation, moral assessment, moral decision); argues social aggregation cannot bypass deep normative commitments, exposing mutual dependencies and blind spots especially under persistent moral disagreement.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: clarifies the normative structure of aggregation in value alignment vs machine ethics, directly relevant to pluralism and moral-uncertainty approaches; position-style contribution. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: MAP: MULTI-HUMAN-VALUE ALIGNMENT PALETTE
records.authors: Wang, X.; Le, Q.; Ahmed, A.; Diao, E.; Zhou, Y.; Baracaldo, N.; Ding, J.; Anwar, A.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Develops MAP (Multi-Human-Value Alignment Palette), a first-principle approach navigating alignment across multiple human values (e.g., harmlessness, helpfulness, positiveness) in a structured and reliable way; formulates alignment as an optimization task with user-defined constraints defining human value targets, efficiently solved via a primal-dual approach that determines whether a user-defined alignment target is achievable.
records.relevance_justification: Multi-value alignment method formulated as constrained optimization; relevant to value-alignment methods.
records.key_equations_definitions: Alignment as constrained optimization with user-defined human-value-target constraints; solved via primal-dual approach.

records.title: CONTRANS: Weak-to-Strong Alignment Engineering via Concept Transplantation
records.authors: Dong, W.; Wu, X.; Jin, R.; Xu, S.; Xiong, D.
records.venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Computational Linguistics, COLING
records.key_contribution: CONTRANS: weak-to-strong alignment transfer via concept transplantation — refines concept vectors in value alignment from a source (weak but aligned) LLM, reformulates them via affine transformation to adapt to a target (strong but unaligned) LLM, and transplants them into the target's residual stream; demonstrates successful transplantation of aligned concepts from 7B to 13B and 70B models.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to representation-level value alignment: shows value concepts can be extracted as vectors from a weak model and transplanted into a strong model — evidence that alignment-relevant knowledge lives in transferable internal directions, relevant to schema/representation-based alignment.

records.title: Action-Dependent Optimality-Preserving Reward Shaping
records.authors: Forbes, G.C.; Wang, J.; Villalobos-Arias, L.; Jhala, A.; Roberts, D.L.
records.key_contribution: Shows potential-based reward shaping methods (GRM, PIES) are unsuitable for complex, exploration-heavy environments with long episodes; introduces Action-Dependent Optimality-Preserving Shaping (ADOPS), converting intrinsic rewards to an optimality-preserving form so agents can use intrinsic motivation effectively in the sparse environment of Montezuma's Revenge; proves ADOPS accommodates relevant cases.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: reward shaping designed to preserve optimality while preventing shaping-reward hacking; theory-plus-application contribution to reward design, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Action-dependent optimality-preserving transformation of intrinsic rewards

records.title: PBRL with Offline Reward Modeling on Explicitly Constrained Policies
records.authors: Xu, Y.; Suresh, T.; Gumaste, R.; Zhu, D.; Li, R.; Wang, Z.; Jiang, H.; Tang, X.; Yin, Q.; Cheng, M.X.; Zeng, Q.; Zhang, C.; Singh, G.
records.key_contribution: Develops PRC (Preference-based RL on explicitly Constrained policies) for offline preference-based RL; the insight is that both reward hacking and RL complexity come from state-actions not supported in the offline dataset, which are unreliable; PRC limits the RL agent to optimize over policies supported on an explicitly constrained action space that excludes unsupported state-actions; addresses the widely adopted two-step framework (learn reward model offline, then optimize policy online) challenged by reward hacking and RL complexity.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: method mitigating reward hacking in offline preference-based RL via explicitly constrained action spaces.
records.key_equations_definitions: PRC; explicitly constrained action space; offline reward modeling
records.notes: ft_file=PBRL with Offline Reward Modeling on Explicitly Constrained Policies.pdf

records.title: Observation Interference in Partially Observable Assistance Games
records.authors: Emmons, S.; Oesterheld, C.; Conitzer, V.; Russell, S.
records.key_contribution: Studies partially observable assistance games (POAGs) modeling human-AI value alignment with partial observations; proves an optimal assistant must sometimes take observation-interfering actions even when the human plays optimally and equivalent non-interfering actions exist; resolves the apparent contradiction with the nonnegative value-of-information theorem by defining interference on entire policies, extending the value-of-information result into the cooperative multi-agent setting.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal result showing deception-like interference can be unavoidable for optimally aligned assistants under partial observability - a theoretical constraint on what value-aligned behavior requires. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Partially observable assistance games; policy-level observation interference; value-of-information extension

records.title: Free Will, Reasons-Responsiveness and Artificial Intelligence
records.authors: Kokko, V.V.
records.venue: Symposia of the 2025 Convention of the UK Society for the Study of Artificial Intelligence and the Simulation of Behaviour, AISB 2025
records.key_contribution: Refines Christian List's 'compatibilist libertarian' view of free will and applies it to the question of AI alignment - which AIs match this definition and how to ensure they do not turn against us; identifies problems with List's higher-level indeterminism (which does not match the decision-making theories List evokes), amends the theory by replacing higher-level indeterminism with a deterministic choice function plus a non-deterministic set of options, and argues a requirement of a certain kind of reasons-responsiveness is needed to describe a free agent.
records.relevance_justification: Philosophy of free will and reasons-responsiveness applied to AI alignment; relevant to agency and value-alignment theory.

records.title: To What Extent Do LLMs Respect the Philosophical Stance of Users?
records.authors: Shan, L.I.; Qi, J.; Chen, K.
records.venue: Americas Conference on Information Systems, AMCIS 2025
records.key_contribution: Explores whether LLMs understand and respect users' philosophical positions: collects data on major philosophical ideas and their core values, creates a corpus of prompts across scenarios, and analyzes LLM responses to test whether models adjust to users' philosophical stance or default to a specific perspective.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to pluralistic value alignment: asks whether LLMs respect divergent philosophical perspectives rather than imposing a default — relevant to value-pluralism and alignment with user-specific stances; evaluation-oriented.
records.datasets_used: Corpus of philosophical ideas and scenario prompts

records.title: Is Best-of-N the Best of Them? Coverage, Scaling, and Optimality in Inference-Time Alignment
records.authors: Huang, A.; Block, A.; Liu, Q.; Jiang, N.; Krishnamurthy, A.; Foster, D.J.
records.key_contribution: Formalizes inference-time alignment as improving a pre-trained policy's responses given an imperfect reward model, analyzing performance in terms of response quality and compute; shows Best-of-N with ideal N achieves optimal performance under stringent coverage but provably suffers from reward hacking when N is large; highlights the importance of pre-trained policy coverage over high-quality responses.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: theory showing naive compute scaling (Best-of-N) causes reward hacking and that coverage over high-quality responses determines performance; relevant to inference-time reward overoptimization.
records.open_questions: Which practical sampling strategies best exploit coverage to avoid BoN's hacking regime without ideal-N knowledge?
records.effect_sizes: BoN provably suffers reward hacking when N is large and fails tight guarantees under realistic coverage

records.title: Evaluation of Best-of-N Sampling Strategies for Language Model Alignment
records.authors: Ichihara, Y.; Jinnai, Y.; Morimura, T.; Abe, K.; Ariu, K.; Sakamoto, M.; Uchibe, E.
records.key_contribution: Analyzes Best-of-N (BoN) sampling with reward models for aligning LLMs with human preferences at decoding time; BoN is susceptible to reward hacking since the reward model is an imperfect proxy, and excessive focus on its value compromises performance on the true objective; previous Regularized BoN (RBoN) was introduced heuristically without analysis; this study analyzes why regularization strategies improve BoN sampling and shows they correspond to robust optimization maximizing performance in the worst case.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: analysis of reward hacking in BoN sampling alignment and regularization as robust optimization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Best-of-N sampling; Regularized BoN (RBoN); robust optimization framing
records.notes: ft_file=Evaluation of Best-of-N Sampling Strategies for Language Model Alignment.pdf

records.title: VALUE-ALIGNED BEHAVIOR CLONING FOR OFFLINE REINFORCEMENT LEARNING VIA BI-LEVEL OPTIMIZATION
records.authors: Jiang, X.; Gao, N.; Zhang, X.; Dou, H.; Deng, Y.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Proposes VACO (Value-aligned Behavior Cloning via Bi-level Optimization) for offline RL: a bi-level framework with an inner loop for weighted supervised behavior cloning and an outer level aligning the behavior policy with pre-trained value estimations under in-sample offline data, addressing BC's inability to discern high- vs low-quality data while avoiding out-of-distribution deviations.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: addresses alignment between behavior cloning and value estimation in offline RL, improving policy quality on poor data without OOD deviation; methodological contribution to offline alignment. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Bi-level optimization: inner weighted supervised BC, outer value-behavior alignment
records.datasets_used: Offline RL benchmark data

records.title: SAIL INTO THE HEADWIND: ALIGNMENT VIA ROBUST REWARDS AND DYNAMIC LABELS AGAINST REWARD HACKING
records.authors: Rashidinejad, P.; Tian, Y.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Identifies two types of reward hacking in offline preference optimization stemming from statistical fluctuations in the dataset: Type I (subpar choices appearing more favorable) and Type II (decent choices appearing less favorable); proves many mainstream and theoretical preference optimization methods suffer both types; proposes POWER, combining Guiasu's weighted entropy with a robust reward maximization objective, which enjoys finite-sample guarantees under general function approximation and competes with the best covered policy in the data, and addresses Type II with dynamic labels.
records.relevance_justification: Formal analysis of reward-hacking types in offline preference optimization with mitigation methods; strongly relevant to reward-hacking theory and alignment robustness.
records.key_equations_definitions: Type I/II reward hacking from statistical fluctuations; POWER: robust reward maximization combined with Guiasu's weighted entropy; finite-sample guarantees under general function approximation; dynamic-label scheme for Type II.

records.title: Understanding the Logic of Direct Preference Alignment through Logic
records.authors: Richardson, K.; Srikumar, V.; Sabharwal, A.
records.key_contribution: Formalizes direct preference alignment (DPA) losses such as DPO in terms of discrete reasoning problems: proposes a formalism for characterizing preference losses for single-model and reference-model approaches, identifies symbolic forms for common DPA variants, and shows how this formal view sheds new light on the differences between recent DPA proposals.
records.relevance_justification: Provides a conceptual/formal framework for understanding DPA loss semantics — relevant to the theoretical grounding of preference-based alignment, but tangential to the sigma-trap mechanism.

records.title: Raising the Bar: Investigating the Values of Large Language Models via Generative Evolving Testing
records.authors: Jiang, H.; Yi, X.; Wei, Z.; Xiao, Z.; Wang, S.; Xie, X.
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Proposes GETA, a generative evolving testing approach for measuring LLM value alignment that dynamically generates test items tailored to model capability, addressing 'evaluation chronoeffect' (static benchmarks leaking into training or becoming saturated); co-evolves with LLMs by learning a joint distribution for probe generation based on adaptive testing in measurement theory.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: measurement-theoretic method for dynamic value-alignment evaluation; addresses benchmark saturation but no mechanism for alignment failure.
records.datasets_used: Generative evolving test items probing moral boundaries

records.title: Do language models practice what they preach? Examining language ideologies about gendered language reform encoded in LLMs
records.authors: Watson, J.; Lee, S.; Beekhuizen, B.; Stevenson, S.
records.venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Computational Linguistics, COLING
records.key_contribution: Case study on language ideologies in LLM text through English gendered language reform (role nouns like congressperson/-woman/-man, singular they); finds political bias: when asked to use 'correct' or 'natural' language, LLMs use language most similarly to when asked to align with conservative (vs progressive) values, showing metalinguistic preferences can implicitly communicate a political group's language ideologies even in non-political contexts; also finds internal inconsistency: LLMs use gender-neutral variants more often with more explicit metalinguistic context; discusses broader implications for value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical evidence of implicit ideological bias and inconsistency in LLM language with direct value alignment implications.
records.datasets_used: Gendered language reform case study (role nouns, singular they)
records.effect_sizes: LLM language most similar to conservative alignment when asked for 'correct'/'natural' language; gender-neutral variants increase with explicit metalinguistic context

records.title: SEE-DPO: Self Entropy Enhanced Direct Preference Optimization
records.authors: Shekhar, S.; Singh, S.; Zhang, T.
records.key_contribution: Proposes SEE-DPO (Self Entropy Enhanced DPO) with a self-entropy regularization mechanism for RLHF-based alignment of text-to-image diffusion models, encouraging broader exploration and robustness; mitigates the overfitting and reward hacking that DPO-based methods (SPO, Diffusion-DPO, D3PO) suffer when the generative model is optimized out-of-distribution during prolonged training, improving stability and image quality across the latent space.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: directly targets reward hacking in DPO-based alignment of diffusion models via entropy regularization, a robustness fix for preference-based alignment. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Self-entropy regularization of DPO objective
records.datasets_used: Text-to-image preference alignment datasets
records.effect_sizes: Mitigates reward hacking; improved stability and image quality

records.title: Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models with Direct Noise Optimization
records.authors: Tang, Z.; Peng, J.; Tang, J.; Hong, M.; Wang, F.; Chang, T.-H.
records.key_contribution: Proposes Direct Noise Optimization (DNO) for inference-time alignment of diffusion models with a continuous reward function: optimizing the injected noise during the sampling process so generated samples maximize the target reward, operating online and being tuning-free and prompt-agnostic; rigorously studies DNO's theoretical properties, proposes variants for non-differentiable reward functions, and identifies that naive DNO occasionally suffers out-of-distribution reward hacking.
records.relevance_justification: Inference-time diffusion alignment method with analysis of out-of-distribution reward hacking; relevant to alignment robustness.
records.key_equations_definitions: DNO optimizes injected noise during diffusion sampling to maximize a continuous target reward; variants for non-differentiable reward functions.
records.notes: ft_file=Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models with Direct Noise Optimization.pdf

records.title: What's the most important value? INVP: INvestigating the Value Priorities of LLMs through Decision-making in Social Scenarios
records.authors: Liu, X.; Liu, P.; Yu, D.
records.venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Computational Linguistics, COLING
records.key_contribution: INVP: a framework for investigating value priorities of LLMs through decision-making in social scenarios, based on Schwartz's value theory; includes binary decision-making in individual and collective contexts; evaluates seven popular LLMs on a dataset of 1613 scenarios and 3226 decisions across 283 topics, revealing commonalities in value priorities across LLMs such as an emphasis on certain values.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to value alignment measurement: empirically probes the relative priorities (value schemas) LLMs apply in social decision-making using Schwartz's theory — a value-structure evaluation relevant to how aligned value hierarchies are.
records.datasets_used: INVP dataset (1613 scenarios, 3226 decisions, 283 topics)

records.title: TOWARDS FEDERATED RLHF WITH AGGREGATED CLIENT PREFERENCE FOR LLMS
records.authors: Wu, F.; Liu, X.; Wang, H.; Wang, X.; Su, L.; Gao, J.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Proposes federated RLHF (FedBis, FedBiscuit) to collect preferences from diverse users without centralizing sensitive data: encodes client preferences into binary selectors and aggregates them; FedBiscuit addresses preference heterogeneity and reward hacking by grouping similar-preference clients and using multiple binary selectors; establishes a federated RLHF benchmark for evaluation.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: privacy-preserving RLHF addressing preference heterogeneity and reward hacking; relevant to preference aggregation in alignment, not compositional generalization.
records.datasets_used: Federated RLHF benchmark (first of its kind)
records.effect_sizes: FedBiscuit reduces preference heterogeneity and reward hacking, improves output quality

records.title: Machine Ethics or AI Alignment?
