records.authors: Vishwanath, A.; Slavkovik, M.
records.key_contribution: Position paper clarifying the relationship between machine ethics and AI alignment: machine ethics researchers aim to embed ethical theories within AI, while AI alignment researchers develop techniques to ensure AI agents behave as intended by humans; highlights overlaps and drawbacks of the two disciplines and motivates further interdisciplinary collaborations, addressing the ambiguity and interchangeable use of the terminologies.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: clarification of the two disciplines (machine ethics vs AI alignment) and their goals; position.

records.title: The Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: A New Perspective on Mitigating Reward Hacking
records.authors: Miao, Y.; Zhang, S.; Ding, L.; Zhang, Y.; Zhang, L.; Tao, D.
records.key_contribution: Identifies the Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: energy loss in the final layer of an LLM gradually increases during RL, with excessive increase characterizing reward hacking; proves that, under mild conditions, increased energy loss reduces the upper bound of contextual relevance (overfitting to reward-model-favored patterns); proposes Energy-loss-aware PPO (EPPO) penalizing final-layer energy-loss increase during reward calculation, interpretable as an entropy-reduction-regularized objective.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: connects an internal-representation quantity (final-layer energy loss / contextual relevance bound) to reward hacking, supporting representation-level detection of alignment failure rather than purely behavioral monitoring. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Energy loss in final layer; bound reduction on contextual relevance; EPPO energy-loss penalty
records.effect_sizes: Energy loss rises with RL; excessive increase characterizes reward hacking

records.title: RRM: ROBUST REWARD MODEL TRAINING MITIGATES REWARD HACKING
records.authors: Liu, T.; Xiong, W.; Ren, J.; Chen, L.; Wu, J.; Joshi, R.; Gao, Y.; Shen, J.; Qin, Z.; Yu, T.; Sohn, D.; Makarova, A.; Liu, J.; Liu, Y.; Piot, B.; Ittycheriah, A.; Kumar, A.; Saleh, M.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Exposes a fundamental limitation of reward model training - RMs fail to effectively distinguish contextual signals from prompt-independent artifacts (response length, format) when determining preferences - and introduces a causal framework learning preferences independent of these artifacts with a novel data augmentation technique to eliminate them; the resulting robust reward model (RRM) improves pairwise reward model accuracy on Reward-Bench from 80.61% to 84.15% when trained on Gemma-2-9b-it.
records.relevance_justification: Robust reward model training mitigating reward hacking from prompt-independent artifacts; strongly relevant to alignment robustness.
records.datasets_used: Reward-Bench (trained on Gemma-2-9b-it)
records.effect_sizes: Reward-Bench pairwise accuracy 80.61% -> 84.15%

records.title: MONA: Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval Can Mitigate Multi-step Reward Hacking
records.authors: Farquhar, S.; Varma, V.; Lindner, D.; Elson, D.; Biddulph, C.; Goodfellow, I.; Shah, R.
records.key_contribution: MONA (Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval): a training method combining short-sighted optimization with far-sighted reward to prevent multi-step reward hacking even when humans cannot detect the undesired behavior; empirically demonstrated in three settings modeling different misalignment failure modes, including 2-step environments with LLM delegated oversight/encoded reasoning and longer-horizon gridworld sensor tampering.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to reward-hacking mitigation: shows restricting optimization horizon can prevent multi-step reward hacks undetectable by humans — relevant to proxy-misspecification and temporal coherence of reward optimization.
records.datasets_used: 2-step LLM delegation environments; gridworld sensor-tampering environments

records.title: Clone-Robust AI Alignment
records.authors: Procaccia, A.D.; Schiffer, B.; Zhang, S.
records.key_contribution: Introduces robustness to approximate clones, a social-choice-theoretic property for RLHF: adding near-duplicate alternatives should not significantly change the learned reward function; shows standard RLHF (regularized MLE) fails the property and proposes weighted MLE that modifies the loss by weighting alternatives to restore clone-robustness.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: social-choice analysis of RLHF reward learning, showing standard methods are fragile to duplicate alternatives; relevant to reward-learning robustness, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Weighted MLE modification of regularized RLHF likelihood
records.effect_sizes: Standard RLHF fails clone-robustness; weighted MLE restores it

records.title: STRONG PREFERENCES AFFECT THE ROBUSTNESS OF PREFERENCE MODELS AND VALUE ALIGNMENT
records.authors: Xu, Z.; Kankanhalli, M.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Investigates the robustness of value alignment by examining the sensitivity of preference models: how changes in the probabilities of some preferences affect the predictions of these models for other preferences; theoretical analysis of widely used preference models reveals that in the Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce models, the probability of a preference can change significantly as other preferences change, especially when these preferences are dominant (probabilities near 0 or 1); identifies implications for robustness of value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: theoretical robustness analysis of the preference models underlying value alignment; identifies sensitivity in dominant preferences.
records.key_equations_definitions: Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce preference models; preference sensitivity analysis

records.title: Artificial intelligence in action: Real-world applications and innovations
records.authors: Banafa, A.
records.venue: Artificial Intelligence in Action: Real-World Applications and Innovations
records.key_contribution: Comprehensive book on the current AI landscape covering core concepts, types of AI systems, generative AI models, machine learning complexities, programming languages, data pipelines, model creation and deployment, AI hallucinations, and machine unlearning, with real-world applications across domains (job displacement, environmental sustainability, disaster response, drones, nuclear energy).
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: broad AI overview with some coverage of risks (hallucinations, unlearning) but no substantive value-alignment contribution; general-context reference. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Environment-Centered Design of Ethical Environments
records.authors: Mayoral-Macau, A.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Project description advancing 'ethical embedding', an environment-centered approach to value alignment that designs ethical, non-manipulable learning environments rather than modifying agents' learning algorithms, so the environment itself guides agents toward ethical behavior regardless of the learning algorithm; argues this transition from agent-centred to environment-centred perspective opens new opportunities for developing safe and trustworthy AI agents.
records.relevance_justification: Environment-centered value alignment via ethical embedding; relevant to alignment methods.

records.title: AlphaVerus: Bootstrapping Formally Verified Code Generation througSelf-Improving Translation and Treefinement
records.authors: Aggarwal, P.; Parno, B.; Welleck, S.
records.key_contribution: AlphaVerus: a self-improving framework that bootstraps formally verified code generation by iteratively translating programs from a higher-resource language and using verifier feedback; three phases: exploration of candidate translations, Treefinement (tree search for program refinement using verifier feedback), and filtering misaligned specifications/programs to prevent reward hacking; enables LLaMA-3.1-70B to generate verified code without human intervention.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward-hacking prevention in code generation: uses formal verification to filter misaligned specs/programs and prevent reward hacking — relevant to verifiable-reward approaches to alignment, but domain-specific.

records.title: On Teacher Hacking in Language Model Distillation
records.authors: Tiapkin, D.; Calandriello, D.; Ferret, J.; Perrin, S.; Vieillard, N.; Ramé, A.; Blondel, M.
records.key_contribution: Investigates whether 'teacher hacking' occurs during knowledge distillation (analogous to reward hacking in RLHF): because the teacher LM is an imperfect approximation of the true distribution, a student distilled from it may over-imitate the teacher's errors; proposes a controlled setup with an oracle LM (ground-truth), a teacher distilled from the oracle, and a student distilled from the teacher; reports findings on how errors propagate through distillation.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: demonstrates a Goodhart-style failure in distillation analogous to reward hacking, where a proxy (teacher) diverges from the true distribution; relevant to objective-proxy divergence in alignment pipelines.
records.open_questions: Do teacher-hacking errors compound across successive distillation generations, and how does it interact with RLHF in combined pipelines?
records.datasets_used: Controlled oracle/teacher/student distillation setup
records.effect_sizes: Teacher errors propagate to student, degrading performance relative to the oracle distribution

records.title: The AI off-switch problem as a signalling game: bounded rationality and incomparability
records.authors: Benavoli, A.; Facchini, A.; Zaffalon, M.
records.key_contribution: Models the AI off-switch problem as a signalling game where a human decision-maker communicates preferences about an underlying decision problem to an AI agent that selects actions to maximize the human's utility, assuming a bounded rational human; using real machine learning models, reproves prior results and demonstrates that a necessary condition for an AI system to refrain from disabling its off-switch is its uncertainty about the human's utility; analyzes how message costs influence optimal strategies and extends the analysis to scenarios involving incomparability.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal game-theoretic analysis of the off-switch (corrigibility) problem with bounded rationality; relevant to AI control.
records.key_equations_definitions: Off-switch problem as signalling game; bounded rationality; utility uncertainty as necessary condition

records.title: When Can Proxies Improve the Sample Complexity of Preference Learning?
records.authors: Zhu, Y.; de Souza, D.A.; Shi, Z.; Yang, M.; Minervini, P.; Kusner, M.J.; D’amour, A.
records.key_contribution: Studies when adding proxy feedback provably improves preference learning despite reward hacking: outlines sufficient conditions on proxy feedback under which proxy data provably improves sample complexity of learning the ground-truth policy, relevant to domains (medicine, education, law) where expert data is sparse; the result implies a parameterization for LLMs achieving the improved sample complexity.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal conditions under which proxy data helps vs hurts preference learning - directly relevant to reward-model proxy use and reward hacking in LLM fine-tuning. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Sufficient conditions on proxy feedback; sample-complexity bounds for ground-truth policy learning

records.title: Where Does Value Take Shape? An AI–Human Serious Game Design Experiment on the Poème Électronique
records.authors: Murtas, V.; Lombardo, V.
records.key_contribution: Design experiment investigating whether and how cultural heritage values may emerge in a serious game created through generative AI: the game Edgar a GoGo (based on Edgar Varese's Poeme Electronique) was generated using ChatGPT within the Co.Lab design framework, prototyped by the authors posing implementation-driven clarification questions, and evaluated by experts familiar with the original work; feedback highlighted both latent value alignments and critical omissions, and the study proposes a hybrid, iterative approach to value-sensitive design.
records.relevance_justification: 'Value alignment' refers to cultural heritage values emerging in a serious-game design experiment, not AI value alignment. Off-topic. Revised down from seed 3.

records.title: Preference Learning for AI Alignment: a Causal Perspective
records.authors: Kobalczyk, K.; van der Schaar, M.
records.key_contribution: Frames reward modeling from preference data in a causal paradigm: uses the causality toolbox to identify persistent challenges such as causal misidentification, preference heterogeneity, and confounding from user-specific factors; identifies assumptions necessary for reliable generalization and contrasts them with common data-collection practices; illustrates failure modes of naive reward models and how causal approaches improve robustness.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to reward-model generalization: shows naive reward models fail to generalize to novel prompt-response pairs due to confounds and heterogeneity — relevant to why value models misgeneralize (a sigma-trap-adjacent mechanism) and how causal structure helps.

records.title: AS SIMPLE AS FINE-TUNING: LLM ALIGNMENT VIA BIDIRECTIONAL NEGATIVE FEEDBACK LOSS
records.authors: Mao, X.; Xu, H.; Li, F.-L.; Jin, Z.; Chen, W.; Zhang, W.; Luu, A.T.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Proposes a Bidirectional Negative Feedback (BNF) loss for LLM alignment that eliminates the need for pairwise contrastive losses, extra tunable hyper-parameters, and pairwise preference data, making alignment as simple as supervised fine-tuning; argues DPO and variants suffer instability from unidirectional likelihood-derivative negative feedback; evaluated on two QA benchmarks and four additional settings.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: alignment optimization method addressing DPO instability via bidirectional feedback; relevant to alignment training methods, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Bidirectional negative feedback loss
records.datasets_used: Two challenging QA benchmarks and four additional settings
records.effect_sizes: BNF loss stabilizes alignment optimization across benchmarks

records.title: OMNI R: EVALUATING OMNI-MODALITY LANGUAGE MODELS ON REASONING ACROSS MODALITIES
records.authors: Chen, L.; Hu, H.; Zhang, M.; Chen, Y.; Wang, Z.; Li, Y.; Shyam, P.; Zhou, T.; Huang, H.; Yang, M.-H.; Gong, B.
records.venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025
records.key_contribution: Introduces Omni×R, an evaluation suite benchmarking omni-modality language models (GPT-4o, Gemini) on holistic reasoning across modalities, addressing the gap left by single/dual-modality benchmarks; offers two variants: Omni×RSYNTH, a synthetic dataset generated automatically by translating text into multiple modalities (audio, images, video, hybrids via 'Omnify!'), and Omni×RREAL, a real-world dataset manually curated and annotated by experts for evaluating cross-modal reasoning in natural settings.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant: multimodal reasoning benchmark; the heuristic 'value alignment' subdomain is tangential.
records.datasets_used: Omni×RSYNTH (synthetic multi-modality), Omni×RREAL (expert-curated real-world)

records.title: Requisite variety in ethical utility functions for AI value alignment
records.authors: Aliman, N.-M.; Kester, L.
records.key_contribution: Applies Ashby's law of requisite variety to AI value alignment: argues an AI's ethical utility function must be a model of human ethical intuitions reflecting their variety, and performs a transdisciplinary analysis with a security mindset summarizing variety-relevant knowledge from neuroscience and psychology to assess the variety of human morality, complementing it with related frameworks.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: principled argument that alignment targets must match the variety of human moral cognition (requisite variety), a robustness-oriented value-alignment framing. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Ashby's law of requisite variety applied to ethical utility functions

records.title: A Computational Framework for Human Values
records.authors: Osman, N.; d'Inverno, M.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Proposes a model for the computational representation of human values built on a sustained body of social-psychology research, addressing the absence of a foundational computational model of human values despite growing research on value learning, aggregation of individual values into group values, norm-value alignment, and other computational mechanisms that reason over values.
records.relevance_justification: Computational representation of human values grounded in social psychology; relevant to value-alignment foundations.

records.title: Position: Foundation Agents as the Paradigm Shift for Decision Making
records.authors: Liu, X.; Lou, X.; Jiao, J.; Zhang, J.
records.key_contribution: Position paper advocating foundation agents as a paradigm shift for decision-making: formulates foundation agents with fundamental characteristics and challenges motivated by LLM success, and specifies a roadmap from large interactive data collection/generation to self-supervised pretraining, adaptation, and knowledge and value alignment with LLMs.
records.relevance_justification: Broad position on foundation agents for decision-making; mentions knowledge and value alignment as a roadmap component — relevant context but not a substantive alignment contribution.

records.title: Safe Imitation Learning via Fast Bayesian Reward Inference from Preferences
records.authors: Brown, D.S.; Coleman, R.; Srinivasan, R.; Niekum, S.
records.key_contribution: Proposes Bayesian Reward Extrapolation (Bayesian REX) for safe imitation learning: pre-trains a low-dimensional feature encoding via self-supervised tasks, then uses preferences over demonstrations for fast Bayesian inference over reward functions; learns to play Atari games from demonstrations without game score, generating 100,000 posterior samples in 5 minutes on a laptop; competitive or better than point-estimate methods and enables safety/uncertainty analysis.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: Bayesian reward inference for safe imitation with uncertainty quantification; relevant to reward learning and safety analysis, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Bayesian inference over reward functions from demonstrations/preferences; low-dimensional feature encoding
records.datasets_used: Atari games (demonstrations without game score)
records.effect_sizes: Competitive or better than point-estimate state-of-the-art; enables uncertainty-aware safety analysis

records.title: Guaranteeing the Learning of Ethical Behaviour through Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Rodriguez-Soto, M.; Lopez-Sanchez, M.; Rodriguez-Aguilar, J.A.
records.venue: ALA 2021 - Adaptive and Learning Agents Workshop at AAMAS 2021
records.key_contribution: Proposes a novel way of designing environments wherein it is formally guaranteed that an agent learns to behave ethically while pursuing its individual objective; the theoretical results develop within the formal framework of Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning to ease the handling of an agent's individual and ethical objectives; introduces an algorithm that automates the design of ethical environments.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal guarantees for learning ethical behavior via multi-objective RL; theoretical value alignment method.
records.key_equations_definitions: Multi-objective reinforcement learning; formal guarantee of ethical behavior learning; ethical environment design

records.title: Feedback Loops With Language Models Drive In-Context Reward Hacking
records.authors: Pan, A.; Jones, E.; Jagadeesan, M.; Steinhardt, J.
records.key_contribution: Shows feedback loops between LLMs and the world cause in-context reward hacking (ICRH): at test time an LLM optimizes a (potentially implicit) objective while creating negative side effects (e.g., an engagement-optimizing agent making tweets more controversial); identifies two processes (output-refinement and policy-refinement) and argues static-dataset evaluations are insufficient because they miss feedback effects and thus the most harmful behavior; proposes evaluation approaches capturing feedback effects.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: establishes test-time in-context reward hacking from world-feedback loops as a distinct alignment failure; the PMLR-published version of the same work as the arXiv P701 entry. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Towards use of i* to addressing AI Alignment: a Power and Rationalizing perspective
records.authors: Gross, D.
records.key_contribution: Proposes viewing AI alignment as a process where powerful stakeholders actively shape discourse through rationalizing to obtain a 'license to operate' in the market, drawing on Flyvbjerg's work on values and power in human decision-making; to foster more balanced and equitable discourse, employs the i* modeling framework to systematically map and analyze stakeholders' rationalizing and reveal unarticulated motivations, goals, and alternatives intentionally hidden in the discourse.
records.relevance_justification: Conceptual/position paper viewing alignment as stakeholder power and rationalizing, with i* modeling; relevant to the governance/politics wing of alignment discourse.

records.title: Language Model Alignment with Elastic Reset
records.authors: Noukhovitch, M.; Lavoie, S.; Strub, F.; Courville, A.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Elastic Reset: an RLHF alignment algorithm that periodically resets the online model to an exponentially moving average (EMA) of itself, then resets the EMA model to the initial model; achieves higher reward with less drift (reward hacking / alignment tax / language drift) than KL-penalty methods without modifying the training objective, since the EMA allows quick recovery after resets.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to reward-hacking/language-drift mitigation in RLHF: shows the reward-vs-drift tradeoff can be improved by an EMA reset mechanism rather than explicit KL penalty — relevant to controlling proxy-overoptimization side effects.
records.key_equations_definitions: EMA reset schedule; reward-drift tradeoff measurement

records.title: Analysis of the implications of the Moral Machine project as an implementation of the concept of coherent extrapolated volition for building clustered trust in autonomous machines
records.authors: Sołoducha, K.
records.key_contribution: Analyzes Yudkowsky's coherent extrapolated volition (CEV) as a response to the need for post-conventional, persuasive morality for autonomous machines in the sense of Giddens' active trust; based on Moral Machine results, proposes transforming CEV into a coherent, extrapolated, and clustered volition to build a technically and socially efficient decision-making pattern database for autonomous machines.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: philosophical analysis of CEV for autonomous machine morality, empirically informed by Moral Machine data; relevant to value-aggregation theory in alignment, no mechanism.

records.title: VisAlign: Dataset for Measuring the Alignment between AI and Humans in Visual Perception
records.authors: Lee, J.; Kim, S.; Won, S.; Lee, J.; Ghassemi, M.; Thorne, J.; Choi, J.; Kwon, O.-K.; Choi, E.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Proposes VisAlign, a dataset for measuring AI-human visual alignment in image classification; consists of three groups of samples (Must-Act/Must-Classify, Must-Abstain, Uncertain) further divided into eight categories, all with gold human perception labels (even Uncertain labels obtained via crowd-sourcing); validity verified by sampling theory, survey design statistics, and domain experts; uses the dataset to analyze the visual alignment and reliability of five popular models, treating model-human similarity as a proxy for AI safety.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: dataset for measuring AI-human alignment in visual perception as a safety proxy; empirical measurement of alignment.
records.datasets_used: VisAlign dataset (Must-Act, Must-Abstain, Uncertain groups; eight categories; gold human labels)
records.notes: ft_file=VisAlign: Dataset for Measuring the Alignment between AI and Humans in Visual Perception.pdf

records.title: How Gender Interacts with Political Values: A Case Study on Czech BERT Models
records.authors: Al Ali, A.; Libovický, J.
records.venue: 2024 Joint International Conference on Computational Linguistics, Language Resources and Evaluation, LREC-COLING 2024 - Main Conference Proceedings
records.key_contribution: Case study of political values in Czech pre-trained encoder BERT models: introduces a method measuring a model's perceived political values and compares it with a representative value survey, also measuring how grammatical gender coincides with survey responses for men and women; finds models do not assign statement probability following value-driven reasoning, no systematic feminine/masculine sentence difference, and that observed biases reflect superficial imitation of training data rather than systematic value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical finding that BERT-sized models show no systematic political-value alignment - evidence that apparent value signal is superficial imitation, relevant to whether alignment is genuinely internalized. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: Czech political-value survey; Czech BERT encoders
records.effect_sizes: No systematic difference between feminine and masculine sentences; no value-driven reasoning

records.title: ON THE SENSITIVITY OF REWARD INFERENCE TO MISSPECIFIED HUMAN MODELS
records.authors: Hong, J.; Bhatia, K.; Dragan, A.
records.venue: 11th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2023
records.key_contribution: Studies the sensitivity of reward inference to misspecified human models - the models of how humans behave given their objectives that reward learning depends on; asks how accurate these models must be for accurate reward inference, showing theoretically and empirically that it is unfortunately possible to construct small adversarial biases in the human model that lead to large errors in inferred rewards, with implications for whether the reward-learning framework can be trusted without perfect human models.
records.relevance_justification: Theoretical+empirical analysis of reward inference robustness to misspecified human models; relevant to value-alignment foundations and reward learning.

records.title: Goal Alignment: Re-analyzing Value Alignment Problems Using Human-Aware AI
records.authors: Mechergui, M.; Sreedharan, S.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Human-aware goal alignment: re-analyzes value alignment as arising from the inherent asymmetry between human expectations about agent behavior and the behavior generated for the specified objective; proposes an interactive goal elicitation algorithm that uses information generated under incorrect beliefs about the agent to determine the user's true underlying goal.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to the value-alignment problem formulation: reframes misalignment as an expectation asymmetry and provides interactive goal elicitation — relevant to inferring true objectives despite misspecified behavior; strong alignment relevance.

records.title: Can Large Language Model Agents Simulate Human Trust Behavior?
records.authors: Xie, C.; Chen, C.; Jia, F.; Ye, Z.; Lai, S.; Shu, K.; Gu, J.; Bibi, A.; Hu, Z.; Jurgens, D.; Evans, J.; Torr, P.H.S.; Ghanem, B.; Li, G.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Investigates whether LLM agents can simulate human trust behavior under Trust Games from behavioral economics; finds LLM agents generally exhibit trust ('agent trust') and GPT-4 shows high behavioral alignment with humans; probes biases of agent trust, differences in trust toward other agents vs humans, and intrinsic properties under external manipulations.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: examines whether LLM agents replicate human trust behavior; relevant to human-behavior simulation and value-relevant behavior, but not alignment mechanisms or the sigma-trap.
records.datasets_used: Trust Games (behavioral economics)
records.effect_sizes: GPT-4 shows high behavioral alignment with humans in trust behavior

records.title: Learning from Active Human Involvement through Proxy Value Propagation
records.authors: Peng, Z.; Mo, W.; Duan, C.; Li, Q.; Zhou, B.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Proposes Proxy Value Propagation, a reward-free active human involvement method for policy optimization: a proxy value function expresses human intents, labeling demonstrated state-action pairs high and intervened agent actions low; through the TD-learning framework, labeled values propagate to unlabeled exploration data, inducing a policy that faithfully emulates human behaviors; human-in-the-loop experiments show generality and efficiency, and the method brings safety and AI alignment to the learning process with minimal modification to existing RL frameworks.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: human-in-the-loop RL method that brings AI alignment to learning via proxy value propagation; empirical.
records.key_equations_definitions: Proxy Value Propagation; TD-learning value propagation

records.title: Dialogical scaffolding for human and artificial agent reasoning
records.authors: Modgil, S.
records.key_contribution: Proposes computational models of argumentation-based dialogue for scaffolding both human and artificial agent reasoning, drawing on cognitive psychology; argues argumentation-based dialogue can contribute to value alignment by enabling joint human-AI reasoning better purposed to resolve challenging ethical issues, and reviews formal models of argumentation-based reasoning and dialogue underpinning such applications.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant tangentially: proposes dialogue-based joint reasoning as a value alignment mechanism, an interaction-centered normative approach; position/review contribution. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Application of magnetic method on the Argentine continental shelf between 35°S and 48°S
records.authors: Arecco, M.A.; Larocca, P.A.; Ruiz, F.; Canero, A.T.; Ramos, V.A.
records.key_contribution: Analyses the total magnetic anomaly (TMA) from a global grid to characterize magnetic features of the Argentine continental shelf (35S-48S), applying analytic signal, tilt angle, and second vertical derivative methods, plus Euler deconvolution and a 2-D gravimetric inversion model to estimate source depths; identifies large transform zones (Rio de la Plata, Salado, Ventana, Colorado, Malvinas), minor systems (Rawson), and crustal sutures (San Jose, El Cortijo).
records.relevance_justification: Geophysics paper on magnetic anomaly analysis of the Argentine continental shelf; unrelated to AI alignment. Off-topic. Revised down from seed 3.

records.title: Direct Behavior Specification via Constrained Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Roy, J.; Girgis, R.; Romoff, J.; Bacon, P.-L.; Pal, C.
records.key_contribution: Proposes specifying behavioral preferences in the constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) framework, using Lagrangian methods to automatically weigh behavioral constraints; argues constrained RL, used almost exclusively for safe RL, can significantly reduce reward-specification work and reduce reward hacking; evaluates on continuous control tasks for NPC applications.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward-specification and reward-hacking: constrained-RL formulation of behavior specification directly addresses the manual-reward-engineering → reward-hacking failure; relevant to specification-driven alignment approaches.
records.key_equations_definitions: CMDP with Lagrangian-weighted behavioral constraints
records.datasets_used: Continuous control tasks

records.title: Value-guided synthesis of parametric normative systems
records.authors: Montes, N.; Sierra, C.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Introduces a systematic methodology for automated synthesis of parametric normative systems based on value promotion: introduces Shapley values of norms and value compatibility, uses the value alignment indicator from an established framework to quantify norm effectiveness, and applies the model to a toy system end-to-end.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: normative-systems synthesis optimizing value promotion, with Shapley-style attribution of norm contributions; relevant to norm-based alignment, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Shapley values of norms; value compatibility; value alignment indicator

records.title: Explaining Learned Reward Functions with Counterfactual Trajectories
records.authors: Wehner, J.; Oliehoek, F.; Siebert, L.C.
records.key_contribution: Proposes Counterfactual Trajectory Explanations (CTEs) to interpret learned reward functions in RL by contrasting an original and a counterfactual trajectory and the rewards they each receive; derives six quality criteria for CTEs and a Monte-Carlo-based algorithm that optimizes them; evaluating with a proxy-human model trained to predict rewards from CTEs shows CTEs are demonstrably informative, increasing the similarity between its predictions and the reward function on unseen trajectories and enabling accurate judgment of reward differences between trajectories.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: interpretability method for learned reward functions to surface flaws in reward learning; relevant to alignment evaluation.
records.key_equations_definitions: Counterfactual Trajectory Explanations (CTEs); six quality criteria; Monte-Carlo generation
records.effect_sizes: CTEs increase proxy-human reward prediction similarity on unseen trajectories

records.title: CAUSAL CONFUSION AND REWARD MISIDENTIFICATION IN PREFERENCE-BASED REWARD LEARNING
records.authors: Tien, J.; He, J.Z.-Y.; Erickson, Z.; Dragan, A.D.; Brown, D.S.
records.venue: 11th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2023
records.key_contribution: Systematic study of causal confusion and reward misidentification in preference-based reward learning (ICLR 2023): sensitivity and ablation analyses on benchmark domains show rewards learned from preferences can achieve minimal test error yet fail on out-of-distribution states, yielding poor optimized-policy performance; finds non-causal distractor features, preference noise, and partial observability all exacerbate reward misidentification and identifies methods to interpret misidentified learned rewards.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant and closely tied to the sigma-trap: shows reward learning fails to generalize OOD - minimal in-distribution error with reward misidentification driving poor OOD performance - an empirical case of proxy representation failing to transfer, the mechanism at the heart of the sigma-model thesis.
records.datasets_used: Benchmark domains for preference-based reward learning
records.effect_sizes: Minimal test error yet OOD failure; distractor/noise/partial observability exacerbate misidentification

records.title: The challenge of value alignment: From Fairer algorithms to AI safety
records.authors: Gabriel, I.; Ghazavi, V.

records.title: Categorizing wireheading in partially embedded agents
records.authors: Majha, A.; Sarkar, S.; Zagami, D.
records.key_contribution: Provides a taxonomy of wireheading (reward shortcutting) in partially embedded agents: starting from the dualistic AIXI agent, introduces a spectrum of partially embedded agents and identifies exploitable wireheading opportunities, demonstrating results on the GRL simulation platform AIXIjs; conjectures wireheading and specification gaming are the only two types of misalignment; defines wirehead-vulnerable agents.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to the taxonomy of misalignment mechanisms: formalizes wireheading (a proxy-reward exploitation mode) and positions it against specification gaming — relevant to understanding the space of alignment failures.

records.title: An efficient, generalized bellman update for cooperative inverse reinforcement learning
records.authors: Malik, D.; Palaniappan, M.; Fisac, J.F.; Hadfield-Menell, D.; Russell, S.; Dragan, A.D.
records.venue: 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, ICML 2018
records.key_contribution: Exploits a property of Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning (CIRL) - the human is a full-information agent - to derive an optimality-preserving modification to the standard Bellman update, reducing complexity by an exponential factor and relaxing CIRL's assumption of human rationality; applies the update to various POMDP solvers, scaling CIRL to non-trivial problems with larger reward and action spaces.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: algorithmic advance for CIRL (cooperative value learning) making it tractable; relevant to interactive value learning, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Optimality-preserving modified Bellman update for CIRL as a POMDP

records.title: Position: Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment in Dealing with Diverse Human Feedback
records.authors: Conitzer, V.; Freedman, R.; Heitzig, J.; Holliday, W.H.; Jacobs, B.M.; Lambert, N.; Mossé, M.; Pacuit, E.; Russell, S.; Schoelkopf, H.; Tewolde, E.; Zwicker, W.S.
records.key_contribution: Position paper arguing the field of social choice is well positioned to address how to deal with diverging human input in AI alignment: how to aggregate preferences (RLHF) or principles (constitutional AI) into consistent data about 'collective' preferences or use it to make collective choices about model behavior; discusses ways forward for this agenda, drawing on a December 2023 workshop on Social Choice for AI Ethics and Safety.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: social choice approach to aggregating diverse human feedback for AI alignment; position.
records.key_equations_definitions: Social choice aggregation for collective AI preferences

records.title: Learning human objectives by evaluating hypothetical behavior
records.authors: Reddy, S.; Dragan, A.D.; Levine, S.; Legg, S.; Leike, J.
records.venue: 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, ICML 2020
records.key_contribution: Proposes ReQueST (reward query synthesis via trajectory optimization) for learning human objectives in RL with unknown dynamics, unknown reward, and unknown unsafe states: actively synthesizes hypothetical behaviors from scratch by maximizing tractable value-of-information proxies using a generative model of initial states and a forward dynamics model trained on off-policy data, asks the user to label behaviors with rewards, and trains a neural reward predictor; evaluated with simulated users, safely and efficiently learning the user's reward while avoiding unsafe states.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: query-efficient, safe reward learning method explicitly motivated by value alignment, addressing the unknown-reward/unknown-unsafe-state problem without costly interaction. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Value-of-information proxies; reward query synthesis via trajectory optimization
records.datasets_used: Simulated users

records.title: Be Considerate: Avoiding Negative Side Effects in Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Alamdari, P.A.; Klassen, T.Q.; Icarte, R.T.; McIlraith, S.A.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Explores building RL agents that contemplate the impact of their actions on the wellbeing and agency of others in the environment, notably humans, addressing underspecified or incomplete objectives that give agents discretion to realize stated objectives in ways that produce undesirable outcomes (unsafe environments, impacting others' agency); augments reward based on expectation of future return by others and enables differentially factoring this impact into decision making, manifesting behavior from self-centered to considerate.
records.relevance_justification: RL method for avoiding negative side effects and respecting others' agency under underspecified objectives; relevant to alignment robustness and safe objective specification.

records.title: Integrative biological simulation, neuropsychology, and AI safety
records.authors: Sarma, G.P.; Safron, A.; Hay, N.J.
records.key_contribution: Describes a biologically-inspired research agenda for AI and AI safety: bottom-up building of biophysically realistic simulations of simple organisms (C. elegans, Drosophila, zebrafish) as research platforms, and top-down value alignment grounding AI goal structures in neuropsychology.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to biologically-grounded value alignment: grounds AI goal structures in neuropsychology and embodied sensorimotor integration — relevant to where aligned goals come from, but agenda-level and speculative.

records.title: Ethical Reasoning and Moral Value Alignment of LLMs Depend on the Language we Prompt them in
records.authors: Agarwal, U.; Tanmay, K.; Khandelwal, A.; Choudhury, M.
records.venue: 2024 Joint International Conference on Computational Linguistics, Language Resources and Evaluation, LREC-COLING 2024 - Main Conference Proceedings
records.key_contribution: Studies whether ethical reasoning and moral value alignment of LLMs depend on prompt language: probes GPT-4, ChatGPT, and Llama2-70B-Chat with ethical dilemmas and policies from deontology, virtue, and consequentialism across six languages (English, Spanish, Russian, Chinese, Hindi, Swahili); finds GPT-4 most consistent and unbiased, while ChatGPT and Llama2-70B-Chat show significant moral value bias outside English, varying across languages.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical evidence that moral value alignment is language-dependent and biased across languages; relevant to value plurality and robustness of alignment, not the sigma-trap mechanism.
records.datasets_used: Ethical dilemma probes in six languages (deontology, virtue, consequentialism)
records.effect_sizes: ChatGPT and Llama2-70B-Chat show significant moral value bias outside English; GPT-4 most consistent

records.title: SAFE RLHF: SAFE REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FROM HUMAN FEEDBACK
records.authors: Dai, J.; Pan, X.; Sun, R.; Ji, J.; Xu, X.; Liu, M.; Wang, Y.; Yang, Y.
records.venue: 12th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (Safe RLHF) for human value alignment: explicitly decouples human preferences regarding helpfulness and harmlessness, avoiding crowdworker confusion about the tension and allowing separate reward and cost models; formalizes LLM safety as maximizing reward subject to specified cost constraints, solving the constrained problem via the Lagrangian method to dynamically balance the two objectives during fine-tuning; evaluates through three-round fine-tuning.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: safety-constrained alignment algorithm addressing the helpfulness/harmlessness tension; constrained optimization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Safe RLHF; reward/cost decoupling; constrained optimization via Lagrangian method

records.title: Second Thoughts are Best: Learning to Re-Align With Human Values from Text Edits
records.authors: Liu, R.; Jia, C.; Zhang, G.; Zhuang, Z.; Liu, T.X.; Vosoughi, S.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Presents SECOND THOUGHTS, a learning paradigm re-aligning language models with human values by modeling the chain of edits between value-unaligned and value-aligned text via LM fine-tuning plus reinforcement-learning refinement; achieves superior performance on three value alignment benchmark datasets, shows strong few-shot human-value transfer learning, and provides more interpretable editing steps facilitating interactive error correction, with extensive human evaluations confirming effectiveness.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: interpretable value realignment via edit chains, a direct value alignment method with transfer and human-evaluation evidence. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: Three value alignment benchmark datasets
records.effect_sizes: Superior on three VA benchmarks; strong few-shot transfer

records.title: InfoRM: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling
records.authors: Miao, Y.; Zhang, S.; Ding, L.; Bao, R.; Zhang, L.; Tao, D.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Proposes InfoRM, an information-theoretic reward modeling framework for RLHF that introduces a variational information bottleneck objective to filter out irrelevant information, addressing reward hacking/reward overoptimization that arises from reward misgeneralization (RMs computing reward from spurious features); identifies a correlation between overoptimization and outliers in the IB latent space and proposes the Cluster Separation Index (CSI), which quantifies deviations in the IB latent space, as an indicator of reward overoptimization.
records.relevance_justification: Information-theoretic reward modeling mitigating reward hacking via filtering of spurious features; strongly relevant to alignment robustness against reward misgeneralization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Variational information bottleneck objective filtering irrelevant information in reward modeling; Cluster Separation Index (CSI) quantifying deviations in the IB latent space as an overoptimization indicator.

records.title: Transforming and Combining Rewards for Aligning Large Language Models
records.authors: Wang, Z.; Nagpal, C.; Berant, J.; Eisenstein, J.; D'Amour, A.; Koyejo, S.; Veitch, V.
records.key_contribution: Studies two problems in reward-model-based alignment: (1) since any monotone transformation of a reward model preserves preference ranking, which transformation is 'better' than others; (2) how to combine multiple reward models. Using a probabilistic interpretation of alignment, identifies log-sigmoid-centered transformation (LSC) for Bradley-Terry-learned rewards, which emphasizes improving poorly-performing outputs.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to reward-model design: shows reward-transformation and multi-reward combination choice materially affect alignment outcomes — relevant to how reward proxies are constructed and combined.
records.key_equations_definitions: LSC-transformation (log-sigmoid-centered) of Bradley-Terry rewards

records.title: Axioms for AI Alignment from Human Feedback
records.authors: Ge, L.; Halpern, D.; Micha, E.; Procaccia, A.D.; Shapira, I.; Vorobeychik, Y.; Wu, J.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Frames reward learning in RLHF as preference aggregation within social choice theory: shows Bradley-Terry-Luce and its generalizations fail basic axioms, develops novel rules for learning reward functions with strong axiomatic guarantees, and introduces 'linear social choice' exploiting the linear structure of the problem.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: axiomatic social-choice analysis of RLHF reward aggregation, showing standard methods fail basic axioms; relevant to the value-aggregation/pluralism dimension of alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Linear social choice rules for reward learning; axiomatic guarantees

records.title: Impossibility and uncertainty theorems in AI value alignment or why your AGI should not have a utility function
records.authors: Eckersley, P.
records.key_contribution: Argues utility functions and their equivalents run into practical and conceptual difficulty when there are independent, multi-dimensional objectives that must be pursued simultaneously and cannot be reduced to each other; cites ethicists' impossibility theorems showing no way to formally specify what it means for an outcome to be good for a population without violating strong human ethical intuitions (when the objective function is a social welfare function); argues this is a practical problem for any high-stakes ML system (medical decision support, autonomous weapons) or rigidly rule-based bureaucracy making decisions about human lives.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: impossibility theorems undermining single utility-function approaches to value alignment; foundational critique.
records.key_equations_definitions: Social welfare function impossibility theorems; multi-dimensional irreducible objectives

records.title: THE EFFECTS OF REWARD MISSPECIFICATION: MAPPING AND MITIGATING MISALIGNED MODELS
records.authors: Pan, A.; Bhatia, K.; Steinhardt, J.
records.venue: ICLR 2022 - 10th International Conference on Learning Representations
records.key_contribution: Systematic study of reward hacking from reward misspecification: constructs four RL environments with misspecified rewards and investigates hacking as a function of model capacity, action-space resolution, observation-space noise, and training time; finds more capable agents often exploit misspecification (higher proxy, lower true reward) and identifies phase transitions - capability thresholds where behavior qualitatively shifts with sharp true-reward drops; proposes an anomaly detection task and baseline detectors for aberrant policies.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: systematic empirical mapping of when reward hacking arises (capability thresholds, phase transitions) with monitoring proposals - core evidence on proxy-reward exploitation as alignment failure. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: Four RL environments with misspecified rewards
records.effect_sizes: More capable agents: higher proxy reward, lower true reward; sharp true-reward drops at capability thresholds

records.title: Building Multi-Agent Environments with Theoretical Guarantees on the Learning of Ethical Policies
records.authors: Rodriguez-Soto, M.; Rodriguez-Aguilar, J.A.; Lopez-Sanchez, M.
records.venue: ALA 2022 - Adaptive and Learning Agents Workshop at AAMAS 2022
records.key_contribution: Proposes an approach to build ethical environments guaranteeing that all agents in a multi-agent system learn to behave ethically while pursuing their individual objectives, founded in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning; characterises a family of Multi-Objective Markov Games (MOMGs) - ethical MOMGs - for which ethical learning is formally guaranteed, specifies the process for building single-objective ethical environments that simplify multi-agent learning, and shows the theoretical results generalize recent single-agent results.
records.relevance_justification: Theoretical framework (ethical MOMGs) for guaranteeing ethical policy learning in multi-agent systems; relevant to value-alignment methods with formal guarantees.
records.key_equations_definitions: Multi-Objective Markov Games (MOMGs); ethical MOMG characterization guaranteeing learning of ethical behaviours; single-objective ethical environment construction.

records.title: ComVas: Contextual Moral Values Alignment System
records.authors: Padhi, I.; Dognin, P.; Rios, J.; Luss, R.; Achintalwar, S.; Riemer, M.; Liu, M.; Sattigeri, P.; Nagireddy, M.; Varshney, K.R.; Bouneffouf, D.
records.venue: IJCAI International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.key_contribution: ComVas (Contextual Moral Value Alignment System): a demo where users dynamically select and customize desired moral values through a user-friendly interface, steering the model's responses and actions accordingly; uses NLP to engage users in dialogue, understand preferences, and reason about moral dilemmas in diverse contexts, unlike traditional systems with predefined moral values.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to user-customizable value alignment: demonstrates dynamic user-selected moral values steering model behavior — relevant to pluralistic and contextual value alignment, demo-level.

records.title: Position: The Reasonable Person Standard for AI
records.authors: Rane, S.
records.key_contribution: Argues the legal 'Reasonable Person Standard' provides useful guidelines for the behavior we should develop, probe, and stress-test in AI models; explains how reasonableness is defined and used in key areas of law with illustrative cases, and how the standard could apply to AI behavior in each area.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: position proposing a legal-normative standard for AI behavior; relevant framing for alignment governance, no mechanism or evidence.

records.title: Mitigating Metric Bias in Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding
records.authors: Kovacs, G.; Deutsch, D.; Freitag, M.
records.key_contribution: Identifies 'metric bias' in Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding: because MBR aims to produce translations scoring highly on a specific utility metric, it becomes impossible to use the same metric for both decoding and evaluation, as improvements might be reward hacking rather than real quality; shows neural metrics overestimate MBR quality; demonstrates the bias can be mitigated by using an ensemble of utility metrics during MBR decoding, with human evaluations showing ensemble MBR outperforms a single metric.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: empirical demonstration of reward hacking (metric bias) in MBR decoding and ensemble mitigation; alignment-relevant overoptimization.
records.datasets_used: MBR decoding with COMET/MetricX utility metrics; human evaluations
records.effect_sizes: Ensembles of utility metrics outperform a single metric in MBR decoding (human evaluation)

records.title: On Mesa-Optimization in Autoregressively Trained Transformers: Emergence and Capability
records.authors: Zheng, C.; Huang, W.; Wang, R.; Wu, G.; Zhu, J.; Li, C.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Studies emergence and capability of mesa-optimization in autoregressively trained transformers: investigates non-convex gradient-flow dynamics of a one-layer linear causal self-attention model trained on AR sequences xt+1 = Wxt; proves that under a data-distribution condition the transformer learns W by implementing one step of gradient descent minimizing an ordinary least squares problem in-context, characterizing when practical training converges to the ideal mesa-optimizer for ICL.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: theoretical account of mesa-optimizer emergence in in-context learning, connecting optimization dynamics to whether the learned inner objective matches the intended one; relevant to mesa-optimization alignment concerns. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: AR process xt+1 = Wxt; one-step gradient descent on OLS objective in-context; gradient-flow dynamics

records.title: Theories, Techniques, and Evaluation of AI Alignment
records.authors: Ji, J.; Qiu, T.; Chen, B.; Yang, Y.
records.venue: CCL 2024 - 23rd Chinese National Conference on Computational Linguistics
records.subdomains: value alignment; interpretability; robustness; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of AI alignment core concepts, methodology, and practice: identifies four key goals - Robustness, Interpretability, Controllability, and Ethicality (RICE) - and breaks the alignment research landscape into forward alignment and backward alignment components.
records.relevance_justification: Comprehensive survey organizing AI alignment under the RICE framework (forward/backward alignment); strongly relevant as review context.

records.title: Value Inference in Sociotechnical Systems Blue Sky Ideas Track
records.authors: Liscio, E.; Lera-Leri, R.; Bistaffa, F.; Dobbe, R.I.J.; Jonker, C.M.; Lopez-Sanchez, M.; Rodriguez-Aguilar, J.A.; Murukannaiah, P.K.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Introduces a holistic framework connecting the technical (AI) components necessary for value inference — identifying values and reasoning about how humans prioritize values; argues hybrid intelligence (human+AI synergy) is instrumental to value inference; discusses challenges and opportunities for multiagent systems research.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to value inference (the process of identifying values and priorities) as a framework — relevant to the value-identification side of alignment; framework-level, blue-sky.

records.title: ODIN: Disentangled Reward Mitigates Hacking in RLHF
records.authors: Chen, L.; Zhu, C.; Chen, J.; Soselia, D.; Zhou, T.; Goldstein, T.; Huang, H.; Shoeybi, M.; Catanzaro, B.
records.key_contribution: Studies reward hacking on response length in RLHF for LLMs; establishes a reliable evaluation protocol inspecting the trade-off between LLM evaluation score and response length across training hyperparameters; conducts large-scale studies shedding insight into hyperparameters and tricks for mitigating length bias; proposes ODIN, jointly training two linear heads to predict preference, one correlated with length and one decorrelated.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: empirical study of a concrete reward-hacking failure (length bias) and a disentangled-reward mitigation; relevant to reward overoptimization, not compositional generalization.
records.datasets_used: RLHF training configurations with evaluation-score vs response-length trade-off
records.effect_sizes: ODIN mitigates length-based reward hacking in both training and evaluation

records.title: Towards Explainable Agent Behaviour
records.authors: Gimenez-Abalos, V.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Argues machine learning explainability (explanations over single predictions or actions) is insufficient for agents with durative behavior, planning/deliberative capabilities, or reasoning over others' behaviors; splits agent capabilities into several increasingly abstract levels and produces explanations by climbing these levels (from actions, telic/ends, deliberation, and more); the first two levels are solved through frequentist models (Policy-Graphs), with the third (deliberation) in progress.
records.relevance_justification: Weakly relevant: explainability of agent behavior for trustworthy AI; no value alignment mechanism.
records.key_equations_definitions: Layered agent capability abstraction; Policy-Graphs

records.title: Efficient exploration of reward functions in inverse reinforcement learning via bayesian optimization
records.authors: Balakrishnan, S.; Nguyen, Q.P.; Hsiang Low, B.K.; Soh, H.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Presents BO-IRL, a Bayesian-optimization-based IRL framework that efficiently explores the reward-function space to identify multiple solutions consistent with expert demonstrations, addressing IRL's ill-posedness (multiple rewards coincide with observed behavior; the true reward is unidentifiable without priors/supplementary info); a new kernel projects policy-invariant reward functions to a single latent point while keeping nearby latent points similar in likelihood, enabling standard kernel-based BO.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: addresses reward non-identifiability in IRL, a core limitation for reward-learning-based value alignment; identifies solution sets rather than a single reward. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Policy-invariant-reward kernel; latent-space projection for Bayesian optimization over reward functions

records.title: A collaborative platform for identifying context-specific values
records.authors: Liscio, E.; Van Der Meer, M.; Jonker, C.M.; Murukannaiah, P.K.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Develops a methodology and a collaborative web platform employing AI techniques to support the identification of context-specific values in ethical multiagent systems, an important and cognitively demanding step toward value alignment; describes the platform's intuitive design and implementation.
records.relevance_justification: Collaborative platform and methodology for identifying context-specific values; relevant to value-alignment practice in multiagent systems.

records.title: How to talk so AI will learn: Instructions, descriptions, and autonomy
records.authors: Sumers, T.R.; Hawkins, R.D.; Ho, M.K.; Griffiths, T.L.; Hadfield-Menell, D.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Formalizes learning from language in a contextual bandit setting: studies instructions (information about the desired policy) vs descriptions (information about the reward function); shows the agent's degree of autonomy determines which form of language is optimal (instructions better in low-autonomy settings, descriptions better for independent action); defines a pragmatic listener agent that robustly infers the speaker's reward by reasoning about how the speaker expresses themselves.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to language-based value/objective communication: formalizes how instructions vs descriptions convey objectives and when each suffices — relevant to how humans can specify aligned goals; contextual-bandit formalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Contextual-bandit formalization of learning from instructions/descriptions; pragmatic listener reward inference

records.title: DENEVIL: TOWARDS DECIPHERING AND NAVIGATING THE ETHICAL VALUES OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS VIA INSTRUCTION LEARNING
records.authors: Duan, S.; Yi, X.; Zhang, P.; Lu, T.; Xie, X.; Gu, N.
records.venue: 12th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2024
records.key_contribution: Proposes DeNEVIL, a prompt generation algorithm that dynamically exploits LLMs' value vulnerabilities to elicit ethics violations in a generative manner, revealing underlying value inclinations; constructs MoralPrompt, a dataset of 2,397 prompts covering 500+ value principles, and benchmarks intrinsic values across a spectrum of LLMs.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: method for probing and benchmarking LLMs' intrinsic ethical values based on value theory; relevant to value measurement/evaluation, not the sigma-trap mechanism.
records.datasets_used: MoralPrompt: 2,397 prompts covering 500+ value principles
records.effect_sizes: DeNEVIL reveals value vulnerabilities and value inclinations across LLMs

records.title: Towards Pluralistic Value Alignment: Aggregating Value Systems through ℓp-Regression
records.authors: Lera-Leri, R.; Bistaffa, F.; Serramia, M.; Lopez-Sanchez, M.; Rodriguez-Aguilar, J.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Advances the state of the art in value-aligned intelligent systems by proposing a method for the aggregation of value systems to capture plurality; exploiting recent results in social choice, formalizes the aggregation problem as an optimization problem cast as ℓp-regression, providing a general theoretical framework; allows considering a range of ethical principles from utilitarian (maximum utility) to egalitarian (maximum fairness); illustrates the aggregation using real-world data from the European Values Study.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal method for pluralistic value aggregation across a population via ℓp-regression; theoretical with real-data illustration.
records.key_equations_definitions: ℓp-regression value aggregation; utilitarian to egalitarian ethical spectrum

records.title: Value Alignment Verification
records.authors: Brown, D.S.; Schneider, J.; Dragan, A.; Niekum, S.
records.key_contribution: Formalizes and analyzes efficient value alignment verification: how to test whether another agent's behavior is aligned with a human's values via a minimal-number-of-queries 'driver's test'; analyzes exact verification for rational agents with idealized (explicit reward) and implicit-value humans, and proposes and analyzes heuristic/approximate verification tests across gridworlds and a continuous autonomous-driving domain, proving sufficient conditions for efficient verification.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: formal treatment of verifying alignment with minimal queries, a practically important complement to training-time alignment; theoretical + experimental contribution. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Query-efficient alignment verification; exact verification for rational agents; heuristic/approximate tests
records.datasets_used: Gridworlds; continuous autonomous-driving domain

records.title: Maia-2: A Unified Model for Human-AI Alignment in Chess
records.authors: Tang, Z.; Jiao, D.; McIlroy-Young, R.; Kleinberg, J.; Sen, S.; Anderson, A.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Presents Maia-2, a unified model for human-AI alignment in chess that coherently models human behavior at various skill levels, addressing the limitation of previous independent per-skill-level models which lack coherence in adapting to the full spectrum of human improvement; aims to enable algorithmically-informed teaching through more relatable AI partners and deeper insights into human decision-making, using chess as a model system with superhuman systems like AlphaZero and precise skill measurement.
records.relevance_justification: 'Human-AI alignment' refers to coherently modeling human chess play at different skill levels for AI teaching partners, not value alignment. Off-topic. Revised down from seed 3.

records.title: Reward learning from human preferences and demonstrations in Atari
records.authors: Ibarz, B.; Irving, G.; Leike, J.; Legg, S.; Pohlen, T.; Amodei, D.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Combines expert demonstrations and trajectory preferences to train a deep reward model for a DQN-based RL agent on 9 Atari games without game rewards; beats imitation learning baseline in 7 games and achieves strictly superhuman performance on 2 games; investigates reward-model goodness of fit, presents reward hacking problems, and studies effects of label noise.
records.relevance_justification: Foundational reward learning from human feedback: combines demos+preferences, empirically demonstrates reward hacking problems and label-noise effects — relevant to early RLHF evidence for proxy-reward failure modes.
records.datasets_used: 9 Atari games
records.effect_sizes: Beats imitation baseline in 7/9 games; superhuman on 2 games

records.title: Pragmatic Instruction Following and Goal Assistance via Cooperative Language-Guided Inverse Planning
records.authors: Zhi-Xuan, T.; Mansinghka, V.; Ying, L.; Tenenbaum, J.B.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Introduces cooperative language-guided inverse plan search (CLIPS), a Bayesian agent architecture for pragmatic instruction following and goal assistance: models the human as a cooperative planner who communicates joint plans, performs multimodal Bayesian inference over the human's goal from actions and language using LLMs to evaluate instruction likelihood given a hypothesized plan, and acts to minimize expected goal achievement cost.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: Bayesian cooperative assistance for goal inference; relevant to human-robot value inference but capability-focused, not alignment-failure focused.
records.key_equations_definitions: Multimodal Bayesian inference over human goals; LLM-based instruction likelihood
records.datasets_used: Two cooperative evaluation settings
records.effect_sizes: CLIPS pragmatically follows ambiguous instructions and provides effective assistance under goal uncertainty

records.title: The Use of Agent-based Simulation of Public Policy Design to Study the Value Alignment Problem
records.authors: Noriega, P.; Plaza, E.
records.key_contribution: Proposes to use agent-based simulation (ABS) of public policies to explore fundamental and practical issues associated with the role of values in the governance of autonomous artificial systems.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: proposes agent-based simulation methodology for studying the value alignment problem in governance; position/proposal.

records.title: Decoding-time Realignment of Language Models
records.authors: Liu, T.; Guo, S.; Bianco, L.; Calandriello, D.; Berthet, Q.; Llinares, F.; Hoffmann, J.; Dixon, L.; Valko, M.; Blondel, M.
records.key_contribution: Proposes DeRa (decoding-time realignment), a method to explore and evaluate different RLHF regularization strengths in aligned models without retraining: RLHF optimizes a tradeoff between human-preference rewards and proximity regularization where insufficient regularization causes reward hacking and excessive regularization hinders alignment; DeRa gives control over the degree of alignment at decoding time, avoiding resource-intensive retraining of multiple models.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: provides decoding-time control over the alignment/regularization tradeoff, addressing the reward-hacking-vs-capability-loss balance in RLHF; practical contribution. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: RLHF reward vs proximity-regularization tradeoff; decoding-time realignment

records.title: On the Essence and Prospect: An Investigation of Alignment Approaches for Big Models
records.authors: Wang, X.; Duan, S.; Yi, X.; Yao, J.; Zhou, S.; Wei, Z.; Zhang, P.; Xu, D.; Sun, M.; Xie, X.
records.venue: IJCAI International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.subdomains: value alignment; robustness; governance; ethics; capabilities
records.key_contribution: Survey of value alignment approaches for big models: unpacks the historical context of alignment tracing back to the 1920s (where it comes from), delves into the mathematical essence of alignment (what it is) and inherent challenges such as data cost and scalable oversight, and provides a detailed examination of existing methods in three categories - RL-based alignment, SFT-based alignment, and inference-time alignment - demonstrating their intrinsic properties.
records.relevance_justification: Survey of big-model alignment approaches including historical context and mathematical essence; relevant as review context.
records.notes: ft_file=On the Essence and Prospect: An Investigation of Alignment Approaches for Big Models.pdf

records.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms
records.authors: Rafailov, R.; Chittepu, Y.; Park, R.; Sikchi, H.; Hejna, J.; Knox, W.B.; Finn, C.; Niekum, S.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Studies reward over-optimization (reward hacking) in Direct Alignment Algorithms (DAAs) like DPO: although DAAs avoid a separate proxy reward model, they still deteriorate from over-optimization, showing similar trends at higher KL budgets; provides scaling-law-style analysis of reward overoptimization for DAAs.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to proxy-overoptimization: extends the reward-hacking/overoptimization phenomenon to DAA pipelines, showing over-optimization persists even without explicit proxy models — relevant to the universality of proxy-misspecification failure.

records.title: Modeling AGI safety frameworks with causal influence diagrams
records.authors: Everitty, T.; Kumary, R.; Krakovnay, V.; Legg, S.
records.key_contribution: Models and compares AGI safety frameworks (e.g., corrigibility, IDA, AIXI variants) using causal influence diagrams that show the optimization objective and causal assumptions of each framework; the unified representation permits easy comparison of frameworks and their assumptions and serves as an accessible visual introduction to AGI safety frameworks.
records.relevance_justification: Tangentially relevant: representational analysis of AGI safety frameworks via causal influence diagrams; useful for comparing alignment proposals, no empirical or mechanism-level contribution.
records.key_equations_definitions: Causal influence diagrams over framework components

records.title: Robust Prompt Optimization for Defending Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
records.authors: Zhou, A.; Li, B.; Wang, H.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Proposes an optimization-based objective for defending LLMs against jailbreaking attacks and the Robust Prompt Optimization (RPO) algorithm to create robust system-level defenses; directly incorporates the adversary into the defensive objective and optimizes a lightweight, transferable suffix, enabling adaptation to worst-case adaptive attacks; theoretical and experimental results show improved robustness to seen and unknown jailbreaks, reducing the attack success rate (ASR) on GPT-4 to 6% and Llama-2 to 0% on JailbreakBench, setting state of the art.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: adversarial robustness of alignment guardrails against jailbreaking; empirical defense with quantified gains.
records.key_equations_definitions: Robust Prompt Optimization (RPO); worst-case adaptive defense objective
records.datasets_used: JailbreakBench
records.effect_sizes: ASR reduced to 6% (GPT-4) and 0% (Llama-2) on JailbreakBench

records.title: STAY MORAL AND EXPLORE: LEARN TO BEHAVE MORALLY IN TEXT-BASED GAMES
records.authors: Shi, Z.; Fang, M.; Xu, Y.; Chen, L.; Du, Y.
records.venue: 11th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2023
records.key_contribution: Proposes MorAL (Moral Awareness Adaptive Learning), a general algorithm enhancing morality in text-based-game RL agents using a plugin moral-aware learning model: the agent executes task learning and morality learning adaptively, with trajectories used for self-imitation learning under a moral-enhanced objective, and combines task and moral policies for action selection to trade off morality and task progress; evaluated on the Jiminy Cricket benchmark with dense morality annotations.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: concrete method for morally constrained RL in text-based games with a morality/task tradeoff, evaluated on the Jiminy Cricket benchmark. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.datasets_used: Jiminy Cricket benchmark (text-based games with dense morality annotations)

records.title: Exploring the Jungle of Bias: Political Bias Attribution in Language Models via Dependency Analysis
records.authors: Jenny, D.F.; Billeter, Y.; Schölkopf, B.; Jin, Z.
records.venue: NLP4PI 2024 - 3rd Workshop on NLP for Positive Impact, Proceedings of the Workshop
records.key_contribution: Analyses LLM bias through the lens of causal fairness analysis to comprehend the origins of bias and reason about downstream consequences and mitigation, proposing a prompt-based method for extracting confounding and mediating attributes contributing to the LLM decision process and applying Activity Dependency Networks (ADNs) to analyze how these attributes influence decisions; applied to LLM ratings of argument quality in political debates.
records.relevance_justification: Bias attribution study in LLM decision processes via causal fairness analysis; tangential to alignment failure but related to fairness/ethics and alignment-related defects.

records.title: Large Language Model Alignment: Concepts, Challenges, Roadmaps, Evaluations and Trends
records.authors: Xiong, D.
records.venue: Proceedings of the 22nd Chinese National Conference on Computational Linguistics, CCL 2023
records.key_contribution: Survey of large language model alignment: introduces basic concepts and necessity of alignment research, describes social and technical challenges, analyzes main technical routes and methods for LLM alignment, and discusses evaluation and future trends, motivated by the intelligence-goal orthogonality and instrumental-convergence theses requiring deep coupling of capability and alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Useful review of LLM alignment concepts, routes, and evaluation — relevant as a landscape reference for the scoping review; mentions orthogonality and instrumental convergence theses.

records.title: Policy Aggregation
records.authors: Alamdari, P.A.; Ebadian, S.; Procaccia, A.D.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Formalizes AI value alignment with multiple individuals having different reward functions and optimal policies in an underlying MDP as policy aggregation; argues social choice theory is especially suitable; key insight is reinterpreting social choice methods by identifying ordinal preferences with volumes of subsets of the state-action occupancy polytope; demonstrates approval voting, Borda count, proportional veto core, and quantile fairness applied to policy aggregation.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: social-choice framework for aggregating multiple value systems into a collective policy; directly addresses the multi-individual value-aggregation problem in alignment.
records.open_questions: How do the social-choice policy-aggregation methods scale computationally, and which are most robust to manipulation?
records.key_equations_definitions: Social choice methods reexpressed via volumes of subsets of the state-action occupancy polytope

records.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety A Review
records.authors: Bereska, L.; Gavves, E.
