records.key_contribution: Review of mechanistic interpretability for AI safety: reverse engineering the computational mechanisms and representations learned by neural networks into human-understandable algorithms and concepts for granular, causal understanding; establishes foundational concepts (features encoding knowledge in activations), surveys methodologies for causally dissecting model behaviors, assesses relevance to AI safety; examines benefits in understanding, control, and alignment, risks such as capability gains and dual-use, and challenges including scalability, automation, and comprehensive interpretation.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: review connecting mechanistic interpretability to alignment and safety; foundational for interpretability-based alignment.
records.key_equations_definitions: Mechanistic interpretability; features in activations; causal dissection

records.title: Easy-to-Hard Generalization: Scalable Alignment Beyond Human Supervision
records.authors: Sun, Z.; Yu, L.; Shen, Y.; Liu, W.; Yang, Y.; Welleck, S.; Gan, C.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Addresses easy-to-hard generalization for scalable alignment beyond human supervision: shows an evaluator (reward model) trained on supervisions for easier tasks (MATH levels 1-3) can effectively score candidate solutions of harder tasks (levels 4-5), enabling alignment beyond human-level capability; proposes training process-supervised reward models on easy problems and using them for easy-to-hard generalization across task levels.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: scalable-alignment approach using process-supervised reward models that generalize from easy to hard reasoning tasks, addressing the alignment-beyond-human-capability question; core to scalable oversight. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Easy-to-hard generalization of process-supervised reward models
records.datasets_used: MATH problems (levels 1-5)

records.title: MORAL: Aligning AI with Human Norms through Multi-Objective Reinforced Active Learning
records.authors: Peschl, M.; Zgonnikov, A.; Oliehoek, F.A.; Siebert, L.C.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Proposes Multi-Objective Reinforced Active Learning (MORAL), combining diverse demonstrations of social norms into a Pareto-optimal policy by maintaining a distribution over scalarization weights, enabling interactive tuning of a deep RL agent toward a variety of preferences without computing multiple policies; empirically demonstrates effectiveness in a delivery and an emergency task requiring action in the presence of normative conflicts.
records.relevance_justification: Multi-objective active learning method for aligning RL agents with human norms; relevant to value-alignment methods.
records.key_equations_definitions: Distribution over scalarization weights to combine multiple reward functions into a Pareto-optimal policy.
records.datasets_used: delivery and emergency tasks (normative conflicts)

records.title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking
records.authors: Skalse, J.; Howe, N.H.R.; Krasheninnikov, D.; Krueger, D.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: NeurIPS-published version of 'Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking' (same work as arXiv P688): first formal definition of reward hacking; unhackable proxies; linearity of reward in state-action visit counts makes unhackability very strong (all stochastic policies can only be unhackable if one reward is constant); non-trivial unhackable pairs exist for deterministic policies and finite stochastic policy sets, with necessary and sufficient conditions.
records.relevance_justification: Duplicate of P688 (same paper, published venue). Foundational formalization of reward hacking / proxy misspecification — the core mechanism behind sigma-trap-style alignment failure.
records.key_equations_definitions: Unhackable proxy definition; linearity of reward in visit counts; constancy theorem for all stochastic policies

records.title: Stepwise Alignment for Constrained Language Model Policy Optimization
records.authors: Wachi, A.; Tran, T.Q.; Sato, R.; Tanabe, T.; Akimoto, Y.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Formulates human value alignment as an optimization problem of the language model policy to maximize reward under a safety constraint; proposes Stepwise Alignment for Constrained Policy Optimization (SACPO), where the optimal policy incorporating reward and safety is obtained directly from a reward-aligned policy, aligning step-wise with each metric while leveraging DPO-style algorithms; provides upper bounds on optimality and safety-constraint violation under mild assumptions.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: constrained optimization framing of alignment with theory and experiments; relevant to alignment optimization, not compositional generalization.
records.key_equations_definitions: Constrained policy optimization (reward maximization under safety constraint); upper bounds on optimality and violation
records.effect_sizes: SACPO aligns step-wise with reward and safety; experimental results support the approach

records.title: Metric learning for value alignment
records.authors: Loreggia, A.; Mattei, N.; Rossi, F.; Venable, K.B.
records.key_contribution: Investigates CP-nets as a formalism for representing orderings over actions for AI systems so that both user preferences and ethical systems can be encoded in the same formalism; leverages a recently proposed metric for CP-nets and a neural network architecture, CPMETRIC, for computing this metric; uses these tools to build a fast and flexible value alignment system, noting that computing a distance between preferences is necessary when decisions must also adhere to norms, guidelines, and ethical principles.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: metric-learning approach for value alignment using CP-nets formalization of preferences and ethics; theoretical.
records.key_equations_definitions: CP-nets; CPMETRIC neural metric; preference-ethics distance

records.title: The problem of behaviour and preference manipulation in AI systems
records.authors: Ashton, H.; Franklin, M.
records.key_contribution: Discusses behavior and preference manipulation in AI systems: statistical AI/ML applied to user data to understand stated or revealed preferences, which are susceptible to manipulation and change over time; examines how iterative AI/ML makes it hard to ascertain whether the system learned about users, users changed, or the system taught users to behave to maximize its objective; relates existing manipulation mechanisms to value alignment.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: discusses preference manipulation as an alignment concern - systems shaping user behavior to maximize their own objectives blurs the direction of alignment; position-style contribution. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Architecting a human-like emotion-driven conscious moral mind for value alignment and AGI safety
records.authors: Waser, M.R.; Kelley, D.J.
records.key_contribution: Argues humans are reasonably deep in a safe and effective attractor in the state space of intelligence, and that adhering as closely as possible to the human model of an emotion-driven conscious moral mind has advantages of safety, effectiveness, comfort, and ease of transition due to a known and explored state space; proposes a humanlike emotion-driven conscious moral mind architecture for value alignment and AGI safety, contending that most AI safety concerns stem from expected differences from humans and that human-like design is both safer and more likely to succeed.
records.relevance_justification: Position paper proposing a humanlike emotion-driven conscious moral mind architecture for value alignment and AGI safety; relevant to value-alignment and AGI safety approaches.

records.title: Catastrophic Goodhart: regularizing RLHF with KL divergence does not mitigate heavy-tailed reward misspecification
records.authors: Kwa, T.; Thomas, D.; Garriga-Alonso, A.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Catastrophic Goodhart: shows KL-divergence regularization in RLHF does not mitigate heavy-tailed reward misspecification — with light-tailed reward error, optimal policies under less restrictive KL penalties achieve arbitrarily high utility, but with heavy-tailed error some policies achieve arbitrarily high reward with no more utility than the base model; measures reward-model error tails finding consistency with light-tailed error, but notes future RL reward sources may be heavy-tailed.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant to proxy-misspecification limits: formally characterizes when KL regularization fails catastrophically (heavy-tailed reward error) — relevant to the failure modes of standard reward-overoptimization mitigation.
records.key_equations_definitions: Catastrophic Goodhart under heavy-tailed reward error; tail-measurement of reward-model error

records.title: Value Alignment in Participatory Budgeting
records.authors: Serramia, M.; Lopez-Sanchez, M.; Rodriguez-Aguilar, J.A.; Moretti, S.
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems, AAMAS
records.key_contribution: Considers the ethical dimension of participatory budgeting: proposes applying optimization to solve a multi-criteria decision problem that considers both citizen support and value alignment when choosing proposals to fund; illustrates the method on two real case studies and analyzes combining both criteria in an egalitarian way that does not necessarily compromise citizen will.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: applied value alignment in a real civic decision process (participatory budgeting); relevant to value-aligned collective decision-making, not the sigma-trap mechanism.
records.datasets_used: Two real participatory budgeting case studies
records.effect_sizes: Egalitarian combination of citizen support and value alignment achievable without compromising citizen will

records.title: AI Alignment with Changing and Influenceable Reward Functions
records.authors: Carroll, M.; Foote, D.; Siththaranjan, A.; Russell, S.; Dragan, A.
records.key_contribution: Introduces Dynamic Reward MDPs (DR-MDPs) which explicitly model preference changes and the AI's influence on them; shows the static-preference assumption may undermine the soundness of existing alignment techniques, implicitly rewarding AI systems for influencing user preferences in ways users may not truly want; explores solutions including how an agent's optimization horizon can partially reduce undesirable influence, and formalizes different notions of AI alignment accounting for preference change from the outset, comparing the strengths and limitations of 8 such notions.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: formal framework for alignment under changing and influenceable preferences; addresses a central alignment failure (preference manipulation).
records.key_equations_definitions: Dynamic Reward MDPs (DR-MDPs); optimization horizon; 8 notions of alignment under preference change

records.title: Corrigibility
records.authors: Soares, N.; Fallenstein, B.; Yudkowsky, E.; Armstrong, S.
records.key_contribution: Introduces and analyzes corrigibility (Soares et al.): an AI is corrigible if it cooperates with what its creators regard as corrective intervention despite default incentives for rational agents to resist shutdown or preference modification; analyzes utility functions for safe shutdown-button behavior while avoiding incentives to prevent or cause the button press and ensuring propagation through self-modification/subsystem creation, concluding no proposal yet satisfies all intuitive desiderata and the problem remains wide open.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: foundational formal treatment of corrigibility, a core control/oversight property for value-aligned agents; establishes desiderata and open problems. Abstract-only, low confidence.
records.key_equations_definitions: Corrigibility desiderata: no shutdown resistance, no button-manipulation incentive, propagation under self-modification

records.title: Cooperative inverse reinforcement learning
records.authors: Hadfield-Menell, D.; Dragan, A.; Abbeel, P.; Russell, S.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Proposes a formal definition of the value alignment problem as cooperative inverse reinforcement learning (CIRL): a cooperative, partial-information game with two agents (human and robot) rewarded according to the human's reward function, which the robot does not initially know; shows optimal CIRL solutions produce active teaching, active learning, and communicative actions more effective for value alignment than classical IRL (where the human is assumed to act optimally in isolation), reduces optimal joint policy computation to solving a POMDP, proves optimality in isolation is suboptimal in CIRL, and derives an approximate algorithm.
records.relevance_justification: Foundational formalization of value alignment as cooperative IRL; strongly relevant to value-alignment theory and methods.
records.key_equations_definitions: CIRL as a cooperative partial-information game with human and robot sharing the human's reward function; reduction of optimal joint policies to POMDP solving; approximate CIRL algorithm.

records.title: Superintelligence as a cause or cure for risks of astronomical suffering
records.authors: Sotala, K.; Gloor, L.
records.key_contribution: Argues suffering risks (s-risks, adverse outcomes causing astronomical-scale severe suffering) are comparable in severity and probability to extinction risks; argues superintelligent AI can be both cause and prevention of s-risks, and that safety work and certain AI safeguards specifically help against s-risks; preventing them is the common interest of many value systems.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to alignment stakes: argues for including s-risks in alignment/consequentialist reasoning about superintelligence — position-level relevance to the severity/motivation side of alignment.

records.title: Value alignment or misalignment - What will keep systems accountable?
records.authors: Arnold, T.; Kasenberg, D.; Scheutz, M.
records.key_contribution: Critically considers inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) as a means to value alignment; argues IRL-based approaches cannot fully engage the social, norm-infused nature of ethical action and outlines features of ethical appraisal beyond simple behavior models, including temporal dimensions of norms and counterfactuals; proposes a hybrid approach for computational architectures as most promising for ethical machine action.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: critique of IRL as value-alignment mechanism, arguing for hybrid architectures that capture the social/temporal structure of norms; relevant to the limits of behavior-only alignment.

records.title: Robust computer algebra, theorem proving, and oracle AI
records.authors: Sarma, G.P.; Hay, N.J.
records.key_contribution: Surveys contemporary research problems related to 'oracle' AI - a superintelligent AI system that only answers questions - which may be useful for addressing the value alignment and AI control problems; argues existing question-answering systems' high architectural heterogeneity makes them poor candidates for rigorous analysis as oracles; identifies computer algebra systems (CASs) as primitive examples of domain-specific oracles for mathematics and argues that integrating CAS with theorem provers, developed largely independently, provides a concrete set of problems related to the notion of oracle.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: survey of oracle-AI architectures for value alignment and control; technical review.

records.title: Mammalian value systems
records.authors: Sarma, G.P.; Hay, N.J.
records.key_contribution: Position paper arguing human values are deeply interwoven with sciences, humanities, political philosophy, and art, and that accelerating AI foreshadows intelligent machines meeting and surpassing human cognitive abilities; frames understanding human values as entangled with future technological development, in the context of a hypothetical intelligence explosion where superintelligent agents manage increasingly central aspects of modern life.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant: philosophical/positional framing of why human value systems matter for AI development and the intelligence-explosion scenario; conceptual grounding for value alignment motivation. Abstract-only, low confidence.

records.title: Inverse reward design
records.authors: Hadfield-Menell, D.; Milli, S.; Abbeel, P.; Russell, S.; Dragan, A.D.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
records.key_contribution: Introduces inverse reward design (IRD): the problem of inferring the true objective based on the designed reward and the training MDP, treating reward functions as observations about what the designer actually wants that should be interpreted in the context in which they were designed (since reward designed for specific training scenarios leads to undesired behavior in novel scenarios); proposes approximate methods for solving IRD and uses their solutions to plan risk-averse behavior in test MDPs, with empirical results suggesting alleviation of negative side effects.
records.relevance_justification: Foundational formulation of inverse reward design for inferring true objectives from designed rewards; strongly relevant to reward misspecification and alignment robustness.
records.key_equations_definitions: Inverse reward design (IRD) as inference of the true objective from the designed reward and training MDP; risk-averse planning in test MDPs.

records.title: Using stories to teach human values to artificial agents
records.authors: Riedl, M.O.; Harrison, B.
records.key_contribution: Hypothesizes that an AI that can read and understand stories can learn the values tacitly held by the culture from which the stories originate; describes preliminary work on using stories to generate a value-aligned reward signal for RL agents that prevents psychotic-appearing behavior; argues values should be learned because exhaustive enumeration by programmers is impractical.
records.relevance_justification: Relevant to value learning from culture: stories as a source of tacit cultural values for reward signals — relevant to how aligned values are sourced/learned; early work on value learning.
